  def _check_json(value: object, depth: int = 0) -> None:
    if isinstance(value, str):
        if _string_size(value) > MAX_STRING_BYTES:
            raise ResourceLimitError("JSON string exceeds the byte limit")
    elif value is None or isinstance(value, bool):
        return
    elif isinstance(value, int):
        if abs(value) >= 10**MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS:
            raise ResourceLimitError("JSON integer exceeds the digit limit")
    elif isinstance(value, float):
        if not math.isfinite(value):
            raise SchemaError("JSON numbers must be finite")
    elif isinstance(value, (dict, list)):
        if depth >= MAX_JSON_DEPTH:
            raise ResourceLimitError("JSON exceeds the nesting limit")
        if isinstance(value, dict):
            for key, item in value.items():
                if not isinstance(key, str):
                    raise SchemaError("JSON object keys must be strings")
                _check_json(key, depth + 1)
                _check_json(item, depth + 1)
        else:
            for item in value:
                _check_json(item, depth + 1)
    else:
        raise SchemaError("Value is not JSON data")

  def decode_json(text: str, *, source: str) -> object:
    """Decode a complete JSON document without duplicate keys or excess resources."""
    if not isinstance(text, str):
        raise SchemaError(f"{source}: expected JSON text")
    if _string_size(text) > MAX_STATE_BYTES:
        raise ResourceLimitError(f"{source}: JSON document exceeds the byte limit")

    def object_pairs(pairs: list[tuple[str, object]]) -> dict:
        result = {}
        for key, value in pairs:
            if key in result:
                raise SchemaError(f"{source}: duplicate object key")
            result[key] = value
        return result

    def parse_integer(value: str) -> int:
        if len(value.lstrip("-")) > MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS:
            raise ResourceLimitError(f"{source}: JSON integer exceeds the digit limit")
        return int(value)

    def reject_constant(value: str) -> object:
        raise SchemaError(f"{source}: invalid JSON number {value}")

    try:
        value = json.loads(text, object_pairs_hook=object_pairs,
                           parse_int=parse_integer, parse_constant=reject_constant)
    except (json.JSONDecodeError, RecursionError) as error:
        raise SchemaError(f"{source}: invalid JSON document") from error
    _check_json(value)
    return value

  def _write_policy(out: Path, output: bytes) -> None:
    """Inspect the opened inode before truncating; aliases cannot redirect a
    write. Opens nonblocking so a FIFO with no reader refuses instead of
    hanging; refuses up front on a platform without O_NOFOLLOW rather than
    crashing on the attribute lookup."""
    if not hasattr(os, "O_NOFOLLOW"):
        raise ValueError(f"{out}: platform has no O_NOFOLLOW support")
    flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK
    try:
        fd = os.open(out, flags, 0o666)
    except OSError as error:
        if error.errno == errno.ENXIO:
            raise ValueError(f"{out} has no reader (FIFO)") from error
        raise
    with os.fdopen(fd, "wb") as sink:
        # `fd` is owned by `sink` from here on: any exception below, including
        # one from set_blocking itself, still closes it via this `with` block.
        os.set_blocking(sink.fileno(), True)
        info = os.fstat(sink.fileno())
        if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_nlink != 1:
            raise ValueError(f"{out} must be a regular file with one hard link")
        os.ftruncate(sink.fileno(), 0)
        sink.write(output)

Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.  ### Actors and lease  Credential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.  owner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Reserved operation names and their unavailable capability mappings are explicit contract declarations, not implemented payload schemas.  Fresh workflow.open on an absent store alone accepts null workflow_id/actor_id/lease_epoch, null job_id, expected_revision 0 and matching project_id. Assign workflow ID once, create operator credential, state and receipt recoverably under one bootstrap lock. Result contains `workflow_id`, `actor_id`, `actor_file`, `lease_epoch`; only credential path is returned. Initialize receipt and revision 0 together. Identical fresh-open replay after lost acknowledgement returns that exact result without creating credentials or workflows; conflicting ID returns revision_conflict. Existing workflow.open requires a valid actor and all existing bindings; it cannot reset or acquire ownership.  Other apply calls authenticate actor-file against its stored current descriptor or a receipt-retained historical descriptor before any mutation. Check project/workflow binding, scope and job first. For an identical recorded request, either a credential matching the receipt's historical authorizing digest or the authenticated current credential of that same actor_id and role at an epoch not earlier than the authorizing epoch may retrieve only that receipt even if its epoch was revoked; this never grants mutation authority. For any new request, require current descriptor and exact current envelope/credential epoch, then CAS and operation preconditions, then persist state plus receipt atomically. Current-credential receipt retrieval uses the historical envelope unchanged and does not require its lease_epoch to equal the current epoch. Historical credentials cannot submit new operations, altered envelopes or recover ownership. Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.  ### Actors and lease  Credential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.  owner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.  ### Export and installed evidence  `contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. Exporter computes SHA-256 of raw schema/fixture bytes and produces `contracts/controller-v1.json`, strict JSON with exactly `{protocol_major, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities}`. protocol_major is integer 1; package_version equals plugin manifest version; digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex; operations/capabilities are unique string lists containing only implemented items. No symlink path components, regular file, under 16777216 bytes. Runtime contract reads installed assets and matches digests/identities; package version may add `+<build>` only. Export is deterministic and cannot read live workflow state. README documents raw bundle SHA-256 and the single installed argv above. No package version bump/publication or installation is authorized.   Details: Documentation-only task. State Python 3.12 minimum, actual implemented operations, raw bundle sha256 and installed argv. Reject duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, bool integers, unknown owned fields and unsupported durable versions; validate before deep copying. Default review cap is 2. Reject process identity, PID, launcher, heartbeat, resource usage and TUI state as workflow fields. Model/session observations later arrive only as explicitly bounded workflow evidence, never execution authority.  Retain source `StateStore(path: Path, *, boundary_hook=None)`, `read()`, `initialize(initial)`, `transaction(mutator, *, expected_revision=None, publication_guard=None)`, `restore(*, expected_revision=None, precondition=None)`, source exception names and six `DurabilityBoundary` values. Preserve source lock/read/publication guards, single-link regular-file checks, bounded reads, CAS under exclusive flock, deep-copy mutation, revision increment, fsync-before-replace, backup/state pair repair and create-only initialization. Keep one last-good `.bak` and `.lock`; failed validation/conflict/publication cannot change the pair. Restore is an offline forensic library primitive, never a CLI operation or a protocol recovery path. It requires readable valid current state and valid backup and refuses with BackupError unless backup lease_epoch, owner, actors and receipts exactly equal current and no credential-intent.json exists. Check these invariants under the same exclusive lock after decoding backup and before any pair publication; precondition(current) alone is insufficient. Only security-identical backups may be restored, with current revision +1. This deliberate tightening of source restore prevents epoch rollback, credential resurrection and receipt loss; characterize it explicitly. Test acquire followed by restore refuses with exact state/backup/credential bytes preserved, and a security-identical backup restore retains source revision and repair outcomes. Corrupt current state refuses with recovery_required and preserves bytes for operator forensic recovery. Never silently overwrite corruption. Test backup/restore and each injected boundary. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.  `resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. The private controller store is `<project-root>/.autopilot/controller/`, directory 0700, with `state.json`, `state.json.bak`, `state.json.lock`, and `actors/`. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. Reject symlink components below the resolved project root, escapes, nonregular/multiply-linked artifacts and payload-selected state paths. Preserve directory descriptor/no-follow creation and ancestor inode identity rechecks from the pinned root resolver; Path.resolve containment alone is insufficient. Project identity is SHA-256 of the resolved root's UTF-8 path. Relocating the installed package preserves functionality; relocating an existing project requires explicit future migration, not identity rewriting.  Durable state has closed top-level keys `schema_version`, `revision`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `repo_root`, `lease_epoch`, `owner`, `actors`, `receipts`, `workflow`. `workflow` is exactly `{batch: null, work: null, tasks: [], review: {cap: 2}, recovery: null, jobs: []}` in this kernel; no operation may mutate these reserves. Later producer PRDs define their expanded schemas and migration. Characterization records each source workflow field and its deferred owner; it does not import process fields or claim full legacy schema equivalence. No generic JSON setter is exported. `owner` is null or `{actor_id, mode, native_session_id, lease_epoch}`; `mode` is `manual\|supervised`. `actors` contains descriptors, never credential secrets. `receipts` maps request IDs to canonical request digests, actor binding and complete original responses. `jobs` is empty and cannot be mutated in AP00018. Actor registry retains only the current operator and current owner descriptors (at most two); historical authorizing digests are receipt-owned, never actor rows. Normal receipt admission stops at 4094 entries. Before writing durable intent or any final credential, serialize and validate the complete candidate and complete response. Normal operation candidates may occupy at most 14680064 bytes (14 MiB), leaving 2097152 bytes for the two emergency operations below the 16777216-byte state ceiling. Each stored core response is bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, including all absolute paths; refuse a root/response that cannot meet this bound before bootstrap. Emergency release/recover may use the reserved bytes only when clearing an active owner; their complete candidate must still validate under the state ceiling. A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. Reserve two further slots exclusively for owner.release/owner.recover; these may clear an active owner at saturation, never acquire a new one. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. CLI callers must bound execution time; tests use a 30-second subprocess deadline. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. Error codes are exactly `invalid_request`, `incompatible_contract`, `revision_conflict`, `wrong_binding`, `missing_capability`, `rejected_evidence`, `recovery_required`. Reject symlink components below the resolved project root, escapes, nonregular/multiply-linked artifacts and payload-selected state paths. Preserve directory descriptor/no-follow creation and ancestor inode identity rechecks from the pinned root resolver; Path.resolve containment alone is insufficient. Project identity is SHA-256 of the resolved root's UTF-8 path. Relocating the installed package preserves functionality; relocating an existing project requires explicit future migration, not identity rewriting.  Durable state has closed top-level keys `schema_version`, `revision`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `repo_root`, `lease_epoch`, `owner`, `actors`, `receipts`, `workflow`. `workflow` is exactly `{batch: null, work: null, tasks: [], review: {cap: 2}, recovery: null, jobs: []}` in this kernel; no operation may mutate these reserves. Later producer PRDs define their expanded schemas and migration. Characterization records each source workflow field and its deferred owner; it does not import process fields or claim full legacy schema equivalence. No generic JSON setter is exported. `owner` is null or `{actor_id, mode, native_session_id, lease_epoch}`; `mode` is `manual\|supervised`. `actors` contains descriptors, never credential secrets. `receipts` maps request IDs to canonical request digests, actor binding and complete original responses. `jobs` is empty and cannot be mutated in AP00018. Actor registry retains only the current operator and current owner descriptors (at most two); historical authorizing digests are receipt-owned, never actor rows. Normal receipt admission stops at 4094 entries. Before writing durable intent or any final credential, serialize and validate the complete candidate and complete response. Normal operation candidates may occupy at most 14680064 bytes (14 MiB), leaving 2097152 bytes for the two emergency operations below the 16777216-byte state ceiling. Each stored core response is bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, including all absolute paths; refuse a root/response that cannot meet this bound before bootstrap. Emergency release/recover may use the reserved bytes only when clearing an active owner; their complete candidate must still validate under the state ceiling. A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. Reserve two further slots exclusively for owner.release/owner.recover; these may clear an active owner at saturation, never acquire a new one. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.  ### Protocol  CLI argv is `["python3", "<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py"]`. Commands are `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`; apply accepts `--actor-file PATH`. No shell invocation or process launch. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. CLI callers must bound execution time; tests use a 30-second subprocess deadline.  Envelope is exactly `{protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id, lease_epoch, payload}`. `protocol_major` is integer 1; request_id and nonnull identities are nonempty strings of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; expected_revision and nonnull lease_epoch are nonnegative integers, never bool. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. Error codes are exactly `invalid_request`, `incompatible_contract`, `revision_conflict`, `wrong_binding`, `missing_capability`, `rejected_evidence`, `recovery_required`. Only revision_conflict is retryable. Rejections retain current revision, or 0 before initialization. Reject malformed envelopes before touching state. Redact diagnostics.  AP00018 implements `workflow.open`, `owner.acquire`, `owner.release`, `owner.recover` and advertises only `workflow.core.v1`. Closed later names are `policy.bind`, `prd.enter`, `task.replace`, `task.start`, `task.finish`, `task.attempt`, `lane.route`, `job.plan`, `job.claim`, `job.record_exit`, `review.record_stage`, `review.close`, `custody.record`, `custody.discharge`, `verification.record`, `phase.handoff`, `prd.stall`, `prd.park`, `prd.defer`, `prd.complete`, `artifact.record`, `records.commit`; these return missing_capability without writes. Unknown operation returns invalid_request. Jobs/reviews/records/waves capabilities are declared unavailable, never advertised or returned as successful stubs.  Payload schemas are closed objects: workflow.open `{}`; owner.acquire `{mode: "manual"\|"supervised", native_session_id: nonempty string}`; owner.release `{}`; owner.recover `{reason: nonempty string, reconciled_job_ids: unique string[]}`. Strings obey the identity bound except reason, bounded to 4096 bytes. Freeze schemas and positive/negative fixtures for all four implemented operations. Reserved operation names and their unavailable capability mappings are explicit contract declarations, not implemented payload schemas.  Fresh workflow.open on an absent store alone accepts null workflow_id/actor_id/lease_epoch, null job_id, expected_revision 0 and matching project_id. Assign workflow ID once, create operator credential, state and receipt recoverably under one bootstrap lock. Result contains `workflow_id`, `actor_id`, `actor_file`, `lease_epoch`; only credential path is returned. Initialize receipt and revision 0 together. Identical fresh-open replay after lost acknowledgement returns that exact result without creating credentials or workflows; conflicting ID returns revision_conflict. Existing workflow.open requires a valid actor and all existing bindings; it cannot reset or acquire ownership.  Other apply calls authenticate actor-file against its stored current descriptor or a receipt-retained historical descriptor before any mutation. Check project/workflow binding, scope and job first. For an identical recorded request, either a credential matching the receipt's historical authorizing digest or the authenticated current credential of that same actor_id and role at an epoch not earlier than the authorizing epoch may retrieve only that receipt even if its epoch was revoked; this never grants mutation authority. For any new request, require current descriptor and exact current envelope/credential epoch, then CAS and operation preconditions, then persist state plus receipt atomically. Current-credential receipt retrieval uses the historical envelope unchanged and does not require its lease_epoch to equal the current epoch. Historical credentials cannot submit new operations, altered envelopes or recover ownership. Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.  ### Actors and lease  Credential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.  owner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.  ### Export and installed evidence  `contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. No symlink path components, regular file, under 16777216 bytes. Runtime contract reads installed assets and matches digests/identities; package version may add `+<build>` only. Export is deterministic and cannot read live workflow state. README documents raw bundle SHA-256 and the single installed argv above. Envelope is exactly `{protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id, lease_epoch, payload}`. `protocol_major` is integer 1; request_id and nonnull identities are nonempty strings of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; expected_revision and nonnull lease_epoch are nonnegative integers, never bool. # Autopilot canonical controller kernel and protocol

Source: [three-layer design](../../designs/00011-autopilot-standalone-design.md). Recovery revision authorized 2026-11-09 by the request to finish portable Autopilot. Supersedes the held v1 for delivery, preserving v1 and its attempt evidence. No publication, live installation, source retirement or custody acceptance.

## Overview

### Problem Statement
Standalone and supervised workflows need the same enforceable writer. The current tested writer lives inside OVCAQ; adding a second legacy backend would split authority.

The v1 attempt stopped during task 7 after prompt-size/replan exhaustion; tasks 1–6 and task-7 tests already landed. Reuse those implementations and evidence after characterization, not by marking new tasks complete from old checkboxes. Close the existing owner, recovery and capacity failures, then complete export and relocation. Preserve the old batch state and counters. Plan bounded tasks with the installed planner's normal budget; do not reuse the failed 40K budget, increase prompt caps or omit test/review roles.

### Target Users
Users running Autopilot independently or through headless OVCAQ, and maintainers verifying the layer boundary.

### Success Metrics
controller_without_upper_layers → one installed writer runs without either upper layer. Named edge/error scenarios must also pass; real-host support requires separate probe evidence.

## Functional Decomposition

### Capability: Kernel

#### Feature: Extract the existing writer
- **Description**: Reuse tested transactional behavior without supervisor dependencies.
- **Inputs**: Pinned OVCAQ state services and characterized source invariants.
- **Outputs**: One packaged Python 3.12 controller and workflow store.
- **Behavior**: Premise: OVCAQ state/store.py and schema.py implement atomic writes, locking and revisions. Extract the workflow kernel with attribution and equivalent corruption/lock/recovery behavior; separate process fields from workflow schema. Recheck current source before moving behavior. Never mutate live source state; no OVCAQ import, process launcher or TUI dependency.

### Capability: Protocol

#### Feature: Typed commands and actor fencing
- **Description**: Publish the canonical controller boundary.
- **Inputs**: Contract A in the design, scoped actor credentials and temporary project roots.
- **Outputs**: Contract/snapshot/apply CLI, immutable export bundle and request receipts.
- **Behavior**: Implement protocol-major 1 and exact envelope/errors from Contract A. Define JSON schemas for every core operation, including explicit fresh-open bootstrap (expected revision zero, workflow ID assigned once). Fresh workflow.open alone permits null workflow/actor/epoch and revision zero on an absent store. Bootstrap creates an operator credential under the private state root (directory 0700, file 0600) and returns only its path. Other apply calls require --actor-file PATH matched to actor ID/scope; credentials never appear in command values or logs. Opening an existing workflow is not an ownership bypass. One execution lease, epoch-fenced job/operator credentials, CAS, identical-payload replay, conflicting-ID refusal and path containment. Bound output/time in clients; no credential values in logs. Publish only implemented kernel operations; later families remain declared but unavailable. CLI: `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`, `--actor-file PATH`. Contract output: protocol_major=1, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities; capability IDs workflow.core.v1, workflow.jobs.v1, workflow.reviews.v1, workflow.records.v1 and optional workflow.waves.v1. Envelope fields: protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id (nullable for operator actions), lease_epoch, payload. Response fields: ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable. Error codes, exactly: invalid_request, incompatible_contract, revision_conflict, wrong_binding, missing_capability, rejected_evidence, recovery_required. Closed operations: workflow.open, policy.bind, owner.acquire/release/recover, prd.enter, task.replace/start/finish/attempt, lane.route, job.plan/claim/record_exit, review.record_stage/close, custody.record/discharge, verification.record, phase.handoff, prd.stall/park/defer/complete, artifact.record, records.commit, plus the optional wave operations.

Contract A bundle for OVCAQ: commit `plugins/autopilot/contracts/controller-v1.json` as a regular file (no symlink in its path, under 16 MiB). It is a strict JSON object (no duplicate keys, no NaN/Infinity) with exactly these keys: protocol_major (int 1), package_version (nonempty str, the plugin manifest version), schema_digest (nonempty str), fixture_digest (nonempty str), operations (list of str), capabilities (list of str). `python3 controller/main.py --json contract` returns the same protocol_major, schema_digest and fixture_digest, a package_version equal to the bundle's or the bundle's plus `+<build>`, and operations/capabilities that are supersets of the bundle's lists. Document the `sha256sum plugins/autopilot/contracts/controller-v1.json` output (sha256 of the raw file bytes) in `plugins/autopilot/README.md`; OVCAQ pins path and digest as `[workflow] contract_bundle` and `contract_bundle_sha256`. The installed controller argv, stated once here and set by OVCAQ as `[workflow] controller_argv`, is `["python3", "<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py"]`.

## Test Strategy

### Critical Scenarios
- **Happy path**: controller_without_upper_layers → one installed writer runs without either upper layer.
- **Edge case**: lost_ack_replay → original receipt survives revision changes.
- **Error case**: lease_exclusion → manual and supervised schedulers cannot both own the workflow.

## Risks

- Do not copy OVCAQ process/run fields into authoritative workflow truth.
- A local credential fence prevents accidental wrong-role calls; it is not a sandbox against unrestricted filesystem access.
- The supported installed workflow builds this package; unavailable package skill entry points stay gated until their own implementation and certification pass. Never modify or run a loop in the frozen claude-autopilot repository.
- Completion requires a fresh-session full review of the whole v2 contract, including reused behavior. Historical AP00018 failures are no longer an acceptable baseline exemption.

## Design Doc

# Autopilot controller kernel and protocol recovery design

## Architecture fit

AP00018 v2 completes the sole portable workflow writer under `plugins/autopilot/controller/`. It does not activate legacy skills or certify a host. AP00019 adds lifecycle/jobs, AP00020 review authority, AP00021 records. OVCAQ remains untouched. Extraction source is OVCAQ commit `cf8be72214a515c84ee42f0d8b30e65cc2a4ebb7`, inspected with `git show`, never checkout HEAD. All tests use temporary roots.

## Module placement

Retain and verify existing runtime files: `controller/main.py`, `controller/autopilot_state/{__init__,schema,store,paths,protocol,actors}.py`, relative to the plugin root. Retain existing schema/fixtures/provenance and add the missing public bundle: `contracts/controller/{workflow-v1,fixtures-v1,provenance}.json` and `contracts/controller-v1.json`. Add maintainer exporter: `tools/autopilot/export-controller-contract.py`. Tests: `tests/autopilot/test_controller_{kernel,protocol,actors}.py`. Edit `plugins/autopilot/README.md` and `plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md`. Characterization/ownership/source-to-target maps live in `contracts/controller/provenance.json`; fixture inputs and expected outcomes live in `fixtures-v1.json`. No supervisor or launcher imports.

## Interfaces & contracts

### Recovery and delivery

Preserve held v1 PRD, receipts, reviews and attempt counters. Re-characterize existing behavior against pinned OVCAQ source before reuse. Do not import old completion flags. All v2 tasks use normal planner budgets and retain independent test writers and patch review. Owner/capacity/recovery tests are mandatory acceptance, never baseline exemptions. Keep package unavailable entry gates and pending custody unchanged.

Refresh tools/autopilot/source-map.json through its generator. Historical AP00013 delivery receipts remain immutable. If shared README/CHANGELOG bytes require later ownership, introduce an explicit tested successor receipt bound to the current revision and raw file digest; do not repin historical receipts or exempt paths. tests/autopilot/test_helper_provenance_real.py and test_package.py must verify successor evidence against current package bytes and actual test results. Final full implementation suite and repository validator must pass. No publication/install/source retirement/push.

### Kernel

Python floor is 3.12; stdlib only. `autopilot_state.schema` exports `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `MAX_STATE_BYTES = 16777216`, `MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2097152`, `MAX_STRING_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 32`, `MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS = 640`, `SchemaError`, `ResourceLimitError`, `decode_json(text: str, *, source: str)`, `validate_state(value: object) -> dict`, and `new_state(*, repo_root: Path, project_id: str, workflow_id: str) -> dict`. Reject duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, bool integers, unknown owned fields and unsupported durable versions; validate before deep copying. Default review cap is 2. Reject process identity, PID, launcher, heartbeat, resource usage and TUI state as workflow fields. Model/session observations later arrive only as explicitly bounded workflow evidence, never execution authority.

Retain source `StateStore(path: Path, *, boundary_hook=None)`, `read()`, `initialize(initial)`, `transaction(mutator, *, expected_revision=None, publication_guard=None)`, `restore(*, expected_revision=None, precondition=None)`, source exception names and six `DurabilityBoundary` values. Preserve source lock/read/publication guards, single-link regular-file checks, bounded reads, CAS under exclusive flock, deep-copy mutation, revision increment, fsync-before-replace, backup/state pair repair and create-only initialization. Keep one last-good `.bak` and `.lock`; failed validation/conflict/publication cannot change the pair. Restore is an offline forensic library primitive, never a CLI operation or a protocol recovery path. It requires readable valid current state and valid backup and refuses with BackupError unless backup lease_epoch, owner, actors and receipts exactly equal current and no credential-intent.json exists. Check these invariants under the same exclusive lock after decoding backup and before any pair publication; precondition(current) alone is insufficient. Only security-identical backups may be restored, with current revision +1. This deliberate tightening of source restore prevents epoch rollback, credential resurrection and receipt loss; characterize it explicitly. Test acquire followed by restore refuses with exact state/backup/credential bytes preserved, and a security-identical backup restore retains source revision and repair outcomes. Corrupt current state refuses with recovery_required and preserves bytes for operator forensic recovery. Never silently overwrite corruption. Test backup/restore and each injected boundary. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.

`resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. The private controller store is `<project-root>/.autopilot/controller/`, directory 0700, with `state.json`, `state.json.bak`, `state.json.lock`, and `actors/`. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. Reject symlink components below the resolved project root, escapes, nonregular/multiply-linked artifacts and payload-selected state paths. Preserve directory descriptor/no-follow creation and ancestor inode identity rechecks from the pinned root resolver; Path.resolve containment alone is insufficient. Project identity is SHA-256 of the resolved root's UTF-8 path. Relocating the installed package preserves functionality; relocating an existing project requires explicit future migration, not identity rewriting.

Durable state has closed top-level keys `schema_version`, `revision`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `repo_root`, `lease_epoch`, `owner`, `actors`, `receipts`, `workflow`. `workflow` is exactly `{batch: null, work: null, tasks: [], review: {cap: 2}, recovery: null, jobs: []}` in this kernel; no operation may mutate these reserves. Later producer PRDs define their expanded schemas and migration. Characterization records each source workflow field and its deferred owner; it does not import process fields or claim full legacy schema equivalence. No generic JSON setter is exported. `owner` is null or `{actor_id, mode, native_session_id, lease_epoch}`; `mode` is `manual|supervised`. `actors` contains descriptors, never credential secrets. `receipts` maps request IDs to canonical request digests, actor binding and complete original responses. `jobs` is empty and cannot be mutated in AP00018. Actor registry retains only the current operator and current owner descriptors (at most two); historical authorizing digests are receipt-owned, never actor rows. Normal receipt admission stops at 4094 entries. Before writing durable intent or any final credential, serialize and validate the complete candidate and complete response. Normal operation candidates may occupy at most 14680064 bytes (14 MiB), leaving 2097152 bytes for the two emergency operations below the 16777216-byte state ceiling. Each stored core response is bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, including all absolute paths; refuse a root/response that cannot meet this bound before bootstrap. Emergency release/recover may use the reserved bytes only when clearing an active owner; their complete candidate must still validate under the state ceiling. A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. Reserve two further slots exclusively for owner.release/owner.recover; these may clear an active owner at saturation, never acquire a new one. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.

### Protocol

CLI argv is `["python3", "<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py"]`. Commands are `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`; apply accepts `--actor-file PATH`. No shell invocation or process launch. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. CLI callers must bound execution time; tests use a 30-second subprocess deadline.

Envelope is exactly `{protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id, lease_epoch, payload}`. `protocol_major` is integer 1; request_id and nonnull identities are nonempty strings of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; expected_revision and nonnull lease_epoch are nonnegative integers, never bool. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. Error codes are exactly `invalid_request`, `incompatible_contract`, `revision_conflict`, `wrong_binding`, `missing_capability`, `rejected_evidence`, `recovery_required`. Only revision_conflict is retryable. Rejections retain current revision, or 0 before initialization. Reject malformed envelopes before touching state. Redact diagnostics.

AP00018 implements `workflow.open`, `owner.acquire`, `owner.release`, `owner.recover` and advertises only `workflow.core.v1`. Closed later names are `policy.bind`, `prd.enter`, `task.replace`, `task.start`, `task.finish`, `task.attempt`, `lane.route`, `job.plan`, `job.claim`, `job.record_exit`, `review.record_stage`, `review.close`, `custody.record`, `custody.discharge`, `verification.record`, `phase.handoff`, `prd.stall`, `prd.park`, `prd.defer`, `prd.complete`, `artifact.record`, `records.commit`; these return missing_capability without writes. Unknown operation returns invalid_request. Jobs/reviews/records/waves capabilities are declared unavailable, never advertised or returned as successful stubs.

Payload schemas are closed objects: workflow.open `{}`; owner.acquire `{mode: "manual"|"supervised", native_session_id: nonempty string}`; owner.release `{}`; owner.recover `{reason: nonempty string, reconciled_job_ids: unique string[]}`. Strings obey the identity bound except reason, bounded to 4096 bytes. Freeze schemas and positive/negative fixtures for all four implemented operations. Reserved operation names and their unavailable capability mappings are explicit contract declarations, not implemented payload schemas.

Fresh workflow.open on an absent store alone accepts null workflow_id/actor_id/lease_epoch, null job_id, expected_revision 0 and matching project_id. Assign workflow ID once, create operator credential, state and receipt recoverably under one bootstrap lock. Result contains `workflow_id`, `actor_id`, `actor_file`, `lease_epoch`; only credential path is returned. Initialize receipt and revision 0 together. Identical fresh-open replay after lost acknowledgement returns that exact result without creating credentials or workflows; conflicting ID returns revision_conflict. Existing workflow.open requires a valid actor and all existing bindings; it cannot reset or acquire ownership.

Other apply calls authenticate actor-file against its stored current descriptor or a receipt-retained historical descriptor before any mutation. Check project/workflow binding, scope and job first. For an identical recorded request, either a credential matching the receipt's historical authorizing digest or the authenticated current credential of that same actor_id and role at an epoch not earlier than the authorizing epoch may retrieve only that receipt even if its epoch was revoked; this never grants mutation authority. For any new request, require current descriptor and exact current envelope/credential epoch, then CAS and operation preconditions, then persist state plus receipt atomically. Current-credential receipt retrieval uses the historical envelope unchanged and does not require its lease_epoch to equal the current epoch. Historical credentials cannot submit new operations, altered envelopes or recover ownership. Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.

### Actors and lease

Credential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.

owner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.

### Export and installed evidence

`contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. Exporter computes SHA-256 of raw schema/fixture bytes and produces `contracts/controller-v1.json`, strict JSON with exactly `{protocol_major, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities}`. protocol_major is integer 1; package_version equals plugin manifest version; digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex; operations/capabilities are unique string lists containing only implemented items. No symlink path components, regular file, under 16777216 bytes. Runtime contract reads installed assets and matches digests/identities; package version may add `+<build>` only. Export is deterministic and cannot read live workflow state. README documents raw bundle SHA-256 and the single installed argv above. No package version bump/publication or installation is authorized.

## Data flow

CLI parses bounded input → resolves explicit project → acquires store lock → validates contract/binding/auth and intent admission → reconciles only an admitted matching intent → checks receipt then current epoch/revision → validates operation → durably prepares intent/staged credentials → publishes credentials and receipt/state → emits bounded redacted response. Bootstrap shares the same lock with concurrent bootstrap calls. Later operation handlers never bypass the store transaction. Contract export is read-only except its explicit output bundle.

## Reuse inventory

- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/state/store.py`: extract StateStore durability implementation and exceptions, replacing only schema imports and temporary-prefix branding where recorded. No simplified second writer.
- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/state/schema.py`: reuse strict bounded JSON and owned-field validation patterns; separate workflow fields and explicit new controller identity/lease/receipt schema. Do not import OVCAQ.
- OVCAQ pinned `src/ovcaq/paths.py`: reuse root/path containment concepts. `state/paths.py` arbitrary mutation is intentionally excluded.
- `tools/autopilot/export-policy.py` and existing contract tests: reuse raw-byte digest/version and installed relocation testing patterns; production imports remain within the plugin root.
- Existing protocol.py implements bootstrap/replay; actors.py implements bootstrap credential intent; owner operations are parsed but currently return missing_capability. Extend these seams rather than replacing the writer. Searches cover read/load/decode, validate/check/verify, create/init, resolve/lookup and store/state/actor/lease/receipt; existing facade/contracts are known-term controls. Research evidence records exact commands and findings.

## Alternatives considered

1. Smallest diff: import OVCAQ services directly. Rejected: independently distributable package cannot rely on upper layers or source checkout.
2. Copy the whole OVCAQ state machine. Rejected: process/capability launcher/control ownership would become duplicate authority and expose later families prematurely.
3. Chosen: extract tested transaction mechanics, explicitly characterize workflow schema adaptation, add four kernel operations and credential/receipt fence. More work than imports buys standalone relocation and a versioned producer boundary without a second backend.

## Risks & edge cases

Bob is the operator and owner of recovery. No live state migration occurs: the new private store refuses foreign/unsupported schema rather than converting the current batch. Immutable package rollback, authenticated intent reconciliation and the explicit private archive/new-workflow procedure provide operator recovery; fenced forensic restore is never a way to roll back protocol effects; downgrade refuses newer state. POSIX flock/fsync support is required and unsupported filesystems fail explicitly. Credentials prevent accidental cross-role use, not unrestricted filesystem access. Finite receipt capacity preserves replay semantics at the cost of eventual explicit recovery/migration. Next changes are lifecycle/jobs, review policy and record commits; reserved namespaces and durable job reconciliation support them without granting their capabilities now. Bootstrap and credential rotation are the largest crash-consistency risks and require boundary injection. Snapshot may reveal workflow metadata but never secrets. No deletion/export compliance obligation beyond local operator-owned files is introduced; snapshot exports nonsecret state, deliberate project removal is operator-controlled.

## Test strategy outline

First freeze source ownership, source-to-target/test maps and fixtures; then test store/schema/path equivalence, protocol/receipts, actor/lease fencing and installed export. Required scenarios: kernel_field_ownership, contract_examples, kernel_equivalence, concurrent_cas (real subprocesses), corrupt_state_recovery, lease_exclusion, wrong_actor, epoch_revoked, lost_ack_replay, fresh_open_replay, controller_bundle_reproducible, controller_without_upper_layers, contract_bundle_pinnable, unsupported_operation_refused. Test rejected calls preserve raw state/backup/credential bytes, duplicate/NaN/deep/oversized inputs, symlink/hardlink/FIFO/path escape, concurrent bootstrap, every durability/credential intent boundary and operator recovery after owner revocation. Installed tests copy only the plugin into an isolated root, exclude checkout/OVCAQ/Tower/author-home from imports and environment, and run CLI subprocesses with bounded deadlines. Run PRD's Python 3.12 pytest command and repository validator. Real host execution remains unavailable without separate probe evidence.

Be extremely concise, skip formalities.\n- Simplest safe assumption when ambiguity isn't material.\n- This file (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md`) is the single source of user-global agent instructions. Claude imports it through `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md`; Codex (`~/.codex/AGENTS.md`), Copilot (`~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md`), Kiro (`~/.kiro/steering/AGENTS.md`), and Pi (`~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) symlink here. Edit this file, never the pointers. New sessions load the updated instructions; custom agent prompts must preserve this shared authority.\n\n## Autonomy — standing authorization\n\n- Own the outcome. For requested work, make the best supported decision, execute, verify, and report. Do not ask the user to approve an obvious next step or end with \"say go\" when the work is already authorized.\n- Routine reversible work is preauthorized: local edits, fixes, documentation, tests, review findings, refactoring needed for the task, dependency/tool use, local commits, and normal fast-forward pushes under the existing git policy. Choose the simplest safe approach; state material assumptions briefly and keep moving. Stay within the requested scope.\n- Ask before an irreversible action or external commitment that is not already authorized: unrecoverable deletion, destructive changes to shared/production data, force pushes, publishing or sending to others, purchases, or access/security changes. Explain the concrete consequence and present the prepared action for approval. A recoverable file edit or a reviewer's low-severity suggestion is not such an action.\n- Investigate missing information first. Prefer a safe reversible default over a preference question. Only request indispensable input when no safe progress is possible; name the blocker once and continue independent work.\n- Review findings are yours to adjudicate: fix supported in-scope defects, reject false positives with evidence, and record genuinely out-of-scope items durably. Do not walk the user through cosmetic or routine technical choices. Preserve every required review lens, test gate, and fresh-session boundary.\n- Respect explicit stops, hard budgets, and scope limits. Use the workflow's existing convergence, deferral, or recovery policy at its cap instead of inventing an approval gate or starting an unbounded repair loop. A routine reversible pause may be resolved under this standing authorization; an irreversible-action pause may not.\n- This policy supersedes older ask-first conventions in personal rules, skills, and host instructions for routine reversible work. Later explicit user restrictions still bind. It does not bypass tool approvals, security controls, or required verification. Carry this authority into delegated tasks and handoffs so another agent does not ask again.\n\n## Workflow\n\n- Preserve model-family diversity independently of the launcher. Anthropic reviewers may use native Claude, Kiro, or Copilot with an explicit Anthropic model of the required tier and effort. Provider quota exhaustion blocks that route, not the model family: try another authorized route before waiting for reset, without asking again. Verify the selected model, retain isolated contexts, every review lens, permissions and evidence gates, and record the actual backend/model. Never substitute `auto`, silently downgrade, retry an exhausted route before reset, or bypass a permission denial. This supersedes older Claude-only routing and Copilot-credit prohibitions; carry it into active-session recovery and handoffs.\n- After completing all PRD tasks, run `/autopilot:review-work-completion` in a fresh session - never from the work session (hand off first; see the review-phase rule below).\n- For end-to-end PRD execution, use `/autopilot:run-autopilot`.\n- Procedures mandated by an invoked skill count as explicitly requested: ponytail (and any other minimalism mode) must never thin, skip, or down-scope skill-mandated steps. Minimalism governs what you build, not whether you follow the skill.\n- Never skip or thin the review phase of `/autopilot:run-autopilot`: every review cycle runs all lenses - consensus (Alice), blind/PRD-only (Blake), doubt+de-slop with rubric R1-R5 (Bob) - regardless of how small, simple, or well-specified the PRD looks. Do not ask whether the review is worth it - the answer is always yes. The worst issues land precisely when the code feels obviously correct. Reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs); the review phase itself runs in a fresh session after the build hand-off (end the turn: set `state.next_phase`, print the banner, STOP; in loop mode the headless session exits and the `autoclaude` wrapper relaunches from `state.json`).
