See `cli/records.py`'s\n`do_stall` docstring for the full contract. **The deferred record is\ndistinct from `state.stall_reason`** — that field is the wrapper's replan\nsignal (`subagent_prompt_overrun`, branch 2 of the Session Loop decision\ntable); `do_stall` never writes it (its own per-PRD reset clears it instead).\n\n| Exit code | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | stalled | print the STALLED banner, continue the batch |\n| 4 | move failed | PAUSE per the mv-verify invariant (`site: \"mv_verify\"`) |\n| 9 | deferred-record I/O failed or custody write failed (PRD already in `hold/`, intent retained; re-run the same stall) | PAUSE (`site: \"statectl_fail\"` family) |\n| 10 | stall_op conflict | PAUSE for human reconciliation |\n| 2 | state unreadable, OR (stderr starts with `autopilot: cap_critical custody capture failed:`) the range capture failed with state and the PRD untouched | corrupted-state row for the former; for the latter retry the same stall ONCE, then PAUSE in every mode: `phase`/`next_phase: \"paused\"`, `pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the capture stderr line>\"}`, PRD left in `wip/`, state otherwise untouched. This is sanctioned batch-halt row 1 (a CRITICAL is about to ship with no custody) — never delete `state.json`, never stall the PRD under another site |\n\nOn exit 0, print the banner and continue the batch:\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── STALLED ({site}) ────────────────\n── moved to docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/ ── advancing to next PRD ─────────\n```\nThen continue: end the turn (the wrapper relaunches on `next_phase:\n\"build\"`), or jump to Phase 0 in-session when interactive. Batch-end review\nlists every stall first, with resume instructions (\"move back to wip/ and\nre-run\").\n\n### Stall `site` slugs\n\nThe `site` slug passed to `autopilot stall --site` (and recorded in its\ndeferred record) names why the PRD stalled. The\nslugs most relevant to the park machinery are below; this is NOT the exhaustive\nenumeration — `references/state-schema.md` is the authoritative list (it also\ncarries `clarification`, `reviewer_fail`, `sub_skill_fail`, and the others):\n\n- `wrapper_died` — the wrapper parked a PRD after a died-session retry budget\n  (or a fingerprint-thrash bound) exhausted; consumed by the Phase 0 \"Handle\n  park request\" handler (`references/phase-build.md`). The `detail` disambiguates\n  death vs thrash, and ends `; lane=<lane_effective>` when the PRD was\n  lane-routed (a solo build that died mid-session, PRD 00205).\n- `design_gate` — a loop-mode Phase 1.5 design gate (`design_gate: user`) that\n  cannot ask a human; records the design doc path in the deferred `detail`.\n- `blocking_escalation` — a loop-mode Phase 5 blocking escalation; records the\n  blocking issue(s) in the deferred `detail`.\n- `design_rework` — a loop-mode Phase 6 rework design (`/autopilot:design-solution\n  --rework`, PRD 00194) that ended with open cardinal sins / blockers after its\n  three dispatches, a missing doc, or an empty `## Review log`; records the\n  rework design doc path and the open finding titles in the deferred `detail`.\n  No fix task was created. On un-park the PRD re-enters the build gate; read\n  the rework doc's open findings before moving it back.\n- `statectl_fail` — a loop-mode `statectl` state-write that failed twice (lock\n  contention, python error, unreadable state); the model no longer hand-edits\n  `state.json` to record this. A failure that survives retry + `autopilot\n  restore` (core `SKILL.md` § State Management) is instead recorded via the\n  `state-write-failed` marker (`references/state-schema.md` § Marker files,\n  raw stderr in `detail`), and the wrapper halts on it.\n- `plan_expansion` — a loop-mode plan that tripped the plan-expansion gate:\n  planned tasks over the loop ceiling (`planned > 15`), an expansion ratio over\n  3.0 with more than 8 planned tasks, or 2 or more unlisted modules against the\n  PRD's Repository Structure tree. `plan-tasks` step 5.5 runs\n  `autopilot check-plan --prd`; exit 3 in loop mode stalls the PRD here before\n  the build starts, so a human splits it instead of the batch grinding on it.\n  Interactive runs only warn. `detail` carries the reasons and the split-note path\n  (`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/split-notes/<prd-stem>.md`, grouped by module, UNLISTED\n  modules first). Records written before PRD 00189 carry the\n  legacy spelling `oversized_plan` for the task-count rule alone. To resume such\n  a PRD deliberately oversized: move it back to `backlog/` and set BOTH\n  `plan_expansion: allow` and an explicit `rework_cap: 3` in its frontmatter\n  before an unattended resume - the gate skips its rules on the override, and\n  neither the gate nor `autopilot frontmatter` raises the cap automatically; an\n  admitted oversized plan needs the extra cycle written down, not assumed.\n- `fast_track_blocked` — a fast-track-lane PRD (`references/lane-fast-track.md`,\n  PRD 00206) whose card's exit rule printed `branch`: a confirmed CRITICAL or\n  HIGH survived the card's roster, so fast-track parked that card's commits\n  under `fast-track/<item>` and the runbook stalls the PRD here. `detail` is\n  `fast-track/<item>: <surviving findings>`. Every earlier card's commits stay\n  on the working branch, since each passed its roster. Phase 0's \"Handle pending\n  custody\" handler (`references/phase-build.md`) closes it with the attended\n  `autopilot custody resolve --prd <stem> --choice <choice>` — `revert`,\n  `branch-and-revert`, or `accept`.\n- `cap_regression` — a loop-mode Phase 5 cap-out whose remaining unresolved\n  findings are all high or below, but `autopilot cap-check` classified at\n  least one of them as a regression introduced by this cycle's own rework\n  (`references/phase-review.md`, the cap-overflow deferral bullet, PRD 00310).\n  `detail` carries the regressed rows' refs and commits from `cap-check`'s\n  stdout (a `\"regression\": null` row gives its ref and reason instead). The\n  stall captures no custody, so no `autopilot custody` command applies to\n  this site. Resume (PRD 00321): the PRD sits in `prds/hold/<filename>`; its\n  regressed rows sit in `deferred/<batch_id>-deferred.json` (the stall row\n  plus the cap-overflow records migrated as `<op_id>-dd<i>`) and in the\n  triage hold stub the cap-out minted after the stall. Fix the regression on\n  a branch, or write a v2 PRD against the stub, then `mv` the original back\n  to `backlog/` when it is ready to run again.\n- `oversized_task`, `escalation_exhausted`, `replan_exhausted`, `clarification` —\n  the pre-existing stall sites (plan-tasks per-task oversize, rework\n  tier-exhaustion, replan-loop exhaustion, and a loop-mode Phase 2 ambiguity\n  under `pause_on_ambiguity`) documented in their own handlers (here and in\n  `references/phase-build.md`) and in `references/state-schema.md`.\n- `assembly_conflict` — a lane `autopilot wave assemble` kept out of the\n  merged assembly, because its rebase conflicted outside the append-only set\n  or its release-checks failed once merged; `detail` names the reason and,\n  for a rebase conflict, the paths. The assemble verb writes this stall site\n  itself, directly, inline in its own merge pass. No session backs it:\n  assemble runs synchronously inside `autopilot wave assemble`'s own\n  process, not as a batch session task. It also carries no state.json behind\n  it, unlike every other stall site in this list, since assemble reads and\n  writes only wave.json.\n\n`scope_alarm` is NOT a stall slug: a loop-mode Phase 5 scope alarm defers the\noverflow (a deferred `scope-overflow` record) and continues; it never stalls the\nPRD (`references/phase-review.md` Safety Checks).\n\n### Systemic-park breaker interaction (`batch.parks_consecutive`)\n\n`batch.parks_consecutive` counts consecutive `wrapper_died` parks with no healthy\nPRD outcome between them; the Phase 0 park handler halts the batch at 2\n(`systemic_park`). `do_stall`'s single commit enforces the reset rule; this\nsection documents it: `batch.parks_consecutive` resets to 0 whenever\n`site != \"wrapper_died\"` — any non-`wrapper_died` stall proves in-skill code\nran and made a decision, so the infrastructure is healthy. The one exception\nis `site == \"wrapper_died\"`: that stall does NOT reset the counter (`do_park`'s\n`_park_mutator` increments it by 1 in the same commit) — otherwise the\nbreaker could never reach 2.\n\n## Cap rotation\n\nReached from **Phase 0** when `state.cap_rotations` gained an entry but no `stall_reason` is set. A Work turn during `build` exceeded the context cap; `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` appended `{task_id, cycle, phase}` to `state.cap_rotations`, reset the in-flight task's status to `pending`, and set `next_phase` to the phase it left (`build` here; a review-phase rework rotation sets `review` and lands on the review gate's Phase 4 third skip instead, PRD 00196) — a ROTATION, not a replan. The session then ends its turn and the loop wrapper relaunches on the non-empty `next_phase`. There is nothing to do here: the rotation is lossless and needs no handler.\n\nThe fresh session resumes `build` by artifact: capsule fresh → skip catchup; `state.tasks` non-empty → skip planning; `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task. Because the in-flight task was reset to `pending`, it is that first non-completed task: its uncommitted partial attempt is discarded and re-attempted. Only the in-flight task's status changes (`in_progress → pending`); other `state.tasks` and `phases_completed` are untouched; `replan_count` is unchanged; no `replan-context.md` is written.\n\n**Livelock guard (in the cap hook).** If the last `cap_rotations` entry already names the in-flight task, a second consecutive fire on the same task means the task is genuinely oversized. The hook does NOT append another rotation; instead it records `stall_reason.stalled == \"oversized_task\"` and instructs the oversized-task stall — handled by the \"plan-tasks stall: oversized task\" procedure below (move the PRD to `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/`, advance to the next PRD). One oversized task costs at most two rotations before a loud stall.\n\n## Work-phase abort: replan procedure\n\nReached from **Phase 0** when `state.stall_reason.stalled` is `\"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (`/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget aborted a task whose assembled prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass). This is the ONE surviving replan path — the context-cap response is rotation (see \"Cap rotation\" above), not replan. The previous session's work aborted from a hook. **The PRD is not broken — one of its tasks produced an oversized subagent prompt.** Instead of stalling the PRD, replan it with smaller tasks and resume.\n\n1. The aborted PRD filename is `state.prd`. Identify the aborted task from `state.task_aborts[-1]` (most recent abort): `task_id`, `cause`.\n2. Read `state.replan_count` (default 0 if absent). Increment in memory.\n3. **Budget floor guard:** compute `target_budget = max(40000, int(75000 / (2 ** (replan_count - 1))))`. This halves the per-task budget on each replan attempt, floored at 40K — the structural minimum for any single-file task (30K overhead + small file + PRD slice). Progression: replan 1 → 75K, replan 2 → 40K (floor), replan 3+ → 40K (floor). If `replan_count > 5` AND the same task keeps aborting, the task is genuinely too execution-heavy for a single agent turn. **In loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set): do NOT pause — the five replans were the retries; follow the \"Loop-mode stall procedure\" above with `site: \"replan_exhausted\"` and continue the batch.** Interactively, PAUSE:\n   ```\n   ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── PAUSED ──────────────────────────\n   ── {replan_count} replans, task still execution-overflowing ───────\n   ── aborted task: {task_id}, cause: {cause} ─────────────────────────\n   ── task may need manual scope reduction in the PRD ─────────────────\n   ```\n   Set `state.phase = \"paused\"` and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`, and write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"replan_exhausted\", \"detail\": \"{replan_count} replans, task {task_id} still execution-overflowing\"}`. Do NOT move the PRD anywhere. Do NOT clear state. STOP and wait for the user. The user will edit the PRD, delete tasks manually, or run `/autopilot:run-autopilot status` to inspect. (Setting `phase`/`next_phase`/`pause_reason` here is what makes the Stop hook halt at this PAUSE — without them, `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` is still set, and Phase 0 would otherwise emit `task_aborted` and re-enter the replan loop.)\n4. Otherwise, prepare the replan:\n   a. Build the completed-work summary AND capture the aborted-task title first (before any deletion). The data available is the `state.tasks[]` snapshot (`{id, name, status, model?, attempts?}` per state-schema row 127) and `state.task_aborts[-1]` (`{task_id, cause}`); `attempts[]` does not carry commit refs (see state-schema row 129 enum). So: for the **completed-work summary**, filter `state.tasks` to `status == \"completed\"` and capture each entry's `name`; if the user wants commit refs in the replan context, they come from `git log` on the active branch, not from `attempts[]`. For the **aborted task**, look up `state.task_aborts[-1].task_id` in `state.tasks[]` and capture its `name`. Description is intentionally not part of the snapshot; the task name + the PRD itself give plan-tasks enough context to scope the replan. Both captures must happen before step 4b clears `state.tasks`.\n   b. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json tasks-clear` (clears `state.tasks`, `tasks_total`, and `tasks_completed` in one write). The completed work is captured in step 4a's summary and the committed code itself; keeping completed entries in `state.tasks` alongside new plan-tasks output would collide on the fresh `task-add` ids (which start at 1) and corrupt the dashboard.\n   c. Write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md` (overwrite if exists):\n      ```markdown\n      # Replan Context\n\n      PRD: {state.prd}\n      Replan attempt: {replan_count}\n      Trigger: {stall_reason.stalled} on task {task_id}\n      Budget: {target_budget} tokens per task\n\n      ## Completed work (do NOT re-plan)\n\n      - {task name from state.tasks[]} {optional: commit-ref from `git log` on active branch, if helpful}\n      - ...\n\n      ## Aborted task\n\n      {aborted task name captured in step 4a; omit this section if step 4a found no matching entry}\n\n      ## Directive\n\n      Plan ONLY the remaining PRD scope (work not in \"Completed work\" above).\n      Target ≤ {target_budget} tokens per task — the last attempt aborted at\n      runtime, so split fine-grained. Budget halves each replan attempt.\n      ```\n   d. Update state:\n      - Set `state.replan_count` to the incremented value.\n      - Leave `phases_completed` as-is — build sub-steps are not tracked there (it should be empty during build); the capsule stays valid for the same branch.\n      - `state.tasks: []`, `tasks_total: 0`, `tasks_completed: 0` (already cleared in step 4b).\n      - Clear `stall_reason`.\n      - Clear `pause_reason` and `cap_pause_reason`, if present (defensive — a stale pause marker from an earlier PAUSE should not survive into the replanned build).\n      - `rework_task_ids: []` (defensive — a stale array would put the next Phase 3 incorrectly into rework mode against deleted task IDs).\n      - Set `phase: \"build\"`, `next_phase: \"build\"`.\n5. Print:\n   ```\n   ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── REPLAN #{replan_count} (≤{target_budget} tok/task) ──\n   ── trigger: {stall_reason.stalled} on {task_id} ────────────────────\n   ── cleared {n} tasks ({m} completed kept in replan-context.md) ─────\n   ── handing off to fresh session for planning ───────────────────────\n   ```\n6. Hand off: end the turn. In loop mode the wrapper reads the non-empty `next_phase: \"build\"` and relaunches; otherwise the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot`. The next session re-enters `build`; with `state.tasks` cleared, Phase 2's tasks-exist skip does not fire, so it plans, detects `replan-context.md`, and passes it to `/autopilot:plan-tasks`.\n\nIf `stall_reason.stalled` is anything else (or absent), return to Phase 0's Normal PRD selection.\n\n## Crash recovery: escalation_exhausted seen at Phase 0\n\n`escalation_exhausted` is owned inline by Phase 6 — the rework path is inside the autopilot flow, so it does its own stall move + clear before signaling. Phase 0 should never see `escalation_exhausted` in normal operation. This handler covers the legacy crash-landed-between-`mv`-and-clear case: a session killed between Phase 6's `mv` and its `stall_reason` clear leaves the PRD already in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` while state still points at it. If it does, treat it as corrupt-state crash recovery: log a warning, do NOT re-run the move (Phase 6 already moved the PRD), and run `autopilot reset-prd` (one call; `cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` is the single authoritative list — it already includes `stall_reason`, so no separate clear is needed) — then fall through to Phase 0's Normal PRD selection so the next PRD gets picked cleanly. A stall performed via `autopilot stall` instead leaves a `state.stall_op` intent on crash, which is reconciled by `autopilot park` (SKILL.md Gate Dispatch's `stall_op` row) or by re-running the stall — not by this handler.\n\n## plan-tasks stall: oversized task\n\nReached from **Phase 2** when `/autopilot:plan-tasks` exits non-zero and writes `state.stall_reason` because a task cannot be split below the per-task budget (150K standard, or the dynamic budget from `replan-context.md` in replan mode — see `plan-tasks/SKILL.md` \"Stall behavior\" and \"Detect replan mode\").\n\n1. Read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`. If `stall_reason.stalled == \"oversized_task\"`, do NOT proceed to Phase 3.\n2. **Delete any tasks `/autopilot:plan-tasks` already created.** `/autopilot:plan-tasks` calls `task-add` before the per-task budget check, so tasks may exist in `state.tasks` by the time the stall fires. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json tasks-clear`. Same pattern as Phase 9 step 5 — prevents Phase 2's `state.tasks`-skip logic from skipping planning on the next PRD.\n3. Run `autopilot stall --prd <filename> --site oversized_task --detail <one-line detail>` (one call — it stamps the intent, moves+verifies, appends the deferred record, and applies the per-PRD reset in its single commit). Delete `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md` if it exists — otherwise the next PRD's planning would falsely enter replan mode (the CLI does not own that file).\n\n   | Exit code | Meaning | Action |\n   |---|---|---|\n   | 0 | stalled | print the STALLED banner below, continue the batch |\n   | 4 | move failed | PAUSE per the mv-verify invariant (`site: \"mv_verify\"`) |\n   | 9 | deferred-record I/O failed or custody write failed (PRD already in `hold/`, intent retained; re-run the same stall) | PAUSE (`site: \"statectl_fail\"` family) |\n   | 10 | stall_op conflict | PAUSE for human reconciliation |\n   | 2 | state unreadable, OR (stderr starts with `autopilot: cap_critical custody capture failed:`) the range capture failed with state and the PRD untouched | corrupted-state row for the former; for the latter retry the same stall ONCE, then PAUSE in every mode: `phase`/`next_phase: \"paused\"`, `pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the capture stderr line>\"}`, PRD left in `wip/`, state otherwise untouched. This is sanctioned batch-halt row 1 (a CRITICAL is about to ship with no custody) — never delete `state.json`, never stall the PRD under another site |\n\n   On exit 0, print:\n   ```\n   ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── STALLED (oversized_task) ─────\n   ── moved to docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/ ── advancing to next PRD ───────\n   ```\n   Then continue: if `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is set, end the turn — the wrapper reads `next_phase: \"build\"` and relaunches (same mechanism as the Phase 9 PRD-to-PRD transition). Otherwise jump back to Phase 0 in this same session to pick the next PRD.\n\n## Rework escalation exhausted\n\nReached from **Phase 6** when a review-flagged task's last attempt was already at tier `\"opus\"` (or at `\"fable\"`, when a rescue attempt was already spent) — the `haiku → sonnet → opus` chain has no higher tier the skill may pick on its own, so the task cannot be reworked automatically. The one exception is the human-gated Fable rescue gate below.\n\nRewrite the attempt entry's `outcome` to `\"rework_failed\"`, then merge into state:\n\n```json\n\"stall_reason\": {\"stalled\": \"escalation_exhausted\", \"task\": \"<id>\"}\n```\n\n(The `outcome` rewrite is forensic — the stall move below clears `state.tasks` immediately after, so the `\"rework_failed\"` value only persists in pre-clear observers (any state.json reader — e.g. the tracon dashboard — catching the window between the rewrite and the clear). It documents the failure mode for external observers in the brief window before reset; the durable record lives in the PRD's commit history and in `stall_reason.stalled` itself.)\n\n### Fable rescue gate (PRD 00076)\n\nRuns BETWEEN the `outcome` rewrite above and the stall move below — after the rewrite so the justification can quote the final `rework_failed` state, before the stall move because that clears `state.tasks`. **Steps 0-4 in this subsection are the GATE's steps** — the stall move below is now one `autopilot stall` call, so a \"step N\" here always means a gate step. `<ledger>` is `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/fable-requests.json` (`references/state-schema.md` § Fable rescue ledger). `fable` is the human-gated rung above `opus` (`references/model-ladder.md` § Rungs); this gate is the only thing that ever selects it.\n\n0. **One-fable-attempt guard.** If the exhausted task's `attempts[-1].model` is already `\"fable\"`, this PRD has had its rescue attempt — skip steps 1 AND 2 entirely and go to step 4 (normal stall). This is a state-side guard, so it holds even if the ledger write of a prior attempt was lost to a crash.\n1. **Spend an approved rescue.** Otherwise run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/fablectl.py <ledger> show <state.prd>`. When it reports `status == \"approved\"`, spend the rescue instead of stalling, **in this order** (each numbered write is durable before the next runs):\n   a. **Queue the retry first** — `task-set-meta <task-id> <meta-json-file>` with payload `{\"model\": \"fable\", \"escalation_reason\": \"fable_rescue\", \"escalated_from\": \"opus\", \"carry_refs\": [\"<Ref cell, upper-cased>\", ...existing entries], \"carry_cycle\": <state.cycle>}` (writes `state.tasks[i].model` directly, no separate mirror write), `task-set-status <task-id> pending`, append the id to `state.rework_task_ids`. These are Phase 6 step 4's existing requeue mechanics (`references/phase-review.md`) with `\"fable\"` as the tier — the gate reuses them, it does not add a dispatch path. `carry_refs` and `carry_cycle` are the link `autopilot review-close` checks before it accepts this task's `carry`-classified findings row, and they are computed by the same conditional union step 4 states; without them the row is refused (`refused: \"carry_unmatched\"`, exit 2).\n   b. **Then claim it** — `fablectl.py <ledger> consume <state.prd>`, which flips `approved` → `consumed`. A second claim for this PRD can never succeed (`consume` exits 3 unless the entry is `approved`).\n   c. **Then clear `stall_reason` from state and continue Phase 6's normal \"Dispatch rework\" path.** Do NOT stall. This path never reaches the stall move below, so `state.tasks` is not cleared and the PRD stays in `wip/` — but that also means the stall move's `autopilot stall` call (whose single-commit reset clears `stall_reason`) never runs, and it is the only other thing that clears `stall_reason`. The `escalation_exhausted` value written above was written in anticipation of a stall that is not happening; leaving it behind would make the next build-gate entry (a cap rotation sets `next_phase: \"build\"`) read it at Phase 0 and run \"Crash recovery: escalation_exhausted seen at Phase 0\" against a healthy PRD that is mid-rework.\n   Any other `show` result (no entry, or `requested` / `rejected` / `consumed`) → continue to step 2.\n2. **Record a new request.** Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/fablectl.py <ledger> request <state.prd> <task_id> <task_name> <batch_id> <justification-json>`, where `justification` is a JSON object with `problem` (what the task could not achieve), `attempts` (the rung-by-rung history, e.g. `haiku(2) -> sonnet(2) -> opus(2), last outcome rework_failed`), and `impact` (what stays broken).\n   - **Exit 3 — the latch already fired** for this PRD (a `rejected` or `consumed` entry): log one line, notify nothing, fall through to step 4.\n   - **Exit 0 — a new request was recorded**: continue to step 3.\n3. **Notify:**\n   ```\n   python3 ~/.claude/hooks/notify.py --send \"autopilot 🆘 <repo>\" \"Fable rescue requested for <prd>: run 'autoclaude approve-fable <prd>' or 'autoclaude reject-fable <prd>'.\"\n   ```\n   `--send` is the CLI path and dispatches unconditionally (the `_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` suppression applies only to hook-event mode), so an in-loop review session does fire this.\n4. **Continue into the stall move below**, unchanged: the PRD parks to `hold/` and the batch drains on. **No new pause path, no new halt class**, and `site` stays `escalation_exhausted`.\n\n**Caller contract for `fablectl` exits 1, 2 and 4** (0 and 3 are normal control flow — `references/state-schema.md` § `fablectl.py`): retry the exact command ONCE. Still 1, 2 or 4 → treat as a sub-skill failure per core `SKILL.md` § Error Handling — loop mode runs the \"Loop-mode stall procedure\" above with `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"` and the raw stderr in `detail`; interactive PAUSEs with the same site. No new halt class.\n\n**Crash windows.** Step 1's queue-then-claim order makes both windows recoverable:\n\n| Crash window | Ledger | State | Next session |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| after (a), before (b) | still `approved` | task queued at `fable` | rework mode dispatches the queued fable retry — the retry is not lost. If it then fails, step 0's guard sees `attempts[-1].model == \"fable\"` and refuses a second rescue |\n| after (b), before (c) | `consumed` | task queued at `fable` | same: rework mode dispatches the queued retry. Nothing re-claims |\n\n### Stall move\n\nThen perform the **stall move**, identical to the \"plan-tasks stall: oversized task\" handler above: run `autopilot stall --prd <filename> --site escalation_exhausted --detail <one-line detail>` (one call — it stamps the intent, moves+verifies, appends the deferred record, and applies the per-PRD reset in its single commit). With the intent-based CLI, the crash window between the move and the reset no longer needs hand-described ordering: a killed stall leaves a `state.stall_op` intent that is reconciled either by `autopilot park` (SKILL.md Gate Dispatch's `stall_op` row) or by re-running the stall.\n\n| Exit code | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | stalled | print the STALLED banner below, continue the batch |\n| 4 | move failed | PAUSE per the mv-verify invariant (`site: \"mv_verify\"`) |\n| 9 | deferred-record I/O failed or custody write failed (PRD already in `hold/`, intent retained; re-run the same stall) | PAUSE (`site: \"statectl_fail\"` family) |\n| 10 | stall_op conflict | PAUSE for human reconciliation |\n| 2 | state unreadable, OR (stderr starts with `autopilot: cap_critical custody capture failed:`) the range capture failed with state and the PRD untouched | corrupted-state row for the former; for the latter retry the same stall ONCE, then PAUSE in every mode: `phase`/`next_phase: \"paused\"`, `pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the capture stderr line>\"}`, PRD left in `wip/`, state otherwise untouched. This is sanctioned batch-halt row 1 (a CRITICAL is about to ship with no custody) — never delete `state.json`, never stall the PRD under another site |\n\nDelete `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md` if it exists (defensive — it should already be gone by the time we reach a rework path; the CLI does not own that file).\n\nOn exit 0, print:\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── STALLED (escalation_exhausted) ──\n── moved to docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/ ── advancing to next PRD ─────────\n```\nThen continue: if `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is set, end the turn — the wrapper reads `next_phase: \"build\"` and relaunches. Otherwise jump back to Phase 0 in this same session to pick the next PRD.\n\n## Cap-Pause Resume Handler\n\nReached from **Phase 0** when `state.phase == \"paused\"` AND `state.cap_pause_reason` is set — Phase 5's cap-pause behavior fired in a prior INTERACTIVE session because the review-rework cap was hit (`state.cycle >= state.rework_cap`). (Loop-mode runs never cap-pause — PRD 00017: they defer ≤high findings and stall on unresolved CRITICALs instead; this handler serves interactive runs only.) The PRD is still in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` and was not advanced. This handler presents the recorded findings to the user and branches on resume or abandon. It is the ONLY consumer of `cap_pause_reason`; it MUST clear the field on resume.\n\n1. **Read the cap-pause state.** From `state.json`: `state.cycle`, `state.rework_cap`, `state.cap_pause_reason.unresolved_findings` (the list of findings Phase 5 collected), and the PRD filename in `state.prd`.\n\n2. **Present the findings to the user.** Use the `AskUserQuestion` tool (the same direct-input mechanism other handlers use for resume/abandon decisions). Show:\n   - The PRD name (strip the `.md` extension).\n   - The cycle / cap (`{cycle}/{cap}`).\n   - Every entry from `cap_pause_reason.unresolved_findings` — each entry's issue, severity, and consensus.\n   Offer two choices:\n   - **Resume** (optionally with a raised cap).\n   - **Abandon** (leave the PRD in place for manual handling).\n\n3. **On \"resume\":**\n   a. Clear `cap_pause_reason` from `state.json` (delete the key entirely; merge-preserving on all other fields).\n   b. Set `state.phase = \"review\"` and `state.next_phase = \"review\"` (the resume continues at Phase 4, which the fresh session reaches via the existing review-phase skip rules).\n   c. If the user selected a raised cap, write the new integer to `state.rework_cap`. Otherwise leave `state.rework_cap` unchanged.\n   d. **Do NOT move the PRD.** It is in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` and stays there.\n   e. **Do NOT replan tasks.** The existing `state.tasks` is preserved; the resume picks up at the next review cycle.\n   f. **Hand off to a fresh session for Phase 4.** End the turn — the same end-turn hand-off as Phase 3. In loop mode the wrapper relaunches on the non-empty `next_phase: \"review\"`; interactively the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` manually.\n   g. Print:\n      ```\n      ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── RESUMING from cap pause ──────\n      ── cap: {cap} ── continuing at Phase 4 (review) in fresh session\n      ```\n   h. STOP.\n\n4. **On \"abandon\":**\n   a. Do NOT clear `cap_pause_reason`. Do NOT change `state.phase` / `state.next_phase`. Do NOT move the PRD. The paused state survives by design — the user wants autopilot to stay out of the way.\n   b. Print:\n      ```\n      ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── ABANDONED at cap pause ──────\n      ── PRD left in docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/ for manual handling ─────────\n      ── re-invoke /autopilot:run-autopilot to revisit, or move/delete the PRD manually\n      ```\n   c. No state advance happens — the wrapper stops on the paused state, so there is no automatic re-entry.\n   d. STOP.\n   e. **Re-entry behavior.** Because the abandon branch leaves `cap_pause_reason` set, a future manual `/autopilot:run-autopilot` invocation will re-trigger this handler with the same findings — it does NOT loop autonomously (no signal is written, so the shell wrapper exited; only an explicit user re-invocation re-enters). To exit the cap-pause loop permanently the user must EITHER pick \"resume\" (clears `cap_pause_reason` per step 3) OR manually edit `state.json` / move the PRD out of `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`.\n\n5. The cap-paused PRD is NEVER re-selected as new work by Phase 0's Normal PRD selection — the handler check fires BEFORE Normal PRD selection (see `references/phase-build.md` Phase 0 \"Handle Work-phase abort\" sub-section) and short-circuits the flow.\n\n6. The handler clears the cap-pause event only on \"resume\" (step 3 deletes `cap_pause_reason`). No publication/install/source retirement/push.\\n\\n### Kernel\\n\\nPython floor is 3.12; stdlib only. `autopilot_state.schema` exports `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `MAX_STATE_BYTES = 16777216`, `MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2097152`, `MAX_STRING_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 32`, `MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS = 640`, `SchemaError`, `ResourceLimitError`, `decode_json(text: str, *, source: str)`, `validate_state(value: object) -> dict`, and `new_state(*, repo_root: Path, project_id: str, workflow_id: str) -> dict`. Reject duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, bool integers, unknown owned fields and unsupported durable versions; validate before deep copying. Default review cap is 2. Reject process identity, PID, launcher, heartbeat, resource usage and TUI state as workflow fields. Model/session observations later arrive only as explicitly bounded workflow evidence, never execution authority.\\n\\nRetain source `StateStore(path: Path, *, boundary_hook=None)`, `read()`, `initialize(initial)`, `transaction(mutator, *, expected_revision=None, publication_guard=None)`, `restore(*, expected_revision=None, precondition=None)`, source exception names and six `DurabilityBoundary` values. Preserve source lock/read/publication guards, single-link regular-file checks, bounded reads, CAS under exclusive flock, deep-copy mutation, revision increment, fsync-before-replace, backup/state pair repair and create-only initialization. Keep one last-good `.bak` and `.lock`; failed validation/conflict/publication cannot change the pair. Restore is an offline forensic library primitive, never a CLI operation or a protocol recovery path. It requires readable valid current state and valid backup and refuses with BackupError unless backup lease_epoch, owner, actors and receipts exactly equal current and no credential-intent.json exists. Check these invariants under the same exclusive lock after decoding backup and before any pair publication; precondition(current) alone is insufficient. Only security-identical backups may be restored, with current revision +1. This deliberate tightening of source restore prevents epoch rollback, credential resurrection and receipt loss; characterize it explicitly. Test acquire followed by restore refuses with exact state/backup/credential bytes preserved, and a security-identical backup restore retains source revision and repair outcomes. Corrupt current state refuses with recovery_required and preserves bytes for operator forensic recovery. Never silently overwrite corruption. Test backup/restore and each injected boundary. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.\\n\\n`resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. The private controller store is `<project-root>/.autopilot/controller/`, directory 0700, with `state.json`, `state.json.bak`, `state.json.lock`, and `actors/`. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\\\\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. Reject symlink components below the resolved project root, escapes, nonregular/multiply-linked artifacts and payload-selected state paths. Preserve directory descriptor/no-follow creation and ancestor inode identity rechecks from the pinned root resolver; Path.resolve containment alone is insufficient. Project identity is SHA-256 of the resolved root's UTF-8 path. Relocating the installed package preserves functionality; relocating an existing project requires explicit future migration, not identity rewriting.\\n\\nDurable state has closed top-level keys `schema_version`, `revision`, `project_id`, `workflow_id`, `repo_root`, `lease_epoch`, `owner`, `actors`, `receipts`, `workflow`. `workflow` is exactly `{batch: null, work: null, tasks: [], review: {cap: 2}, recovery: null, jobs: []}` in this kernel; no operation may mutate these reserves. Later producer PRDs define their expanded schemas and migration. Characterization records each source workflow field and its deferred owner; it does not import process fields or claim full legacy schema equivalence. No generic JSON setter is exported. `owner` is null or `{actor_id, mode, native_session_id, lease_epoch}`; `mode` is `manual|supervised`. `actors` contains descriptors, never credential secrets. `receipts` maps request IDs to canonical request digests, actor binding and complete original responses. `jobs` is empty and cannot be mutated in AP00018. Actor registry retains only the current operator and current owner descriptors (at most two); historical authorizing digests are receipt-owned, never actor rows. Normal receipt admission stops at 4094 entries. Before writing durable intent or any final credential, serialize and validate the complete candidate and complete response. Normal operation candidates may occupy at most 14680064 bytes (14 MiB), leaving 2097152 bytes for the two emergency operations below the 16777216-byte state ceiling. Each stored core response is bounded to 65536 UTF-8 bytes, including all absolute paths; refuse a root/response that cannot meet this bound before bootstrap. Emergency release/recover may use the reserved bytes only when clearing an active owner; their complete candidate must still validate under the state ceiling. A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. Reserve two further slots exclusively for owner.release/owner.recover; these may clear an active owner at saturation, never acquire a new one. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.\\n\\n### Protocol\\n\\nCLI argv is `[\\\"python3\\\", \\\"<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py\\\"]`. Commands are `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`; apply accepts `--actor-file PATH`. No shell invocation or process launch. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. CLI callers must bound execution time; tests use a 30-second subprocess deadline.\\n\\nEnvelope is exactly `{protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id, lease_epoch, payload}`. `protocol_major` is integer 1; request_id and nonnull identities are nonempty strings of at most 256 UTF-8 bytes; expected_revision and nonnull lease_epoch are nonnegative integers, never bool. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. Error codes are exactly `invalid_request`, `incompatible_contract`, `revision_conflict`, `wrong_binding`, `missing_capability`, `rejected_evidence`, `recovery_required`. Only revision_conflict is retryable. Rejections retain current revision, or 0 before initialization. Reject malformed envelopes before touching state. Redact diagnostics.\\n\\nAP00018 implements `workflow.open`, `owner.acquire`, `owner.release`, `owner.recover` and advertises only `workflow.core.v1`. Closed later names are `policy.bind`, `prd.enter`, `task.replace`, `task.start`, `task.finish`, `task.attempt`, `lane.route`, `job.plan`, `job.claim`, `job.record_exit`, `review.record_stage`, `review.close`, `custody.record`, `custody.discharge`, `verification.record`, `phase.handoff`, `prd.stall`, `prd.park`, `prd.defer`, `prd.complete`, `artifact.record`, `records.commit`; these return missing_capability without writes. Unknown operation returns invalid_request. Jobs/reviews/records/waves capabilities are declared unavailable, never advertised or returned as successful stubs.\\n\\nPayload schemas are closed objects: workflow.open `{}`; owner.acquire `{mode: \\\"manual\\\"|\\\"supervised\\\", native_session_id: nonempty string}`; owner.release `{}`; owner.recover `{reason: nonempty string, reconciled_job_ids: unique string[]}`. Strings obey the identity bound except reason, bounded to 4096 bytes. Freeze schemas and positive/negative fixtures for all four implemented operations. Reserved operation names and their unavailable capability mappings are explicit contract declarations, not implemented payload schemas.\\n\\nFresh workflow.open on an absent store alone accepts null workflow_id/actor_id/lease_epoch, null job_id, expected_revision 0 and matching project_id. Assign workflow ID once, create operator credential, state and receipt recoverably under one bootstrap lock. Result contains `workflow_id`, `actor_id`, `actor_file`, `lease_epoch`; only credential path is returned. Initialize receipt and revision 0 together. Identical fresh-open replay after lost acknowledgement returns that exact result without creating credentials or workflows; conflicting ID returns revision_conflict. Existing workflow.open requires a valid actor and all existing bindings; it cannot reset or acquire ownership.\\n\\nOther apply calls authenticate actor-file against its stored current descriptor or a receipt-retained historical descriptor before any mutation. Check project/workflow binding, scope and job first. For an identical recorded request, either a credential matching the receipt's historical authorizing digest or the authenticated current credential of that same actor_id and role at an epoch not earlier than the authorizing epoch may retrieve only that receipt even if its epoch was revoked; this never grants mutation authority. For any new request, require current descriptor and exact current envelope/credential epoch, then CAS and operation preconditions, then persist state plus receipt atomically. Current-credential receipt retrieval uses the historical envelope unchanged and does not require its lease_epoch to equal the current epoch. Historical credentials cannot submit new operations, altered envelopes or recover ownership. Thus in-place operator-file rotation does not prevent the caller reopening that path and retrieving its original receipt after lost acknowledgement; a caller retaining the old bytes may also retrieve that receipt only. Same canonical complete envelope (including expected_revision) under an authenticated binding returns the original response even after revision changes; changed request ID payload/envelope conflicts. Historical receipt retrieval is the sole exception to execution-epoch revocation and returns no credential contents; it cannot replay effects into new ownership. Retain each receipt's original authorizing digest and response until explicit future migration; capacity refusal never evicts them. Unsupported operation and rejected requests never create receipts or change revisions. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.\\n\\n### Actors and lease\\n\\nCredential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.\\n\\nowner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.\\n\\n### Export and installed evidence\\n\\n`contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. Exporter computes SHA-256 of raw schema/fixture bytes and produces `contracts/controller-v1.json`, strict JSON with exactly `{protocol_major, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities}`. protocol_major is integer 1; package_version equals plugin manifest version; digests are lowercase SHA-256 hex; operations/capabilities are unique string lists containing only implemented items. No symlink path components, regular file, under 16777216 bytes. Runtime contract reads installed assets and matches digests/identities; package version may add `+<build>` only. Export is deterministic and cannot read live workflow state. README documents raw bundle SHA-256 and the single installed argv above. Contract/snapshot do not acquire execution ownership; snapshot excludes all credential material.\\n\\n### Actors and lease\\n\\nCredential files are strict JSON with closed keys `{actor_id, project_id, workflow_id, role, lease_epoch, native_session_id, secret}`. Generate secrets using `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`, store only SHA-256 digests in durable actor descriptors, compare with `hmac.compare_digest`. Credential root 0700/file 0600; reject symlinks, hardlinks, wrong permissions and bindings. File contents never enter logs, responses, bundle fixtures or public snapshot. Bootstrap operator is role operator at epoch 0. Execution credential role is owner; its scope allows release and future permitted lifecycle actions, never operator recovery. Future job role is declared but no job credential issuance occurs here.\\n\\nowner.acquire requires current operator authority and no owner; increment epoch, rotate the operator credential to that epoch, and issue one owner credential bound to mode/native_session_id. Operator actor ID remains stable, its new secret replaces the old secret; every epoch-changing operation rotates it in the same recoverable publication. owner.acquire returns `actor_file`/`actor_id`/`lease_epoch` for the owner and `operator_actor_file` for the refreshed operator. Return its path, actor ID and epoch. Concurrent acquires have exactly one winner; an existing owner blocks even when mode differs. owner.release requires the current owner credential; increment epoch and revoke owner credentials. Preserve operator recovery authority across every acquire/release/recover by rotating its descriptor and credential through recoverable intent; do not make an old execution credential an operator. owner.recover requires operator authority plus reason and reconciliation of the durable active/unreconciled jobs; never timeout alone. AP00018 has no jobs and requires both durable jobs and reconciled_job_ids empty. Increment epoch, revoke prior execution actors and clear owner; acquiring again is explicit. Return current operator credential path/epoch where rotation is required. Lost acknowledgements at every credential publication boundary must leave either the old consistent pair or a recoverable intent; never a committed receipt pointing at missing credential bytes. Recovery retries reconcile intent before new work. Failure to reconcile returns recovery_required without accepting another owner. Intent records contain paths/digests/IDs, never plaintext secrets; staged credential bytes remain private 0600. Use one fixed private `credential-intent.json` and private staged/rollback files under actors. Before changing final credentials, stage+fsync all new bytes and rollback copies, then persist+directory-fsync intent containing the canonical request digest, old revision/state digest, candidate state, response/receipt and old/new credential descriptors/paths/digests. Candidate state contains no secrets. Publish final credential files with fsync/replace/directory-fsync, then publish state+receipt through StateStore, then remove intent and private stages with directory fsync. Bootstrap uses the state sidecar lock without recursively locking; factor a locked initialization entry internally. Never acquire a second flock for the same operation. A crash before durable intent leaves only unreferenced private stages; it changes no final credential or state. Bound all controller-owned staging/rollback/temp artifacts to 64 files and 16777216 aggregate bytes. Under the exclusive store lock, descriptor-check and count the existing owned stage/temp files and budget the full proposed set before creating any; refuse with recovery_required without modifying evidence if the new set would exceed either limit, or an owned artifact is unsafe/unreadable. This budget covers bootstrap and owner intent temp files as well as credential stages/rollback files. Never delete an orphan automatically. Document private offline archive/hash verification and attended orphan recovery; archive-based recovery requires the operator to take the workflow offline, retain all bytes, and restore the verified consistent state/credentials before retry. Tests repeatedly crash before durable intent and prove bounded file/byte growth and fail-closed admission at the limit. A crash after intent is reconciled forward exactly once from validated old/candidate state and verified staged/final hashes, or returns recovery_required retaining evidence. A successful receipt is never emitted until final files match its descriptors. Reconciliation admission: strict envelope and project/workflow binding validation precede reconciliation; only the identical intent request authenticated by its recorded old/new authorizing descriptor (or the identical null-bootstrap request) may finish it. All unrelated/invalid requests return recovery_required/wrong_binding without changing bytes. Snapshot never reconciles; it reports recovery_required while an intent exists. A changed bootstrap request ID cannot reconcile another bootstrap. Frozen fixtures enumerate crashes at stage, intent, each credential publication, state publication and cleanup; after recovery the original caller can retrieve the exact receipt using its historical credential. Rejection byte preservation is measured after admitted intent reconciliation only for that successful matching recovery request; rejected calls never reconcile.\\n\\n### Export and installed evidence\\n\\n`contracts/controller/workflow-v1.json` is canonical JSON Schema for durable state and protocol/payload/response definitions. `fixtures-v1.json` freezes named positive/negative scenarios with explicit expected errors and no real secrets. `provenance.json` records OVCAQ repository, exact pin, source-to-target symbol and test maps, hashes, preserved invariants and deliberate exclusions/divergences; preserve MIT attribution in extracted files. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.\\n\\n`resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\\\\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.\n- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`refer\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
