\"style_gate\": \"clean\" | \"fixed:<sha>\" | \"failed:<detail>\" | \"skipped:tier\" | null,\n  \"devon\": \"skipped:prose\" | \"exploit_fixed\" | null,\n  \"devon_exploit\": <string | null>,\n  \"devon_weak_points\": <int | null>,\n  \"devon_in_contract\": [<string>] | null,\n  \"split_hygiene\": \"clean\" | \"fixed:<sha>\" | \"failed:<detail>\" | \"skipped:no-tests\" | null,\n  \"micro_lane\": \"overrun\" | null,\n  \"reflow\": \"<path>:<hunks>\" | null,\n  \"review\": \"failed:<cause>\" | \"failed:invalid_output\" | \"skipped:test-only\" | \"resume_failed\" | null\n}\n```\n\n**Timing is deliberately not an attempt field.** No timestamp, duration or prompt size is stamped here: an attempt spans several dispatches — Tess, Ivan, Pat and their retries — so one pair of stamps could not say which of them took the hour. Those live in the dispatch ledger, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (a start row and one or more end rows per dispatch, joined on `id`, plus one row per session-handoff edge; `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), and a task's runtime is read from its rows there, keyed on `task`.\n\n**Cardinality (PRD 00065)**: today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today.\n\n**Field semantics**:\n\n- `attempt`: 1-indexed; `len(existing) + 1`.\n- `model`: the tier `/autopilot:work` used for this pass. Read from `state.tasks[i].model` when set. On legacy plans where `state.tasks[i].model` is absent, record the effective session-inherited tier as a string (e.g. `\"sonnet\"` for a Work-phase Sonnet 4.6 launch). Always a string — never `null`.\n- `outcome`: `/autopilot:work` writes `\"completed\"`, `\"aborted\"`, or `\"escalated\"`. The `\"escalated\"` value (PRD 00065) is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:\"qwen\"`). Later phases upgrade earlier entries — `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 (Rework) step 2 rewrites a `\"completed\"` entry's outcome to `\"review_flagged\"` at the start of escalation, then later rewrites a flagged entry's outcome to `\"rework_failed\"` when the rework pass also fails at the top of the chain.\n- `review_cycle`: `null` on a first/Phase-3 attempt; set to the current `state.cycle` integer when the pass is a rework re-dispatch (see `SKILL.md` step 1.5 \"Rework-mode task filter (PRD 00025)\").\n- `cause`: `null` on success; on abort or output rejection, the reason — `\"context_overrun\"`, `\"subagent_prompt_overrun\"`, `\"timeout\"`, `\"error\"`, `\"subagent_infra_failure\"`, `\"commit_rejected\"` (a commit blocked by `validate_commit_msg`/warden that the one-retry repair could not fix — `SKILL.md` step 5), `\"codex_no_edit\"` (PRD 00077; the no-edit infra arm, stamped when the codex helper exited 0 with a non-empty output file but produced no working-tree change — the hook-blocked, prose-only case; classified as INFRA, so the attempt falls back to Claude at the task's own tier with no `escalation_reason` stamp). Qwen output rejections use `\"qwen_no_edit\"` (no task-owned implementation diff) or `\"qwen_test_mutation\"` (Tess tests differ from their test commit), with `outcome: \"escalated\"` on the rejected Qwen row; both are capability failures before staging/gating, never infra.\n- `implementor`: which agent actually ran the attempt — `\"claude\"` (Agent dispatch at any Claude tier, including a Claude fallback when qwen preflight failed), `\"gemini\"` (UI task via `use-gemini` helper), `\"qwen\"` (backend qwen-eligible task with healthy preflight, dispatched via `use-qwen` helper), `\"codex\"` (a codex-eligible backend task the step-3 interception routed to the codex rung, dispatched via the `use-codex` helper), or `\"orchestrator\"` (PRD 00148; a rework task the micro lane kept in-session — the orchestrator edited it with the Edit tool and no implementor subagent dispatched at all). Sourced from the routing decision in `work` SKILL.md step 3 — the value reflects what dispatched, not what the routing table initially picked: a qwen-eligible task that preflight-failed and fell back to Claude records `\"claude\"`; likewise, a codex-eligible task whose batch health probe came back unhealthy and fell back to Claude records `\"claude\"`, not `\"codex\"`. **Multi-implementor pass (qwen → Claude retry):** under default escalation, each rung writes its own entry: the rejected Qwen row stays `implementor: \"qwen\"`, `outcome: \"escalated\"`, and the Sonnet row records `implementor: \"claude\"`, `escalation_reason: \"gate_failure\"`, `escalated_from: \"qwen\"`. This also applies to pre-commit output rejections under `legacy`, which must retain their failure cause. The old single task-exit row applies only to legacy test-gate retries that committed Qwen code, not output rejections. Tess / Devon / code reviewer dispatches do not write attempt entries themselves; this field labels the Ivan-implementor pass.\n- `preflight_outcome`: only meaningful for attempts on qwen-eligible tasks (those whose effective eligibility remains true after write-set reconciliation). For qwen-eligible attempts: one of `\"healthy\"`, `\"pi_missing\"`, `\"endpoint_unreachable\"`, `\"model_id_missing\"`, `\"completion_failed\"` — the verdict of the four-check probe defined in `references/qwen-integration.md` (Preflight section). For non-qwen-eligible attempts: `null`. A qwen-eligible attempt that the breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) rerouted also records `null`, because the probe never ran. Sourced from the preflight probe in `work` SKILL.md step 3.\n- `pipeline`: which pipeline depth this attempt ran, keyed on the task tier (PRD 00044) — `\"minimal\"` (haiku: Tess + Ivan, 2 subagents), `\"lean\"` (sonnet: + step-5.7 reviewer, 3 subagents), or `\"full\"` (opus: + Devon at step 2.9, 4 subagents). Mapped from `state.tasks[i].model`: `haiku` → `\"minimal\"`, `sonnet` → `\"lean\"`, `opus` → `\"full\"`; absent/legacy `state.tasks[i].model` is treated as `sonnet` → `\"lean\"` (matching the step-2.9 and step-5.7 tier gates). Written at every task exit alongside `implementor`. A Phase-6 escalation to `opus` therefore records `\"full\"` for the rework attempt. Always a string — never `null`. **In-loop escalation (PRD 00065):** an escalation re-dispatches the implementor for the higher rung and re-runs the tier-appropriate post-implementor gates (step 5.7 reviewer for sonnet+, plus the step-5.5 gate); Devon (step 2.9, pre-implementation adversarial tests) is NOT re-run mid-task. So an in-loop opus escalation stamps `pipeline:\"lean\"` (implementor+reviewer), reserving `\"full\"` for a from-scratch opus task/rework that actually ran Devon.\n- `escalation_reason` (PRD 00065): string?; `\"gate_failure\"` stamped directly by `/autopilot:work` on the entry of the rung it escalated INTO (in-loop diagnosis). `\"review_flag\"` reaches the entry a different way: phase-review Phase 6 writes it (with `escalated_from`) into `state.tasks[i]` via `task-set-meta`, and `/autopilot:work`'s attempt write copies both from `state.tasks[i]` onto the rework entry (`SKILL.md` step 6 point 1 / step 1.5) — the task entry is the carrier, the copy is the wiring. Compound path: if that review-flagged rung then escalates in-loop, the copy happens at `SKILL.md` step 5.5 ESCALATE point 2 (onto the escalate-away entry) and `state.tasks[i]`'s `escalation_reason`/`escalated_from` are cleared at point 3, so the higher in-loop rung records its own `gate_failure` (not a leaked `review_flag`). Absent = neither (legacy / no escalation).\n- `escalated_from` (PRD 00065): string?; a tier (`\"qwen\"`|`\"codex\"`|`\"haiku\"`|`\"sonnet\"`|`\"opus\"`) — on the entry of the rung escalated INTO, the immediate-prior rung it came from. Set directly by `/autopilot:work` on the in-loop `gate_failure` path; carried from `state.tasks[i]` (as above) on the `review_flag` path. Absent on non-escalated entries.\n- `diagnosis` (PRD 00065): string?; `\"spec_gap\"`|`\"solid_spec\"` — the 2nd-failure diagnosis verdict, stamped on the entry of the rung that was diagnosed.\n- `repair_used` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a task-description repair; absent otherwise (never written `false`).\n- `breaker_skipped` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on a qwen-eligible attempt the breaker rerouted off qwen — to codex (PRD 00077) or to Claude at original tier (no preflight probe). Absent otherwise.\n- `qwen_excluded_reason` (PRD 00075): string?; `\"memory_pressure\"` (row 4's `check_memory_pressure.py` exited 1) or `\"memory_probe_failed\"` (exited 2) — stamped on the entry when `work` SKILL.md step 3 row 4 fired; or `\"files\"` when runtime write-set reconciliation excludes Qwen; key omitted otherwise. This is an attempt-scoped RUNTIME field, distinct from the plan-time `state.tasks[i].qwen_excluded_reason` (`\"ui\"`/`\"tier\"`/`\"files\"`/`\"contract\"`) that `/autopilot:plan-tasks` writes — `/autopilot:work` never rewrites planner metadata. Absent on every attempt written before PRD 00075; readers treat absence as \"no runtime exclusion\", never an error — the same absence tolerance the neighbouring PRD-00065 fields (`breaker_skipped`, `qwen_gate_failed`) get.\n- `qwen_gate_failed` (PRD 00065): bool?; `true` stamped on an `implementor:\"qwen\"` entry whose pre-commit output guard or step-5.5 gate FAILED — the durable signal the qwen capability breaker keys on. Absent otherwise.\n- `codex_no_edit` (PRD 00077): bool?; the LATCHED detector result, captured at the dispatch boundary (`work/SKILL.md` step 4, before step 5's `git add`) by comparing the task's own file-slice porcelain before and after the codex dispatch; step 5.5 reads the latched flag and never re-runs the detector. Absent on non-codex attempts and on attempts written before PRD 00077.\n- `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` (PRD 00077): int?; the detector's own exit code, recorded ONLY when the detector exited non-zero — a non-zero exit means the probe is INDETERMINATE, not \"no change\": `codex_no_edit` is NOT latched and the attempt continues on the capability path normally. Exists so a broken detector is visible in the record instead of silently reclassifying every real codex capability failure as infra. Absent when the detector ran cleanly and on attempts written before PRD 00077.\n\n**Best-effort gate stamps (fail-loud markers, PRD 00084 R2d)**: each records that a per-task gate was skipped or failed rather than passed, so a skipped check never reads as a passed one (`rules/operating-principles.md`). All optional — absent means the gate ran normally (or its tier-skip applied). They are pass-through markers: none blocks the task or changes `outcome`.\n\n- `verification`: string?; `\"skipped:<cause>\"` when step 5.5's per-task test verification could not run (e.g. the build lock was contended and cargo was backgrounded — `SKILL.md` step 5.5 / the \"test verification is blocked\" rule), or `\"timeout:<command>\"` (PRD 00167) when step 5.5's narrow tests hit their 300000 ms Bash `timeout` budget and then hit the 600000 ms re-run too, leaving no verdict (`references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Foreground command budgets). `<command>` is the command that timed out, so the record says which one. Two neighbouring timeouts are recorded elsewhere and never here: a step-2.95 red-check takes `red_check: \"skipped:<cause>\"` from its own ladder (`references/red-check.md`), and step 7's suite runs after every attempt entry is written, so its timeout is recorded in the phase report (`references/final-verification.md` § Timed-out commands). The two values are deliberately distinct: `skipped:` means the check was never attempted, `timeout:` means it was attempted and returned no verdict. Absent when the task's tests ran.\n- `red_check`: string?; `\"skipped:<cause>\"` when step 2.95's red-check could not run standalone (tests import the not-yet-built feature, or the runner cannot execute them), or `\"n/a:new_module\"` when the check was inapplicable because a Contract-named target the tests import does not exist on disk yet — a module that cannot be imported can only fail with `ImportError`, which proves nothing, so step 2.95 records this and skips both pytest invocations. Or one of `\"n/a:test-only-task\"`, `\"n/a:docs-only-task\"`, `\"n/a:config-only-task\"` (PRD 00141) when step 2.7 skipped Tess for that task class, or `\"n/a:micro-lane\"` (PRD 00148) when the micro lane skipped steps 2.7-2.95 outright, so step 2.95 has no newly committed tests to run — the value names WHICH class, because the three take different downstream paths (a test-only task still reaches step 5.7's gate, where PRD 00159 skips Pat outside rework mode and stamps `review: \"skipped:test-only\"`; docs-only and config-only never reach it). The two families are deliberately distinct: `skipped:` means the check could not be run, `n/a:` means it had no signal to give. Absent when the red-check ran (saw red, or strengthened-then-red).\n- `self_deslop`: string?; the step-5.6 self-deslop outcome — `\"committed:<sha>\"` (a `chore: prune slop` cleanup landed), `\"noop\"` (ran, no slop), `\"skipped:trivial\"` (skip rule fired — diff <30 net lines OR <2 files), `\"skipped:test-only\"` (PRD 00159; every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` is test or fixture code, so the pass was never dispatched — a distinct value from `\"skipped:trivial\"` because the two skips answer different questions and a batch needs to tell them apart), `\"timeout\"` (watchdog killed it), or `\"errored:<cause>\"` (dispatch failed). Canonical shape mirrored in `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` `tasks[].attempts[].self_deslop`. Absent on legacy attempts.\n- `style_gate` (PRD 00163): string?; the step-5.65 style-limit verdict for this task's own diff — `\"clean\"` (the gate passed, or the task's diff held no `.py` file to measure), `\"fixed:<sha>\"` (it exited 1, one fix dispatch landed, and the re-run was clean), `\"failed:<detail>\"` (`<detail>` is the violation lines joined by `\"; \"` when the re-run still exited 1, or the script's stderr when the gate could not run at all), or `\"skipped:tier\"` (a `haiku` task, the one tier that skips it). Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `self_deslop` follows. Absent on legacy attempts and on every attempt written before this PRD, when the gate ran once per phase and stamped nothing per task.\n- `split_hygiene` (PRD 00166): string?; the step-5.65 split-hygiene verdict on the test files this task touched — `\"clean\"` (the check passed), `\"fixed:<sha>\"` (it exited 1, one deletion-only fix dispatch landed, and the re-run was clean), `\"failed:<detail>\"` (`<detail>` is the reported lines joined by `\"; \"` when the re-run still exited 1, or the script's stderr when the check could not run at all), or `\"skipped:no-tests\"` (the task's candidate list held no test path, so `check_split_hygiene.py` was never invoked). It is a separate field from `style_gate` on purpose: the two run in the same step but answer different questions over different file sets — line spans across every `.py` file versus bindings inside test files — so one verdict can never stand in for the other. Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `style_gate` follows. Absent on legacy attempts and when the step's haiku tier-gate skipped it.\n- `devon` (finding 16, 2026-09-20): string?; `\"skipped:prose\"` when step 2.9's prose gate skipped Devon because every test file Tess created or changed for the task has a basename ending in `_prose.py` (a substring pin cannot see negation, inversion or past-tense narration, so a Devon round on such a task keeps nothing), or `\"exploit_fixed\"` when Devon broke the tests, Tess strengthened them once, and the task proceeded on the strengthened tests (no second Devon dispatch). Held in-session and written into step 6's `task-done` payload, the same rule `style_gate` follows. Absent when Devon ran clean or when the tier gate skipped him. Mirror in `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` already documents `devon`/`devon_weak_points`/`devon_in_contract`.\n- `devon_exploit`: string?; Devon's one-line weak-point summary, stamped alongside `devon: \"exploit_fixed\"`. Absent otherwise.\n- `devon_weak_points`: int?; the count of weak points Devon's numbered `Weak points:` list named, stamped alongside `devon: \"exploit_fixed\"`. Absent otherwise.\n- `devon_in_contract`: string[]?; each `\"N. in-contract: ...\"` line Tess returned when answering Devon's weak points, stamped alongside `devon: \"exploit_fixed\"`. Absent otherwise.\n- `micro_lane` (PRD 00148): string?; `\"overrun\"` stamped when the micro lane's post-edit ceiling fired (`net_lines >= 30` OR `file_count > 2`), the edit was reverted with `git checkout --`, and the task fell through to the normal lane at step 2.7 — so the record shows the shortcut was tried and abandoned, not that the task was always normal. Absent otherwise; never written on a lane that stayed under the ceiling (`implementor: \"orchestrator\"` already says it ran).\n- `reflow` (PRD 00148): string?; `\"<path>:<hunks>\"` (`;`-joined for several) when step 5's `check_reflow.py` flagged a staged file at or above the hunk threshold, or `\"failed:<stderr>\"` when the script exited 2. The file is still committed — the field and the phase report are what make an unrequested formatter sweep visible instead of silently re-reviewed next cycle. Absent when nothing was flagged.\n- `review`: string?; the step-5.7 reviewer lane (Sonnet via `use-sonnet`) — `\"failed:<cause>\"` when it failed twice (runner unavailable, nonzero exit, or empty output); `\"failed:invalid_output\"` (PRD 00159) when it ran twice and both replies broke the reporting contract, so `parse_review.py` exited 1 on each and the correction retry was spent — the task still proceeds and the PRD-level review is what catches whatever Pat did not report; `\"skipped:test-only\"` (PRD 00159) when every path in `<task_base_sha>..HEAD` was test or fixture code and the task was not in rework mode, so no reviewer was dispatched at any tier. `\"resume_failed\"` (PRD 00165) when a re-review's `-R` dispatch could not resume the reviewer's session (nonzero exit or an empty output file) and the lane fell back to one full-diff dispatch — the review still ran, so this is a cost note, not a failure; it is what tells a reader why a cycle that should have sent a delta sent the whole diff. It stands alone as the whole field when nothing else needed stamping, and joins any other value with `\"; \"` (for example `\"medium-retry:fixed; resume_failed\"`) — one separator, so a reader and a future parser split the field the same way. The two `failed:` values are deliberately distinct: one means the lane never produced a reply, the other means it produced one nobody can act on. Absent when the review ran cleanly or its haiku tier-gate skipped it.\n\n**Attribution row ownership (PRD 00065)**: under one-entry-per-rung, each field lands on a specific row — do not lump them all on one entry:\n\n| Field | Row it is stamped on |\n|-------|----------------------|\n| `diagnosis` | the diagnosed (lower) rung's entry |\n| `qwen_gate_failed` | the qwen (lower) rung's entry |\n| `repair_used` | the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a repair (that rung's entry) |\n| `escalation_reason:\"gate_failure\"` | the rung escalated INTO (higher)'s entry |\n| `escalated_from` | the rung escalated INTO (higher)'s entry |\n\n**Append procedure**: write the entry object to `docs/dev/tmp/attempt-task-<id>.json` with the **Write tool** (never a shell redirect, and never an inline shell argument — an attempt record carries quotes and newlines), then pick the call by exit path:\n\n| Exit path | Call |\n|---|---|\n| **Task completed** (`SKILL.md` step 6) | `statectl.py <state.json> task-done <task-id> docs/dev/tmp/attempt-task-<id>.json` |\n| **Abort or escalate-away** (step 4 timeout / context exceeded / error after debug, Subagent Dispatch Budget overrun, an `\"escalated\"` rung entry) | `statectl.py <state.json> append-attempt <task-id> docs/dev/tmp/attempt-task-<id>.json` |\n\n`task-done` is the **only** call the success path makes: it appends the entry, sets `tasks[i].status = \"completed\"`, and recomputes `tasks_completed` in one locked atomic write, resolving the task by `tasks[].id` rather than array position. Do not pair it with a separate status write or a `tasks_completed` write — the count is derived and must never be passed in.\n\nThe abort and escalate-away paths keep the generic `append` form precisely because the task does **not** become `completed` there: the entry is recorded while the task stays open, so the status and the count must not move. `i` is this task's index in `state.tasks`.\n\nBoth forms create the array if absent, append under an advisory lock, and replace the file atomically while preserving every sibling field, so the manual read-modify-write is gone (`run-autopilot` SKILL.md § State Management). Resolve `<state.json>` by walking up from the resolved physical cwd to find the autopilot dir, same pattern as the cap-marker reset in `SKILL.md` step 2.\n\nTwo top-level fields, `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive` and `qwen_breaker`, track the qwen capability breaker across the batch (PRD 00065); see `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` Field Descriptions for their canonical shape.\n\nCross-reference: `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` `tasks[].attempts` row defines the canonical shape.\n\n**Stamp grammar enforcement (PRD 00342-v1)**: `statectl.py`'s `task-done` and `append-attempt` writers refuse any value outside this grammar for the fields above that have one (`implementor`, `red_check`, `self_deslop`, `style_gate`, `split_hygiene`, `devon`, `review`) - an invented word like `\"orchestrator-reviewed\"` now exits 1 with the state file byte-unchanged, instead of landing silently.\n\n## Dispatch-provenance fields (moved from SKILL.md, PRD 00119-v2)\n\n- **`implementor`** — `\"claude\"`, `\"gemini\"`, `\"qwen\"`, `\"codex\"`, or `\"orchestrator\"`, reflecting what actually dispatched, NOT what the step-3 routing table initially picked (a qwen pick that fell back to Claude on preflight failure records `\"claude\"`). `\"orchestrator\"` is the one value meaning nothing dispatched: the micro lane (`references/rework-mode.md`) edited in-session. A micro-lane attempt that overran and fell through to a real dispatch records that dispatcher instead, with `micro_lane: \"overrun\"` alongside.\n- **`preflight_outcome`** — from the step-3 preflight probe. Always written explicitly — never omit the key. Qwen-eligible attempts record one of `\"healthy\"`, `\"pi_missing\"`, `\"endpoint_unreachable\"`, `\"model_id_missing\"`, `\"completion_failed\"`; non-qwen-eligible attempts record the literal JSON `null`. A pressure-gated attempt (row 4 fired, the probe never ran) also records the literal JSON `null` — the same carve-out already granted to a breaker-skipped attempt (row 3).\n- **`qwen_excluded_reason`** — `\"memory_pressure\"` (row 4 fired, `check_memory_pressure.py` exited 1) or `\"memory_probe_failed\"` (row 4 fired, exited 2); or `\"files\"` when runtime write-set reconciliation excludes Qwen; key omitted when neither exclusion fires. Attempt-scoped RUNTIME field — distinct from the plan-time `state.tasks[i].qwen_excluded_reason` (`\"ui\"`/`\"tier\"`/`\"files\"`/`\"contract\"`) that `/autopilot:plan-tasks` writes; `/autopilot:work` never rewrites planner metadata. Absent on every attempt written before PRD 00075 — readers treat absence as \"no runtime exclusion\", never an error.\n\n## task-done semantics (moved from SKILL.md step 6, PRD 00119-v2)\n\n`task-done` sets `tasks[i].status = \"completed\"`, appends the record to `tasks[i].attempts`, and **recomputes `tasks_completed` from the task array** — all three inside one locked atomic write. Do NOT set `status`, append the attempt, or set `tasks_completed` separately; the count is derived and is not passed in. The task is resolved by matching `tasks[].id`, so the `tasks[N]` index form is not used here (rework appends `[D{cycle}]` follow-ups, after which array position stops matching id).\n\n## Assumption ledger (moved from SKILL.md § Assumptions footer, PRD 00119-v2)\n\nCollect the returned lines: step 6 appends non-`none` entries to `docs/dev/project-management/meta/assumptions.md` under a `## <task-id>: <task subject>` heading (Write/Edit tool, never shell redirects). On the first completed task of a full-plan pass, replace the file instead of appending - the ledger is per-plan. Step 7's phase report includes the ledger so the user and the review phase can examine what the implementors guessed in a 30-second read.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_31","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; x=Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/SKILL.md\\\").read_text(); a=x.index(\\\"## State Management\\\"); print(x[a:a+6000]); print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md\\\").read_text()[:10000]); print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md\\\").read_text()[:12000])'\"","aggregated_output":"## State Management\n\nAll autopilot artifacts live under `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`, organized by type:\n\n```\ndocs/dev/project-management/autopilot/\n  state.json                              # current cycle state\n  last-session.log                        # loop-teed raw output of the last headless session\n  reports/{batch_id}-report.md            # batch audit report\n  deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json       # unresolved items across PRDs\n```\n\nState file: `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — see `references/state-schema.md` for schema.\n\n**`statectl` is the sole writer of `state.json`.** Apply every field mutation with `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set|append|del <json-path> <json-value>` (read one field with `get`); it takes an advisory lock, backs up to `<state.json>.bak`, changes only the named path while preserving all siblings, and replaces the file atomically — so it cannot leave a half-written or unparseable state, and it never trips the \"not read yet\" / \"modified since read\" errors the editing tools hit. Since PRD 00089 it is a shim over `cli/state.transaction`, so every write is schema-validated too: a value that is malformed **for the field it targets** is rejected with exit 1 and the file left byte-unchanged (an unrelated pre-existing odd field blocks nothing). **Phase transitions are not field mutations** — use `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` (§ Session handoff procedure), never a hand-written `set phase` / `set next_phase` pair, so a transition cannot land without the effects it mandates. Resolve `<state.json>` by walking up from the resolved physical cwd to the autopilot dir (the `_walk_up.py` pattern in `/autopilot:work` step 2). The terse `set X` / `write field Y` / per-PRD-reset instructions throughout these skills and the gate files name the fields to change; each is applied with `statectl`, never by hand-editing the file.\n\nDocumented human fallback: outside the loop a person may still Edit or Write `state.json` by hand (for forensics or recovery — the model itself never hand-edits `state.json`; a statectl failure has its own marker-based recovery below); `validate_state_json_hook.py` catches a hand-edit that leaves the file unparseable and now also runs `cli.schema.validate` on it, and `statectl` reads whatever valid JSON it finds on its next mutation.\n\n**When `statectl` itself fails** (nonzero exit — advisory-lock contention, a Python error, an unreadable `state.json`): retry the exact command ONCE. If it fails again, do NOT improvise a partial write and do NOT proceed on the stale state — a lost mutation strands the loop on the wrong `next_phase`. Run `autopilot restore` (rolls `state.json` back to `<state.json>.bak`) and retry the statectl command once more. If the failure persists (`autopilot restore` itself fails, or the subsequent statectl write still fails), WRITE THE MARKER `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state-write-failed` with the Write tool — ONE line of JSON `{\"site\": \"statectl_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the statectl command and its raw stderr>\"}` — and END THE TURN: the wrapper halts on the marker and surfaces the `detail` itself, so no further state write is needed. Interactive sessions ALSO report the same failure to the user directly (there is no wrapper watching an interactive terminal). The raw stderr rides into the marker's `detail` so the failure is diagnosable, never silent (`rules/operating-principles.md`). (Lock contention on the single-writer model implies a second loop or a stale lock; the concurrent-loop guard below now refuses a second loop up front, so a persistent lock is a stale one — the retry clears it or the marker records it.)\n\nCreate `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/` and subdirectories if missing. Initialize state file at PRD selection. Update state at every phase transition. Autopilot also keeps a per-PRD **decision audit log** at `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/<prd-base>-audit.md`, **rendered once at Phase 9 finalize from the `state.json` decision arrays** (`autonomous_decisions`, `deferred_decisions`, `doubts`). `state.json` is the single in-run source of truth — decisions are NOT mirrored to `audit.md` incrementally per decision. Each rendered entry carries a **source** label (`autonomous`, `deferred`, or `doubt`); cycle/phase context goes in the entry body so the Phase 9 `decisions.md` projection can filter autonomous entries by label. The render is `autopilot render audit` (PRD 00107); the label set and the projection live in `references/audit-log-format.md`.\n\n**Invariant:** every state mutation that advances `phase` SHOULD also set `next_phase` to the same value. The three gates are `build` | `review` | `done` (plus `paused`). `build` is ONE session: selection, catchup, design, planning, and work all run under `phase: \"build\"` with no mid-build handoff. The review surface runs in its own fresh session; blind and doubt scrutiny are LENSES inside every review cycle (Blake and Bob in `review-work-completion`'s roster), not separate phases — reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs). Legacy `blind`/`doubt` phase values in pre-00015 state files map to `review` on resume. Per-task implementor tiering inside `/autopilot:work` is unchanged. The authoritative resume signal is `phase` + `phases_completed`; build sub-step skipping is by ARTIFACT (capsule freshness, design-doc-exists, tasks-exist, all-done), not by `phases_completed` membership. This resume decision (phase + phases_completed + artifact checks → next step) is encoded canonically in `cli/resume.py` (`scripts/resume_target.py` re-exports it), which `scripts/test_autopilot_resume.py` imports — editing the resume logic there flips a test red rather than silently drifting from this prose. Run `autopilot resume-target` at Phase 0 to print what that encoding says the next action is, and reconcile it against the handler you are about to f\n---\nname: python-patterns\ndescription: Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Python code. Covers idioms, naming, traps, toolchain, and security. Triggers on Python file edits, \"pythonic\", \"PEP 8\", \"python best practices\", \"python idioms\", \"bandit\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the strunk plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n# Python Patterns\n\nPick a side. These are the rulings, not a tutorial.\n\n## Idioms that earn their place\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n| `X \\| Y`, not `Union[X, Y]` | 3.10+ runtime syntax; clearer. On 3.9 it parses only under `from __future__ import annotations` and still breaks `get_type_hints`/`isinstance` — keep `Optional`/`Union` if you support 3.9. |\n| `Protocol`, not `ABC`, for duck typing | Structural typing; no inheritance you don't control. |\n| `@dataclass(frozen=True)` for immutable records, plain `dataclass` only when you must mutate, `NamedTuple` for lightweight immutable rows | Pydantic only when you need validation. |\n| `raise New(...) from e` | Marks the explicit cause. A bare `raise New()` still chains implicitly (\"During handling...\"); use `from None` to suppress. |\n| `@functools.wraps` on every decorator | Without it the wrapper loses `__name__`, `__doc__`, signature. |\n| `pathlib.Path`, not `os.path` | One object, no string surgery. |\n\n## Naming (PEP 8)\n\n`snake_case` for modules, functions, variables. `CapWords` for classes. `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Leading `_` for internal names.\n\n**Never name a `.py` file in kebab-case.** `my-script.py` is not importable (`import my-script` is a `SyntaxError`). Kebab-case belongs only in the `pyproject.toml` distribution name and the CLI command, both of which map to a `snake_case` module.\n\n## Traps\n\n```python\n# Mutable default argument — shared across calls\ndef bad(items=[]): ...\ndef good(items=None):\n    items = [] if items is None else items\n\n# Bare except — swallows SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt\ntry: ...\nexcept Exception as e: ...        # name the exception\n\n# __slots__ kills __dict__ and dynamic attributes — use only on fixed,\n# memory-sensitive classes you won't extend.\n\n# __double_leading is name-mangled to _Class__double_leading.\n# Surprises you in subclasses, pickling, and monkey-patching.\n\nif value is None: ...             # never == None\n```\n\nAvoid `from module import *`. Use `isinstance`, never `type(x) ==`.\n\n## Toolchain\n\n**black** to format, **isort** for imports, **ruff** to lint. Type annotations on every function signature — no exceptions for \"obvious\" returns.\n\n## Resources and laziness\n\nContext managers (`with`) for anything holding a resource. Generators for lazy iteration over anything you would otherwise materialize into a list.\n\n## Security\n\n- Read secrets with `os.environ[\"API_KEY\"]`, never `.get()` — a missing secret must raise `KeyError` at startup, not surface as `None` at request time.\n- `python-dotenv` loads a local `.env` in development only. Never commit one.\n- `bandit -r src/` for static security analysis.\n\n---\nname: python-testing\ndescription: Use when writing, fixing, or reviewing Python tests with pytest. Covers TDD, fixtures, mocking, parametrization, coverage. Triggers on \"pytest\", \"python test\", \"conftest\", \"pytest.mark\", \"parametrize\", \"pytest fixture\", \"python mock\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the strunk plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n# Python Testing\n\nTDD: write the failing test (RED), make it pass (GREEN), refactor. One behavior per test. No logic in tests. Coverage target 80%, higher on critical paths.\n\n## Rulings\n\n**Mocking**\n- Patch where the name is *used*, not where it's defined: `@patch(\"myapp.service.requests\")`, not `@patch(\"requests\")`.\n- `autospec=True` so the mock rejects calls the real API would reject.\n- Mock at the boundary (I/O, network, clock). Never mock the thing under test.\n- Async: assert with `assert_awaited_once()`, not `assert_called_once()`.\n\n**Fixtures**\n- `yield` for teardown; the line after `yield` is the cleanup.\n- Default to function scope. Widen to `module`/`session` only for genuinely expensive resources.\n- `autouse` hides dependencies — use sparingly; prefer explicit injection.\n- `tmp_path` for temp files (auto-cleanup, `Path` API), not `tempfile`.\n\n**Parametrize**\n- `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over loops — distinct test IDs, filterable with `-k`.\n- Pass `ids=[...]` when params are objects or tuples; pytest already auto-names plain str/int/bool readably.\n\n**Config**\n- One config in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`), not a separate `pytest.ini`.\n- `--strict-markers` so a typo'd marker fails instead of silently passing.\n- Register custom markers — e.g. `slow`, `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration` — so `--strict-markers` catches a typo.\n- Coverage locally: `pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` — the missing-line report is the point; a bare percentage is not actionable.\n\n**Async (pytest-asyncio)**\n- Default mode is `strict`: an async test with no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` is silently not collected. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to drop the per-test marker.\n- Use `@pytest_asyncio.fixture` for async fixtures in strict mode.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Build the stage list: the paths from Ivan's `FILES_TOUCHED:` footer (see **Assumptions footer**), plus any build-generated files this task's changes legitimately produced (lockfiles, snapshots, generated bindings) — identified from `git status --porcelain` output, never guessed.\n2. Fallback when the footer is absent or `none` while the tree is dirty (legacy retry prompts, malformed report): stage the intersection of dirty paths with the exact files the plan task names; treat every other dirty path as foreign.\n3. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_reflow.py <stage list>` over that list: exit 1 → stamp `reflow: \"<path>:<hunks>\"` (`;`-joined for several) on the attempt and name the files in the phase report; exit 2 → `reflow: \"failed:<stderr>\"`; exit 0 → no field. Staging and the commit proceed unchanged in every branch — see `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Reflow tripwire.\n\n```bash\ngit add <path> [<path> ...]\n```\n```bash\ngit commit -m \"<type>(<scope>): <description>\"\n```\n\nAny other dirty path is **foreign**: leave it unstaged and untouched, and name it in the phase report (fail loud) — the same never-commit-foreign-work rule the step-5.5 ESCALATE reset guard enforces. A store write (state.json, a ledger append, a review file) is never foreign dirt here: `autopilot dirty` is store-exempt, and that is the check this rule means.\n\nNever chain these with `&&` in a single Bash call. Commit message rules: conventional commit format, one line, no period, reference the task ID if available.\n\nBefore committing a `feat`/`fix` (or breaking) change, verify CHANGELOG.md is staged in the same commit per rules/changelog.md — repos with a declared no-changelog exception (e.g. the buvis home repo) skip this check.\n\n**If a commit (or its `git add`) is rejected** — `aegis`'s `validate_commit_msg.py` blocks a non-conventional message (boilerplate trailer, HEREDOC, bad format — `rules/development-workflow.md`), or warden denies the `git add`/`git commit` command: read the deny reason from the blocked tool result (aegis names the format violation; warden's reason usually names the preferred command form), fix the message or the command accordingly, and **retry the commit ONCE**. Still rejected after the one repair → ESCALATE: append an attempt-log entry (`outcome: \"aborted\"`, `cause: \"commit_rejected\"`), then report to the user (interactive) or take the loop-mode stall path (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md`, `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`, `detail` = the deny reason) — never leave the task's work uncommitted-and-unrecorded, and never reach for `--no-verify` to bypass the hook. Self-deslop pre-commit pass\n\nAfter step 5.5's tests pass and BEFORE the per-task code review at step 5.7, dispatch a fresh subagent to prune slop from the implementor's diff. The per-task review then runs against the leaner diff, which means review-rework cycles add defensive fixes on top of a smaller base. Best-effort: this step never blocks the task and never triggers retries.\n\n**Skip rules, in order.** First, list `git diff --name-only <task_base_sha>..HEAD` and apply `test_only_diff` from `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py`: true means skip the dispatch, record `self_deslop: \"skipped:test-only\"`, and proceed to step 5.65 (`references/self-deslop-prompt.md` § Test-only diffs). +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_41","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/work/references/style-gate.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"# Style-Limit Gate (step 5.65)\n\nMoved out of SKILL.md step 7.0, which measured a whole phase at once (PRD\n00163). The gate now runs on one task's own diff, so an oversize file is split\nwhile the context that produced it is still in session, and step 5.7's reviewer\nreads an already-conforming diff.\n\nBase = `<task_base_sha>`, the HEAD SKILL.md step 2 captures right after\n`task-start`. Every git invocation below runs with the repo's own\n`--git-dir`/`--work-tree` flags in a bare-repo home, and every interpolated path is\n`shlex.quote()`-d before it lands in a command - `git ls-files` reports whatever\nnames exist on disk, spaces and `$(...)` included. Commands are written on one\nline each; do not re-wrap them.\n\n## Diff construction\n\nWrite the committed range with `git diff <base>..HEAD --output=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/task-diff-<task-id>.txt`, then cover the Python files no commit holds yet: for every path `git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- '*.py'` prints, append its whole-file add block with `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <path> >> ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/task-diff-<task-id>.txt` (`--no-index` exits 1 whenever it finds differences, which is the normal case here — only exit ≥2 is a real failure), and `mv ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/task-diff-<task-id>.txt docs/dev/tmp/task-diff-<task-id>.txt` once the appends are done: stage it outside `docs/dev/project-management/` because a shell append into that tree is blocked, and with no untracked `.py` file the moved diff is byte-identical to the committed range.\n\n## Invocation\n\nThe candidate list is the changed Python files from `git diff --name-only --diff-filter=d <base>..HEAD -- '*.py'` (deleted files excluded: the script reads every path it is given) plus those untracked paths. The combined list is empty — a docs-only or config-only task, or any task that touched no `.py`: skip the script and record `style_gate: clean`. Otherwise:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_style_limits.py --diff docs/dev/tmp/task-diff-<task-id>.txt <every candidate as an absolute path>\n```\n\nFunction spans come from `review-work-completion/scripts/compute_mech_facts.py`,\nreused by import (see SKILL.md `## Dependencies`).\n\n## Outcome ladder\n\nCarried over from step 7.0 unchanged except for what follows a failure: the task\nproceeds to step 5.7, where the phase used to proceed to its suite.\n\n- **Exit 0**: record `style_gate: clean`.\n- **Exit 1**: write the violation lines to the `FAILING_TESTS` scratch file\n  (`docs/dev/tmp/ivan-style-violations-<task-id>.md`) and run the fix dispatch\n  below once, commit per step 5, then re-run from § Diff construction - the fix\n  commit moved HEAD, so rebuild both the diff and the candidate list or a sibling\n  module the fixer just created is never measured. Clean ->\n  `style_gate: fixed:<sha of the fix commit>`; still exit 1 ->\n  `style_gate: failed:<the violation lines, joined by \"; \">` and proceed to step\n  5.7 anyway (fail loud, never silent).\n- **Exit 2** (or any other non-0/1 exit): the gate could not run at all, so\n  there are no violation lines to hand a fix agent — record\n  `style_gate: failed:<the script's stderr message>`, do NOT dispatch Ivan, and\n  proceed to step 5.7 anyway (fail loud, never silent, same as the\n  still-failing exit-1 case).\n\nA `failed:` value never blocks the task and never changes its `outcome`: it is a\nfail-loud marker, so a skipped check never reads as a passed one.\n\n## Fix dispatch\n\nExit 1 only, and the one Ivan dispatch that carries a widened allowlist —\nsplitting an 800-line file needs sibling modules that are by construction absent\nfrom the task's Contract paths, and `agents/ivan.md` tells a fixer to report a\nblocker rather than touch a file nobody listed.\n\nWrite `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-style-files.txt`: one absolute path per\nviolating file (every violation line names one), then one absolute directory\npath per distinct parent directory of those files, each directory line suffixed\n` (new modules may be created here)`. Parent directories of violating files\nonly — never the repo root, never a directory walked further upward. Every other\nIvan dispatch keeps passing `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-files.txt` unchanged.\n\nRender and dispatch with `references/gate-failure.md` § Style-fix render, whose\n`RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is verbatim:\n\n```\nFix only the listed style-limit violations. You may create new modules in the directories marked above and update imports in the listed files to use them. Do not change behavior, do not touch other code, and do not modify tests except to split a test file a violation line names.\n```\n\n`agents/ivan.md` stays untouched: `{RETRY_INSTRUCTION}` is already free text, and\na persona edit would reach every dispatch instead of this one.\n\n## Split hygiene\n\nRuns immediately after the style-limit ladder above, on the same candidate list\nnarrowed to test paths — `is_test_path` from\n`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py` decides, so the\nsubset is the one steps 5.6 and 5.7 already agree on. Build it concretely:\n\n```bash\npython3 -c \"import sys;sys.path.insert(0,sys.argv[1]);import work_routing;print('\\n'.join(p for p in sys.argv[2:] if work_routing.is_test_path(p)))\" ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts <every candidate as a REPO-RELATIVE path>\n```\n\nRepo-relative on the way in: `is_test_path` matches directory segments and\nbasenames, so an absolute path drags in `/Users/...` segments it never meant to\nsee. Absolute on the way out — the checker takes absolute paths, and the fix\ndispatch reads its file list off the reported lines. `conftest.py` is in\n`is_test_path`'s basename globs, so it lands in the subset; the UNUSED rule then\nexcludes it wholesale while the SHADOWED rule still applies to it.\n\nEmpty subset: record `split_hygiene: skipped:no-tests` and run nothing.\n\nThis is the mechanical half of a question the self-deslop pass is forbidden to\nanswer (PRD 00166). It reports bindings only — a module-level name nothing in\nthe file reads, a local reassigned before its previous value is read — never an\nassertion, test function, fixture or parametrization, so the fix that follows is\ndeletion-only.\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_split_hygiene.py <every test candidate as an absolute path>\n```\n\nNo `--diff` here, unlike the style gate: a binding a split left dead is dead\nwhether or not a hunk touched its line, and the checker has no diff to consult.\n\n## Split-hygiene outcome ladder\n\n- **Exit 0**: record `split_hygiene: clean`.\n- **Exit 1**: write the reported lines to the `FAILING_TESTS` scratch file\n  `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-split-hygiene-<task-id>.md` and run the fix dispatch below\n  once, commit per step 5, then re-run from § Split hygiene — the fix commit\n  moved HEAD, so rebuild the candidate list. Clean →\n  `split_hygiene: fixed:<sha of the fix commit>`; still exit 1 →\n  `split_hygiene: failed:<the reported lines, joined by \"; \">` and proceed to\n  step 5.7 anyway (fail loud, never silent).\n- **Exit 2** (or any other non-0/1 exit): the check could not run, so there are\n  no lines to hand a fix agent — record\n  `split_hygiene: failed:<the script's stderr message>`, do NOT dispatch Ivan,\n  and proceed to step 5.7 anyway.\n\nA `failed:` value never blocks the task and never changes its `outcome`, exactly\nas `style_gate` does not.\n\n## Split-hygiene fix dispatch\n\nExit 1 only. Render and dispatch with `references/gate-failure.md` § **Retry**\nrender — not § Style-fix render, which widens the allowlist to whole\ndirectories. **Three** lines differ from that shape, not two: `FAILING_TESTS`\nis the split-hygiene scratch file, `FILE_PATHS` is the hygiene list defined in\nthe next paragraph (NOT § Retry render's default `ivan-<task-id>-files.txt`),\nand `RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is the deletion-only string below.\n\n`FILE_PATHS` is `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-hygiene-files.txt`: one absolute\npath per violating file, read off the reported lines (each names exactly one),\nand **no directory lines at all** — a deletion never creates a module, so\n**no widened allowlist here**. Build that list rather than reusing the task's\n`ivan-<task-id>-files.txt`: when the style gate has just split an oversize test\nfile, the new sibling module is by construction absent from the task's Contract\npaths, and `agents/ivan.md` makes a fixer stop on any file its list does not\nname. Deriving the list from the violations is what keeps the dispatch both\nreachable and never wider than the files it must edit.\n\n`RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is verbatim:\n\n```\nDelete only the listed unused or shadowed bindings. Do not change any assertion, test function, fixture or parametrization. Do not add code.\n```\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_42","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/catchup/SKILL.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: catchup\ndescription: Use when starting work on a project and need local branch/repo context (full diff, GitHub state, capsule refresh). Triggers on \"catchup\", \"catch up\", \"catch-up\", \"what changed on this branch\", \"project overview\", \"refresh capsule\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the git-ferry plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n# Catch Up\n\nHydrate context before starting work. Load raw sources directly. The capsule captures derived insight (invariants, decisions, health signals), not paraphrases of files you can read.\n\nLoad generously, but the diff and changed files are the priority. On a clearly huge branch, fall back to a stat-only pass rather than blowing the context window.\n\n## Phase 1: Gather (run concurrently)\n\nRun the scripts and read the files in parallel; don't serialize.\n\n**Scripts** (skip on failure, note the gap):\n\n```bash\n\"~/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/branch-diff.sh\"   # skip if on master\n\"~/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/github-state.sh\"  # skip if no gh / no remote\n\"~/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/load-memories.sh\" # skip if no memories\n```\n\nIf a script fails, read it and run its git/gh commands directly.\n\n**Sources** (read each if it exists):\n\n- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` — **first**. They may define project-specific catchup rules, priority areas, or \"always check X\" constraints. Follow any project catchup checklist in addition to this workflow, and let these rules shape what you flag in Phase 5.\n- `README.md`, `agent_docs/*`, PRDs in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`\n- Build/config: `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`, etc.\n- Top 3 levels of `src/`/`lib/`/`app/`; domain model dirs (`models/`, `types/`, `schemas/`, `entities/`)\n- `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` (prior invariants/health), `docs/dev/project-management/meta/decisions.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/meta/troubleshooting.md`, `~/.claude/decisions.md`. These keepers live in `docs/dev/project-management/meta/`; if `meta/` has no copy, read the older `docs/dev/project-management/<name>` instead (unmigrated store).\n\n**Recent master:**\n\n```bash\ngit log --oneline -20 master\n```\n\n**Review harvest** (skip on failure, note the gap):\n\nHarvest this repo's review files into engram, best-effort, so their findings survive once those files are garbage-collected. Skip if `engram` is not on PATH, or if a glob below matches no files.\n\n```bash\nengram harvest docs/dev/project-management/reviews/*.md docs/dev/tmp/*review*.md\n```\n\n**Related context** (never silently absent — on any failure, write the section with a one-line gap note):\n\nRetrieve prior work related to what this session is about, so the capsule can point at it. If `engram` is not on PATH, skip the commands — but still write the section, saying engram was unavailable.\n\nBuild ONE topic string from what the session is already about: the current branch name (drop the `feature/`-style prefix and turn separators into spaces) plus, when `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` holds exactly one PRD, that PRD's title (its first `# ` heading). On master with no single wip PRD there is no topic: skip the queries rather than searching a branch name that says nothing, and record that as the gap note. Do not drop the section — \"no topic this session\" is itself worth telling the reader, and on a master-default workflow it is the common case.\n\n**The topic is untrusted input.** It is built from a branch name and a PRD title, either of which can contain `\"`, a backtick, or `$(`. Never paste it into a double-quoted shell string. Put it in a variable and pass that variable quoted, so the shell treats it as one literal argument:\n\n```bash\ntopic='<topic>'                                # single quotes; escape any literal ' in the topic\nengram index                                   # refresh this repo first (defaults to --scope repo)\nengram query --scope repo \"$topic\" -k 5\nengram query --scope portfolio \"$topic\" -k 5\nengram status --scope portfolio                # staleness of the widest scope you queried\n```\n\n`engram index` refreshes the repo scope only, so the portfolio hits may come from an older index — that is what the staleness stamp in the capsule section records. Ask `status` for `--scope portfolio` so the stamp actually covers the portfolio query above it; a repo-scoped stamp would describe a narrower scope than the hits it sits under. A nonzero `engram status` means stale or dead rows; report the stamp, don't hide it.\n\n## Phase 2: Branch context (feature branches only, skip on master)\n\nAfter `branch-diff.sh`, load the full picture:\n\n```bash\ngit diff $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD             # full diff, don't sample\ngit diff $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD --name-only # then read each changed file in full\n```\n\nThe diff shows what changed; the full file shows how it fits.\n\n**Blast radius:** for each changed file, trace its consumers (imports + call sites of any changed symbol) to surface ripple effects the diff alone won't show. Prefer `ast-grep`/`sg` over text grep — it won't false-positive on comments or strings. Read any consumer that looks impacted; always trace consumers of changed utilities, types, and interfaces.\n\n**The \"why\":** extract issue/PR references (`#NNN`, `fixes #NNN`) from branch commit messages and load full bodies:\n\n```bash\ngit log $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD --format=\"%B\"\ngh issue view {number} --json title,body,labels,state,comments\ngh pr view --json title,body,comments,reviews   # if an open PR exists\n```\n\n## Phase 3: Synthesize\n\nUpdate or create `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`, creating `meta/` if absent. Write there even when an older `docs/dev/project-management/project-capsule.md` is what you read. It is NOT a summary of what you read — it captures cross-file insight no single file holds.\n\n```markdown\n# Project Capsule: {project name}\n\nGenerated: {date}\n\n## Key Invariants\n{domain rules, boundaries, data-flow constraints; implicit/undocumented rules; what agents most often get wrong}\n\n## Architecture Decisions\n{why it's structured this way; tradeoffs; patterns that look wrong but are intentional}\n\n## Component Boundaries\n{what talks to what; which modules own which data; where the seams are}\n\n## Active Work\n{current branch purpose, PRDs in wip/, recent focus; if autopilot batch active: completed/remaining PRDs, cycle counts}\n\n## Related context\n{engram hits for this session's topic, from Phase 1. Repo hits first, then portfolio. One line per hit: `file:line — score`, plus a half-line on why it is relevant. End with the topic queried and the staleness stamp from `engram status --scope portfolio`. Always write this section: when there were no hits, no topic, or engram was unavailable, say so in one line instead — a silently missing section reads as \"nothing related exists\", which is a different and wrong claim}\n\n## GitHub State\n{open issues + notable ones; open/stale PRs; active/orphaned branches; latest release + unreleased commits; failing/recurring CI}\n\n## Project Health\n{is CI green? are PRs flowing? is debt accumulating? risks or blockers}\n\n## Project Memories\n{gotchas, patterns, feedback from memory files — omit section entirely if none}\n```\n\nRules: don't restate README/CLAUDE.md/config (already in context). Focus on cross-file insight (\"auth assumes X because Y\", not \"auth is in src/auth/\"). Update changed sections, leave accurate ones alone. First-time capsule: leave Architecture/Health sparse, they fill in over sessions.\n\n## Phase 4: Restore tasks\n\nAuto-restore the task list from the most-recent prior session. No prompt; silent if nothing to restore.\n\n```bash\n\"~/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/list-task-sessions.sh\"   # JSON: {\"sessions\":[...]} or {\"error\":...}\n```\n\nHandle the result:\n\n- `{\"sessions\": [...]}` non-empty → take `sessions[0].sessionId` (most recent with tasks), proceed below.\n- Empty `sessions`, or `error` in (`no_project_data`, `no_tasks_dir`, `no_index`) → skip Phase 4 silently.\n- `error` is `schema_unexpected` or `index_unreadable` → **do not skip silently.** Claude Code's on-disk layout drifted and the script can no longer find tasks. Flag it in the Phase 5 report: \"task restore disabled — `list-task-sessions.sh` needs updating (`{detail}`).\"\n\nWhen proceeding, dump the chosen session:\n\n```bash\n\"~/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/dump-tasks.sh\" <sessionId>   # JSON array of {id,subject,description,activeForm,status,blocks,blockedBy}\n```\n\nFor each task in original `id` order: call `TaskCreate` with `subject`, `description`, `activeForm`. Then for any task with non-empty `blockedBy`, call `TaskUpdate` with `addBlockedBy`. Do NOT restore `status` — every restored task starts pending so the new session re-evaluates progress.\n\nNote in the Phase 5 report: `Restored N tasks from session {sessionId-short} ({modified-date})`.\n\n## Phase 5: Report\n\nSummarize what you loaded and learned. Flag:\n\n- **Gaps**: missing arch docs, no tests, unclear boundaries\n- **Risks**: failing CI, stale PRs, dependency/security advisories\n- **Blast radius**: impacted files not on the branch (reverse deps), open PRs touching the same areas\n- **CI status**: if red, include the specific errors/stack traces, not just \"CI is red\"\n- **Linked context**: issues/decisions explaining why current work exists\n- **AGENTS.md flags**: project rules/priorities that should guide upcoming work\n- **Suggestions**: things to address before starting new work\n\n## Capsule maintenance during work\n\nUpdate the capsule when you discover something that belongs there (new invariant, architecture decision, clarified boundary, PRD moved/started). Keep it surgical: change the section, bump the date, move on. GitHub State is refreshed only on catchup runs, not during work.\n\n## Error handling\n\n| Situation | Action |\n|-----------|--------|\n| On master, no capsule | Load sources + GitHub state, generate capsule, skip branch diff |\n| On master, capsule exists | Load sources, update stale capsule sections |\n| No remote | Use local master as base for branch diff |\n| Detached HEAD | Report current commit, ask user for base branch |\n| Not a git repo | Load sources only, skip all git/GitHub operations |\n| `gh` missing/unauthenticated, no GitHub remote, or rate limited | Skip GitHub state, note gap in report |\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
