+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_45","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc 'bash /Users/bob/.agents/skills/catchup/scripts/load-memories.sh'","aggregated_output":"--- autocodex-pause-recovery.md ---\n---\nname: autocodex-pause-recovery\ndescription: \"How to clear an autocodex clarification pause by hand in this repo (state CLI verbs, gitignored state.json, task-body refresh, codex wait false-DONE)\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: a511aef8-d874-4e86-847a-20d6d673106e\n  modified: 2026-10-27T20:44:26.530Z\n---\n\nRecovering a paused autocodex run (done 2026-10-26 for AP 00012 Task 2):\n`~/.config/autocodex/host.md` wants the fix made interactively, then an\nexplicit state-CLI resume, then `autocodex` relaunched by the user.\n\n**Why:** the wrapper exits immediately while `phase` is `paused`, and\n`state.json` is gitignored (`docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`), so\nnothing but the on-disk state carries the resume; a wrong edit path (Write/Edit\non state.json) bypasses the single validated writer.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Fix the blocker in its durable home first (here: the design doc), run the\n  design-solution review loop by hand (Claude `Plan` agent, then\n  `codex-run.sh -f <prompt> -o <out>` in the background; the mandatory codex\n  dispatch), and end the `## Review log` with a `result: ok` line.\n- Task bodies embed the design's `## Interfaces & contracts` entries verbatim\n  between `Contract (verbatim):` and `Acceptance criteria:`, but ONLY the `###`\n  entries the task's Location files implement. Embedding the whole section\n  (55 KB in AP 00012) made every body 55 KB, Devon's prompt 69 KB against the\n  50 KB dispatch cap, and the replan then parked the PRD (a 110 KB reference\n  copy cannot fit the 75 K replan budget). Regenerate every pending body and\n  apply with `statectl.py <state> task-set-body <id> <file>` or Tess keeps\n  reading the stale contract.\n- Parked PRD + empty backlog: the build session drains (`phase: done`,\n  `next_phase: \"\"`, `prd` kept) and the adapter paused it as \"build skipped\n  the fresh review handoff\" until the hold/ exemption (2026-10-27). Un-park\n  with `mv hold/ -> backlog/`, set phase/next_phase build, del pause_reason,\n  restore `work_start_sha` to the PRD's original base, and pass planning\n  constraints with `autocodex --scope docs/dev/project-management/plans/<file>.md`.\n- Resume with the shim `skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state>`:\n  `set-contract-card <file>`, `set phase '\"build\"'`, `set next_phase '\"build\"'`,\n  `del pause_reason`; then `autopilot resume-target --state <state>` should print\n  `/work continues at first non-completed task N`.\n- `await_reviewer_outputs.py` returns `DONE` while codex is still reasoning (the\n  `-o` file is a streaming transcript that goes quiet); trust the background\n  task's completion notification or `pgrep -f \"codex exec\"`, and read the\n  findings from the last `codex` section of the `-o` file.\n- The autocodex session `.jsonl` and `autocodex-metrics.jsonl` are the\n  wrapper's own bookkeeping; leave them unstaged for its next state commit.\n- `site: commit_signing` (\"1Password: agent returned an error\", 2026-10-26)\n  means codex ran outside `~/bin/run-agent`, which swaps signing to\n  `ssh-keygen` + `~/.ssh/agent_github`; the `autocodex` shell function now wraps\n  run-agent (needs a fresh shell to reload). Recovery: make the exact commit\n  codex attempted from a run-agent Claude session (signature shows `G`), reset\n  `phase`/`next_phase` to `build`, `del pause_reason`, and leave\n  `stall_reason`/`task_aborts` alone so Phase 0 runs the overrun replan\n  (`resume-target` prints `replan: clear tasks, ...`). Any warrant codex filed\n  for the 1Password commit just expires (no deny verb; `warrant list` is\n  denied in the sandbox). Dotfile edits are sandbox-denied: patch a scratchpad\n  copy, `diff -u --label a/... --label b/...` into an mbox, warrant one\n  `git --git-dir=~/.buvis --work-tree=~ am <mbox>` with `--cwd ~`.\n\nRelated: [[review-work-completion-recipe]].\n\n--- autopilot-work-host-quirks.md ---\n---\nname: autopilot-work-host-quirks\ndescription: \"In autopilot work sessions here, a formatter hook reflows any file a subagent touches, and sonnet-run.sh Pat dispatch fails on revoked OAuth\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 82a9d050-1cab-4615-9f4f-8b28368a9436\n  modified: 2026-11-01T19:15:44.747Z\n---\n\nSeen 2026-11-01 (PRD 00013 build):\n- A formatter hook re-wraps (black-style, 88 cols) every Python file a subagent reads or edits, including already-committed test files. Before staging, `git diff --stat` the tree and `git checkout --` formatter-only churn; apply one-line test fixes with `sed -i` (retry once past the Echo hook) so the formatter does not reflow the file.\n- `sonnet-run.sh` (nested `claude -p`) exits \"OAuth token revoked\". Run Pat via native `autopilot:worker-opus` with `model: sonnet` instead; see [[host-tests-from-inside-a-session]] for the setup-token route.\n- `git show <rev>:<path> --output=...` ignores `--output` and dumps the blob to stdout; never use it for large files.\n\n**Why:** each cost a retry or ~25K context. **How to apply:** check these before the first task of a work session.\n\n--- copilot-review-empty-verdict.md ---\n---\nname: copilot-review-empty-verdict\ndescription: \"Copilot PR review banner \\\"Needs a closer look\\\" beside \\\"No open issues\\\" means zero findings; count reviewThreads via GraphQL instead of reading the banner\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: reference\n  originSessionId: db85b09c-d05f-4b83-95e3-3066e8cdcce6\n  modified: 2026-10-19T06:45:16.586Z\n---\n\nOn PR 5 (2026-10-18) the Copilot review body opened with \"Needs a closer look / One or more issues must be addressed before approval\" and then said \"No open issues\" with a 407-row file table of boilerplate. There were no findings: GraphQL `reviewThreads { totalCount }` was 0, `pulls/5/comments` and `issues/5/comments` were empty.\n\n**Why:** the banner is Copilot's template header, not a verdict; reading the 47KB body or chasing the banner wastes calls.\n\n**How to apply:** check Copilot findings with one call, `gh api graphql` on `pullRequest(number:N) { reviewThreads(first:100) { totalCount nodes { isResolved path comments(first:20) { nodes { body } } } } }`. totalCount 0 means nothing to answer; do not post a \"nothing to address\" comment. See [[review-work-completion-recipe]] for the rest of the close-out.\n\n--- fix-guards-at-source.md ---\n---\nname: fix-guards-at-source\ndescription: \"When a user-owned guard hook misfires on a decided layout, the user wants it fixed at its source repo first, not bypassed for the session\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: feedback\n  originSessionId: e86cf29d-585f-4dee-8a0f-e3636f2af093\n  modified: 2026-10-02T20:57:34.641Z\n---\n\nOn 2026-10-02 the autopilot plugin's `enforce_prd_location.py` blocked every\nedit under `docs/dev/project-management/intake/` (decided 2026-09-27 for\nspecflow). Offered a scratchpad apply script (bypass), fixing the hook first,\nor batching decisions; the user chose \"Fix the hook first\" even though it\nmeant a cross-repo change mid-review.\n\n**Why:** a guard that is wrong stays wrong for every later session if it is\nonly worked around; the user treats their hooks as product code with\nfail-first tests, changelog entries, and releases.\n\n**How to apply:** when a buvis plugin hook blocks a path or action the user\nhas already decided on, fix the hook in its source repo (`claude-autopilot`,\n`claude-aegis`, ...) with a regression test and changelog entry, then patch or\nupdate the installed cache copy; do not route the edit through Bash or a\nscript to dodge the hook. Check whether an autopilot loop is running in that\nrepo first (`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`), since the loop stands\ndown on foreign edits. Related: [[specflow-intake-layout]].\n\n--- host-tests-from-inside-a-session.md ---\n---\nname: host-tests-from-inside-a-session\ndescription: \"How to run the real Claude Code and Codex CLIs for specflow host tests from inside a Claude Code agent session (setup token, nested sandboxes, marketplace installs, profile cleanup), learned on 00008 T-043 to T-045\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 64329de9-63ea-47cc-b4d3-8d5e2127e4ff\n  modified: 2026-11-01T19:11:37.555Z\n---\n\nOn 2026-11-01 the 00008 host tests (T-043, T-046, T-045) ran from inside a\nClaude Code agent session instead of the developer's Terminal.\n\n**Why:** the handoff assumed a Terminal run because a nested `run-agent`\nlaunch fails with `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`\n(exit 71). Nested `claude -p` itself works, as `sonnet-run.sh` already\nrelies on; only the nested Seatbelt fails.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is absent from the session's Bash environment,\n  but `~/.local/secret/claude-setup-token` is readable from the sandbox:\n  a launcher script reads it with `$(<file)`, exports it (never prints it),\n  sets `CLAUDE_NESTED=1` and `_CLAUDE_NOTIFY_QUIET=1`, and runs\n  `claude --plugin-dir <abs plugin> --print ... --output-format stream-json\n  --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools ...`. The pattern is\n  `docs/dev/tmp/specflow/hosts/claude-start-insession.bash` +\n  `capture-claude.py` in the 00008 worktree; the init event of the stream\n  holds `claude_code_version`, `model`, `plugins[]` (source `<name>@inline`\n  for `--plugin-dir`) and `skills[]` (`specflow:spec-workflow`). A 50-turn\n  skill run cost about 3 USD; a one-word `-p` probe about 0.7 USD.\n- Codex's own sandbox cannot apply inside the session Seatbelt: under\n  `--sandbox read-only` or `workspace-write` every shell command exits 71\n  with the same `sandbox_apply` error (probe it with `echo`). For a scratch\n  workspace run `codex-run.sh -y` (bypasses Codex's sandbox; the session\n  Seatbelt still confines it), forbid writes in the prompt, and prove it\n  with `shasum -a 256` of every workspace file before and after. The\n  `CODEX_SESSION_ID` recursion guard only fires inside a Codex session.\n- Codex plugin installs need no model session: `codex plugin marketplace add\n  <checkout|owner/repo --ref x> --json` then `codex plugin add\n  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json` in a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME`; Codex\n  reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as written and copies the plugin to\n  `$CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`.\n- Claude Code marketplace check in the developer's own profile: `claude\n  plugin marketplace add <checkout> --json`, `claude plugin install\n  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json`, `claude plugin details <id>`,\n  then `claude plugin uninstall <id> --json` and `claude plugin marketplace\n  remove <name>`; a folder marketplace reads the plugin in place (`plugin\n  list` says \"Read from: <checkout>/plugins/specflow\") and also writes\n  `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/...`. `claude plugin validate\n  --strict .` validates the root marketplace and advises a README install\n  line (`/plugin install specflow --marketplace <owner>/<repo>`).\n- `gh pr create --base master --head <branch> --body-file <f>` works with\n  the agent PAT; the Validate job finishes in about 30 s.\n- Kiro IDE's GitHub import (Powers panel, Add Custom Power, Import power\n  from GitHub, repository URL) has no headless form: it stays a developer\n  hand-off. See [[review-work-completion-recipe]] for the review side.\n\n--- repo-structure-plan.md ---\n---\nname: repo-structure-plan\ndescription: \"The user's \\\"AI-age repo structure\\\" plan overrides layout recommendations (skill homes, agent-private dirs, links); check it before proposing any\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: reference\n  originSessionId: 02e9b1bf-0c8a-4c00-b452-9fa698cc3aad\n  modified: 2026-10-03T18:57:40.381Z\n---\n\nThe user keeps a repo-structure design at\n`~/.kiro/crew/workspace/ai-age-repo-structure.md` (status on 2026-10-03:\n\"design, for review\", no code yet; the path is a Kiro Crew workspace and may\nmove). On 2026-10-03, during the specflow docs-review walkthrough, the user\npointed me to it after I had recommended committed symlinks under\n`.claude/skills/` and a plugin-owned `.kiro/specs` relink tool. Both\nrecommendations contradicted it and were withdrawn.\n\nRules from it that changed decisions here:\n\n- `.agents/` is the only committed agent config tree; `.agents/skills/` holds\n  the only committed skill copy.\n- No committed `.claude/`, `.kiro/`, `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, and no committed\n  symlinks to them (Windows `core.symlinks` problem). Agent-private dirs are\n  local, gitignored projections made by one idempotent `tools/onboard`.\n- `tools/` holds dev-only scripts; specs live in\n  `docs/dev/project-management/specs/`; decisions are meant to move to\n  `docs/dev/architecture/`.\n\n**How to apply:** before recommending where a skill, config file, link, or\nagent-private folder lives in a buvis repo, read that plan (verify it still\nexists and its status) and frame options against it. My interpretation, not\nthe user's words: treat it as settled intent even while marked \"for review\".\nRelated: [[fix-guards-at-source]].\n\n--- review-work-completion-recipe.md ---\n---\nname: review-work-completion-recipe\ndescription: \"How /autopilot:review-work-completion runs standalone on this specflow-layout repo (no prds/wip, no state.json), which lanes fail every cycle, how the rework after the walkthrough goes, and how a spec closes out once the loop converges\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 633465ce-871a-420b-925a-f87699fb6773\n  modified: 2026-11-01T20:42:15.985Z\n---\n\nStandalone review cycles of spec 00004 (cycles 1-11, 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14) ran with no autopilot state and no `prds/wip/`: the target is `docs/dev/project-management/specs/<spec>/requirements.md`, the design doc is `design.md` beside it, and tasks come from a hand-written `docs/dev/tmp/review-tasks-<id>.json` (copy the previous cycle's; all ten are completed since cycle 6).\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Stage with `python3 ~/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/<ver>/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py review-stage --cycle-id 00004c<N> --repo-root <repo> --tasks-json ... --prd ... --design-doc ... --roster alice,blake,bob,carl --since <prior head_sha> --replay-cmd \"python3 -m pytest\" --prior-findings ... --settled-ledger docs/dev/project-management/reviews/00004-artifact-state-contract-ledger.json --gate-command \"sh <repo>/docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/gate.sh\"`. It finishes in about 10 s.\n- Reusable tooling is saved in `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` (untracked): `gate.sh` runs the five CI steps from `.github/workflows/validate.yml` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, one log each under `gate-logs/`; `build_bob_retry.py <cycle> <base> <head>` builds Bob's inlined retry prompt from the staged files and those logs. `review-stage` cannot parse unittest counts, so compose the `Tests:` line from the `Ran N tests` lines (cycle 11 review: 12 + 52 + 304 = 368; after its rework the contract suite is 308).\n- The spec has no frontmatter, so `consensus_engine` is `legacy` and `doubt_reviewer` is `codex`; Eve stays disabled (no state file, no codex-implemented task record).\n- The Agent tool in this build has no `run_in_background` parameter; subagents run in the background by default. Dispatch Alice and Blake as `autopilot:alice` / `autopilot:blake` with `effort: high`, with a prompt that tells them to Read their rendered prompt file and follow it. Bob and Carl are background Bash. No Watcher (interactive session).\n- Bob's resumed-thread run refuses for lack of input every cycle (cycles 2-11; codex sandbox blocks reads: `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`; in 00006 cycle 1 the aegis Fact-Forcing Gate hook blocked his `cat` instead, same remedy). The inlined retry was 773 KB for 00006 (560 KB diff) and codex handled it in a few minutes. In cycle 11 the refusal was prose only, with no `[BOB] ⚪ Cannot statically verify` line, so the three-pattern rule did not match literally; treat it as the refusal (it is also the malformed-output trigger) and dispatch the pre-built inlined retry without `--resume-thread`. Copy the first output to `bob-output-<id>-first.txt` before the retry overwrites it. The retry overwrites `bob-thread-<id>.txt` with its own thread; stamp that one. His `[BOB]` lines were unbulleted in cycles 10-11; strip a `- ` bullet into a `-lines.txt` copy only when present.\n- Carl failed cycles 2-8 with copilot \"Authentication failed\" (exit 1); cycles 9-11 ran fine (exit 0, `gemini-3.8-flash`). Always dispatch him; on failure, one unchanged retry per policy, then record unavailable; nothing to latch standalone. His `-o` file includes copilot's tool transcript before the `[CARL]` line; the consolidator copes. In cycle 11 his shell ran the suite without `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, then `find . -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +` in the repo: check `git status --ignored=matching plugins tools tests` afterwards (00005 and 00006 left `__pycache__` under `tests/` and `tools/`; `git clean -X -d -f -- plugins tools tests` removes only those).\n- The engram pack fails with a readonly sqlite DB every cycle (in a worktree: \"not inside a registered repo\"); degraded, not blocking.\n- From 00005 on (2026-10-16), work happens in per-spec worktrees under `~/git/src/worktrees/agent-plugins/feature-specflow-<spec>`. `review-tools/` hardcodes the main checkout, so copy `gate.sh` and `build_bob_retry.py` into the worktree's `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` with the worktree path; CI has 7 steps since 00005 (adds `tests/specflow/rules` and `check_rules.py --area ...`, nine areas since 00006). The 00006 worktree already holds seven-step copies. A standalone cycle 1 in a worktree passes `--since <merge-base with master>`; the whole staging took 8 s and the four reviewers about 25 min (Carl last). `rg` skips gitignored `docs/dev/tmp/` unless `--no-ignore`. aegis blocks shell redirects into `docs/dev/tmp/`: send Carl's stderr to the scratchpad. Commit messages: aegis blocks `Co-Authored-By` trailers.\n- The pytest fail-first replay reports `subTest` failures as passes. Always do the unittest replay by hand: a detached worktree at the base sha, copy HEAD's tests in with `cp -R src/. dst/`, run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/specflow/contract -t tests/specflow/contract -k <name> -k <name>...` with bytecode off. The same worktree moved to HEAD (`git checkout -f --detach <head>`) serves mutation runs; remove it with `git worktree remove --force`.\n- `consolidate_findings.py` merges findings on the same file too eagerly: the \"two shared all-digit tokens\" rule fires on requirement IDs like `VAL-001.8` (ledger mis-dismissals, cycle 10), and \"matched only after suffix stripping\" merged two different `checks.py` defects at `:507` and `:528` into one row (cycle 11). Read the merge warning line and the Auto-dismissed block every cycle and split or restore by hand.\n- CI pins Python 3.10 while local `python3` is 3.14: OS-error edge cases differ (`Path.exists()` raises `PermissionError` on 3.10, returns False on 3.14). Probe with `uv run --no-project --python 3.10 python -I <script>`; the contract suite under 3.10 takes 4 s.\n- A ledger entry whose reason is time-bound (\"trial open\") keeps dismissing after the fact changes: cycle 6 restored Blake's Kiro-link finding after T-027 closed. Prune or update such entries when their condition ends.\n- A direct test run writes `plugins/specflow/skills/spec-workflow/scripts/__pycache__`, which then fails `test_script_runs_from_any_python_start_and_leaves_no_bytecode` and `verify_release.py`. Keep `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (or `python3 -B` for probes that import the helper). `verify_release.py` also refuses modified tracked package files: commit the fix first, then re-run it.\n- Blake's F23 re-raises (placeholder and bugfix checks, deferred to 00005/00006) and the cycle-10 F10 scans are absorbed by the ledger every cycle; the script prints the placeholder entry's reason for the bugfix line. The consolidator only dismisses a blind reviewer's ledger re-raises when told so: `consolidate_findings.py --ledger <ledger> --ledger-dismiss blake alice:<f> blake:<f> bob:<f> carl:<f>` (00006 cycle 2: three of Blake's rows dismissed, each with the ledger reason).\n- `check_review_file.py` takes `--review-file <path> --require-codex-guard` (a bare path is a usage error). `--prior-findings` is inlined verbatim under \"### Prior cycle findings\", so write `docs/dev/tmp/review-prior-findings-<id>.md` as the prior table with a Disposition column (fixed, accepted, ledger) and the rework commits named; reviewers then verify fixes instead of re-raising rows.\n- A cycle-1 🟠 that gets fixed means an incremental cycle 2: `--since <cycle-1 head_sha>` (the diff then covers the review-doc, decisions, fix and outcome commits), `--prior-findings`, `--settled-ledger`, and Bob with `--resume-thread <cycle-1 thread>`, which refused for lack of input again (00006 cycle 2); the inlined retry for a 200 KB diff was 201 KB and took about four minutes. Cycle 2 staged in 6 s; the reviewers took 5 min (Alice, Bob retry, Carl) to 10 min (Blake). The lead may downgrade a reviewer's 🟠 with evidence (00006 cycle 2, F2 and F3), but ask the developer whether the downgrades stand before calling the cycle converged.\n- The pytest replay flags a coverage test of a branch that already existed (00006 F9's eight tests) as \"passes at base\": a fact, not a defect.\n\n**Rework after the walkthrough (cycle-10 and cycle-11 pattern):** one `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N walkthrough decisions` commit (minutes appended to the review file, ledger entries), then `fix(specflow): apply the 00004 cycle-N review decisions` (code, tests, CHANGELOG line under `### Fixed`, which is the last section), then `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N outcome`. +{"type":"item.started","item":{"id":"item_48","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"README.md\\\").read_text()[:14000]); print(\\\"Root config:\\\", [p.name for p in Path(\\\".\\\").iterdir() if p.name in (\\\"pyproject.toml\\\",\\\"Makefile\\\",\\\"package.json\\\")]); print(\\\"Personal decisions:\\\"); p=Path.home()/\\\".claude/decisions.md\\\"; print(p.read_text()[:3000] if p.exists() else \\\"absent\\\")'\"","aggregated_output":"","exit_code":null,"status":"in_progress"}}
+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_48","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"README.md\\\").read_text()[:14000]); print(\\\"Root config:\\\", [p.name for p in Path(\\\".\\\").iterdir() if p.name in (\\\"pyproject.toml\\\",\\\"Makefile\\\",\\\"package.json\\\")]); print(\\\"Personal decisions:\\\"); p=Path.home()/\\\".claude/decisions.md\\\"; print(p.read_text()[:3000] if p.exists() else \\\"absent\\\")'\"","aggregated_output":"# buvis agent plugins\n\nPortable agent plugins published by [buvis](https://github.com/buvis).\n\nThis monorepo targets the\n[Agent Plugins specification](https://agent-plugins.org/) v1.0.0. Each\ndirectory under [`plugins/`](plugins/) is an independent, self-contained\nplugin package; the repository itself is not one large plugin.\n\n## Status\n\nThe repository scaffold is ready. No plugins are published yet.\n\n| Plugin | Purpose | Version |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [autopilot](plugins/autopilot/README.md) | Gated review-contract foundation; no host certification or publication. | 0.10.0 |\n\n## Portable scope\n\nAgent Plugins v1 standardizes two portable component types:\n\n- Agent Skills at `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.\n- MCP servers in an optional root `mcp.json`.\n\nCustom agents, commands, hooks, rules, and LSP servers are not portable v1\ncomponents. Keep those in a client-documented reverse-domain extension such as\n`com.github.copilot/`, or in that client's compatibility package. Never add\nclient-only fields directly to the closed portable `plugin.json` schema.\n\n## Repository layout\n\n```text\n.\n├── plugins/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/\n│       ├── plugin.json\n│       ├── README.md\n│       ├── CHANGELOG.md\n│       ├── skills/\n│       │   └── <skill-name>/\n│       │       ├── SKILL.md\n│       │       ├── scripts/       # optional\n│       │       ├── references/    # optional\n│       │       └── assets/        # optional\n│       ├── mcp.json               # optional\n│       └── <reverse.domain.client>/ # optional client extension\n├── templates/example-plugin/\n├── scripts/\n│   ├── validate.py\n│   └── test_validate.py\n├── tools/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/             # maintainer tools, never shipped\n├── tests/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/             # maintainer tests, never shipped\n├── .agents/skills/                # maintainer-only skills, never shipped\n└── .github/\n    ├── workflows/validate.yml\n    └── dependabot.yml\n```\n\nEvery plugin must be usable as though its directory were distributed alone.\nDo not reference files above the plugin root or use symlinks that resolve\noutside it.\n\n`plugins/specflow/` is specflow's only distributable root. Its maintainer\ntools, tests, skills, and scratch files stay outside it, in `tools/specflow/`,\n`tests/specflow/`, `.agents/skills/`, and `docs/dev/tmp/specflow/`.\n\n## Add a plugin\n\nStart from the valid example package:\n\n```bash\ncp -R templates/example-plugin plugins/my-plugin\n```\n\nThen:\n\n1. Rename the plugin and skill directories.\n2. Update `plugin.json`, including `name`, `version`, and description.\n3. Update each skill's `SKILL.md`; its `name` must match its directory.\n4. Remove the example skill or replace it with real instructions.\n5. Add `mcp.json` only when the plugin provides an MCP server.\n6. Document setup, permissions, data access, and a safe first test in the\n   plugin README.\n7. Record user-visible changes in the plugin's `CHANGELOG.md`.\n8. Validate the repository:\n\n   ```bash\n   python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts\n   python3 scripts/validate.py\n   ```\n\nThe repository validator enforces the pinned v1.0.0 manifest shape, names,\nportable layout, basic Agent Skills metadata, MCP transport configuration, and\npackage path containment. The published\n[Agent Plugins specification](https://agent-plugins.org/specification) and\n[Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) remain\nauthoritative.\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the publishing checklist.\n\n## Distribution\n\nAgent Plugins deliberately leaves installation and catalogs to clients. This\nrepository therefore has no invented \"universal marketplace\" manifest.\nClient-specific catalogs will be added only after that client is tested; if\nmore than one catalog is needed, they should be generated from the portable\nplugin manifests to prevent metadata drift.\n\nThe Claude Code catalog, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, is generated from\nthe portable manifests by `python3 scripts/generate_marketplace.py`, is never\nedited by hand, and CI checks it with `--check`.\n\nThe current list of implementations is maintained on the\n[compatible clients](https://agent-plugins.org/compatible-clients) page.\n\n## Security\n\nPlugin instructions and MCP servers can cause tools or code to run with the\nuser's permissions. Review each plugin before installation. Never commit\ncredentials in `mcp.json`, environment values, headers, fixtures, or examples.\nUse client-managed authentication and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` for writable runtime\nstate.\n\nReport vulnerabilities as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).\n\n## License\n\n[MIT](LICENSE). A plugin may carry a different license only when both its\nmanifest and bundled license file say so clearly.\n\n## References\n\n- [Agent Plugins v1.0.0 specification](https://agent-plugins.org/specification)\n- [Canonical Agent Plugins example](https://github.com/agentplugins/agent-plugins-example)\n- [Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification)\n- [Plugin and MCP JSON Schemas](https://agent-plugins.org/schemas)\n\nRoot config: []\nPersonal decisions:\nabsent\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Unlike a thought exercise, Devon must actually write the code and run the tests to prove its exploit works.\n\n## Procedure\n\nDispatch Devon to try to write a **wrong** implementation that passes all of Tess's tests. Devon's goal is to exploit weak tests.\n\n**Devon runs as:** Claude Code subagent (Agent tool) — it needs file write access and the project's test runner to execute its wrong implementation against the tests. **Devon receives only:** the test files from Tess, public interfaces/types (so its wrong implementation compiles), and test-runner access. No task description, no acceptance criteria, no architecture docs.\n\n**Devon's job:** Write an implementation that is clearly wrong (hardcoded values, ignored edge cases, shortcut if/else chains), run the tests against it, and report which tests it broke through.\n\n**Outcomes:**\n\n| Devon result | Action |\n|----------------|--------|\n| Cannot break tests (tests catch all exploits) | Tests are strong. Proceed to 2.95 (the tests were committed at step 2.85, before Devon ran). |\n| Breaks tests with wrong impl that passes | Send Devon's exploit back to Tess as a numbered weak-point list (see Feedback to Tess below). +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_86","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/work/references/test-author-prompt.md\\\").read_text()); print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/work/references/red-check.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"# Test Author Prompt (Tess)\n\nTess writes tests from requirements. She has NOT seen and must NOT think about implementation.\n\n## Prompt Template\n\nThe prompt template lives in `work/references/tess-prompt.md` (single source\nof truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`\nconsumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table).\n\n## Context Selection\n\nWhen building Tess's prompt, include:\n\n| Include | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Task description + acceptance criteria | The spec Tess tests against |\n| Public types/interfaces | So Tess knows the API surface |\n| One sample test file | So Tess follows project conventions |\n| Test framework config | So imports and assertions are correct |\n| `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`, when it exists | The project's own harness rules, for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>` the task touches |\n\n| Exclude | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Architecture docs | Would leak implementation thinking |\n| AGENTS.md internals | Same - Tess doesn't need to know how things are built |\n| Implementation files | Defeats the entire purpose |\n| \"How to build this\" guidance | Tess is a test author, not an implementor |\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.7 (PRD 00119-v2) — the two lists the\nstep used to spell out inline. **Read this section before the first Tess\ndispatch of a batch.**\n\n**Tess receives:**\n- Task description and acceptance criteria\n- The **exact file paths** the task touches — spelled **absolute** — and the **exact symbol names** to test, taken from the plan task — not \"find the relevant file\"\n- Public interfaces/types relevant to the task\n- The project's test-harness contract when one exists (PRD 00141): for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>`, `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md` joins the `PUBLIC_INTERFACES` `--set-cmd`, once per distinct file; no such file adds nothing. It carries harness rules, never implementation — a harness can make a test pass for reasons requirements cannot reveal (a `capture_main` that installs its own `sys.stdin`, so a \"marker checked before stdin\" test passes against the old code too)\n- Existing test patterns (one sample test file from the project)\n- Test framework and conventions used\n\n**Tess does NOT receive:**\n- Implementation strategy or architecture docs (loaded in step 2.5 for the main session and Ivan only)\n- \"How to build this\" context\n- Access to modify non-test files\n\nThe stdout integer from step 2.7's render call **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement — no separate `wc -c`. `tess-prompt.md` bakes in the read-only-scope instruction, the dispatch prologue, the Assumptions footer and the size limits (rule 12: functions under 50 lines, files under 800) permanently (mirroring `ivan.md`), so nothing further needs adding to the prompt by hand — open-ended discovery is where subagents burn turns and stall, and keeping Tess scoped to the listed files/symbols is the template's job now. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source. The template also embeds Simplicity/Think-Before-Coding/Surgical rules to prevent Tess from writing speculative tests or silently assuming input shape.\n\n## Quality gate (step 2.8)\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.8 (PRD 00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the\ngate rule and the total-Tess budget; the rubric and the retry render live here.\n**Read this section before running the gate on Tess's first test file.**\n\n**Run the computed shape check first**, on every test file Tess wrote or changed:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/detect_tautological_tests.py <test file>...\n```\n\nIt prints one `[MECH] {emoji} <test> <reason> | File: <path>:<line> | Task: general` line per test whose shape cannot fail (a constant or self-comparing assert, an `A or B` hedge, a swallowed exception, `raises(Exception)`, no assertion at all) and always exits 0. **Every `[MECH]` line is a check-4 failure**: copy it verbatim into the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` file, then judge the four checks below by reading. The script sees shape only; a test that restates the code in a perfectly valid shape is still check 4's to catch by hand. The same script runs at review (`review-work-completion` step 3), so a shape that slips past here comes back as a `mech-check` finding and a rework cycle — cheaper to fix now.\n\nBefore committing Tess's tests, review them in the main session against this checklist:\n\n1. **Behavior names?** Each test name describes a behavior (\"rejects empty email\"), not an implementation detail (\"calls validateEmail\")\n2. **Real assertions?** Assertions check outputs/effects, not mock internals\n3. **Edge cases?** Empty, null, boundary, error, and concurrent cases covered where relevant\n4. **No tautologies?** Tests don't just restate what the code obviously does\n5. **Exploit classes covered?** Every tested function has the six rule-6a assertions (two fixture values per asserted field, a near-miss negative, a multi-element and an empty input, an accept and a reject case of the same shape, a surfaced error, a dependency assertion); a missing one is a check-5 failure and names the class.\n\nIf any check fails, dispatch Tess again with specific feedback about what's weak. Render the retry the same way as the initial dispatch — never author it by hand:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md \\\n  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>-retry-<n>.txt \\\n  --set-file QUALITY_FEEDBACK=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-gate-<n>.txt \\\n  --set-file TASK_DESCRIPTION=<the same scratch file step 2.7 used> \\\n  --set-file TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-acceptance.txt --dispatch-kind tess --dispatch-task <task-id>\n```\n\nWrite the gate findings (one per line) to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file with the Write tool. Max 2 quality gate retries.\n\n### Style limits on the test files\n\nOnce the four checks pass, run the step-5.65 gate over the test files only, so an oversized test file is split by a Tess retry now (cheap, tests-only) instead of an Ivan style-fix dispatch after implementation (PRD 00197; `tess-prompt.md` rule 12 already tells her the limits). Build the diff the way `references/style-gate.md` § Diff construction does, over this task's test files alone: `git diff <task_base_sha> --output=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt -- <tracked test files>` (`--output=` goes before `--`; after it git reads it as a pathspec and prints the diff to stdout instead), then `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <file> >> ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt` per untracked test file (exit 1 is the normal case; only exit ≥2 is a failure), then `mv ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt`. Then:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_style_limits.py --diff docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt <each new or changed test file as an absolute path>\n```\n\nExit 0 is clean. Exit 1 is a quality-gate failure: write the violation lines to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file and render the retry above; it counts toward the two quality-gate retries. Exit 2 (the script could not run) is not a Tess failure: name it in the task output and proceed, step 5.65 measures the same files again after implementation.\n\n## Retry Prompt (after quality gate failure)\n\nThe retry template lives in `work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md` (single\nsource of truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`\nconsumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table). It\ntakes `{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}`, `{TASK_DESCRIPTION}` and\n`{TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}`, and bakes in the same fixed guards the initial\ntemplate carries (read-only scope, 100K abort line, dispatch prologue,\nASSUMPTIONS footer).\n\n`{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}` is the step-2.8 gate's own findings, one per line, e.g.:\n\n- Test \"handles validation\" is too vague. Name the specific behavior.\n- Test 3 would pass with a function that always returns true. Add constraints.\n- No edge case for empty input.\n\n# Red-Check Detail (step 2.95)\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.95 (PRD 00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the\nrun-it-once rule, the `n/a:new_module` verdict and the skip-when-2.7-skipped\nrule; the target resolution and the outcome ladder live here. **Read this file\nbefore the first red-check of a batch.** \"The check\" below is step 2.95's own run: the newly committed tests once, at the narrowest scope, with the outcomes in § Outcomes.\n\n## New-module pre-check\n\n**New-module pre-check — skip the pytest invocation, don't just expect it to fail.** Before running the pytest command, identify the target module using the task's own `Contract` section (the exact file path(s) the task implements, per `plan-tasks`' own contract convention) — not every import in the test file, only the one under test. The target module is the test file's import whose resolved filesystem path matches one of those Contract paths; this sidesteps import-parsing ambiguity entirely, since the task plan already names the file being built.\n\n**Only the Contract paths the test file actually imports are candidates.** A Contract routinely names files the new tests never import — an edited caller, a schema doc, a reference page — and a missing one of those does not imply an `ImportError`, so it must not suppress the run. Intersect first: take the Contract paths, keep those the test file imports, and judge existence on that set alone.\n\nIf any **imported** Contract-named target path does not yet exist on disk, skip the pytest invocation for this step entirely: write `red_check = \"n/a:new_module\"` to the attempt entry and proceed straight to step 3 (still \"expected red\" semantically — a module that doesn't exist cannot pass). A Contract naming multiple imported files, some new and some existing, still takes this branch if ANY of them is missing — partial existence still guarantees an `ImportError` on the missing half, so running pytest gains nothing.\n\n**No Contract section, or no Contract path the tests import** (a legacy plan task, or a task whose Contract names only non-imported files): there is nothing to resolve, so do NOT skip. Run the check exactly as below — an unresolvable target is a reason to gather real evidence, never a reason to record `n/a:new_module` on a module that may well exist.\n\nOtherwise (every imported Contract-named target already exists — this is an edit to an existing module, not a new one), run the check exactly as below.\n\n## Outcomes\n\n| Outcome | Action |\n|---------|--------|\n| ≥1 test fails | Expected red. Proceed to step 3. |\n| All pass | Accidentally-green tests bind nothing. Send the run output back to Tess (\"these tests pass with no implementation — strengthen them to fail against the current tree\"); this consumes the **Total Tess budget** (step 2.8; on exhaustion flag and proceed per that step). Commit the strengthened tests (`test(<scope>): strengthen tests for <feature>`), re-capture `<test_commit_sha>` per step 2.85, and re-run this check. |\n| Tests cannot run standalone (they import the not-yet-built feature, or the runner cannot execute them) | Record `red_check: skipped:<cause>` in the task's attempt entry and the phase report (fail loud; a skipped check must never read as a passed one), then proceed to step 3. |\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Other provider hosts use their host mapping.\n\n# Autopilot\n\nOrchestrate the full PRD lifecycle: catchup → design → plan-tasks → work → review-rework loop (consensus + blind + doubt lenses, every cycle) → done.\n\nMakes autonomous decisions backed by research (dependencies, recurring issues, API/schema changes when PRD-driven) and pauses only for critical security, requirements ambiguity, or blocking decisions.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Pack skills (invoked as phases): `design-solution`, `plan-tasks`, `work`,\n  `review-work-completion`\n- Plugin skills: `git-ferry:catchup` (Phase 1, unless the PRD sets `catchup: skip`)\n- Files read from other skill dirs:\n  `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py`\n  (Watcher keep-alive)\n- Hooks outside the skill dir: `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`\n- Shell wrapper outside `~/.claude`: `autoclaude` in\n  `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash` - operator subcommands +\n  tracon front-end; it hands off to `autopilot loop` (`cli/loop.py`), the\n  unattended session loop since PRD 00106\n- Scripts (own dir, model-invoked as a CLI): `scripts/statectl.py` — the sole\n  `state.json` mutator (`get`/`set`/`append`/`del`; atomic, advisory-locked,\n  one rotating `.bak`)\n- CLIs: `claude` (headless `-p`), `python3` (>= 3.11), `git`, `awk`\n- Optional: `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`; the default `autoclaude` front-end since PRD 00062, `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0` or no tty/`uv` falls back to `render_stream.py`) - dashboard only, absence changes nothing\n\n## Execution Model\n\n**Run all phases in sequence without stopping.** After each phase completes, immediately update state and proceed to the next phase. Do not pause between phases, do not summarize progress, do not wait for user input - unless the phase explicitly says PAUSE or STOP. Completing a sub-skill invocation (`/git-ferry:catchup`, `/autopilot:plan-tasks`, `/autopilot:work`, `/autopilot:review-work-completion`, etc.) is NOT a stopping point. It is an intermediate step. Continue.\n\nReview sessions run on opus at xhigh in cycle 1 and at high on cycle 2 and later; _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW forces one effort for every cycle and _AUTOPILOT_EFFORT_REVIEW_RERUN sets the rerun value. A rework resume (the cycle's review file exists and `rework_task_ids` names an unfinished task) runs on the queued tasks' own tier instead, sonnet unless one is opus or fable (`references/model-ladder.md` § Review sessions, PRD 00207).\n\n## Entry Points\n\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot` — auto-select PRD (wip first, then backlog), run full cycle\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot <prd-filename>` — full cycle with specific PRD\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot status` — print current dashboard, no action\n- `/autopilot:run-autopilot review-batch` — interactively review a finished batch's deferred items\n\nIf invoked with `status`, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`, print phase/cycle/task summary, and stop.\n\nIf invoked with `review-batch`, load the newest `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json` and run the \"Batch-End Review\" presentation (`references/phase-done.md`) against it — chunked by PRD, wait for user decisions, execute \"fix now\" items. No state changes; the batch is already closed. Stop when all chunks are reviewed (or the user says stop).\n\nPreflight for a batch rooted at `~/.claude`: the launching shell must `export _AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA=\"$HOME/.config/bash:$HOME/.codex:$HOME/.local/bin\"`, or the write-scope fence (`hooks/enforce_write_scope.py`) false-denies edits under those roots and the task parks; `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE=off` disarms the fence for the batch.\n\n## Gate Dispatch\n\nThe full per-phase instructions live in three gate reference files; this core deliberately carries only the shared contract plus the invariants below. After the entry-point checks, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` and **Read the matching gate file now; do not execute a gate from memory**:\n\nA state carrying `stall_op` runs `autopilot park` to reconcile before any gate file is read.\n\n| resume state | Read this gate file |\n|--------------|---------------------|\n| `phase: \"build\"` — or `state.json` missing (fresh start) | `references/phase-build.md` |\n| `phase: \"review\"` — or a legacy `\"blind\"`/`\"doubt\"` value (pre-00015 state), which maps to `review` | `references/phase-review.md` |\n| `phase: \"done\"` | `references/phase-done.md` |\n| `phase: \"paused\"` — or `stall_reason` set | `references/phase-build.md` (its Phase 0 abort/pause handlers own this resume) |\n\n`status` and `review-batch` invocations do not dispatch a gate (see Entry Points).\n\n## State Management\n\nAll autopilot artifacts live under `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`, organized by type:\n\n```\ndocs/dev/project-management/autopilot/\n  state.json                              # current cycle state\n  last-session.log                        # loop-teed raw output of the last headless session\n  reports/{batch_id}-report.md            # batch audit report\n  deferred/{batch_id}-deferred.json       # unresolved items across PRDs\n```\n\nState file: `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — see `references/state-schema.md` for schema.\n\n**`statectl` is the sole writer of `state.json`.** Apply every field mutation with `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set|append|del <json-path> <json-value>` (read one field with `get`); it takes an advisory lock, backs up to `<state.json>.bak`, changes only the named path while preserving all siblings, and replaces the file atomically — so it cannot leave a half-written or unparseable state, and it never trips the \"not read yet\" / \"modified since read\" errors the editing tools hit. Since PRD 00089 it is a shim over `cli/state.transaction`, so every write is schema-validated too: a value that is malformed **for the field it targets** is rejected with exit 1 and the file left byte-unchanged (an unrelated pre-existing odd field blocks nothing). **Phase transitions are not field mutations** — use `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` (§ Session handoff procedure), never a hand-written `set phase` / `set next_phase` pair, so a transition cannot land without the effects it mandates. Resolve `<state.json>` by walking up from the resolved physical cwd to the autopilot dir (the `_walk_up.py` pattern in `/autopilot:work` step 2). The terse `set X` / `write field Y` / per-PRD-reset instructions throughout these skills and the gate files name the fields to change; each is applied with `statectl`, never by hand-editing the file.\n\nDocumented human fallback: outside the loop a person may still Edit or Write `state.json` by hand (for forensics or recovery — the model itself never hand-edits `state.json`; a statectl failure has its own marker-based recovery below); `validate_state_json_hook.py` catches a hand-edit that leaves the file unparseable and now also runs `cli.schema.validate` on it, and `statectl` reads whatever valid JSON it finds on its next mutation.\n\n**When `statectl` itself fails** (nonzero exit — advisory-lock contention, a Python error, an unreadable `state.json`): retry the exact command ONCE. If it fails again, do NOT improvise a partial write and do NOT proceed on the stale state — a lost mutation strands the loop on the wrong `next_phase`. Run `autopilot restore` (rolls `state.json` back to `<state.json>.bak`) and retry the statectl command once more. If the failure persists (`autopilot restore` itself fails, or the subsequent statectl write still fails), WRITE THE MARKER `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state-write-failed` with the Write tool — ONE line of JSON `{\"site\": \"statectl_fail\", \"detail\": \"<the statectl command and its raw stderr>\"}` — and END THE TURN: the wrapper halts on the marker and surfaces the `detail` itself, so no further state write is needed. Interactive sessions ALSO report the same failure to the user directly (there is no wrapper watching an interactive terminal). The raw stderr rides into the marker's `detail` so the failure is diagnosable, never silent (`rules/operating-principles.md`). (Lock contention on the single-writer model implies a second loop or a stale lock; the concurrent-loop guard below now refuses a second loop up front, so a persistent lock is a stale one — the retry clears it or the marker records it.)\n\nCreate `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/` and subdirectories if missing. Initialize state file at PRD selection. Update state at every phase transition. Autopilot also keeps a per-PRD **decision audit log** at `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/<prd-base>-audit.md`, **rendered once at Phase 9 finalize from the `state.json` decision arrays** (`autonomous_decisions`, `deferred_decisions`, `doubts`). `state.json` is the single in-run source of truth — decisions are NOT mirrored to `audit.md` incrementally per decision. Each rendered entry carries a **source** label (`autonomous`, `deferred`, or `doubt`); cycle/phase context goes in the entry body so the Phase 9 `decisions.md` projection can filter autonomous entries by label. The render is `autopilot render audit` (PRD 00107); the label set and the projection live in `references/audit-log-format.md`.\n\n**Invariant:** every state mutation that advances `phase` SHOULD also set `next_phase` to the same value. The three gates are `build` | `review` | `done` (plus `paused`). `build` is ONE session: selection, catchup, design, planning, and work all run under `phase: \"build\"` with no mid-build handoff. The review surface runs in its own fresh session; blind and doubt scrutiny are LENSES inside every review cycle (Blake and Bob in `review-work-completion`'s roster), not separate phases — reviewers get isolated contexts by construction (subagent prompts, external CLIs). Legacy `blind`/`doubt` phase values in pre-00015 state files map to `review` on resume. Per-task implementor tiering inside `/autopilot:work` is unchanged. The authoritative resume signal is `phase` + `phases_completed`; build sub-step skipping is by ARTIFACT (capsule freshness, design-doc-exists, tasks-exist, all-done), not by `phases_completed` membership. This resume decision (phase + phases_completed + artifact checks → next step) is encoded canonically in `cli/resume.py` (`scripts/resume_target.py` re-exports it), which `scripts/test_autopilot_resume.py` imports — editing the resume logic there flips a test red rather than silently drifting from this prose. Run `autopilot resume-target` at Phase 0 to print what that encoding says the next action is, and reconcile it against the handler you are about to follow: a disagreement means the prose and the encoded contract have drifted, and the encoding wins. It also runs the schema-version preflight, so an old or future `state.json` is surfaced there rather than resumed blindly. It answers for the `build` and `review` gates; `phase: \"done\"` returns `unknown phase: done` by design — the done gate is routed by the table above, not by this function.\n\n### Retention\n\nEverything under `docs/dev/project-management/` is tracked work-management state. It is never age-purged. Completed PRDs, reviews, designs, audit logs, reports, ledgers, deferred records, telemetry, and the project capsule therefore remain available to remotes. Runtime control files such as `state.json`, marker files, lane files, and wave slots may still be removed by their explicit lifecycle transitions, but never by a generic stale-file collector.\n\n- **Durable** (never delete): `docs/dev/project-management/prds/done/` and its PRDs, `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/` (per-cycle review files, blind/doubt reviews, and the `<prd-base>-audit.md` audit renders), `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` (per-PRD design docs), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/` (batch reports), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred/` (the `{batch_id}-deferred.json` records), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/loop-metrics.jsonl` (the ledger mirror, the durable copy to read), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/attempts.jsonl` (per-attempt rows appended at every PRD close, `references/state-schema.md` § Attempt ledger), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/custody.jsonl` (the custody journal, the push guard's restore source when the `critical-on-master` marker is removed, `references/state-schema.md` § Custody journal), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (per-dispatch timing rows and session-handoff edges, `work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`, and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/<wave id>-wave.md` (the ledger mirror of the wave summary report `autopilot wave assemble` writes, the durable copy to read). The `reports/<wave id>-wave.md` copy it mirrors is tracked as well, but the ledger mirror is the one to read.\n- **Not durable** (untracked scratch): `docs/dev/tmp/`, the only tree `purge-devtmp` touches.\n- **Disposable** (removed by their lifecycle transitions, by name): `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wrapper.log`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/paused-by-operator`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` (re-rendered at every handoff), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.session-left` (overwritten at every loop-mode handoff), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/lanes/` (one marker per live CLI reviewer lane, removed when the lane exits), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` (at batch end only — in loop mode the wrapper archives it to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`; see `references/phase-done.md`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wave.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/wave-slots/` and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/review-paths` (a wave's control file, its per-wave review-slot directory, and the review's path-scoping list — the last removed with the assembly worktree at wave end, same lifecycle as the other two — none is a durable PRD-lifecycle artifact; `references/waves.md`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json.bak`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/**/*.lock` (the flock files beside `state.json` and beside each `deferred/*.json`), `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.turn-counts.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.handoff-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.cap-fired`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-verification.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.review-gate-blocks`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.review-gate-failed`, and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.lane-guard-blocks`.\n\nThe machine form of this list is `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`, shipped by the Phase 0 `mkdir` step; a test keeps the two in step.\n\nTemporary review context and other reproducible scratch material belongs under the globally ignored `docs/dev/tmp/` tree. `purge-devtmp` operates only there, preserves files linked to live PRDs, and never traverses `docs/dev/project-management/`.\n\nBatch end and cleanup steps enumerate lifecycle-owned runtime files explicitly; they never remove a directory wholesale. This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\n### Resuming\n\nWhen `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.\n- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).\n\n**Hand-off = write state, print banner, end the turn.** After the process exits, the loop driver reads `state.json` and branches:\n\n0. `state-write-failed` marker present → stop the loop and notify with its `detail`, without needing `state.json` to be readable.\n1. `pause_reason` set or `phase == \"paused\"` → notify the user with the pause detail, stop the loop, state left intact.\n2. `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (set by `/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass; `/autopilot:work` also appends to `state.task_aborts`) → continue the loop; Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place (PRD stays in `wip/`; see the build gate's abort handlers). This is the one surviving replan path.\n3. `next_phase == \"\"` (empty) → backlog drained: the loop archives `state.json` to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`, notifies, and stops the loop.\n4. `next_phase` non-empty → relaunch a fresh session, which resumes from state by artifact — capsule fresh → skip catchup, tasks exist → skip planning, `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task.\n5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies \"died\" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.\n\nA Work-turn context-cap overrun is just branch 4: `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` records the rotation (appends to `state.cap_rotations`, resets the in-flight task to `pending`, sets `next_phase: \"build\"`), the turn ends, and the fresh session resumes `build` by artifact — NO replan.\n\n**Stand-down procedure (a peer session owns the PRD).** A headless session never works a PRD another session is already working: two writers on one `state.json` and one set of task artifacts corrupt both, and the one-loop-per-repo guard sees only wrappers, not a bare interactive session. Phase 0 asks before it pauses. A peer counts only when `ListAgents` shows a busy interactive session whose name starts with this repository's directory basename (`basename \"$PWD\"`, e.g. `agent-skills-`); a session named for another repository is never evidence, whatever it is busy with (the two 2026-09-14 false stand-downs in agent-skills each cited a `claude-autopilot-*` session, the other repo's own loop). When such a peer exists, send it one `SendMessage` naming the PRD and wait at most 120 s for a reply. Stand down only when the reply claims the PRD (condition `peer_claimed`), or when writer evidence is present: `autopilot dirty` prints at least one path (condition `dirty_tree`; store writes never count as this evidence), or the mtime of `state.json` or `contract-card.md`, truncated to whole seconds, is greater than the `at` of the most recent `kind: \"handoff\"` row with `edge: \"leave\"` and this PRD's `prd` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (condition `state_after_leave`; the rows carry no batch id, so the `prd` filter is what keeps an older batch's row out; when no such `leave` row exists, skip the mtime test and let the dirty-tree test and the reply decide). That comparison holds only because every handoff site writes its `leave` row AFTER its last state and card write (§ Session handoff procedure orders step 1 before step 2; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff must set `next_phase` before its row too): a site that touches `state.json` after its row makes every next session read its own hand-off as peer evidence. A bare recent mtime is not evidence (a reader that inspects state while the loop writes, or this batch's own per-PRD reset, satisfies it), commit trailers are not consulted (no commit here carries a session trailer), and a peer that only reads, or never answers, never pauses a batch. To stand down: do not select, move, or write anything else; write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` with the Write tool as one JSON line, `{\"reason\": \"<peer session> owns <prd> (<evidence>)\", \"condition\": \"<peer_claimed | dirty_tree | state_after_leave>\"}`, and end the turn. The loop reads a marker written during the session as a stand-down (branch 5 above): it stops with state intact, burns no retry, writes no park marker, quotes the reason in its stop line and notification, and records `stood_down` and `stood_down_condition` in the session's `loop-metrics.jsonl` row; `autoclaude` alone resumes once the peer is done. Before this procedure existed (2026-09-02, agent-skills PRD 00010) four stand-downs read as deaths and parked a healthy PRD mid-task.\n\nThe model's only job at a hand-off is to write `state.next_phase` (and `phase`/`stall_reason`) accurately, print the banner, and end the turn. The model never writes any signal and never inspects the loop's decision table — writing accurate state IS the hand-off. Interactive (non-loop) semantics are identical minus the loop: the same state writes happen, and the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` manually.\n\n**End the turn only at a real hand-off.** A phase is complete only when its artifacts are written and `state` is advanced (`phases_completed` updated, `next_phase` set). Dispatched work — `Agent` calls and background Bash — returns its results **within the same headless turn**: the harness re-invokes you with each `<task-notification>` before the turn can end, so dispatch, overlap independent work, wait for the results, and finish the phase. Do not end the turn to \"wait for\" something you dispatched.\n\n**Background Bash alone cannot hold a headless session open.** Documented `-p` behavior: live subagents keep the process alive across turn ends and re-invoke on completion, but background Bash tasks are killed ~5s after the final result. A turn that ends while ONLY background Bash (codex/gemini/qwen, `cargo test`, …) is still running kills that work and strands the phase (2026-07-12: the review session died this way twice — codex killed mid-review, state untouched, loop halted). Whenever dispatched background Bash may outlive every live subagent, dispatch a **Watcher subagent** in the same message that re-runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py` against the expected output files until `DONE` (procedure: `/autopilot:review-work-completion` step 5). The loop's session runner exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` so the subagent wait has no 10-minute ceiling; the session wall-clock cap stays the backstop.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
