Verify THIS task's tests pass\n\n**Any other value / absent — diagnose→repair/escalate flow (default):**\n\nPer-rung budgets are declared once in `model-ladder.md` § Per-rung budgets — cite, do not restate: Claude rungs (haiku/sonnet/opus) get 2 dispatches (initial + one feedback retry) before diagnosis; the codex rung gets 2 dispatches (initial + one feedback retry), and never a repair; the `fable` rescue rung gets 1 capability dispatch per PRD, ever (no feedback retry, no repair); the qwen rung gets 1 dispatch (no feedback retry — the existing one-shot carve-out, named the ladder's `qwen -> sonnet` capability edge); repair is capped at 1 per task, total, and is Claude-rungs only (qwen never repairs).\n\n**Codex attempt classification — three arms.** Use the arms declared in `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung:\n\n1. **Infra:** an unhealthy batch probe, watchdog timeout, or missing/empty `-o` file falls back to Claude at the task's tier with no `escalation_reason`.\n2. **Infra (no-edit arm):** when the `-o` file is non-empty and the helper exited 0 but the run produced no working-tree change, classify the hook-blocked prose-only run as infra: fall back to Claude at tier, with no feedback retry and no `escalation_reason`, and record `cause: \"codex_no_edit\"`.\n3. **Capability:** a step-5.5 test-gate failure after a run that did edit the tree enters diagnosis and escalates with a stamp.\n\nThe no-edit detector runs at the dispatch boundary, **not at step 5.5**. Step 5 commits the implementation before the step-5.5 gate, so the porcelain is clean at 5.5 for both a successful codex run and a no-edit run; checking there cannot distinguish them. Capture porcelain for the task's own file slice immediately before the codex dispatch, then capture it again immediately after the helper returns and before step 5's `git add` (both captures are checklist steps in `references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex dispatch); latch the comparison as `codex_no_edit` in the attempt record, and have step 5.5 read only that latched flag — never re-run `git status` here. Scoping both snapshots to the task's own file slice prevents a concurrent user edit elsewhere in the live worktree from masking this arm.\n\nBoth snapshots MUST use the same Git context as the `repo_root` invariant. A bare `git status` fails for a bare-repo-backed worktree: measured 2026-07-22, running `git status --porcelain <path>` from `/Users/dev/.claude` exits 128 with `fatal: not a git repository (or any of the parent directories): .git`, because `~/.claude` is tracked by the `~/.buvis` bare repo with work-tree `$HOME` and has no `.git` of its own. Use:\n\n```bash\ngit --git-dir=<bare-git-dir> --work-tree=<work-tree> status --porcelain -- <file slice>\n```\n\nFor this repo the context is `--git-dir=/Users/dev/.buvis --work-tree=/Users/dev`. If either snapshot exits non-zero, the probe is **INDETERMINATE**, not \"no change\": do not latch `codex_no_edit`; record the exit code in `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` and continue through the capability path normally. A broken detector must never silently reclassify real codex capability failures as infra. These classification semantics live as a hand-maintained model in `scripts/work_routing.py`, tested in isolation by `scripts/test_work_routing.py` — kept in sync with this prose by review, not by a test that goes red when the prose changes.\n\n```\ngate fail #1 at current rung → feedback retry: dispatch Ivan with the failure output, SAME tier\n                                (haiku/sonnet/opus and codex rungs only, never fable - the qwen rung has no\n                                feedback retry: its single gate failure goes straight to DIAGNOSE\n                                below, per the 1-dispatch budget)\ngate fail #2 at current rung → DIAGNOSE:\n  1. Write task.description (from state.tasks[i].description, already in hand from step 1's\n     pending scan) to docs/dev/tmp/diagnose-task-<id>.txt and run:\n       python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/diagnose_task.py <task-file> --repo-root <project-root>\n     `<project-root>` = the dir containing docs/dev/project-management/, resolved by walking up from cwd (same anchor\n     as _walk_up.py) — NOT state.repo_root, which differs under a bare-repo-backed project.\n     verdict \"spec_gap\" (exit 0) → REPAIR path below, if repair unused this task AND current rung\n     is a haiku, sonnet, or opus rung, never fable (qwen never repairs — see budgets above)\n  2. verdict \"pass\", OR the script errored (exit 2, shape-check inconclusive) → inline rubric\n     judgment, this session, at its current tier: spec_gap | solid_spec, with a one-line\n     justification, stamped as `diagnosis` on the diagnosed rung's attempt entry (see Attribution\n     below). The orchestrator never overrides a deterministic spec_gap verdict from step 1.\nREPAIR (spec_gap, repair not yet used this task, current rung is\n  haiku, sonnet, or opus, never fable): fill the identified gaps (missing Contract, missing\n  Acceptance criteria, dangling file references) from the PRD + design doc, rewrite the task\n  description via `task-set-body <task-id> <body-file>` — the canonical store /autopilot:work reads\n  directly from `state.tasks[i].description` — and re-dispatch Ivan at the SAME tier ONCE.\n  Stamp `repair_used:true` on that rung's attempt entry. A gate failure after the repair takes\n  the solid_spec path below — repair is exhausted for this task.\nESCALATE (solid_spec, OR spec_gap with repair unavailable/already used, OR any qwen-rung spec_gap):\n  1. Reset guard — capture `<candidate_head>` = `git rev-parse HEAD` first, then require BOTH:\n     - **uncommitted:** `git status --porcelain` is empty (no foreign/uncommitted working-tree files), AND\n     - **committed range:** `git rev-list <test_commit_sha>..<candidate_head>` contains ONLY this\n       task's own implementation commit(s) (the commits step 5 made after the test commit).\n     Passing the guards is necessary but NOT sufficient — a foreign commit can still land between the\n     check and the reset (a live worktree; project_autopilot_head_moves_midreview), and `git reset\n     --hard <test_commit_sha>` would silently discard it. So move the ref ATOMICALLY, never with a\n     bare `git reset --hard` off a stale check:\n     - both guards pass → compare-and-swap the branch ref to the test commit, succeeding ONLY if HEAD\n       is still `<candidate_head>`: `git update-ref refs/heads/<current-branch> <test_commit_sha>\n       <candidate_head>` (the third arg is git's old-value guard — the CAS; `<current-branch>` from\n       `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD`). Then `git reset --hard` (the ref already points at the test\n       commit, so this only cleans the worktree). `<test_commit_sha>` is this task's own test commit,\n       captured in-session right after step 2.85 (or the step-2.9 strengthen commit, whichever\n       is the last test commit) — never a prior task's commit.\n     - the CAS fails (HEAD moved — a foreign commit raced in), OR either guard failed (foreign\n       uncommitted files, or a foreign commit already in `<test_commit_sha>..<candidate_head>`) → do\n       NOT reset; escalate fix-forward instead (dispatch the higher rung against the current tree +\n       failing tests, no reset) and log the deviation on the attempt. Never discard commits or files\n       this task did not create (memory: feedback_subagents_vs_live_worktree,\n       project_autopilot_head_moves_midreview). Fix-forward is the safe default whenever the reset is\n       not provably this-task-only AND atomic.\n  2. Stamp the LOWER rung's entry: `outcome:\"escalated\"`, `diagnosis:<verdict>` (+\n     `qwen_gate_failed:true` if that rung's implementor was qwen, + `repair_used:true` if a repair\n     ran at that rung). **If the task's `state.tasks[i]` entry carries a review-flag escalation\n     (`escalation_reason:\"review_flag\"` + `escalated_from`, set by /autopilot:run-autopilot Phase 6 when this\n     rung IS the review-flagged rework rung), copy both onto THIS lower-rung entry now** — Phase 6\n     escalated INTO this rung, so the `review_flag` reason belongs here; capturing it before step 3\n     clears it is what keeps the review-flag source recorded when a review-flagged task ALSO escalates\n     in-loop (otherwise the reason would be lost on this entry and mis-stamped on the higher rung).\n  3. `task-set-meta <task-id> <meta-json-file>` with the payload\n     `{\"model\": \"<new tier>\", \"escalation_reason\": null, \"escalated_from\": null}` — one call, one\n     payload file, three keys. The `model` key writes `state.tasks[i].model` directly in one locked\n     write, so there is no separate mirroring step. Run it BEFORE the dispatch below, so the\n     **Per-task model dispatch** rule picks up the escalated tier for Ivan and every downstream\n     read this task (step 5.6, step 5.7's tier gate). The two `null` values\n     **clear any `escalation_reason`/`escalated_from` from `state.tasks[i]` here** (`task-set-meta`\n     deletes a key whose value is JSON `null`) — point 2 already copied a\n     review-flag reason onto the lower-rung entry, and the higher in-loop rung records its OWN\n     `escalation_reason:\"gate_failure\"` at point 5. Leaving the sticky `review_flag` in `state.tasks[i]`\n     (which `task-set-meta` merges, not replaces) would make step 6's task-entry→attempt-entry copy mis-stamp\n     `review_flag` onto this `gate_failure` rung.\n  4. Dispatch ONE rung up (per `model-ladder.md` § Capability ladders — qwen -> sonnet skipping\n     haiku, haiku -> sonnet -> opus) with a FAILURE SUMMARY: failing test names, the last\n     gate-output excerpt, the diagnosis verdict, and the prior implementor + tier. **Codex carve-out:**\n     after the second gate failure at the codex rung, DIAGNOSE and dispatch Claude at the task's OWN\n     tier — never a repair and never one rung above the task's tier. The capability edge is\n     `codex -> claude at the task's own tier`, so Claude-at-tier is the rung above codex.\n  5. Stamp the HIGHER rung's NEW attempt entry: `escalation_reason:\"gate_failure\"`,\n     `escalated_from:<prev tier>`.\n  6. At the new rung the budget resets (initial + one feedback retry, per `model-ladder.md` §\n     Per-rung budgets), then this same gate-failure flow re-applies if it fails again.\n  Opus-rung exhaustion (2 failures at opus) flows into the existing abort/stall machinery (PRD\n  00017) — do not invent a new halt class.\n  A `fable` attempt has **no rung above it**: its gate failure goes straight to that same\n  exhaustion path, never to an escalation (`model-ladder.md` § Capability ladders).\n```\n\n**Attribution row ownership** (one entry per rung/dispatch-group — never lump every field onto a single entry; see `references/attempt-logging.md` § Attribution row ownership):\n\n| Field | Row it is stamped on |\n|-------|----------------------|\n| `diagnosis` | the **diagnosed** (lower) rung's entry |\n| `qwen_gate_failed` | the qwen (lower) rung's entry |\n| `repair_used` | the entry of the same-tier attempt that ran after a repair (that rung's entry) |\n| `escalation_reason:\"gate_failure\"` | the rung escalated **INTO** (higher)'s entry |\n| `escalation_reason:\"review_flag\"` | the review-flagged rework rung's OWN entry (Phase 6 escalated INTO it): copied from `state.tasks[i]` at step 6 if that rung exits there, or at ESCALATE point 2 (then cleared at point 3) if it escalates in-loop |\n| `escalated_from` | the rung escalated **INTO** (higher)'s entry (both `gate_failure` and `review_flag` paths) |\n\nFor codex attribution, `attempts[].model` records the task's own tier (for example, `\"sonnet\"`) while `implementor: \"codex\"` carries the backend identity. This is the same split as qwen, whose attempt records `model: \"sonnet\"` with `implementor: \"qwen\"`. On a codex capability failure, stamp the codex entry `outcome: \"escalated\"` and `diagnosis: <verdict>`; the Claude entry it escalates into receives `escalation_reason: \"gate_failure\"` and `escalated_from: \"codex\"`.\n\n**Pipeline stamping on escalation.** An in-loop escalation re-dispatches the implementor at the higher rung and re-runs the tier-appropriate post-implementor gates (step 5.7 reviewer for sonnet+, and this step-5.5 gate) — it does NOT re-run Devon (2.9; the tests are already committed). Stamp the escalated-into entry `pipeline:\"lean\"` (implementor + reviewer), never `\"full\"` — `\"full\"` stays reserved for a from-scratch opus task/rework that actually ran Devon.\n\n**qwen capability breaker counter (this gate).** Guarded by `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"`, same as the routing consult in step 3. On an `implementor:\"qwen\"` attempt only: gate pass → reset `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive = 0`; gate fail → stamp that attempt `qwen_gate_failed:true` and increment `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive`; at 2 consecutive → latch `qwen_breaker = {tripped:true, after_task:<this task id>, failed_tasks:[<the two ids>], batch_id:<effective batch id>}` (batch-scope check as in step 3). Keys off the stored `qwen_gate_failed` field, not `outcome` (an escalated-away qwen entry reads `outcome:\"escalated\"`), keeping the increment jq-expressible. Rework attempts never touch the breaker — rework never routes qwen. A non-qwen task between two qwen failures leaves the counter unchanged (`run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive`).\n\n**Deterministic precedence — two separately-scoped orderings** (`model-ladder.md` § Ordering; NOT one linear chain):\n- **Routing-time** (step 3, per task): qwen breaker consult → memory-pressure gate → qwen infra preflight → dispatch.\n- **Failure-classification** (here, or on a lost result per step 4.2): an infra failure (preflight fail, watchdog/lost result) falls back at the SAME tier and never enters diagnosis or touches the breaker; a capability failure (a real test-gate failure, this section) enters diagnosis, where repair precedes escalate.\n\n## Qwen output rejection\n\nBefore step 5 or any fallback, the output guard can reject a Qwen attempt with\n`qwen_no_edit` (exit-zero with no task-owned implementation diff; foreign dirt does not count)\nor `qwen_test_mutation` (any Tess-owned index/worktree difference from this\ntask's `<test_commit_sha>`). Mutation wins when both apply. Do not stage,\ncommit, accept Qwen's report, or run the altered tests as an oracle.\n\nUse the existing one-shot `qwen -> sonnet` capability edge, never a Qwen retry\nor a Codex interception. Record the rejected Qwen entry with its guard cause,\n`outcome: \"escalated\"`, `qwen_gate_failed: true`, and the diagnosis from the\nexisting DIAGNOSE flow (Qwen never repairs). Update the breaker exactly once\nas a capability failure under the default mode; preserve the healthy preflight\ncache. Under `legacy`, retain the guard, cause and separate escalation rows,\nbut leave diagnosis and the breaker disabled. Neither failure consumes a\nSonnet retry slot.\n\n**Restore the oracle before Sonnet.** The attempt has no step-5 implementation\ncommit, so uncommitted output normally fails the existing ESCALATE reset guard;\nuse its fix-forward path and leave foreign files/commits untouched. For a test\nmutation, first confirm the Qwen helper has exited and that the captured test\npaths were exclusively task-\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_159","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; x=Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/SKILL.md\\\").read_text(); a=x.index(\\\"### Session handoff procedure\\\") if \\\"### Session handoff procedure\\\" in x else x.index(\\\"## Session handoff procedure\\\"); print(x[a:a+6500])'\"","aggregated_output":"### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)\n\nEvery session handoff is the same three steps:\n\n1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). It reads the current phase from `state.json`, looks the pair up in `cli/transitions.py`, and commits the next phase together with every field effect that transition mandates — in ONE transaction. There is no `--phase` flag and no per-effect flag: a caller cannot supply a mismatched phase, and cannot forget an effect.\n2. **Write the session brief, then the `leave` handoff row, then record the store, then print the site's banner** (shown at the invoking site in the gate file). The brief comes first, after the contract card (§ Contract card): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> write-brief docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` renders `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` from the state step 1 committed (where the batch stands, the card verbatim, the files the next gate needs), so the next session orients from one page (PRD 00201); the loop's launch prompt names it whenever it exists. A failed write is one stderr line, never a phase failure: carry on to the row. The row is `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site <build|review|done> --edge leave --phase <state.phase> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry); `state.phase` already names the next session's phase because step 1 committed it. A new site row in the table below gets its row from this step, not from a per-site sentence. Under `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` the row is also the session's point of no return: `hooks/note_session_leave.py` records it, and `hooks/guard_skill_after_leave.py` denies any `autopilot:*` (or `git-ferry:catchup`) `Skill` call this session makes afterwards, so a session that prints its banner and then re-invokes a gate is stopped by the harness, not only by this prose (PRD 00211). After the row, and as the LAST write before STOP, record the store with `autopilot record-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py record-store --state <state.json> --site <build|review|done> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort like the row (a failure is one stderr line, never a reason to skip the row or the STOP). It runs at every site in the table below and comes after the row, never between the brief and the row: the row itself appends to the tracked `dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, so only a commit that follows it sweeps that append in.\n3. **End the turn.** In loop mode the loop driver reads `state.json` and relaunches per its decision table above; outside the loop the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` and the same resume logic applies. Do NOT continue into the next gate's phases in this session, even if context budget appears sufficient.\n\n| site | `--outcome` | what the transition commits |\n|------|-------------|-----------------------------|\n| **build → review** (`phase-build.md`, after Phase 3) | `tasks_done` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`. `phases_completed` unchanged — the build gate leaves no membership marker. `state.tasks` is already current — every producer (`task-add`/`task-start`/`task-done`/`task-set-meta`) writes it directly via `statectl`, so there is nothing to query or snapshot at this handoff. |\n| **review → review** (`phase-review.md` Phase 6, after rework when the loop continues) | `rework` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`, `cycle` incremented, `rework_task_ids` cleared — all in one commit. `state.tasks` untouched. `phases_completed` unchanged — only convergence adds `\"review\"`. |\n| **review → done** (`phase-review.md`, on loop convergence) | `converged` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"done\"`, and `\"review\"` appended to `phases_completed` — the convergence marker the review gate's loop-level skip reads. It lands *because this is convergence*, not because a flag asked for it. |\n| **build → done** (`references/lane-solo.md` § Close, a lane-routed PRD whose one review pass wrote its review file) | `lane_reviewed` | Convergence's own effect set: `phase`/`next_phase: \"done\"` and `\"review\"` appended once to `phases_completed`, so `review_coverage_hook.py` gates the lane's `-review-1.md` with `--require-codex-guard` exactly as a full-lane cycle's. An escalating solo build takes the **build → review** row instead. |\n| **PRD → PRD** (`phase-done.md`, step 10 more-PRDs branch) | `more_prds` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"build\"`, `phases_completed` reset to `[]`, and the whole per-PRD reset (`cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` — the one authoritative list); `batch` preserved in full. |\n| **batch end** (`phase-done.md`, no more PRDs) | `drained` | `phase: \"done\"` and the EMPTY `next_phase` the loop reads as drained. Not a handoff — nothing relaunches. Also legal from `build`, which is where Phase 0's \"No PRDs anywhere\" reaches it. |\n\nWriting any of these fields by hand with `statectl set` is a bug: it is how a mandatory effect gets dropped. The `cycle` increment is the one that has already cost a real batch — the Phase 5 cap gate reads it, and losing it once let a loop run past its cap.\n\n### Contract card (compaction re-anchor)\n\nWithin-session compaction can drop this skill's text mid-procedure, after which the session drifts off-contract with nothing to re-anchor it. To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:\n\n- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:\n  ```bash\n  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md\n  ```\n  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind right now> | next: <the next gate + its precondition>`. **Never pass the card as an inline shell argument** — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline `set contract_card '<string>'` form failed three consecutive times on quoting in a real build session (2026-08-02, engram session 6).\n- **Interactive (no state.json):** the file write above is the whole step; skip the statectl call.\n\nThe session brief (`write-brief`, § Session handoff procedure step 2) is rendered right after this call so \n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

A declared capability is one the adapter implements, so the contract and the bundles are identical on every machine; auth presence appears only in per-run probe evidence, never in a committed artifact. Claude declares identity, delegation, isolation and interception; Codex declares isolation only; Gemini declares none, because neither host implements native session identity or in-session delegation yet. Capability status is a static observation (binary on PATH plus auth presence), never a live invocation. No host execution or certification is claimed.\n- Add stdlib-only, read-only dirty-tree checks and verify log-sink refusal with a descriptor-pinned sink opener, keeping the pinned semantics.\n- Add the advisory local AP00012 review evidence checker that validates policy invariants, closed wire shapes, and every semantic defect against an independent expected context, without certifying host execution.\n- Add stdlib-only session helpers that read consolidated review findings, strip finding-line leads, and group findings into rework tasks with the pinned semantics.\n- **autopilot**: add packaged review staging helper (review_stage)\n- Add a stdlib-only review-close helper that prepares task and decision proposals from validated review evidence.\n- Add stdlib-only cap-check and custody proposal helpers.\n- Add a stateless optional catchup probe for gh and engram.\n- Add a bounded verification runner and artifact reuse check.\n- Add versioned local facade operations for review staging, grouping, evidence checks, close proposals, catchup probes and verification, with a controller-required refusal.\n- Add helper provenance (`helper_dispositions`) to the source map, which keeps controller-owned functions controller-only and reassigns no regression owner, plus a README section on the local helper operations and their limits.\n- Add the bounded public controller CLI with private workflow bootstrap, authenticated exact replay, read-only snapshots, installed contract metadata, and durable matching-request credential-intent recovery.\n- Add read-only explicit project-root resolution with descriptor-based private path and fixed artifact alias checks.\n- Add the locked, atomic controller state store with fsynced state/backup publication, exact failure repair, revision checks, artifact alias guards, directory binding, and security-identical offline restore.\n\n- Add the versioned controller state schema with bounded JSON decoding and isolated state creation and validation.\n- Add read-only local PRD prerequisite diagnostics based on completed PRD filenames.\n- Add the local contract-capabilities and canonical policy-export facade, with packaged-policy digest and integer-domain checks and a delegating maintainer exporter.\n- Add the explicit pinned-source provenance audit for source files, asset sections, behavior anchors, and regression identities and digests.\n- Add 55 self-contained golden review evidence fixtures and alternate policy binding, covering complete lane rosters, fallback and retry histories, stale bindings, input isolation, attribution, artifacts, and rubric verdicts. No host execution or certification is claimed.\n- Add the draft 2020-12 review evidence schema and expected-context definition, with closed wire shapes and conditional validation. No host execution or certification is claimed.\n- Add gated review policy foundation data with pinned source bindings and test-only dependencies. No host execution or certification is claimed.\n- Add the gated package README with preserved historical source sections, current local facade usage, delivery receipts, and a dedicated Python 3.12 integration CI job. No host execution or certification is claimed.\n\n### Fixed\n\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` accepts a relative `--project-root` again and judges it exactly as its absolute spelling, instead of refusing every output path it resolves with `unsafe-artifact-path`.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` proves both its log sink and its result-artifact sink openable before it spawns the child and judges each sink by the file it actually opened; when the spawn fails, an existing log and result artifact stay byte-identical and a log this run created is removed; it reports a sink open, write or close failure as its own controlled error with the child killed, stops the child's leftover processes when a sink fails late, and removes only a leaf it created; `--export-policy --out` refuses a reader-less FIFO instead of hanging and refuses up front where `O_NOFOLLOW` is missing; the log sink judges containment before it reads a Git pointer.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` removes only the result artifact that its own failed run created; a file that took the artifact's name during the run, a leaf that became a directory, or a parent that became a symlink is left untouched and never replaces the run's own reported failure.\n- **autopilot**: after a failed result-artifact write or close, `--verify` empties (or makes unparseable) the written file wherever it was moved, and reports in its reason when even that fails. A write that failed before it began leaves an existing artifact's earlier record in place.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` and the log-sink check judge an output path by its components after the leading spelling of the project root: any symlink below the root (including one that leaves the project and returns, or one to the root itself) or a `..` component below the root is refused with `unsafe-artifact-path`, whichever way the root is spelled; a symlinked ancestor of the root stays allowed.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` and the log-sink check no longer read a nested repository's Git pointer.\n- **autopilot**: review staging refuses a destination whose Git check cannot answer, refuses a reviewer whose grant omits the PRD instead of inlining an empty one, and fills the shared context file with granted input kinds only.\n- **autopilot**: review staging accepts a clean destination outside any repository under a non-English Git locale, writes no context content when no reviewer reads the shared context, and reports a missing PRD grant in the standard refusal shape.\n- **autopilot**: session helpers refuse hardlinked policy outputs, case aliases of verification inputs and worktree Git pointers, and external Git metadata staging roots; failed process starts preserve outputs and return a controlled report.\n- **autopilot**: staged context obeys every input-kind grant, tail sweeps accept selected finding subsets while preserving attribution checks, and attempt validation uses memory bounded by the submitted history.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` log-sink validation opens no file it refuses by location and refuses a path under a not-yet-created directory of a nested repository; review-close refuses a row whose issue differs from the review table and rejects malformed carry snapshot tasks.\n- **autopilot**: review staging given a subdirectory as `project_root` writes its artifacts under the repo root, not a stray `docs/dev/tmp/` tree in that subdirectory.\n- **autopilot**: malformed `--group-findings`, `--prepare-close` and `--stage-review` request values exit 2 as usage errors instead of crashing.\n- **autopilot**: review staging and `--export-policy` refuse live workflow state in any spelling case, and staging applies the tracked-file, live-state and symlink checks to artifact roots outside the project.\n- **autopilot**: a staged reviewer prompt omits the diff, pack and history its manifest does not list.\n- **autopilot**: a staged reviewer prompt reaches pack findings and settled history only through a per-job context file that its manifest allows.\n- **autopilot**: `--verify` refuses a log or artifact path that is an argv input file, and a modified store file named by a tracked product symlink makes the artifact non-reusable.\n- **autopilot**: review staging refuses a destination with its standard controlled refusal, instead of a traceback, when the git-dir check times out or git cannot start.\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_293","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/work/references/self-deslop-prompt.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"# Self-Deslop Prompt Template\n\nThis is the prompt template dispatched by `/autopilot:work` step 5.6 — the per-task\nself-deslop pass that runs between test-pass verification (step 5.5) and the\nper-task code review (step 5.7).\n\n`/autopilot:work` step 5.6 substitutes the placeholders below before dispatching the\nsubagent. **`{{slop_catalog}}` is filled in at dispatch time** by reading the\ncurrent `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/prompts/de-sloppify.md`, extracting the\n`## What to remove` section verbatim, and inlining it here. The subagent\nreceives one self-contained prompt with no extra filesystem reads required.\nThis keeps `prompts/de-sloppify.md` as the single source of truth for slop\npatterns: when it evolves, the next step-5.6 dispatch picks up the new catalog\nwith no edit to this template.\n\nPlaceholders:\n\n- `{{task_subject}}` — `tasks[i].name`, read directly from `state.tasks` (no\n  native tool field).\n- `{{task_description}}` — `tasks[i].description` (full text), read directly\n  from `state.tasks`; falls back to a name-only body when absent, and an\n  empty-string `description` counts as absent.\n- `{{task_acceptance_criteria}}` — a text-extraction of the `Acceptance\n  criteria:` section from `tasks[i].description` (there is no native\n  `acceptance_criteria` field), or the literal string `(none recorded)` when\n  absent.\n- `{{test_files}}` — comma-separated paths of the test files Tess wrote in\n  step 2.7 and the implementor just made pass in step 5.5.\n- `{{diff_files}}` — comma-separated paths of files touched in the implementor's\n  most recent commit (`git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r HEAD`).\n- `{{slop_catalog}}` — verbatim contents of `## What to remove` from\n  `prompts/de-sloppify.md`.\n\n---\n\n## Prompt Template\n\n```\nA diff has been written to satisfy this task. The implementation passed its\ntests. Your job: prune slop from the diff while keeping every test green.\nThis is best-effort cleanup, not a correctness rework — do not change\nbehavior, do not modify tests, do not refactor.\n\nTask: {{task_subject}}\n\nDescription:\n{{task_description}}\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n{{task_acceptance_criteria}}\n\nTests that the diff made pass (do NOT modify):\n{{test_files}}\n\nFiles in the diff:\n{{diff_files}}\n\nProcedure:\n\n1. Read the diff for each file in scope (`git diff HEAD~1..HEAD <file>` or\n   equivalent in your environment).\n2. For each line, block, helper, comment or docstring added in the\n   diff, ask:\n     \"Does this trace to a failing test, an acceptance criterion, or\n     existing-behavior preservation?\"\n   If the answer is no, mark the construct for removal.\n3. Apply removals one at a time. After each individual removal, re-run the\n   tests listed above (the narrow set Tess wrote). If any test fails,\n   restore that single removal and move on to the next candidate. Never\n   delete the test that fails — the test is authoritative.\n4. If no removal survived its test re-run, exit WITHOUT committing. Return\n   the literal string \"no slop found\" so the caller can record a noop.\n5. If at least one removal survived, commit with message:\n     chore: prune slop from {{task_subject}}\n   No CHANGELOG entry. No HEREDOC. No Co-Authored-By trailer. One commit\n   only — do not split into multiple cleanup commits.\n\nRules:\n\n- **Do not modify tests.** If a test reads as weak, that is the per-task\n  reviewer's call (step 5.7), not yours. Leave it. Dead bindings a split left\n  behind in a test file are not yours either: `check_split_hygiene.py` answers\n  that mechanically at the task boundary (step 5.65), with `ast` rather than\n  judgment, so you never have to guess which test binding is safe to drop.\n- **Do not change behavior.** Tests prove behavior; if you cannot satisfy\n  the tests, the deletion is wrong. Restore.\n- **Do not refactor.** This pass deletes; it does not move code around,\n  rename symbols, or extract helpers. If a slop pattern would only resolve\n  through restructuring, note it in the return message instead of acting.\n- **Do not touch files outside the diff.** The cleanup is scoped to what\n  the implementor just produced. Adjacent slop in untouched files is out\n  of scope here — the post-session codex pass catches it separately.\n\nSlop patterns to look for (catalog inlined from `prompts/de-sloppify.md`):\n\n{{slop_catalog}}\n\nReturn one of:\n  - \"no slop found\" — exited without commit, nothing to clean.\n  - \"committed {sha}\" — committed `chore: prune slop from ...` at {sha},\n    test suite green.\n  - \"errored: {short reason}\" — dispatch problem; do not commit, just\n    explain so the caller can record the failure.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Test-only diffs\n\nSKILL.md step 5.6 applies `test_only_diff` (from\n`skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py`) to\n`git diff --name-only <task_base_sha>..HEAD` **before** the 30-line/2-file rule.\nWhen every changed path is test or fixture code, there is no dispatch: record\n`self_deslop: \"skipped:test-only\"` and proceed to step 5.65. The stamp is\ndistinct from `\"skipped:trivial\"` so the two skips stay tellable apart in the\nattempt data.\n\nThis skip applies in rework mode too, unlike step 5.7's — de-slopping a test\ndiff has nothing to close on, and the prompt below forbids touching tests\nanyway. One production path anywhere in the diff runs the procedure below.\n\n## Procedure\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 5.6 (PRD 00119-v2). The skip rule, the\ndescription-fallback rule and the outcome-logging rule stayed in the body; this\nis everything the caller needs once the skip rule did NOT fire.\n\n**Dispatch contract.** Otherwise, dispatch a **fresh** Agent call (NOT the implementor's session — fresh context breaks the \"I built this\" attachment; why: `references/design-rationale.md` § fresh dispatch) at `state.tasks[i].model`. Same tier as the implementor keeps cost proportional. The dispatch must satisfy the **Subagent Dispatch Budget** and the **Subagent Watchdog**.\n\n**Prompt construction.** Build the subagent prompt from `references/self-deslop-prompt.md` by substituting:\n\n- `{{task_subject}}` from `tasks[i].name`, `{{task_description}}` from `tasks[i].description` (full text, falling back to the name-only body when `description` is absent or an empty string), and `{{task_acceptance_criteria}}` from a **text-extraction** of the `Acceptance criteria:` section of that same `tasks[i].description` (falling back to the literal string `(none recorded)` when absent) — all read directly from the current task's `state.tasks` entry, already in hand from step 1's pending scan. The criteria are parsed out of the stored body; there is no `acceptance_criteria` field to read.\n- `{{test_files}}` from the tests Tess wrote in step 2.7 (the same set step 5.5 just ran).\n- `{{diff_files}}` from `git diff-tree --no-commit-id --name-only -r HEAD`.\n- `{{slop_catalog}}` from the `## What to remove` section of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/prompts/de-sloppify.md` — read the file at dispatch time and inline the section verbatim. This keeps the deslop prompt as the single source of truth for slop patterns; when it grows entries, the next step-5.6 dispatch picks them up without a code change here.\n\n| Subagent outcome | `self_deslop` value | Steps 5.65 and 5.7 then see |\n|------------------|---------------------|------------------------|\n| Committed `chore: prune slop from ...` | `\"committed:{sha}\"` (full SHA from the new commit) | the pruned diff (HEAD now includes the cleanup commit) |\n| Returned \"no slop found\", no commit | `\"noop\"` | the original implementor diff |\n| Watchdog timeout (`TaskStop` fired) | `\"timeout\"` | the original implementor diff |\n| Dispatch failed or subagent errored | `\"errored:{short_cause}\"` (e.g. `errored:dispatch_failed`, `errored:prompt_overrun`) | the original implementor diff |\n| Skip rule fired | `\"skipped:trivial\"` (no dispatch occurred) | the original implementor diff |\n\nIn every non-committed outcome, the implementor's original commit stands and is what step 5.65 measures and step 5.7 reviews.\n\n---\n\n## Dispatch contract reminders\n\nThe `/autopilot:work` step 5.6 caller, NOT the subagent, is responsible for:\n\n- The 30-net-lines / 2-files skip rule. The subagent only sees prompts for\n  non-trivial diffs.\n- The fresh-Agent-dispatch requirement (not the implementor's session).\n- The 15-minute watchdog and `TaskStop` on timeout.\n- Carrying the outcome into step 6's `task-done` payload as the attempt\n  record's `self_deslop` field (never a separate indexed state write).\n\nSee `SKILL.md` step 5.6 for the full contract.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

If it succeeds, the tests are too weak. Unlike a thought exercise, Devon must actually write the code and run the tests to prove its exploit works.\n\n## Procedure\n\nDispatch Devon to try to write a **wrong** implementation that passes all of Tess's tests. Devon's goal is to exploit weak tests.\n\n**Devon runs as:** Claude Code subagent (Agent tool) — it needs file write access and the project's test runner to execute its wrong implementation against the tests. **Devon receives only:** the test files from Tess, public interfaces/types (so its wrong implementation compiles), and test-runner access. No task description, no acceptance criteria, no architecture docs.\n\n**Devon's job:** Write an implementation that is clearly wrong (hardcoded values, ignored edge cases, shortcut if/else chains), run the tests against it, and report which tests it broke through.\n\n**Outcomes:**\n\n| Devon result | Action |\n|----------------|--------|\n| Cannot break tests (tests catch all exploits) | Tests are strong. Proceed to 2.95 (the tests were committed at step 2.85, before Devon ran). |\n| Breaks tests with wrong impl that passes | Send Devon's exploit back to Tess as a numbered weak-point list (see Feedback to Tess below). Commit the strengthened tests as `test(<scope>): strengthen <feature>` (this commit is now `<test_commit_sha>`), record `devon: exploit_fixed` and `devon_exploit: <Devon's one-line weak-point summary>`, `devon_weak_points: <count of Devon's list>` and `devon_in_contract: [<each \"N. in-contract: ...\" line Tess returned>]` in the task's attempt entry, proceed to 2.95. A weak point Tess neither strengthened nor marked in-contract goes back to Tess in the same strengthen dispatch's one correction retry; the orchestrator never dismisses one itself (V33). |\n\n## Prompt Template\n\n```\nYou are an adversarial test validator. Your job is to BREAK these tests by writing a wrong implementation that passes all of them.\n\nTest files:\n{test file contents}\n\nPublic interfaces/types (so your implementation compiles):\n{type definitions, function signatures, module exports}\n\nTest runner command: {the command that runs ONLY this task's test files, e.g. uv run --no-project --with pytest python -m pytest -q --tb=line <the task's test files>; never a whole test directory}\n\nYour goal:\nWrite an implementation that makes ALL tests pass but is clearly WRONG. Strategies:\n- Return hardcoded values that happen to match test expectations\n- Ignore parameters and return constants\n- Handle only the exact cases the tests check, fail on everything else\n- Use if/else chains that match test inputs specifically\n- Skip validation that tests don't verify\n\nProcess:\n1. Read the tests carefully\n2. Write a deliberately wrong implementation\n3. Run the test runner command above against your wrong implementation\n4. If tests pass: you broke them. Keep going: show every other weak point you can prove the same way, up to 8 in total, before reporting.\n5. If tests fail: try a different exploit. After 3 failed attempts, report \"Tests are robust.\"\n\nRules:\n1. You MUST run the tests to verify your exploit actually works - no guessing\n2. Your implementation MUST be obviously wrong (not just suboptimal)\n3. Do NOT modify test files\n4. For each exploit, explain which test is too weak and what assertion would prevent it\n5. Clean up your wrong implementation before returning. Do NOT use `rm` — it is denied to subagents and will fail. Instead, use the Write tool to OVERWRITE every file you created with a single placeholder line (`# adversarial placeholder - overwritten by implementor`). The Write tool always works. Never ask for permission to delete; just overwrite and report the path.\n6. Run only the test runner command above, once per exploit; never a whole test directory.\n\nOutput format:\n- If you CAN break the tests: show the wrong implementation and the passing test output, then a numbered `Weak points:` list, one line each: `N. <test name> - <what a wrong implementation gets away with> - <assertion that would prevent it>`\n- If you CANNOT break the tests: say \"Tests are robust\" and explain why each shortcut you tried was caught\n\nYou receive NOTHING about what the code should actually do. You only see tests and types.\n```\n\n## Context Selection\n\n| Include | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Test file contents | The thing Devon is trying to break |\n| Public types/interfaces | So wrong implementation compiles |\n| Test runner command (the task's test files only) | So Devon can verify exploits without a full-suite run per attempt |\n\n| Exclude | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Task description | Devon shouldn't know what \"correct\" looks like |\n| Acceptance criteria | Same - would leak the spec |\n| Architecture docs | Not needed for adversarial validation |\n\n## Feedback to Tess (when Devon succeeds)\n\nWhen Devon finds an exploit, send this back to Tess:\n\n```\nYour tests can be passed by a wrong implementation:\n\n{Devon's wrong implementation}\n\nTest output (all passing):\n{Devon's test run output}\n\nWeak points:\n{Devon's numbered weak-point list, verbatim}\n\nAddress every numbered weak point. Answer each in your reply as\n`N. strengthened: <test name>` or `N. in-contract: <why the behavior is allowed>`.\nDo not change tests that Devon could NOT break.\n\nRun only the test files this task names (the tests you wrote, or the\nfailing tests in your prompt), with `-q --tb=line`. Never run a whole test\ndirectory or `dev/bin/release-checks`: the orchestrator runs the full suite\nonce, after every task. SKILL.md keeps the trigger rule and the\nno-pending-tasks skip; this file owns the handoff procedure.\n\nThe autopilot context-cap hook (`autopilot_context_cap_hook.py`) writes a `.handoff-requested` marker into the autopilot dir when the headroom rule fires (PRD 00200) — below the **hard** cap that triggers the rotation. Handing off at a task boundary, where every task through step 6 is committed and `state.tasks` is synced, is lossless: the next session re-enters the phase it left and resumes with the remaining pending tasks. This keeps a multi-task phase from ballooning into the hard cap.\n\n## Marker format\n\n`.handoff-requested` is JSON with four required fields: `phase`, `session`, `at`, `task_id` — the phase the writer was in when it wrote the marker, the writing session's id, an ISO-8601 timestamp, and the in-flight task id. `/work` compares the marker's own `phase` against the session's current phase (`state.phase` in `state.json`) instead of assuming every handoff is a build handoff.\n\nFor back-compat, a legacy marker (plain text, not JSON) is also accepted. A non-empty legacy marker (a bare task id) is treated as a build request, matching the original behavior. An empty legacy marker is treated as the session's current phase — this is the format the context-cap hook wrote before this fix, not hardcoded to build. Worked example — the case this fix exists for: a legacy empty marker present while the session is in the review phase keeps review as the handoff target, never build.\n\n## Procedure\n\n1. **If no pending tasks remain**, skip this step — proceed to step 7. Final verification runs in whichever session finishes the last task.\n2. Resolve the autopilot dir and check for the marker:\n   ```bash\n   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/_walk_up.py --bash\n   ```\n   It prints the absolute autopilot dir. Read `<dir>/.handoff-requested`. **If it is absent**, return to step 1 for the next task — no handoff.\n3. **If `.handoff-requested` is present:**\n   a. Read `<dir>/state.json` for the session's current phase (`state.phase`). **If `state.json` cannot be read**, there is nothing to compare the marker's phase against: do not hand off, do not invent or assume a phase, and do not remove the markers — leave both in place and return to step 1; re-check at the next task boundary.\n   b. Resolve the marker's own phase:\n      - Valid JSON — an object whose four fields `phase`, `session`, `at` and `task_id` are each a string, with a non-empty `task_id` → the marker's phase is its `phase` field.\n      - Legacy, non-empty (a bare task id, not JSON) → the marker's phase is `\"build\"`.\n      - Legacy, empty (no content) → the marker's phase is the session's current phase (`state.phase`).\n      - JSON-looking but invalid — fails to parse, parses to a non-object, is missing a field, has a field whose value is a non-string (a non-string field value is malformed), or has an empty `task_id` — is **malformed**, a different failure than a clean phase mismatch: print `autopilot: malformed handoff marker (invalid JSON or missing field) — treating as absent` to stderr, remove both `<dir>/.handoff-requested` and `<dir>/.cap-fired`, and continue exactly as if no marker had been present (return to step 1, no handoff).\n   c. **If the marker's phase does not match `state.phase`**, it is stale: print `autopilot: stale handoff marker from phase {marker phase} removed` to stderr. Remove both `<dir>/.handoff-requested` and `<dir>/.cap-fired`, then continue exactly as if no marker had been present (return to step 1 for the next task, no handoff).\n   d. **Otherwise the marker's phase matches `state.phase`** — hand off within that phase:\n      e. Confirm the working tree is clean: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py dirty --state <dir>/state.json` comes back empty. Every task through step 6 commits its tests (step 2.85) and implementation (step 5), so it should be. `autopilot dirty` excludes the store, which matters here: durable store artifacts written mid-phase (ledger `.jsonl` appends, review files) are real uncommitted tracked paths once the store is tracked, so a raw whole-tree check would block the handoff with nothing actually wrong. If it is NOT clean, do not hand off — investigate and commit or resolve the uncommitted work first.\n      f. Remove both `<dir>/.handoff-requested` and `<dir>/.cap-fired`, inlining the absolute paths from step 2 (no shell variable, so the permission matcher resolves the command). The fresh session re-evaluates its budget from a clean slate.\n      g. Print the handoff banner:\n         ```\n         ── WORK ── handoff at task boundary ────────────────────────────\n         ── {completed} tasks done, {pending} pending — headroom rule fired\n         ── fresh session resumes the remaining tasks ───────────────────\n         ```\n      h. **Write the contract card** (run-autopilot § Contract card): the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate, so a session compacted after this boundary re-anchors instead of drifting. Write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then (autopilot only) load it with `statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md`. Never pass the card as an inline shell argument — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline form failed three times in a row on quoting in a real build session. Interactive runs stop after the file write. Then write the session brief — `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> write-brief docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` — so the next session orients from one page (PRD 00201). Then set `state.next_phase` to the marker's (matching) phase. Then write the `leave` handoff row — `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site <marker phase> --edge leave --phase <marker phase> --prd <state.prd>` — best-effort, never a reason not to hand off (`references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry); it is the last write before the stop that touches state, so the next session's `state_after_leave` check (PRD 00199) never reads this session's own `next_phase` write as peer evidence. After the row, and as the LAST write before STOP, record the store with `autopilot record-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py record-store --state <state.json> --site <marker phase> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort like the row (a failure is one stderr line, never a reason to skip the STOP); it writes no state, and it comes after the row because the row itself appends to the tracked `dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, so only a commit that follows it sweeps that append in, then STOP — end the turn. In loop mode the wrapper reads the non-empty `next_phase` and relaunches a fresh session in that phase (the headless hand-off contract in `run-autopilot/SKILL.md` § Session Loop); the model writes no signal.\n\n      **Do NOT return to step 1, and do NOT run step 7.** `phases_completed` stays without the current phase (this session did not finish it), so `/autopilot:run-autopilot` re-enters that phase and resumes with the remaining pending work. null\n}\n```\n\n**Timing is deliberately not an attempt field.** No timestamp, duration or prompt size is stamped here: an attempt spans several dispatches — Tess, Ivan, Pat and their retries — so one pair of stamps could not say which of them took the hour. Those live in the dispatch ledger, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (a start row and one or more end rows per dispatch, joined on `id`, plus one row per session-handoff edge; `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), and a task's runtime is read from its rows there, keyed on `task`.\n\n**Cardinality (PRD 00065)**: today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today.\n\n**Field semantics**:\n\n- `attempt`: 1-indexed; `len(existing) + 1`.\n- `model`: the tier `/autopilot:work` used for this pass. Read from `state.tasks[i].model` when set. On legacy plans where `state.tasks[i].model` is absent, record the effective session-inherited tier as a string (e.g. `\"sonnet\"` for a Work-phase Sonnet 4.6 launch). Always a string — never `null`.\n- `outcome`: `/autopilot:work` writes `\"completed\"`, `\"aborted\"`, or `\"escalated\"`. The `\"escalated\"` value (PRD 00065) is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:\"qwen\"`). Debug on error\n\nIf the tool returned an error, invoke the `debug-stuck-agent` skill to diagnose the root cause before reporting to the user. If debugging resolves the issue, continue to step 5. If not, report to user and keep task in_progress.\n\n### 5. Commit changes\n\nStage exactly this task's files, then commit in a separate Bash call. **Never `git add -A` or `git add .`** — the worktree is live (the user edits files during dispatches), and a bulk add sweeps foreign uncommitted work into the task commit (memory: feedback_subagents_vs_live_worktree).\n\n1. Build the stage list: the paths from Ivan's `FILES_TOUCHED:` footer (see **Assumptions footer**), plus any build-generated files this task's changes legitimately produced (lockfiles, snapshots, generated bindings) — identified from `git status --porcelain` output, never guessed.\n2. Fallback when the footer is absent or `none` while the tree is dirty (legacy retry prompts, malformed report): stage the intersection of dirty paths with the exact files the plan task names; treat every other dirty path as foreign.\n3. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_reflow.py <stage list>` over that list: exit 1 → stamp `reflow: \"<path>:<hunks>\"` (`;`-joined for several) on the attempt and name the files in the phase report; exit 2 → `reflow: \"failed:<stderr>\"`; exit 0 → no field. Staging and the commit proceed unchanged in every branch — see `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Reflow tripwire.\n\n```bash\ngit add <path> [<path> ...]\n```\n```bash\ngit commit -m \"<type>(<scope>): <description>\"\n```\n\nAny other dirty path is **foreign**: leave it unstaged and untouched, and name it in the phase report (fail loud) — the same never-commit-foreign-work rule the step-5.5 ESCALATE reset guard enforces. Without the plugin, verify recovered work with\n  whatever review the host offers; nothing in this workflow hard-fails.\n\n## Scope Boundaries\n\nActivate this skill for:\n- maximum tool call / loop-limit failures, or repeated retries with no forward progress\n- context growth or prompt drift that starts degrading output quality\n- file-system or environment state mismatch between expectation and reality\n- tool failures likely recoverable with diagnosis and a smaller corrective action\n\nDo not use this skill as the primary source for:\n- feature verification after code changes; use `autopilot:review-work-completion` or `autopilot:review-blindly`\n- framework-specific debugging when a narrower skill already exists\n- runtime promises the current harness cannot enforce automatically\n\n## Four-Phase Loop\n\n### Phase 1: Failure Capture\n\nBefore trying to recover, record the failure precisely — fill every field of\nthe \"Failure Capture\" template in `references/capture-templates.md` (error,\nlast tool sequence, goal in progress, context pressure, environment\nassumptions).\n\n### Phase 2: Root-Cause Diagnosis\n\nMatch the failure to a known pattern before changing anything.\n\n| Pattern | Likely Cause | Check |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Maximum tool calls / repeated same command | loop or no-exit observer path | inspect the last N tool calls for repetition |\n| Context overflow / degraded reasoning | unbounded notes, repeated plans, oversized logs | inspect recent context for duplication and low-signal bulk |\n| `ECONNREFUSED` / timeout | service unavailable or wrong port | verify service health, URL, and port assumptions |\n| `429` / quota exhaustion | retry storm or missing backoff | count repeated calls and inspect retry spacing |\n| file missing after write / stale diff | race, wrong cwd, or branch drift | re-check path, cwd, git status, and actual file existence |\n| tests still failing after \"fix\" | wrong hypothesis | isolate the exact failing test and re-derive the bug |\n\nDiagnosis questions:\n- is this a logic failure, state failure, environment failure, or policy failure?\n- did the agent lose the real objective and start optimizing the wrong subtask?\n- is the failure deterministic or transient?\n- what is the smallest reversible action that would validate the diagnosis?\n\n### Phase 3: Contained Recovery\n\nRecover with the smallest action that changes the diagnosis surface\n(checklist: \"Recovery Action\" in `references/capture-templates.md`).\n\nSafe recovery actions:\n- stop repeated retries and restate the hypothesis\n- trim low-signal context and keep only the active goal, blockers, and evidence\n- re-check the actual filesystem / branch / process state\n- narrow the task to one failing command, one file, or one test\n- switch from speculative reasoning to direct observation\n- escalate to a human when the failure is high-risk or externally blocked\n\nDo not claim unsupported auto-healing actions like \"reset agent state\" or \"update harness config\" unless you are actually doing them through real tools in the current environment.\n\n### Phase 4: Introspection Report\n\nEnd with a report that makes the recovery legible to the next agent or human\n(template: \"Agent Self-Debug Report\" in `references/capture-templates.md`).\nNever end with \"I fixed it\" alone — the filled report is the deliverable.\n\n## Recovery Heuristics\n\nPrefer these interventions in order:\n\n1. Restate the real objective in one sentence.\n2. Verify the world state instead of trusting memory.\n3. Shrink the failing scope.\n4. Run one discriminating check.\n5. Only then retry.\n\nBad pattern: retrying the same action three times with slightly different\nwording. Good pattern: capture → classify → one direct check → change the\nplan only if the check supports it.\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `autopilot:review-work-completion` after recovery if code was changed\n- `convene-council` when the issue is decision ambiguity, not technical failure\n- `git-ferry:resolve-git-conflicts` when the failure came from conflicting local state\n- `git-ferry:catchup` if the failure came from missing project context\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+# Autocodex host contract
+
+## Interactive recovery
+
+When the operator asks you to read this file for interactive recovery, work from
+the intended repository root. If its path placeholders are still unresolved,
+run `mise exec -- python3 ~/.config/autocodex/driver.py --dry-run` there and read
+the resolved host instructions it prints. This starts no agent and changes no
+workflow state. Do this once; the resolved output needs no further dry run.
+
+Use the resolved paths and host adaptations below to read the installed
+run-autopilot skill and its referenced Resume procedure. Inspect the committed
+pause reason and review evidence, then obtain any required operator decision
+interactively. The unattended execution wording below does not authorize
+clearing a pause, raising a cap, or starting repairs by itself. Keep Codex as
+coordinator and use the model-provider review routing defined below.
+Use the existing state CLI for any authorized transition. Preserve the fresh
+work/review session boundary, then exit so the operator can run `autocodex` again.
+
+## Phase execution
+
+The user requests unattended PRD execution through autocodex, inspired by
+autoclaude, with Codex driving and Claude taking the former external Codex role.
+Project root: /Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/agent-plugins
+This fresh session's phase: build
+
+First read the global and repository AGENTS.md, then activate
+`/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/SKILL.md` by reading it and following its
+referenced procedure for the committed phase. Read the actual referenced files;
+a slash command need not be registered in this host. Resolve every
+`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` reference to `/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0`. Personal skills continue to
+resolve through `~/.agents/skills`. Read missing plugin skills from the installed
+plugin's source rather than inventing their behavior. If a required capability
+cannot be adapted, record a precise pause through the state CLI.
+
+The following are explicit host adaptations authorized by the user's role swap.
+They override Claude-specific dispatch examples in the source skills; all task,
+coverage, evidence, review and transition obligations remain in force.
+
+- Native Claude Agent/Task calls become native Codex subagent calls with isolated
+  prompts. Load the complete referenced persona and rubric into each prompt;
+  custom `autopilot:*` agent registrations are not presumed installed here.
+  No parent conversation for reviewers. Await every dispatched agent and process
+  in this session. Use the available native agent tools; never shell out to a
+  nested Codex CLI to simulate a native subagent.
+- The main session coordinates and delegates substantive work. Its model/effort
+  do not prescribe worker or reviewer settings. Always set model and reasoning
+  effort explicitly when dispatching native agents; do not inherit the parent's
+  low effort. Use isolated prompts (no parent-history fork) to apply overrides.
+- Logical worker tiers: haiku = gpt-6-luna / low; sonnet = gpt-6.1-sol / medium; opus = gpt-6.1-sol / high.
+  Use the tier selected by the task classifier and escalation policy, recording
+  the logical tier in existing schema fields and the actual provider/model in
+  dispatch evidence. These are role mappings, not identical-capability claims.
+  After a failed opus attempt with a concrete unresolved defect, failed check,
+  or documented reasoning blocker, use gpt-6-astra / high for the next bounded
+  attempt when the source escalation policy permits it. Record the trigger and
+  actual settings. Do not escalate merely because the logical tier is opus.
+  Fable remains a distinct, human-gated rescue tier, not an alias for Astra.
+- A source `/use-codex` implementation dispatch becomes a Claude dispatch through
+  the real use-sonnet skill and its wrapper. Preserve guards and permissions.
+- Before any implementation dispatch, check that its model provider has an
+  independent review route supported by this host and its driver. If the source
+  routing table selects a provider without that support (including Gemini for
+  UI work), use the native worker at the task's existing logical tier and the
+  resolved mapping above. This operator-authorized fallback overrides the source
+  "Gemini if available" rule even when its CLI is installed; no further operator
+  decision is required. Record the selected source route, missing review support
+  and effective native dispatch in the build evidence. Preserve all task gates,
+  tier/escalation rules and review lenses. Do not change permission-denial or
+  supported-reviewer failure handling. This fallback applies only before
+  dispatch: it never relabels existing implementation evidence or supplies a
+  guessed review mapping for code already contributed by an unsupported model.
+- Review routing uses the **actual implementation model's company**, never the
+  launcher name. Codex, Claude, Kiro and Copilot are launchers, not evidence of
+  model origin. This operator-authorized policy replaces the source's
+  `implementor == "codex"` / additive Eve guard and the former fixed host roster.
+  Keep all three lenses, their complete rubrics, isolation and coverage.
+
+## Model evidence and review routing
+
+Before every review cycle, inspect the current PRD's actual implementation logs:
+raw worker/session metadata and dispatched model, dispatch-ledger records, and
+per-task build evidence. Correlate task/attempt/session IDs and the work range;
+exclude planning, coordinator and read-only review models. Include test writers,
+repairs, prior contributing attempts, split tasks, model switches and fallbacks.
+Do not grep the entire transcript for model names and treat prompt examples or
+reviewer models as implementors. Prefer observed model metadata over requested
+configuration; a requested auto/tier alias does not prove the served model.
+
+Populate `tasks[].attempts[].actual_model` and `actual_provider` accurately via
+statectl from that evidence. Retain launcher identity separately. Never rewrite
+history to fit routing. Missing, ambiguous or conflicting evidence pauses for
+operator clarification; neither launcher identity nor the coordinator model is
+an acceptable fallback. Unknown model families require an explicit verified
+mapping, never a guess. Kiro/Copilot auto routing requires the resolved model in
+logs; if those logs do not expose it, pause.
+
+Write a durable audit at
+`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/<prd-stem>-implementation-models.json`:
+`{"fingerprint": <driver.implementation_fingerprint(state)>,
+"snapshot": <driver.implementation_snapshot(state)>, "evidence": [...]}`.
+Each evidence row contains `task`, `role: "implementation"`, exact `model`, a
+repo-relative `path`, 1-based `line`, and SHA-256 of that line's bytes (excluding
+its newline). Cite all observed contributing models, not just one model per task.
+Explain the correlation in a sibling Markdown audit. The fingerprint binds PRD,
+cycle, work_start_sha and implementation attempt provenance; regenerate before
+each new review. Keep the reviewed snapshot through rework: the boundary checks
+receipts against that snapshot. Convergence requires unchanged implementation
+provenance except for the source's completed Tail sweep described below.
+
+### Tail-sweep completion
+
+Follow the source Tail sweep steps, including its normal work verification and
+per-task review, then finalize without another completion review or cycle
+increment. Keep the original implementation audit and all review receipts intact.
+The host accepts only added `[D{cycle}] Tail sweep: ...` tasks when this review's
+`decision-gate` and `tail-sweep` batches are recorded, every task is completed,
+each added task has a completed final attempt, and all its attempts name the
+current `review_cycle`. Previously reviewed task provenance, PRD, cycle and work
+start must remain unchanged. Ordinary rework never qualifies for this exception.
+
+Before the finalize hand-off, write a companion audit at
+`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/<prd-stem>-tail-sweep-models.json`.
+Use the same fingerprint/snapshot/evidence format above for the **entire current
+task set**. Copy the unchanged original evidence rows and append log-backed
+evidence for every sweep implementor, including retries and model switches.
+Never replace the original audit, relabel a task, or alter old attempts to pass.
+This companion records model provenance; it does not claim the sweep received
+the earlier three-lens review. The source work pipeline remains responsible for
+sweep verification, task review, and recorded verify/sweep escapes.
+
+For an existing `host_tail_sweep_provenance` pause, retain completed sweep tasks
+and their evidence. Prepare the companion audit and check `adapter.review_gap`
+on an in-memory `phase: "done"` candidate before the normal authorized Resume
+and finalize hand-off. Do not implement the sweep again or reopen review.
+
+### Cap-regression stall boundary
+
+Keep the source cap and cap-check decision unchanged. Before the canonical
+`cap_regression` stall, record all required cap-overflow decisions through the
+state CLI, then run:
+
+    python3 /Users/bob/.config/autocodex/driver.py --cd /Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/agent-plugins review-stall-snapshot
+
+This validates every provider receipt, raw result, rubric and implementation
+audit, and preserves the current reviewed state before `stall` resets it.
+The snapshot is immutable and idempotent; a differing existing snapshot is a
+boundary failure, never permission to overwrite it. Capture the latest review
+state even when this session produced the review after launch. A launch snapshot
+alone cannot prove that review ran. This command changes no workflow state.
+
+Then run the source `autopilot stall --site cap_regression` and, on exit 0,
+`autopilot mint-stubs`, write the normal contract card, and end the session for
+its fresh build handoff. Retain the snapshot and every underlying evidence file.
+The adapter verifies the intact hold move, fresh batch deferred record, migrated
+cap-overflow decisions and canonical reset. Only canonical minted-stub additions
+and the contract card may follow that reset. Missing or changed review evidence
+still refuses the boundary. This adaptation authorizes neither a cap increase
+nor further implementation repairs. Other stall sites retain their existing
+boundary behavior.
+
+### Review dispatch
+Use actual log/evidence files, not a new restatement of the model claim.
+
+Run `python3 /Users/bob/.config/autocodex/driver.py --cd /Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/agent-plugins review-route` before dispatch. It validates audit
+freshness, evidence hashes and task coverage and returns the required providers:
+
+- OpenAI GPT implementation → Anthropic Claude Opus/xhigh for Alice, Blake, Bob.
+- Anthropic Claude implementation → OpenAI gpt-6.1-sol / high for Alice, Blake, Bob.
+- Mixed implementation → both complete three-lens rosters, independently. Each
+  roster reviews the whole change so interactions also receive review. Consolidate
+  all findings; no same-company review replaces the opposite-company coverage.
+
+Alice retains the complete consensus rubric and implementation context. Blake
+gets only the PRD and repository access: no diff, file list, plan, history,
+implementation audit or sibling findings. Bob retains the full assembled persona,
+D1-D5 doubt rubric and de-slop appendix. Every invocation is fresh and isolated.
+Carl remains optional under the source rules. Eve is not added merely because
+Codex implemented a task: the provider guard now establishes independence. An
+explicit separate Fable rescue request remains human-gated.
+
+For these review lanes only, use real external reviewer processes via the helper
+below, including GPT reviewers. This is an explicit external-review transport,
+not an attempt to simulate native subagents; it overrides native reviewer dispatch
+examples. Do not strip nesting guards or resume an implementation thread. If the
+launcher cannot run the reviewer with its guards intact, preserve evidence and
+pause. Native work delegation remains as specified above.
+
+    python3 /Users/bob/.config/autocodex/driver.py --cd /Users/bob/git/src/github.com/buvis/agent-plugins reviewer --lens alice|blake|bob -m <model> -f <assembled-prompt> -o <unique-output>
+
+Use `opus` for Anthropic and the model portion of `gpt-6.1-sol / high` for OpenAI;
+GPT effort follows AUTOCODEX_REVIEW_EFFORT (default high). Pass absolute paths and
+argument arrays (or safe shell quoting). Await every process. The helper checks
+the selected lens's full rubric and writes immutable raw evidence and a receipt.
+
+External reviewer dispatches need network access in the calling Codex command.
+When that command's sandbox restricts network access, request
+`sandbox_permissions="require_escalated"` for the exact helper or dispatch
+command, with a narrow justification. Let the host's approval review decide;
+preserve the launcher's permission settings and nesting guards. An inherited
+network restriction can report `ENOTFOUND` even while the host can reach the API.
+If a dispatch already failed inside that sandbox, retain its evidence and follow
+the host tool's required approved retry before treating it as a terminal reviewer
+failure. If approval is denied, record the denial and pause. The terminal-failure
+rule below applies after dispatch with the required network access.
+
+The helper saves immutable raw JSONL, stderr, reviewer text, and a receipt at
+`<unique-output>.receipt.json`. Include in the consolidated review top matter:
+
+    autocodex_<lens>_<provider>_receipt: <absolute receipt path>
+
+Use lens alice/blake/bob and provider anthropic/openai. Include every required
+receipt, including both providers for mixed work. Record `provider_review_guard:
+satisfied` on one line only after all required rosters succeed. The host gate
+checks each receipt, raw successful output, provider and complete rubric. Record
+`codex_rung_guard: not fired` only as the legacy compatibility field and explain
+that the model-provider guard supersedes it; never claim Eve ran.
+
+Anthropic model origin is independent of the launcher. The helper tries Kiro,
+Copilot, then native Claude by default; `AUTOCODEX_ANTHROPIC_BACKENDS` sets the
+order or excludes a known unavailable route. Kiro/Copilot use an explicit model
+of the requested tier at xhigh effort. Their raw metadata must prove both.
+Quota/auth failures and missing CLIs try the next route before waiting.
+Permission denials, incomplete evidence and other failures still stop review.
+Kiro/Copilot permit read tools only: include applicable gate results in the
+prompt without adding implementation context to Blake's blind review.
+The prompt file's contents are delivered directly, including gitignored rubrics.
+
+Before dispatch, explicitly tell each Kiro/Copilot reviewer to use its read,
+glob and grep tools, never a shell (including git, rg or test commands). Supply
+required gate evidence through the coordinator. Check that every referenced
+input is readable under that backend's policy before launching the roster.
+Do not stage required inputs under ignored/denied paths such as docs/dev/tmp.
+An existing denial requires interactive recovery; do not copy denied inputs
+elsewhere or switch launchers to evade it. If coverage requires an unavailable
+capability, report the capability gap before spending a full review cycle.
+
+Kiro tool-call policy denials and failed approval requests invalidate the review
+even when runFinished reports success and the process exits zero. The helper
+also checks stderr and binds it into new Kiro receipts. Existing raw evidence
+must remain intact; a successful completion message never overrides a denial.
+
+After alternatives are exhausted, a final native Claude API 429 with a verified
+reset may wait until reset plus five seconds within the existing deadline.
+Await that helper; do not launch duplicate reviewers or retry exhausted routes.
+Already-running helpers need a safe restart to load updated routing code.
+Preserve evidence and use existing recovery for paused workflows; do not edit
+state.json or turn an incomplete review into a successful receipt.
+
+Retain every raw rubric verdict in the corresponding consolidated section:
+Alice's R rules, Blake's B rules, Bob's D1-D5. For mixed work, preserve both
+provider outputs under each persona heading, with explicit provider subheadings.
+Keep actual provider, model, effort, session and source evidence accurate. Do not
+reuse a Codex thread ID for Claude. Source schema enum labels are not provenance.
+
+Use the existing single state writer, never Write/Edit state.json directly:
+
+    python3 /Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py <verb> <args>
+    python3 /Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state-path> <verb> <args>
+
+These explicit paths replace shell functions `autopilot` and `statectl` when
+they are unavailable in a headless shell. State is rooted at the exact project
+directory above, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`. Never attach to a different
+ancestor or import another workflow's state.
+
+Claude hooks are not assumed to run inside Codex. Perform the source-mandated
+checks explicitly, including state/schema validation, task count consistency,
+review coverage and full rubrics, and required quality/build gates. The wrapper
+also checks review artifacts before it can advance. Do not omit a check merely
+because the source expected a hook. Use Codex native compaction; do not copy
+Claude's 500K context threshold or force a claimed 1M window.
+
+Complete the active phase, commit the canonical phase transition, write the
+handoff/contract card, then END this session. Never enter completion review from
+a session that implemented the work; a fresh process must receive that handoff.
+Review/rework follows the source's one-cycle-per-session procedure, followed by
+a fresh review session. Do not invoke the next gate after its handoff. Final
+prose is not a completion signal. Only committed state and a successful process
+result authorize the wrapper to continue. A genuine missing user decision or
+permission denial becomes a precise persisted pause; elapsed time is not consent.

+
