a test keeps the two in step.\n\nTemporary review context and other reproducible scratch material belongs under the globally ignored `docs/dev/tmp/` tree. `purge-devtmp` operates only there, preserves files linked to live PRDs, and never traverses `docs/dev/project-management/`.\n\nBatch end and cleanup steps enumerate lifecycle-owned runtime files explicitly; they never remove a directory wholesale. This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\n### Resuming\n\nWhen `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.\n- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for `state.next_phase`, then exits, never relaunching or parking, and refuses any phase but `review` or `done` before spawning. Export `_AUTOPILOT_WRITE_SCOPE_EXTRA` first when the project spans roots outside its repo (`~/.claude/AGENTS.md` § Toolchain), same as for a batch. Each launch passes `--strict-mcp-config --mcp-config <value>` so a loop session loads only the Context7 MCP server instead of every claude.ai connector on the account; `_AUTOPILOT_MCP_CONFIG=inherit` restores the unscoped launch, and any other value overrides the config verbatim (`mcp_config_for`, `cli/runner.py`).\n\n**Hand-off = write state, print banner, end the turn.** After the process exits, the loop driver reads `state.json` and branches:\n\n0. `state-write-failed` marker present → stop the loop and notify with its `detail`, without needing `state.json` to be readable.\n1. `pause_reason` set or `phase == \"paused\"` → notify the user with the pause detail, stop the loop, state left intact.\n2. `stall_reason.stalled == \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` (set by `/autopilot:work`'s Subagent Dispatch Budget when an assembled subagent prompt exceeded 50K after one trim pass; `/autopilot:work` also appends to `state.task_aborts`) → continue the loop; Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place (PRD stays in `wip/`; see the build gate's abort handlers). This is the one surviving replan path.\n3. `next_phase == \"\"` (empty) → backlog drained: the loop archives `state.json` to `reports/{batch_id}-state-final.json`, notifies, and stops the loop.\n4. `next_phase` non-empty → relaunch a fresh session, which resumes from state by artifact — capsule fresh → skip catchup, tasks exist → skip planning, `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task.\n5. `state.json` missing, unreadable, or untouched by the session → first a stand-down check: a `pause-requested` marker written during the session means the session found another session owning its PRD and stood down on purpose (the stand-down procedure below) — the loop consumes the marker, stamps `paused-by-operator`, notifies with the marker's reason, and stops with state intact; no retry burned, no park marker, `autoclaude` alone resumes (PRD 00172). Otherwise a usage-limit check against the captured session log (`last-session.log`; a live limit means sleep-until-reset and continue). Otherwise a genuine death: with a PRD selected (`state.prd` non-empty) the loop retries the relaunch once (`_AUTOPILOT_DIED_RETRIES_MAX`, default 1), then on exhaustion PARKS it — writes `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (`{prd, reason}`) and relaunches, so the next session's Phase 0 park handler sidelines the sick PRD to `hold/` and the batch keeps draining (PRD 00066). Only a **bootstrap** death (no PRD selected — nothing to park) notifies \"died\" and stops loud; an unconsumed park marker trips the loop's park-loop guard (also a loud stop; guarded relaunches back off `_AUTOPILOT_PARK_BACKOFF`, default 30s, and a marker whose write fails outright halts loud rather than handing off an empty marker). These two are rows 8 and 10 of the Error Handling § sanctioned batch-halt list.\n\nA Work-turn context-cap overrun is just branch 4: `autopilot_context_cap_hook.py` records the rotation (appends to `state.cap_rotations`, resets the in-flight task to `pending`, sets `next_phase: \"build\"`), the turn ends, and the fresh session resumes `build` by artifact — NO replan.\n\n**Stand-down procedure (a peer session owns the PRD).** A headless session never works a PRD another session is already working: two writers on one `state.json` and one set of task artifacts corrupt both, and the one-loop-per-repo guard sees only wrappers, not a bare interactive session. Phase 0 asks before it pauses. A peer counts only when `ListAgents` shows a busy interactive session whose name starts with this repository's directory basename (`basename \"$PWD\"`, e.g. `agent-skills-`); a session named for another repository is never evidence, whatever it is busy with (the two 2026-09-14 false stand-downs in agent-skills each cited a `claude-autopilot-*` session, the other repo's own loop). When such a peer exists, send it one `SendMessage` naming the PRD and wait at most 120 s for a reply. Stand down only when the reply claims the PRD (condition `peer_claimed`), or when writer evidence is present: `autopilot dirty` prints at least one path (condition `dirty_tree`; store writes never count as this evidence), or the mtime of `state.json` or `contract-card.md`, truncated to whole seconds, is greater than the `at` of the most recent `kind: \"handoff\"` row with `edge: \"leave\"` and this PRD's `prd` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (condition `state_after_leave`; the rows carry no batch id, so the `prd` filter is what keeps an older batch's row out; when no such `leave` row exists, skip the mtime test and let the dirty-tree test and the reply decide). That comparison holds only because every handoff site writes its `leave` row AFTER its last state and card write (§ Session handoff procedure orders step 1 before step 2; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff must set `next_phase` before its row too): a site that touches `state.json` after its row makes every next session read its own hand-off as peer evidence. A bare recent mtime is not evidence (a reader that inspects state while the loop writes, or this batch's own per-PRD reset, satisfies it), commit trailers are not consulted (no commit here carries a session trailer), and a peer that only reads, or never answers, never pauses a batch. To stand down: do not select, move, or write anything else; write `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` with the Write tool as one JSON line, `{\"reason\": \"<peer session> owns <prd> (<evidence>)\", \"condition\": \"<peer_claimed | dirty_tree | state_after_leave>\"}`, and end the turn. The loop reads a marker written during the session as a stand-down (branch 5 above): it stops with state intact, burns no retry, writes no park marker, quotes the reason in its stop line and notification, and records `stood_down` and `stood_down_condition` in the session's `loop-metrics.jsonl` row; `autoclaude` alone resumes once the peer is done. Before this procedure existed (2026-09-02, agent-skills PRD 00010) four stand-downs read as deaths and parked a healthy PRD mid-task.\n\nThe model's only job at a hand-off is to write `state.next_phase` (and `phase`/`stall_reason`) accurately, print the banner, and end the turn. The model never writes any signal and never inspects the loop's decision table — writing accurate state IS the hand-off. Interactive (non-loop) semantics are identical minus the loop: the same state writes happen, and the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` manually.\n\n**End the turn only at a real hand-off.** A phase is complete only when its artifacts are written and `state` is advanced (`phases_completed` updated, `next_phase` set). Dispatched work — `Agent` calls and background Bash — returns its results **within the same headless turn**: the harness re-invokes you with each `<task-notification>` before the turn can end, so dispatch, overlap independent work, wait for the results, and finish the phase. Do not end the turn to \"wait for\" something you dispatched.\n\n**Background Bash alone cannot hold a headless session open.** Documented `-p` behavior: live subagents keep the process alive across turn ends and re-invoke on completion, but background Bash tasks are killed ~5s after the final result. A turn that ends while ONLY background Bash (codex/gemini/qwen, `cargo test`, …) is still running kills that work and strands the phase (2026-07-12: the review session died this way twice — codex killed mid-review, state untouched, loop halted). Whenever dispatched background Bash may outlive every live subagent, dispatch a **Watcher subagent** in the same message that re-runs `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py` against the expected output files until `DONE` (procedure: `/autopilot:review-work-completion` step 5). The loop's session runner exports `CLAUDE_CODE_PRINT_BG_WAIT_CEILING_MS=0` so the subagent wait has no 10-minute ceiling; the session wall-clock cap stays the backstop.\n\nAn idle end-of-turn (phase unfinished, nothing pending) no longer thrashes anything — the loop relaunches and the next session resumes the phase by artifact (self-healing) — but it burns a session start, so treat it as waste, not as a mechanism.\n\nFor long **Bash** (builds, tests), still prefer the FOREGROUND with an explicit `timeout` (up to 600000 ms) so the result is in hand directly. If genuine work cannot finish in this session, that is a PAUSE (`phase: \"paused\"` + `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"work_incomplete\", \"detail\": \"<what could not finish>\"}` + end turn), not a silent idle stop.\n\n### Session handoff procedure (canonical — gate files invoke it by site name)\n\nEvery session handoff is the same three steps:\n\n1. **Apply the transition** with one `autopilot phase-done --outcome <outcome>` call (table below). It reads the current phase from `state.json`, looks the pair up in `cli/transitions.py`, and commits the next phase together with every field effect that transition mandates — in ONE transaction. There is no `--phase` flag and no per-effect flag: a caller cannot supply a mismatched phase, and cannot forget an effect.\n2. **Write the session brief, then the `leave` handoff row, then record the store, then print the site's banner** (shown at the invoking site in the gate file). The brief comes first, after the contract card (§ Contract card): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> write-brief docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` renders `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` from the state step 1 committed (where the batch stands, the card verbatim, the files the next gate needs), so the next session orients from one page (PRD 00201); the loop's launch prompt names it whenever it exists. A failed write is one stderr line, never a phase failure: carry on to the row. The row is `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site <build|review|done> --edge leave --phase <state.phase> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry); `state.phase` already names the next session's phase because step 1 committed it. A new site row in the table below gets its row from this step, not from a per-site sentence. Under `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` the row is also the session's point of no return: `hooks/note_session_leave.py` records it, and `hooks/guard_skill_after_leave.py` denies any `autopilot:*` (or `git-ferry:catchup`) `Skill` call this session makes afterwards, so a session that prints its banner and then re-invokes a gate is stopped by the harness, not only by this prose (PRD 00211). After the row, and as the LAST write before STOP, record the store with `autopilot record-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py record-store --state <state.json> --site <build|review|done> --prd <state.prd>`, best-effort like the row (a failure is one stderr line, never a reason to skip the row or the STOP). It runs at every site in the table below and comes after the row, never between the brief and the row: the row itself appends to the tracked `dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, so only a commit that follows it sweeps that append in.\n3. **End the turn.** In loop mode the loop driver reads `state.json` and relaunches per its decision table above; outside the loop the user re-invokes `/autopilot:run-autopilot` and the same resume logic applies. Do NOT continue into the next gate's phases in this session, even if context budget appears sufficient.\n\n| site | `--outcome` | what the transition commits |\n|------|-------------|-----------------------------|\n| **build → review** (`phase-build.md`, after Phase 3) | `tasks_done` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`. `phases_completed` unchanged — the build gate leaves no membership marker. `state.tasks` is already current — every producer (`task-add`/`task-start`/`task-done`/`task-set-meta`) writes it directly via `statectl`, so there is nothing to query or snapshot at this handoff. |\n| **review → review** (`phase-review.md` Phase 6, after rework when the loop continues) | `rework` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"review\"`, `cycle` incremented, `rework_task_ids` cleared — all in one commit. `state.tasks` untouched. `phases_completed` unchanged — only convergence adds `\"review\"`. |\n| **review → done** (`phase-review.md`, on loop convergence) | `converged` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"done\"`, and `\"review\"` appended to `phases_completed` — the convergence marker the review gate's loop-level skip reads. It lands *because this is convergence*, not because a flag asked for it. |\n| **build → done** (`references/lane-solo.md` § Close, a lane-routed PRD whose one review pass wrote its review file) | `lane_reviewed` | Convergence's own effect set: `phase`/`next_phase: \"done\"` and `\"review\"` appended once to `phases_completed`, so `review_coverage_hook.py` gates the lane's `-review-1.md` with `--require-codex-guard` exactly as a full-lane cycle's. An escalating solo build takes the **build → review** row instead. |\n| **PRD → PRD** (`phase-done.md`, step 10 more-PRDs branch) | `more_prds` | `phase`/`next_phase: \"build\"`, `phases_completed` reset to `[]`, and the whole per-PRD reset (`cli/records.PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS` — the one authoritative list); `batch` preserved in full. |\n| **batch end** (`phase-done.md`, no more PRDs) | `drained` | `phase: \"done\"` and the EMPTY `next_phase` the loop reads as drained. Not a handoff — nothing relaunches. Also legal from `build`, which is where Phase 0's \"No PRDs anywhere\" reaches it. |\n\nWriting any of these fields by hand with `statectl set` is a bug: it is how a mandatory effect gets dropped. The `cycle` increment is the one that has already cost a real batch — the Phase 5 cap gate reads it, and losing it once let a loop run past its cap.\n\n### Contract card (compaction re-anchor)\n\nWithin-session compaction can drop this skill's text mid-procedure, after which the session drifts off-contract with nothing to re-anchor it. To survive that, **at each gate transition write a compact contract card** — the current step, the active invariants, and the next gate:\n\n- **Autopilot (state.json world):** write the body to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md` with the **Write tool**, then load it with one call:\n  ```bash\n  python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> set-contract-card docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/contract-card.md\n  ```\n  Keep it a few lines: `step: <phase/step> | invariants: <the 2-3 that bind right now> | next: <the next gate + its precondition>`. **Never pass the card as an inline shell argument** — it carries quotes, newlines and `$`, and the inline `set contract_card '<string>'` form failed three consecutive times on quoting in a real build session (2026-08-02, engram session 6).\n- **Interactive (no state.json):** the file write above is the whole step; skip the statectl call.\n\nThe session brief (`write-brief`, § Session handoff procedure step 2) is rendered right after this call so it carries the card just loaded; `/autopilot:work`'s task-boundary handoff and `/autopilot:review-work-completion`'s cycle transition write the brief the same way where they write their cards.\n\n`reinject_contract_card.py` is a SessionStart hook **matched to `compact` only** (startup/resume/clear stay unmatched, so there is no standing token cost); after a compaction it reads the card back and re-injects it as additionalContext. `/autopilot:work` (task-boundary transitions) and `/autopilot:review-work-completion` (cycle transitions) write their own cards the same way — `contract_card` in `references/state-schema.md`.\n\n### Loop Detection\n\nThe `autoclaude` wrapper exports `_AUTOPILOT_LOOP=$$` before launching each headless session. Skills branch on it for loop-mode behavior only — the `AskUserQuestion` ban (Error Handling), git-push deferral, notify suppression in `~/.claude/hooks/notify.py`. Hand-off sites do NOT check it: the state writes are the same in and out of the loop.\n\n**Review-file gate (in-session quality gate).** `review_coverage_hook.py` stays registered on Stop: at the done hand-off, when the saved review file is missing or fails the `cli/gate.py` shape check (missing reviewer section, verdict, or tests line — PRD 00016, absorbed into the CLI as `autopilot gate` by PRD 00107), it exit-2-blocks the turn's end and feeds the gap back to the model so the review can be finished before the turn ends. Exit-2 Stop-hook blocking works in `-p` mode (`references/design-rationale.md` § Review-file gate). This is a completeness gate on review artifacts, not loop orchestration.\n\n**State-write gate (in-session integrity gate).** `statectl` is the normal writer and cannot produce an invalid `state.json`, but a stray hand-edit still can, so `validate_state_json_hook.py` stays registered on PostToolUse for the `Edit`/`Write`/`MultiEdit` matchers: any such mutation that leaves the file unparseable exit-2-feeds the parse error back to the model immediately, while the session can still rewrite it. Without it, the corruption surfaces only at session exit, where the wrapper's `jq` check misreads a healthy PAUSE as `died` (state file unreadable) and halts the loop (harness-tag bleed appended `</content>` to a hand-edited write, ddb 2026-07-16).\n\n**Loop sketch** (the real driver — `cli/loop.py`, invoked as `autopilot loop` — adds the memory circuit-breaker, the session wall-clock cap, orphan cleanup, metrics, notifications, and the operator-view renderer — `scripts/render_stream.py` turns the stream-json terminal output into one-line summaries while `last-session.log` keeps the raw events; the bash `autoclaude` wrapper keeps only the operator subcommands, the tracon presentation front-end, and the hand-off):\n\n```\nautoclaude                 # bash: subcommands + tracon front-end, then\n  -> autopilot loop        # cli/loop.py, the driver:\n       while True:\n           pause marker?  -> consume it, notify, stop\n           spawn the routed `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"` (raw events kept in last-session.log)\n           read state.json, branch per the decision table above (0-5)\n```\n\n## Phase 0 invariants (selection — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\nTest-pinned invariants the build gate's Phase 0 references; they live here so every session carries them.\n\n`autopilot enter` is the first Bash call of a build session: it runs this whole step chain and prints one JSON line (`references/phase-build.md` § \"Enter in one call\").\n\n**Lifecycle directories first.** Before the abort handlers and before PRD selection, as its own Bash call:\n\n```bash\nmkdir -p docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip docs/dev/project-management/prds/done docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold docs/dev/project-management/reviews docs/dev/tmp docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/deferred\n```\n\nIdempotent, safe on every invocation. `mkdir` before any move is mandatory: a move into a missing destination silently misplaces the PRD (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\nThen, right after that `mkdir -p` and as its own Bash call, run `autopilot ensure-store`: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py ensure-store --state <state.json>`. It writes `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`, the machine form of the § Retention Disposable list, whenever that file is missing or differs from the list; it is idempotent, exits 0 either way, and needs no `state.json` to exist yet. The file is written by code, never with the Write or Edit tool: `hooks/enforce_prd_location.py` rejects a top-level store file outside its keeper list for editor tools, and that refusal is correct and stays. The patterns themselves live once, as `STORE_GITIGNORE` in `cli/store_tree.py`, and a test holds them against § Retention. `autopilot enter` runs this step itself.\n\n**Verified moves.** Every lifecycle `mv` (backlog→`wip/` at selection, and equally wip→done / wip→hold at the other gates) is immediately followed by a verification: confirm the moved PRD now exists in the destination directory. If it does not, the `mv` failed — set `state.phase = \"paused\"` and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`, write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"mv_verify\", \"detail\": \"<source, destination, and the mv error>\"}`, and PAUSE naming the source, the destination, and the `mv` error; do not continue past a failed move.\n\n**Batch-identity rollover.** When `state.batch` already exists at selection, mint a fresh `batch.id` (new `<yyyymmddHHMM>` timestamp, reset `completed_prds: []`) ONLY for a *genuinely closed* surviving batch: `phase == \"done\"` AND `next_phase == \"\"` (empty). Both conditions are required — only the batch-end \"No more PRDs\" branch writes the empty `next_phase`, while Phase 9 step 2 sets a transient `phase: \"done\"` (with `next_phase: \"done\"`) BEFORE the verified wip→done move, so a failed move or mid-Phase-9 crash leaves that shape and must NOT roll over (rolling over there would wipe the in-progress batch's `completed_prds` and mint a spurious id). Every normal in-progress resume preserves `batch.id` unchanged. (Forensics: `references/design-rationale.md` § Batch-identity rollover.)\n\nOn that closed-batch rollover, delete `batch.unavailable_reviewers`,\n`batch.unavailable_reviewer_details` and `batch.minted_stubs` (so the next\nbatch's `{s} stubs` count starts empty, PRD 00195) in the same state update as\nthe new id.\nInteractive batch end retains `state.json`, so expiry cannot depend on file\ndeletion. Every in-progress resume preserves both fields, including transitions\nto another PRD in the same batch; only a new batch tries a rejected Carl again.\n\n## Phase 3 invariants (work — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\n**`work_start_sha` is captured once per PRD.** Run `git rev-parse HEAD` and write it to `state.work_start_sha` before dispatching `/autopilot:work`, but only if it is unset for the current PRD (`state.work_start_sha` absent or empty). If it is already set, **do NOT re-capture** — a cap-rotation (or any other build re-entry on resume) re-enters the build gate with pending tasks, and the existing value marks the true PRD start; re-capturing the HEAD-at-rotation would shrink the review diff (`work_start_sha..HEAD`) to post-rotation commits only. `review-work-completion` uses `work_start_sha..HEAD` as the full-review diff range, so the doubt lens sees the PRD's whole work range. Phase 9 step 10 clears the field on the PRD-to-PRD reset, so each PRD in a multi-PRD batch captures fresh and ranges never overlap.\n\n**If `git rev-parse HEAD` fails at capture** — an unborn branch or a repo with no commits yet (a *detached* HEAD resolves fine and is not this case; a bare-repo-backed root like `~/.claude` must run rev-parse in the SAME git context `repo_root` uses — the `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` flags — not a bare `git rev-parse` that would fail or resolve a parent repo): there is no base commit to diff against. Do NOT leave `work_start_sha` unset (an absent value makes the review range undefined and crashes the doubt lens). Set it to the git **empty-tree sentinel** `4b825dc642cb6eb9a060e54bf8d69288fbee4904`, log a one-line warning, and note the fallback in the batch report — the review range `4b825dc…..HEAD` then spans the whole tree once `/autopilot:work` has committed, which is the correct scope for a first-commit repo.\n\n## Phase 9 invariants (completion — full procedure: `references/phase-done.md`)\n\n**Verified finalize move.** The move of the PRD from `wip/` to `done/` keeps the `00XXX-` prefix and is verified: confirm the PRD now exists in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/done/`; on failure PAUSE per the verified-moves rule above (`site: \"mv_verify\"`) — never append to `completed_prds` or advance to the next PRD with the PRD in the wrong folder.\n\n**Report identity.** The batch report filename is built from the current `state.batch.id` — `reports/{state.batch.id}-report.md`; before appending, verify the target filename's id matches `state.batch.id`. Never glob `reports/*.md` to choose a file, and never append to a report whose id differs from `state.batch.id` — a mismatch is a batch-identity error; create a fresh `{state.batch.id}-report.md` instead.\n\n## Design-gate invariant: empty-review-log gate (Phase 1.5 — full procedure: `references/phase-build.md`)\n\nPhase 1.5 must verify the design doc's `## Review log` actually holds at least one reviewer dispatch summary line — a silently-skipped review leaves it empty, and nothing else checks that the review ran. Run the gate on this success path (after a successful `/autopilot:design-solution` run) AND on this artifact-reuse path (when an existing design doc is reused); `design_mode == \"skip\"` bypasses the empty-review-log gate entirely (no doc exists by design). Inline the design-doc path from `state.design_doc` directly into this exact section-scoped check (one `awk`, no pipe, no shell variable — assignments break permission-prefix matching; exit-code based — it counts only pinned dispatch-summary lines that appear inside the `## Review log` section, so the design doc's own example lines in `## Interfaces & contracts` cannot false-pass it):\n\n```\nawk '/^## Review log/{f=1;next} /^## /{f=0} f && /dispatch [0-9]+ \\((claude|codex|claude-fallback)\\): cardinal-sin [0-9]+, blocker [0-9]+, non-blocker [0-9]+, question [0-9]+/{hit=1} END{exit !hit}' <path-from-state.design_doc>\n```\n\n- **exit 0** (≥1 in-section dispatch summary line) → proceed to Phase 2 (planning).\n- **exit non-zero** (empty `## Review log` — the review never ran) → treat as a sub-skill failure: set `state.phase = \"paused\"` and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`, write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"design doc has empty ## Review log (review never ran)\"}`, and do NOT proceed to planning. Surface the remedy: delete the design doc and let Phase 1.5 regenerate it.\n\nThe check is deterministic (the pinned `awk` above), NOT a model judgment.\n\n## Shell Command Rules\n\n- Never call bash `head`, `tail`, `cat`, `grep`, or `find` - a hook blocks them. Use the Read tool (offset/limit), `rg`, or `rg --files` instead. Never pipe between heterogeneous commands and never combine an inspection (read, list, search, diff) with a test, lint or build invocation in one Bash call - run them as separate calls. Pass an explicit `timeout` on every Bash call: 60000 ms for an inspection, 300000 ms for a lint run or a narrow test run, 600000 ms for a full suite or a full build.\n- **Never chain commands** with `&&`, `|`, or `;` in a single Bash call. Use separate Bash tool calls instead.\n- **Never use redirections** like `2>/dev/null`. Handle missing files by checking existence or catching errors in the tool result.\n- Use `Read` for file contents; for existence and listing checks Bash `ls` is fine (the native `Glob` tool is absent in this build - rules/tools.md).\n- Use `mkdir -p` in its own Bash call when creating directories.\n\n## Error Handling\n\n| Situation | Interactive | Loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set, PRD 00017) |\n|-----------|-------------|------------------------------------------------|\n| Sub-skill invocation fails outright (no usable result; the phase cannot proceed) | PAUSE, report which skill failed and error. A transient reviewer/sub-skill error *during the review-rework cycle* is the review gate's Safety Checks row's domain instead (graceful degradation, not a PAUSE). | Re-invoke the sub-skill ONCE; if it fails again, stall the PRD (`recovery.md` → \"Loop-mode stall procedure\", `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`) and continue the batch |\n| No PRDs anywhere | STOP with message about /create-prd | Run `autopilot phase-done --outcome drained` (it writes `phase: \"done\"` and the empty `next_phase`) so the wrapper stops as drained, not died, preceded by `autopilot init --prd \"\"` only when `state.json` is absent: `phase-done` exits 2 on a missing state file and the wrapper reads that as *died*, but the entry verb already creates `state.json` before this row is normally reached, so an unconditional `init` always hits the exit-7 re-run guard. |\n| State file corrupted | Delete it, restart from Phase 0 | Same (in-session recovery, no pause) |\n| `statectl` state-write fails (lock contention, python error, unreadable state) | Retry once; still failing → `autopilot restore` and retry once more; still failing → write the `state-write-failed` marker (`site: \"statectl_fail\"`) with the raw stderr in `detail`, end the turn, and also report the failure to the user directly — never proceed on the stale state | Retry once; still failing → `autopilot restore` and retry once more; still failing → write the `state-write-failed` marker (`site: \"statectl_fail\"`) with the raw stderr in `detail`, end the turn — the wrapper halts on it and surfaces the detail |\n| Review produces no parseable output | PAUSE, report — don't retry | Re-run the review ONCE; still unparseable → stall the PRD (`site: \"reviewer_fail\"`), continue the batch |\n| All reviewers fail | PAUSE, report — partial results usable if user confirms | Re-invoke ONCE; still nothing → stall the PRD (`site: \"reviewer_fail\"`), continue the batch |\n| `docs/dev/project-management/` doesn't exist | Create it | Same |\n| Task tools unavailable | STOP, report — can't operate without tasks | Same (a broken harness is not a per-PRD failure) |\n| Git push fails (auth, locked signing agent, network) | Report and let the user retry. A push denied by hooks/guard_push_on_critical.py names a pending cap_critical custody: resolve it with autopilot custody resolve, never bypass the hook. | Log to `deferred_decisions[]`, leave the commits local (the user pushes manually per Phase 9), CONTINUE — a locked signing agent on an unattended host is expected (`references/design-rationale.md` § Git push failures). A guard denial is closed at the next attended Phase 0 (`references/phase-build.md` § Handle pending custody), where the operator picks revert, branch-and-revert or accept; loop mode leaves the commits local and continues without any git mutation. |\n| `mv` verify fails (backlog→wip, wip→done, wip→hold) | PAUSE per the mv-verify sites | Retry the `mv` ONCE after re-running `mkdir -p`; persistent failure is a sanctioned batch halt (row 3 of the sanctioned batch-halt list below) |\n| **Security-critical finding** (exposed secret, vulnerability being shipped) | PAUSE | **PAUSE — sanctioned batch halt, row 1** (set `phase: \"paused\"` + `pause_reason`; the wrapper notifies and halts) |\n| **Detected data-loss risk** | PAUSE | **PAUSE — sanctioned batch halt, row 2** (same mechanics) |\n\n**Loop mode never halts the whole batch for a per-PRD decision.** After PRD 00066 the loop-mode turn-ending *decision*-PAUSE list is empty: a blocking escalation and the Phase 1.5 design gate STALL the PRD (`references/recovery.md` Loop-mode stall procedure), a scope alarm DEFERS-and-continues, and a Phase 2 ambiguity is resolved by the simplest safe assumption (or stalls under `pause_on_ambiguity: true`) — none write `phase: \"paused\"`. Everything else stalls the PRD or defers and continues. The ONLY conditions that stop the whole batch (a loud halt, not a per-PRD park/stall) are the sanctioned batch-halt list below. Future edits must not re-grow the loop-mode decision-PAUSE list, nor add a halt outside that list.\n\n**Sanctioned batch-halt list (the complete set of whole-batch loud stops):**\n\n1. **Security-critical finding** — exposed secret or a vulnerability being shipped (including a cap_critical custody capture that fails twice) (skill PAUSE; `pause_reason` set by the Error Handling row above).\n2. **Detected data-loss risk** (skill PAUSE).\n3. **`mv`-verify exhaustion** — a lifecycle move that keeps failing after the retry (skill PAUSE, `mv_verify`).\n4. **Sustained memory pressure** (wrapper memory circuit-breaker).\n5. **Usage-limit beyond `_AUTOPILOT_LIMIT_WAIT_MAX`** (wrapper `died`).\n6. **Net-retries exhausted** (wrapper `died`).\n7. **Operator pause** — the `pause-requested` marker (wrapper stop).\n8. **Died bootstrap session** — a session died before any PRD was selected, so there is nothing to park (wrapper `died`).\n9. **Systemic-park breaker** — 2 consecutive `wrapper_died` parks with nothing healthy between (skill PAUSE, `systemic_park`; Phase 0 park handler, `references/phase-build.md`).\n10. **Unwritable or unconsumed park marker** — the park hand-off itself is broken: the wrapper cannot write the `park-requested` marker (the write-failure guard in the `park)` else branch, so it never hands off an empty marker) OR a written marker is never consumed (the park-loop guard). Either is a wrapper loud halt.\n11. **Plugin version drift** (PRD 00086 R3) — the loop's plugin-pin preflight (`plugin_drift` in `cli/loop.py`) found an enforcement plugin (aegis/warden) whose installed version differs from the `state.batch.plugin_versions` pin recorded at batch selection: the batch's enforcement code auto-updated mid-run, so the wrapper halts loud with state intact rather than run a session on unpinned enforcement code.\n\nRows 1–8 are the PRD 00066 Success-Metrics list; rows 9–10 are the two systemic backstops the PRD Risks section mandates (adopted at the design gate, 2026-07-18); row 11 is the plugin-pin preflight (PRD 00086 R3). Nothing outside these eleven stops the batch — Success Metric 2 is read as \"no UNSANCTIONED halts\".\n\n**Turn-ending PAUSE rows must set `state.phase = \"paused\"` (and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`) before stopping, and must also write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"<slug>\", \"detail\": \"<one-line human string>\"}`.** `pause_reason` is a durable marker so the loop halts even if the model forgets `phase=\"paused\"`; unlike `phase` it is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared on resume (see `### Resuming` cleanup). Without it the wrapper — seeing a non-empty `next_phase` — would take its continue branch and relaunch the failed phase instead of stopping for you to intervene; a paused state is the wrapper's stop-and-notify branch (Session Loop branch 1), and the wrapper surfaces `pause_reason.detail` in its notification. This applies to \"Sub-skill invocation fails outright\" (`pause_reason.site = \"sub_skill_fail\"`), \"Review produces no parseable output\" (`\"reviewer_fail\"`), \"All three reviewers fail\" (`\"reviewer_fail\"`), and \"statectl state-write fails\" (`\"statectl_fail\"`). Exceptions that need no `phase` change: \"State file corrupted\" (delete it and restart from Phase 0 in the same session; the freshly-written state is what the wrapper reads at turn end) and \"No PRDs anywhere\" (see its row — the drained state write covers the loop). PAUSE sites that ask via `AskUserQuestion` mid-turn (Phase 1.5 design gate, Phase 2 clarification, Phase 5 blocking escalation and scope alarm) do NOT end the turn and need no `phase` change — **but only outside the loop. When `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is set there is no human to answer, and (post-00066) none of these pause the batch: each takes its per-PRD path instead. The design gate and a blocking escalation run the Loop-mode stall procedure (`references/recovery.md`; `site: \"design_gate\"` recording the design doc path, `site: \"blocking_escalation\"` recording the blocking issue in the deferred JSON `detail`); a scope alarm defers-and-continues (a `scope-overflow` deferred record — the top-10 fixes proceed); a Phase 2 ambiguity is resolved by the simplest safe assumption, or stalls (`site: \"clarification\"`) under `pause_on_ambiguity: true`. None writes `phase: \"paused\"` — the batch keeps draining and a human resolves the parked PRD on the next manual `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (see `references/decision-framework.md` → \"Autonomy in loop mode\"). A mid-turn question on the unattended path has stranded the loop for hours (`references/design-rationale.md` § No mid-turn questions).**\n\n## Reference Files\n\n- `references/phase-build.md` — build gate (selection/aborts, catchup, design, planning, work)\n- `references/phase-review.md` — review gate (lenses, decision gate, cap, rework)\n- `references/phase-done.md` — done gate (completion, continuation, batch-end review)\n- `references/state-schema.md` — state file JSON schema and skip logic\n- `references/decision-framework.md` — auto-fix vs escalate classification rules\n- `references/recovery.md` — rare-path handlers (abort/replan, stalls, escalation-exhausted, cap-pause resume)\n- `references/design-rationale.md` — incident history behind the rules (non-normative)\n- `references/dashboard-format.md` — live dashboard via tracon (render_stream fallback; plain text via `autopilot status`)\n- `references/batch-report-format.md` — batch report sources and semantics (render: `autopilot render report`)\n- `references/audit-log-format.md` — audit label set and decisions.md projection (render: `autopilot render audit`)\n- `references/doubt-review-rubric.md` — Bob's doubt-lens rubric (D1-D5)\n- `references/waves.md` — the `autopilot wave` verbs, what a lane worktree holds, and what is deferred\n\n\nBUILD PROCEDURE\n\n# Build Gate (`phase: \"build\"`)\n\nRouted here when `state.phase` is `\"build\"`, `state.json` is missing, or the\nstate is `\"paused\"`/aborted (the Phase 0 handlers below own that resume).\n`build` is ONE session — selection, catchup, design, planning, work — with no\nmid-build handoff; sub-steps skip by ARTIFACT, never by `phases_completed`\nmembership. Core `SKILL.md` (always loaded) carries the shared mechanics and\nthe test-pinned invariants this file references.\n\n## Phase 0: PRD Selection\n\nRead `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/session-brief.md` if it exists (PRD 00201). Its Where section replaces the state reads below; open only the files its Read next section lists. When its phase disagrees with `state.json`, fall back to the state reads.\n\n### Enter in one call\n\nRun `autopilot enter` (one Bash call). It runs the whole documented Phase 0 step\nchain below and prints one JSON line whose `stop` names the first step that\nhalted.\n\nWhen `stop` is null every step passed: print the PRD banner and go straight to\nPhase 1, using the `catchup` and `design` decisions the call returned,\nwithout re-running any of the Phase 0 steps below by hand.\n\nWhen the session brief has an `## Entry` section (PRD 00282: the loop already\nran Phase 0 before launch), take `prd`, `catchup`, and `design` from it\ninstead — running `autopilot enter` anyway replays the same stored line\nrather than re-running Phase 0.\n\nWhen `stop` is set, follow the table below: it maps each `stop` value to the\nexisting section that owns that halt.\n\n| `stop` | owner |\n|---|---|\n| `fs_error` | § Ensure lifecycle directories exist when `detail` names the `mkdir`; the `--prds` flag when `detail` names a shallow path; the design-gate invariant's non-zero branch when `detail` names the design doc |\n| `park_halt` | § Handle park request: exit-code row 5 when `detail` says systemic halt; otherwise `detail` names an exit code outside the table's 0/3/4/5/9/10 rows (`do_park` returned something `enter.py` does not recognize) — PAUSE (`site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`, `detail` = the unmapped-exit-code message) |\n| `mv_verify` | § Handle park request row 4, or Normal PRD selection's verified move, whichever move failed |\n| `deferred_io` | routed by `detail`: `do_park exited 9: a deferred-record append failed` → § Handle park request row 9; an unreadable custody entry (`custody.CustodyError` from the pending-custody count) → § Handle pending custody's exit-9 branch, PAUSE in every mode with `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"` and the `detail` as the pause detail |\n| `stall_op_conflict` | § Handle park request row 10 |\n| `stall_op_malformed` | § Handle park request row 10's action — PAUSE for human reconciliation: a half-written `stall_op` (a missing required key, or a half-captured `cap_critical` range) that `autopilot park` refuses to reconcile. `state.json` is readable, so row 2's corrupted-state path does NOT apply and state is never deleted |\n| `park_precondition_failed` | `references/recovery.md`'s exit-code table row 2, second branch — the `detail` names the cause (a missing `batch.id`, or a failed `cap_critical` range capture): retry the stall ONCE, then PAUSE in every mode (`phase`/`next_phase: \"paused\"`, `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`), PRD left in `wip/`, and never delete `state.json`. NOT § Handle park request row 2's corrupted-state row |\n| `replan` | § Handle Work-phase abort, the `subagent_prompt_overrun` bullet |\n| `escalation_exhausted` | § Handle Work-phase abort, the `escalation_exhausted` bullet |\n| `cap_pause` | § Handle Work-phase abort, the cap-pause bullet |\n| `custody` | § Handle pending custody |\n| `drained` | Normal PRD selection, the `drained` row |\n| `prd_not_found` | Normal PRD selection step 1, the named PRD is in neither `wip/` nor `backlog/` |\n| `batch_init` | Normal PRD selection step 3, then run `autopilot enter` again. A `state.batch` with no string `id` is ABSENT however many other keys it holds, and minting preserves any existing `batch.skips` rather than replacing the object |\n| `lane` | § 5.5. Route by lane |\n| `state_write_failed` | § Frontmatter parse, the state write failed; Error Handling's statectl row |\n| `design_review_log_empty` | the design-gate invariant's non-zero branch (Phase 1.5) |\n\n`autopilot enter` prints no banner of its own. It prints the one JSON line\n(frontmatter warnings go to stderr); every banner is still this skill's to\nprint, from the fields that line returned.\n\nA non-null `parked` means `autopilot park` parked that PRD: print the STALLED\nbanner and continue selection (§ Handle park request's exit-0 row).\n\nA non-zero `custody_pending` in loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set) is the cue\nto print `custody: <n> entries await an attended resume` (`<n>` =\n`custody_pending`) and continue (§ Handle pending custody's loop-mode branch).\n\n`enter` makes no capsule read: before Phase 1, read the Active Work section of\n`docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` yourself if it exists\n(§ Normal PRD selection step 6).\n\nA non-zero exit prints NO JSON line — the diagnostics go to stderr, so read\nstderr and the exit code instead of waiting for a `stop` value that never\ncomes:\n\n| exit | cause |\n|---|---|\n| `1` | no autopilot dir above cwd and no `--state` given; this call runs before the `mkdir -p` block, so a from-nothing repo hits it on its very first call. Re-run with `--state <project>/docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — `enter` builds the whole lifecycle tree itself from that path, so the dir need not exist yet. Running from the project root only helps once the tree is already there |\n| `2` | `state.json` is corrupt (`StateError`) — the corrupted-state row of core `SKILL.md` § Error Handling owns it |\n| `6` | a future `schema_version` stamp, refused rather than resumed blindly (the same preflight `autopilot resume-target` makes) |\n\n### Ensure lifecycle directories exist\n\nBefore anything else — before the abort handlers and before PRD selection — run\nthe lifecycle `mkdir -p` block from core `SKILL.md` § \"Phase 0 invariants\" as\nits own Bash call (idempotent; mandatory before any move can run). Then, right\nafter it and as its own Bash call, run `autopilot ensure-store`:\n`python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py ensure-store --state <state.json>`.\nIt ships the store's `docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore` idempotently and\nexits 0 either way. That file is written by code, never with the Write or Edit\ntool: `hooks/enforce_prd_location.py` rejects a top-level store file outside its\nkeeper list for editor tools, and that refusal stays.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs both steps; the instructions below stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n### Clear inherited hand-off markers\n\nThen, still before the abort handlers, run `autopilot markers --clear`:\n`python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py markers --clear handoff-requested cap-fired`\n(one Bash call; exits 1 only when no autopilot dir is found above cwd - an\nunlink failure is not caught today). It removes any `.handoff-requested` and\n`.cap-fired` beside `state.json`.\nA marker present when a session starts was written by an earlier session for a\nboundary that session never reached (a wall-cap kill, a crash, a plugin upgrade\nbetween sessions); it is never this session's to act on, and left in place it\nmakes step 6.5 hand off after the first task (PRD 00210: a 1-byte marker from\n2026-09-14 did exactly that on 2026-09-20). Markers this session's own hook\nwrites later are untouched: this is the session's first Bash call after the\n`mkdir`.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions below stay the hand-run\nreference. Unlike the script above, `autopilot enter` names none of the removed\nmarkers on stderr — it clears them silently, so no removal time appears there.\n\n### Handle park request (FIRST abort-handler check)\n\nThe wrapper parks a sick PRD by writing `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/park-requested` (a\none-line JSON `{\"prd\": \"<basename>\", \"reason\": \"<one-line cause>\"}`) and\nrelaunching — never by editing `state.json` (state surgery stays in-skill). This\nhandler runs BEFORE the `stall_reason` checks below. The pure decision core\n`park_decision(marker, wip_filenames, parks_consecutive)` in `cli/resume.py`\nencodes the classification (no marker / malformed / stale / park→continue /\npark→systemic-halt); `autopilot park` executes its verdict.\n(`scripts/resume_target.py` still re-exports it for callers that name that\npath.)\n\nRun `autopilot park` (one Bash call). It consumes the marker, reconciles any\npending `stall_op` first, performs the verified `wip/`→`hold/` move, the\ndeferred record, and a single-commit reset/increment/pause, then deletes the\nmarker last. See `cli/records.py`'s `do_park` docstring for the full contract.\nThe deferred record's `detail` is the marker's reason plus a\n`; lane=<lane_effective>` term when the parked PRD was lane-routed (PRD\n00205), so a solo PRD parked by the died-retry carries its lane.\n\n| Exit code | Meaning | Action |\n|---|---|---|\n| 3 | no/ignored/reconciled marker | fall through to the next abort handler / normal selection |\n| 0 | parked | print the STALLED banner, continue selection |\n| 5 | parked AND systemic halt | `pause_reason` is already written — print the PAUSE banner, end the turn |\n| 4 | move failed | PAUSE per the mv-verify invariant (`site: \"mv_verify\"`) |\n| 9 | deferred-record I/O failed | PAUSE (`site: \"statectl_fail\"` family) |\n| 10 | stall_op conflict | PAUSE for human reconciliation |\n| 2 | state unreadable | the corrupted-state row of Error Handling applies |\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions below stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n### Handle Work-phase abort (from a prior session)\n\nBefore anything else, read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` and check `stall_reason`:\n\n- `stall_reason.stalled` is `\"subagent_prompt_overrun\"` — the previous session's work aborted from a hook. The PRD is not broken; one task was scoped too big. **Follow `references/recovery.md` → \"Work-phase abort: replan procedure\"**, then STOP (the next session re-enters `build` at planning). This is the one surviving replan path.\n- `stall_reason.stalled` is `\"escalation_exhausted\"` — Phase 6 owns this inline; seeing it at Phase 0 means a crash landed mid-stall-move. **Follow `references/recovery.md` → \"Crash recovery: escalation_exhausted seen at Phase 0\"**, then fall through to Normal PRD selection.\n- `state.phase == \"paused\"` AND `state.cap_pause_reason` is set (the previous session's review-gate cap-pause behavior fired). The capped PRD is still in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`; do NOT treat it as fresh PRD selection. **Follow `references/recovery.md` → \"Cap-Pause Resume Handler\"** — it presents the recorded unresolved findings and cycle count via the `AskUserQuestion` tool and branches on resume/abandon.\n- `state.cap_rotations` has a new entry but none of the above holds — the previous session hit the Work-turn context cap and the cap hook rotated to a fresh session. The cap hook recorded the rotation (appended `cap_rotations`, reset the in-flight task to `pending`, set `next_phase: \"build\"`); that session then ended its turn and the loop wrapper relaunched on the non-empty `next_phase`. NOT a replan. A `cap_rotations` entry is **informational only** and needs no special handling here: the dead session's `.cap-fired` marker was already removed by § Clear inherited hand-off markers above, so it no longer de-duplicates this session's hook fires. Fall through to Normal PRD selection, which resumes `build` by artifact (capsule fresh → skip catchup; tasks exist → skip planning; `/autopilot:work` continues at the first non-completed task — the rotated task, now reset to `pending`).\n- None of the above (neither a recognised `stall_reason` value nor the cap-pause condition `phase == \"paused\"` + `cap_pause_reason`) — continue with Normal PRD selection below.\n\nBefore acting on whichever branch matched, run `autopilot resume-target` (one Bash call) and compare its line to the handler you picked. It is the executable form of this same contract (`cli/resume.py`), so a disagreement means the prose and the encoding have drifted — follow the encoding and say so. The line adjudicates the abort handlers and the resume point only: `/work continues at first non-completed task <id>` means planning is done, not that Phase 1 is skipped; every build entry still runs § Batch cache check and takes the delta or full path it decides (PRD 00209). It also runs the schema-version preflight, refusing with exit 6 on a future-schema `state.json` rather than resuming it blindly. Exit 2 means there is no state file yet, which is a normal fresh start, not an error.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions below stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n### Handle pending custody\n\nA loop-mode `cap_critical` stall (`references/recovery.md` § Stall `site` slugs) leaves a custody entry behind: a CRITICAL shipped to master with its commit range recorded for an attended decision. Run `autopilot custody list` (one Bash call). It prints one JSON line per pending entry — the marker ∪ the journal, so a journal-only entry whose marker was trashed is still listed. No lines → nothing is pending; fall through to Normal PRD selection. Exit 9 → the marker or the journal is present but unreadable: PAUSE in every mode (`site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`, the stderr line as `detail`) — unreadable custody state must not be walked past.\n\nWith entries listed:\n\n- **Interactive:** for each entry, ask via `AskUserQuestion` with the three choices — `revert` (revert the range on master), `branch-and-revert` (preserve the work on a branch, then revert master), `accept` (keep it on master, close custody) — then run `autopilot custody resolve --prd <stem> --choice <choice>` (one Bash call per entry). Exit 0 → next entry, then Normal PRD selection. Exit 1 → no pending entry, or a different choice was already recorded (cleanup still ran): report it and move on. Exit 5 → git refused or failed (wrong checkout, an unfinished revert/merge/cherry-pick, a partial revert, a conflict; custody retained): report git's message and STOP the turn — do not select a PRD while a revert is unfinished. The operator finishes or aborts it, then closes custody with `--choice accept` or re-runs the same choice. Exit 9 → ledger/marker/journal read or write failed: PAUSE as above.\n- **Loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set):** there is no human to answer, so this handler neither asks nor runs `custody resolve`. Print `custody: <n> entries await an attended resume` (`<n>` = the line count) and continue with Normal PRD selection.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions below stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n### Normal PRD selection\n\n1. If argument provided, find that PRD in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` or `docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/`. If found in backlog, move it to `wip/` under the **verified-move invariant** (core `SKILL.md` § \"Phase 0 invariants\"): confirm arrival, else pause with `site: \"mv_verify\"`; do not continue.\n2. Otherwise, auto-select (never ask the user). Run `autopilot select` (one Bash call). It reads `wip/` then `backlog/` and picks the lowest `00XXX-` sequence in the first that has one; it never scans `hold/` — `cli/selection.py`'s `select()` takes no hold argument at all, so the parked/deferred exclusion is structural rather than a rule to remember. It prints one JSON line, `{\"prd\": ..., \"source\": ...}`, and exits 0 in every case including drained. Do NOT list the lifecycle directories and re-derive the choice yourself.\n\n   | `source` | Action |\n   |---|---|\n   | `wip` | announce the PRD and resume it in place — no move |\n   | `backlog` | move it to `wip/` under the **verified-move invariant** above (confirm arrival, else PAUSE with `site: \"mv_verify\"`), then announce |\n   | `drained` | STOP: \"No PRDs found. Create one with /create-prd.\" (Loop mode: first write the drained state per the Error Handling row \"No PRDs anywhere\" — which also covers the case where `state.json` does not exist yet, since `phase-done` cannot advance a file that is not there.) |\n\n   `select` decides only. The move stays here on purpose — it is the one step that must be verified, and `autopilot stall`/`park` own the other lifecycle moves.\n\n   **Eligibility gate (PRD 00137).** Before returning a `backlog` candidate, `select` runs that PRD's `eligibility:` frontmatter command, if it declares one. Exit 0 = eligible. Anything else — non-zero, unknown binary, timeout, an unusable cwd — is UNMET, and an unmet PRD is **skipped, never parked**: the file stays in `backlog/`, gets no session, and `select` moves to the next candidate. A later drain re-evaluates it, so an unblocked PRD unblocks itself with no human `mv`. Mechanics: the command runs from the **project root** (the directory holding `docs/dev/project-management/`) under a **30-second timeout**, with output captured and dropped; the convention is **read-only checks only**, which nothing enforces — these strings are PRD-authored and run through `subprocess` inside the CLI, where warden never sees them. `wip/` candidates are never gated: the check decides what to START, and a PRD already in flight is past that question.\n\n   The JSON line carries a third field, `skipped`, holding one record per skip — `{\"prd\", \"command\", \"exit_code\", \"note\", \"at\"}`, `[]` when nothing was skipped. `note` names the failure mode (`\"timeout\"`, `\"error: <msg>\"`) only when the command never got to answer; those exit `-1`, which no shell produces, so \"the check said no\" is distinguishable from \"the check could not be run\". When `state.json` already exists, `select` appends each record to `state.batch.skips[]` itself and exits 2 (naming the failure on stderr) if that write fails; the pick is printed first either way, so a bookkeeping failure never swallows it.\n3. Initialize `batch` in state file if not already present: `id: \"<yyyymmddHHMM>\"` (current timestamp), `mode: \"autopilot\"`, `completed_prds: []`, and **`plugin_versions`** — a pin of the enforcement plugins' resolved versions so the wrapper can refuse to run the batch on rotated enforcement code (PRD 00086 R3). Read `aegis` and `warden` versions from `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (`.plugins[\"aegis@buvis-plugins\"][0].version`, `.plugins[\"warden@buvis-plugins\"][0].version`) and write `plugin_versions: {\"aegis@buvis-plugins\": \"<v>\", \"warden@buvis-plugins\": \"<v>\"}` via statectl. (Extend the pinned set if other enforcement plugins are added.) The `autoclaude` wrapper's plugin-pin preflight compares these at each relaunch and halts loud on any drift. On a FRESH batch, also seed `batch.skips` from the `skipped` list step 2 printed: that pick ran before `state.json` existed, so `select` could not persist it itself, and this is the one hand-off the CLI cannot make. Write it with `statectl` as part of this same `batch` initialization; an empty list needs no write. **Already present** means `state.batch.id` holds a string, not that the `batch` key merely exists: a `batch` carrying only `skips` counts as absent and needs an `id` minted, and that mint writes the new keys INTO the existing object rather than replacing the whole `batch` — never replace it, or the `batch.skips` already persisted there are destroyed. If `state.batch` IS already present, apply the **batch-identity rollover invariant** (core `SKILL.md` § \"Phase 0 invariants\") — mint a fresh `batch.id` only for a genuinely closed surviving batch; every normal in-progress resume preserves `batch.id` unchanged (and its `plugin_versions` pin); a fresh rollover re-pins from the current install.\n   A closed-batch rollover also clears `batch.unavailable_reviewers` and\n   `batch.unavailable_reviewer_details` in the same state update as the new id,\n   per the core invariant. Normal resumes and per-PRD transitions preserve them.\n4. Write the selected PRD's basename to `state.prd` **before** the frontmatter call. On a multi-PRD batch `state.prd` still names the PREVIOUS PRD at this point — `more_prds` deliberately preserves it, and Phase 9 already moved that PRD to `done/` — so anything reading `state.prd` here reads a stale name pointing at a file no longer in `wip/`.\n5. Apply the PRD frontmatter with one `autopilot frontmatter` call (below).\n6. Read the Active Work section of `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` if it exists. This contains PRD progress and operational context from previous sessions. Use it to inform work in this session.\n7. Update the remaining state fields for the selected PRD, preserve `batch` field\n8. Print progress:\n   ```\n   ── AUTOPILOT ── PRD {n}: {prd-name} ─────────────────────────────\n   ```\n   Where `{n}` = `len(batch.completed_prds) + 1`\n9. Write the `resume` handoff row, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site build --edge resume --phase build --prd <state.prd>`. Its gap to the previous session's `leave` row is the handoff latency nothing else measures; it is written after selection so `<state.prd>` names this session's PRD.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs these steps except step 6 — it makes no capsule read, so\nthe Active Work read stays this session's own (§ Enter in one call). The\ninstructions above stay the hand-run reference.\n\n### Frontmatter parse (step 5)\n\n```bash\nautopilot frontmatter --prd docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/<state.prd>\n```\n\n`<state.prd>` is correct here only because step 4 already wrote the selected\nbasename. Run them in that order, or a multi-PRD batch reads the PREVIOUS\nPRD's path, finds nothing in `wip/`, and exits 1.\n\nOne Bash call does all of it: parses the block, applies the Phase-0 defaults,\nwrites every resulting field to `state.json` in ONE transaction, echoes the\napplied fields as JSON on stdout, and prints any warning to stderr. Do NOT\nread the PRD and derive these fields yourself, and do NOT write them with\n`statectl` — `cli/frontmatter.py` is the single definition of which fields are\nrecognized, what values they accept, and what each defaults to.\n\nFields it recognizes and their state targets: `catchup`→`catchup_mode`,\n`rework_cap`, `design`→`design_mode`, `design_gate`, `doubt_reviewer`,\n`consensus_engine`, `pause_on_ambiguity`, `session_model` (the build\nsession's model, `sonnet` by default; PRD 00200). Three dispositions, and the\ndifference between them matters when reading the output: an **invalid** value\ntakes the default and warns naming the field; an **absent** field takes the\ndefault silently; a **malformed or missing block** takes every default and\nwarns exactly once. It never crashes Phase 0 on a frontmatter problem.\n\nFrontmatter is the source of truth; once Phase 0 has applied it, do not\nre-parse it after Phase 0. (Exception by design: `default_model` belongs to\n`/autopilot:plan-tasks` and is re-read from the PRD at Phase 6 rework dispatch — Phase 0\nnever touches it, and `frontmatter.py` deliberately does not recognize it. It\nfloors the per-task tier only; the session's model is `session_model`, which\n`cli/routing.build_model` re-reads from the PRD at every launch.)\n\n`eligibility:` is likewise not recognized here, and deliberately so: it is not\na state field. `cli/eligibility.py` reads it at **pick time** (step 2), one\nstep before this call, and its answer decides whether there is a PRD to parse\nfrontmatter for at all. Nothing about it reaches `state.json` except the skip\nrecords under `batch.skips[]`.\n\nSemantics the table cannot carry:\n\n- `catchup`: `run` honors the Phase 1 batch cache; `skip` bypasses catchup entirely; `force` ignores the cache at the PRD's first entry (no `state.tasks` yet) and reads as `run` on a same-PRD resume (PRD 00209).\n- `rework_cap` is consumed by the review gate's cap check (`references/phase-review.md` § Cap check).\n- `doubt_reviewer`: `fable` adds Eve to the review batch as a fifth lens; `codex` runs the standard roster.\n- `consensus_engine`: selects the engine behind Alice's consensus leg (`review-work-completion` step 1). `legacy` is today's single subagent; `workflow` makes the `review-fanout` workflow her leg; `shadow` runs both, with legacy gating and the workflow recorded as a non-gating observation.\n- `pause_on_ambiguity: true` — in loop mode a requirements ambiguity STALLS the PRD instead of being resolved by assumption; it never pauses the batch (see Phase 2).\n\nThe same call also classifies the PRD's effort lane (`cli/lane.py`) and writes `lane`, `lane_reason` and `lane_effective` in the same transaction; step 5.5 reads them.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions above stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n### 5.5. Route by lane\n\nRead `state.lane_effective`, which step 5 wrote beside `state.lane` and `state.lane_reason` (`cli/lane.py` decides; three lanes: `solo`, `fast-track`, `full`). When it differs from `state.lane`, print\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── lane: <lane> (<reason>), running full ──\n```\n\nThen branch on `state.lane_effective`:\n\n- `full`: continue to Phase 1.\n- `solo`: read `references/lane-solo.md` and follow it; Phases 1 to 3 do not run for this PRD. The runbook builds the PRD in this session, runs `autopilot lane-check`, takes one zero-context review pass and closes with `autopilot phase-done --outcome lane_reviewed`, or escalates into the full review gate with `--outcome tasks_done`.\n- `fast-track`: read `references/lane-fast-track.md` and follow it; Phases 1 to 3 do not run for this PRD unless the runbook falls back to full. The runbook renders one card per `lane.plan_cards` plan with `cards_from_prd.py` (an exit 2 there writes `lane_effective: \"full\"` and `lane_reason: \"uncardable\"` and continues to Phase 1), runs `/autopilot:fast-track` per card, consolidates the cards' tables into the review file and closes with `--outcome lane_reviewed`, or stalls a parked card with site `fast_track_blocked`.\n\nAn unreleased lane (one outside `lane.RELEASED_LANES`) always reads `full` here, with the `running full` banner above; the lane is still recorded in the session rows and the batch report. `_AUTOPILOT_LANES=off` in the loop environment forces `full` for every PRD.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this step; the instructions above stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n## Phase 1: Catchup\n\n**Skip if:** the batch cache is fresh (the batch-cache freshness check below holds — the capsule is already current), OR `state.catchup_mode == \"skip\"`. The skip is by ARTIFACT (capsule freshness), not `phases_completed` membership.\n\nWhen skipped via `catchup_mode == \"skip\"`: do not invoke `/git-ferry:catchup`. Set `state.catchup_mode = \"skipped\"` (so subsequent re-entries also skip), keep `phase: \"build\"` and `next_phase: \"build\"`, and proceed to Phase 1.5 (Design).\n\nOtherwise, decide between **full catchup** and **delta refresh** using the batch cache.\n\n### Batch cache check\n\nThe capsule (`docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`) is the persisted output of catchup: invariants, architecture decisions, GitHub state, project memories. Subsequent phases and their subagents read the capsule when they need that context — not `state.json`. Between PRDs in the same batch on the same branch, re-running the heavy gather phase costs ~60-95s and ~50K tokens with no information gain (`references/design-rationale.md` § Batch catchup cache).\n\n`state.batch.catchup_completed_at` (ISO 8601) and `state.batch.catchup_head_sha` (current branch HEAD when last full catchup completed) record the cache.\n\n**First-entry `force` rule (checked before the conditions below).** PRD frontmatter `catchup: force` overrides the cache at the PRD's first entry only, and ONLY when `state.tasks` is still empty or absent. A `state.tasks` that is not a list reads as absent (full catchup, the safe side). On that first entry, conditions 1-3 do not apply, condition 2's freshness check included: the result is delta iff a `batch.catchup_head_sha` is recorded AND every commit since it has committer `autopilot-loop/<batch.id>` (loop-only commits), full otherwise (including no recorded SHA, or a git failure).\n\n**Skip the full catchup and run a delta refresh** when ALL of the following hold:\n\n1. `state.catchup_mode != \"force\"`, OR `state.tasks` is a non-empty list (the first-entry `force` rule above covers the empty or absent case). Once planning has run for this PRD, this entry is a same-PRD resume (a task-boundary hand-off or a rotation, with the brief already read) and `force` is spent (PRD 00209): print `── AUTOPILOT ── catchup: force already spent on this PRD (tasks present) ──` and evaluate conditions 2 and 3 as for `run` — a spent `force` gets no loop-only shortcut of its own; a stale cache (condition 2) still returns `full` even when every commit since is loop-only, because condition 3's loop-only escape is reached only after condition 2 passes. Measured 2026-09-20: a forced re-run on a resume cost ~180K tokens and five minutes before the first task started.\n2. `state.batch.catchup_completed_at` is present AND less than 4 hours old.\n3. `state.batch.catchup_head_sha` matches the current `git rev-parse HEAD` on the active branch — **or**, when it does not match, every commit past `catchup_head_sha` has committer `autopilot-loop/<batch.id>` (loop-only commits): a moved HEAD that fails the exact-match test still reads delta in that case.\n\nIf any condition fails → **full catchup**: before invoking `/git-ferry:catchup`, run `autopilot catchup-probe` (one Bash call). Its `skip` list names which of `github-state.sh`/the `gh` commands, and `engram`, to omit this run — pass that list to `/git-ferry:catchup` as \"do not run `github-state.sh` or any `gh` command\" / \"do not run any `engram` command\" per entry. Write one gap line per skipped step in the capsule's relevant section (GitHub State / Related context), same as today's manual skip-on-failure handling, just decided before the attempt instead of after a failed one. Then invoke `/git-ferry:catchup`. After completion, write `state.batch.catchup_completed_at = <now>` and `state.batch.catchup_head_sha = <current HEAD>`. These fields persist across PRDs in the batch (Phase 9 step 10 preserves them).\n\nIf all conditions hold → **delta refresh** (no `/git-ferry:catchup` invocation):\n\n- Re-read all PRDs in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` (the active set has changed since last catchup; new PRDs may have entered, old ones moved to `done/`).\n- Update the Active Work section of `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` with the current PRD list (use the same format Phase 9 step 8 uses). Leave Key Invariants, Architecture Decisions, Component Boundaries, GitHub State, Project Health, and Project Memories untouched — those reflect batch-stable knowledge.\n- Print a one-line note: `── AUTOPILOT ── catchup: delta refresh (cache <Xm> old, HEAD <sha7>) ──`\n\n`autopilot enter` runs this check and returns its verdict as the `catchup`\ndecision; the instructions above stay the hand-run reference.\n\nAfter either path completes, proceed to Phase 1.5 (Design). Stay on `phase: \"build\"` and `next_phase: \"build\"`; do NOT add anything to `phases_completed`.\n\n## Phase 1.5: Design (build-gate sub-step)\n\nBetween catchup (Phase 1) and planning (Phase 2), in the SAME build session. Design turns the PRD's requirements (the WHAT) into a reviewed implementation design doc (the HOW) before tasks are planned. This is a BUILD-GATE SUB-STEP: `state.phase` stays `\"build\"`, there is **no** new phase enum value, **no** `phases_completed` entry, and **no** session handoff. The skip is by ARTIFACT (the design doc), exactly like catchup's capsule-freshness skip.\n\nLet `<prd-stem>` = `state.prd` with its trailing `.md` removed. The design doc artifact path is `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md`.\n\n**Skip if `state.design_mode == \"skip\"`:** do not invoke `/autopilot:design-solution`.
