Set `state.design_mode = \"skipped\"`, leave `state.design_doc` unset, and proceed to Phase 2. (This skip also bypasses the empty-review-log gate — no doc exists by design.)\n\n**Skip if the artifact already exists:** when `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md` is already on disk (a manual `/autopilot:design-solution` run earlier, or a work-abort replan re-entering the build gate). Log a one-line reuse note (`── AUTOPILOT ── design: reusing existing <prd-stem>-design.md ──`), set `state.design_doc` to that path, then **run the empty-review-log gate** (core `SKILL.md` § \"Design-gate invariant\") **on the artifact-reuse path** — an existing doc from a manual or aborted run is exactly where a skipped review hides — and proceed to Phase 2 only if the gate passes; do NOT re-invoke the skill. This artifact-based skip is what lets work-abort replans reuse the design with no extra logic.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs the design-doc existence check and its empty-review-log\ngate, returning the verdict as the `design` decision (a failed gate stops it\nwith `design_review_log_empty`); the instructions above stay the hand-run\nreference.\n\n**Otherwise, run design:**\n\n1. Invoke `/autopilot:design-solution` with the wip PRD path (`docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/<state.prd>`).\n2. **On success (exit 0):** set `state.design_doc` to the artifact path it printed (`docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md`). Log the design decision (chosen approach + any unresolved non-blockers from the doc's `## Review log`) to `state.autonomous_decisions` under the existing audit label `autonomous` — do NOT add a `design` audit label (the audit-log label set is closed). Then **run the empty-review-log gate** (core `SKILL.md` § \"Design-gate invariant\") **on the success path** before proceeding to Phase 2.\n3. **On failure (non-zero exit — unresolved cardinal sins/blockers after 3 reviewer dispatches):** treat as a sub-skill failure. PAUSE per the Error Handling table's \"Sub-skill invocation fails outright\" row — set `state.phase = \"paused\"` and `state.next_phase = \"paused\"`, write `state.pause_reason = {\"site\": \"sub_skill_fail\", \"detail\": \"design-solution failed with open findings\"}`, report the open findings, and do NOT proceed to planning.\n\n**Design gate (`state.design_gate == \"user\"`):** after a successful design (or an artifact reuse), and only when `state.design_gate == \"user\"`:\n\n- **Interactive:** PAUSE before planning — present the design doc summary plus any unresolved non-blockers from `## Review log` via `AskUserQuestion`, and proceed to Phase 2 only after the user answers. This is a mid-turn `AskUserQuestion` PAUSE; it does not end the turn, so no `phase` change is needed.\n- **Loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set):** there is no human to answer the gate — do NOT pause the batch. Follow the **Loop-mode stall procedure** (`references/recovery.md`) with `site: \"design_gate\"`, recording the design doc path in the deferred JSON `detail`, and continue the batch. On un-park (`hold/`→`backlog/`), the PRD re-enters the build gate and re-fires the design gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip — so a human resolves it interactively on the next manual run. (This is the new `design_gate` stall slug — `references/recovery.md` § Stall `site` slugs.)\n\nAfter design completes (run, skipped, or reused), stay on `phase: \"build\"` and `next_phase: \"build\"`; do NOT add anything to `phases_completed`. Then run the **gate-edge headroom check** below and, if it passes, proceed to Phase 2.\n\n### Gate-edge headroom check (design->plan and plan->work edges, PRD 00200)\n\nThe cap hook's headroom rule never fires between tasks (no task is in progress, so there is no task boundary to hand off at), yet a design step alone has used 249 calls and 338K before planning started (PRD 00187), which left the plan or the first task to die at the hard cap or the tripwire. So the build gate applies the hook's own rule itself at its two pre-task edges, with the first-task estimates: read `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/.turn-counts.json` with the Read tool and take `last.count` and `last.usage` (the hook's record of its latest fire: this session's tool-call count and context total). **Hand off to a fresh build session when `TURN_TRIPWIRE - count < FIRST_TASK_CALLS_ESTIMATE` (450 - count < 200) or `USAGE_CAP - total < FIRST_TASK_USAGE_ESTIMATE` (500000 - usage < 150000).** This edge deliberately stays unmargined: the hook's own `HEADROOM_MARGIN` (1.25x) guards a real measured last-task cost against task-to-task variance, but this pre-task check has no completed task yet to measure from and instead uses the fixed, already-conservative `FIRST_TASK_CALLS_ESTIMATE`/`FIRST_TASK_USAGE_ESTIMATE` constants, so margining an already-fixed estimate would not address the variance the margin exists for. The handoff is not a transition: `phase` and `next_phase` already read `\"build\"`, so run no `phase-done`; write the `leave` row `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site build --edge leave --phase build --prd <state.prd>` (best-effort), print `── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── headroom gone at the {design|plan} edge, handing off ──`, and STOP; the loop relaunches on the non-empty `next_phase` and the fresh session resumes by artifact (the design doc and the tasks that exist skip their sub-steps). A missing file or a missing `last` means the hook has not fired this session; continue. A null `usage` (no usage line in the transcript yet) drops only the usage comparison: the calls comparison stays in force. `last` always describes the running session: the hook rewrites it on every fire, including the fires a leftover `.cap-fired` marker de-duplicates after a rotation, so a dead session's exhausted values can never hand this one off. Interactive runs apply the same check and re-invoke `/autopilot:run-autopilot`.\n\n## Phase 2: Planning\n\n**Skip if:** `state.tasks` contains any pending or completed tasks (tasks already exist). This skip is by ARTIFACT (tasks exist), not `phases_completed` membership.\n\n### Replan mode\n\nBefore invoking `/autopilot:plan-tasks`, check for `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md`. Write it with `statectl` as part of this same `batch` initialization; an empty list needs no write. **Already present** means `state.batch.id` holds a string, not that the `batch` key merely exists: a `batch` carrying only `skips` counts as absent and needs an `id` minted, and that mint writes the new keys INTO the existing object rather than replacing the whole `batch` — never replace it, or the `batch.skips` already persisted there are destroyed. If `state.batch` IS already present, apply the **batch-identity rollover invariant** (core `SKILL.md` § \"Phase 0 invariants\") — mint a fresh `batch.id` only for a genuinely closed surviving batch; every normal in-progress resume preserves `batch.id` unchanged (and its `plugin_versions` pin); a fresh rollover re-pins from the current install.\n   A closed-batch rollover also clears `batch.unavailable_reviewers` and\n   `batch.unavailable_reviewer_details` in the same state update as the new id,\n   per the core invariant. Normal resumes and per-PRD transitions preserve them.\n4. Write the selected PRD's basename to `state.prd` **before** the frontmatter call. On a multi-PRD batch `state.prd` still names the PREVIOUS PRD at this point — `more_prds` deliberately preserves it, and Phase 9 already moved that PRD to `done/` — so anything reading `state.prd` here reads a stale name pointing at a file no longer in `wip/`.\n5. Apply the PRD frontmatter with one `autopilot frontmatter` call (below).\n6. Read the Active Work section of `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` if it exists. Update the remaining state fields for the selected PRD, preserve `batch` field\n8. Write the `resume` handoff row, best-effort (`work/references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry): `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/record_dispatch.py handoff --site build --edge resume --phase build --prd <state.prd>`. Its gap to the previous session's `leave` row is the handoff latency nothing else measures; it is written after selection so `<state.prd>` names this session's PRD.\n\n`autopilot enter` runs these steps except step 6 — it makes no capsule read, so\nthe Active Work read stays this session's own (§ Enter in one call). The\ninstructions above stay the hand-run reference.\n\n### Frontmatter parse (step 5)\n\n```bash\nautopilot frontmatter --prd docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/<state.prd>\n```\n\n`<state.prd>` is correct here only because step 4 already wrote the selected\nbasename. Do NOT\nread the PRD and derive these fields yourself, and do NOT write them with\n`statectl` — `cli/frontmatter.py` is the single definition of which fields are\nrecognized, what values they accept, and what each defaults to.\n\nFields it recognizes and their state targets: `catchup`→`catchup_mode`,\n`rework_cap`, `design`→`design_mode`, `design_gate`, `doubt_reviewer`,\n`consensus_engine`, `pause_on_ambiguity`, `session_model` (the build\nsession's model, `sonnet` by default; PRD 00200). +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_15","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; paths=[\\\"docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/00018-autopilot-controller-kernel-v2.md\\\",\\\"docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md\\\",\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/design-solution/SKILL.md\\\"]; [print(\\\"\\\\nFILE \\\"+p+\\\"\\\\n\\\"+Path(p).read_text()) for p in paths]'\"","aggregated_output":"\nFILE docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/00018-autopilot-controller-kernel-v2.md\n---\ndefault_model: opus\nmodel_tier_rationale: Extraction equivalence, public contracts and concurrent workflow authority require judgment.\nlane: full\nrework_cap: 3\nplan_expansion: allow\neligibility: ls docs/dev/project-management/prds/done/00012-* # link-ok: lifecycle output\n---\n# Autopilot canonical controller kernel and protocol\n\nSource: [three-layer design](../../designs/00011-autopilot-standalone-design.md). Recovery revision authorized 2026-11-09 by the request to finish portable Autopilot. Supersedes the held v1 for delivery, preserving v1 and its attempt evidence. No publication, live installation, source retirement or custody acceptance.\n\n## Overview\n\n### Problem Statement\nStandalone and supervised workflows need the same enforceable writer. The current tested writer lives inside OVCAQ; adding a second legacy backend would split authority.\n\nThe v1 attempt stopped during task 7 after prompt-size/replan exhaustion; tasks 1–6 and task-7 tests already landed. Reuse those implementations and evidence after characterization, not by marking new tasks complete from old checkboxes. Close the existing owner, recovery and capacity failures, then complete export and relocation. Preserve the old batch state and counters. Plan bounded tasks with the installed planner's normal budget; do not reuse the failed 40K budget, increase prompt caps or omit test/review roles.\n\n### Target Users\nUsers running Autopilot independently or through headless OVCAQ, and maintainers verifying the layer boundary.\n\n### Success Metrics\ncontroller_without_upper_layers → one installed writer runs without either upper layer. Named edge/error scenarios must also pass; real-host support requires separate probe evidence.\n\n## Functional Decomposition\n\n### Capability: Kernel\n\n#### Feature: Extract the existing writer\n- **Description**: Reuse tested transactional behavior without supervisor dependencies.\n- **Inputs**: Pinned OVCAQ state services and characterized source invariants.\n- **Outputs**: One packaged Python 3.12 controller and workflow store.\n- **Behavior**: Premise: OVCAQ state/store.py and schema.py implement atomic writes, locking and revisions. Extract the workflow kernel with attribution and equivalent corruption/lock/recovery behavior; separate process fields from workflow schema. Recheck current source before moving behavior. Never mutate live source state; no OVCAQ import, process launcher or TUI dependency.\n\n### Capability: Protocol\n\n#### Feature: Typed commands and actor fencing\n- **Description**: Publish the canonical controller boundary.\n- **Inputs**: Contract A in the design, scoped actor credentials and temporary project roots.\n- **Outputs**: Contract/snapshot/apply CLI, immutable export bundle and request receipts.\n- **Behavior**: Implement protocol-major 1 and exact envelope/errors from Contract A. Define JSON schemas for every core operation, including explicit fresh-open bootstrap (expected revision zero, workflow ID assigned once). Fresh workflow.open alone permits null workflow/actor/epoch and revision zero on an absent store. Bootstrap creates an operator credential under the private state root (directory 0700, file 0600) and returns only its path. Other apply calls require --actor-file PATH matched to actor ID/scope; credentials never appear in command values or logs. Opening an existing workflow is not an ownership bypass. One execution lease, epoch-fenced job/operator credentials, CAS, identical-payload replay, conflicting-ID refusal and path containment. Bound output/time in clients; no credential values in logs. Publish only implemented kernel operations; later families remain declared but unavailable. CLI: `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`, `--actor-file PATH`. Contract output: protocol_major=1, package_version, schema_digest, fixture_digest, operations, capabilities; capability IDs workflow.core.v1, workflow.jobs.v1, workflow.reviews.v1, workflow.records.v1 and optional workflow.waves.v1. Envelope fields: protocol_major, operation, request_id, expected_revision, project_id, workflow_id, actor_id, job_id (nullable for operator actions), lease_epoch, payload. Response fields: ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable. Error codes, exactly: invalid_request, incompatible_contract, revision_conflict, wrong_binding, missing_capability, rejected_evidence, recovery_required. Closed operations: workflow.open, policy.bind, owner.acquire/release/recover, prd.enter, task.replace/start/finish/attempt, lane.route, job.plan/claim/record_exit, review.record_stage/close, custody.record/discharge, verification.record, phase.handoff, prd.stall/park/defer/complete, artifact.record, records.commit, plus the optional wave operations.\n\nContract A bundle for OVCAQ: commit `plugins/autopilot/contracts/controller-v1.json` as a regular file (no symlink in its path, under 16 MiB). It is a strict JSON object (no duplicate keys, no NaN/Infinity) with exactly these keys: protocol_major (int 1), package_version (nonempty str, the plugin manifest version), schema_digest (nonempty str), fixture_digest (nonempty str), operations (list of str), capabilities (list of str). `python3 controller/main.py --json contract` returns the same protocol_major, schema_digest and fixture_digest, a package_version equal to the bundle's or the bundle's plus `+<build>`, and operations/capabilities that are supersets of the bundle's lists. Document the `sha256sum plugins/autopilot/contracts/controller-v1.json` output (sha256 of the raw file bytes) in `plugins/autopilot/README.md`; OVCAQ pins path and digest as `[workflow] contract_bundle` and `contract_bundle_sha256`. The installed controller argv, stated once here and set by OVCAQ as `[workflow] controller_argv`, is `[\"python3\", \"<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py\"]`.\n\n## Structural Triggers on \"design solution\", \"design this PRD\".\nargument-hint: \"<prd-path> [--rework <review-file>]\"\n---\n\n# Design Solution\n\nTurn a PRD (the WHAT) into a reviewed implementation design doc (the HOW): module\nplacement, exact interfaces, data flow, reuse of existing code, and alternatives\nweighed - then critique the draft with an autonomous adversarial reviewer before\nhanding it to `/autopilot:plan-tasks`.\n\nThis skill runs **unattended** inside the autopilot build gate. It never asks the\nuser anything. It is **state-agnostic**: it prints the design doc path on success\nand, when unresolved cardinal sins or blockers remain, ends with an explicit\nFAILED report naming them (a model-followed skill has no exit code - the report\nis the observable signal the caller checks); the caller records the path.\n\nIt **never edits the PRD**. The design refines the PRD; acceptance criteria stay\nPRD-owned.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Own files: `references/cardinal-sins.md` (the severity taxonomy, inlined into\n  every reviewer prompt). It ships with this pack; `review-design-doc` keeps its\n  own copy for its own use, so edit the two together when the taxonomy changes.\n- Pack skills (files read at runtime): `use-codex` (`scripts/codex-run.sh`)\n- CLI: `codex` (review dispatch). Unavailable: fall back to the Claude subagent\n  reviewer documented in the review step\n- Optional: `~/.claude/rules-library/rationalizations.md` (host-local; supplies\n  the synonym sets for the reuse sweep). Absent: run the sweep with your own\n  verb/noun synonyms and say so in the sweep's summary line.\n- Optional: cartographer atlas `~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`\n  (skipped silently when absent)\n\n## Inputs\n\n- **PRD path** (argument). If omitted, auto-select the single PRD in\n  `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`. Error and stop if `wip/` holds zero or 2+ PRDs\n  (\"ambiguous - pass the PRD path explicitly\").\n- **Rework mode** (`--rework <review-file>`): design one review cycle's\n  CRITICAL fixes instead of the PRD's first implementation - see\n  `## Rework mode`.\n- **Architecture context**, loaded when present (skip silently if absent):\n  - the cartographer atlas for this repo\n    (`~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`)\n  - `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`\n  - `AGENTS.md` / `agent_docs/`\n\n## Output\n\n`docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md`, where `<prd-stem>` is the PRD filename\nminus its `.md` extension. Create `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` if missing - it is a\ndurable artifact dir, like `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/`.\n\nIn rework mode the output is `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md`,\nwhere `<cycle>` is the review file's `review:` frontmatter value.\n\n## Rework mode\n\n`/autopilot:design-solution <prd-path> --rework <review-file>` designs one\nreview cycle's CRITICAL fixes (PRD 00194). `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6\ninvokes it once per cycle, before any fix task is created. Steps 1-5 run as\nin default mode except where a bullet below says otherwise.\n\n- **Inputs** (step 1): the PRD, plus from `<review-file>`: `<cycle>` = its\n  `review:` frontmatter value, and the CRITICAL rows = every\n  `## Consolidated Findings` table row whose Severity cell is `🔴 Critical`.\n  `<work_start_sha>` = the left side of the `Diff range:` line in the cycle-1\n  review file beside it, `<prd-stem>-review-1.md` (or `-review-01.md`) - under\n  autopilot that range is `work_start_sha..HEAD`, so no flag carries it. Run\n  `git diff --stat <work_start_sha>..HEAD` for the PRD's whole work range, and\n  on cycle 2 or later also `git diff --stat` over `<review-file>`'s own\n  `Diff range:` (the prior cycle's rework commits, the range the prior fix\n  changed); a `Diff range:` holding a single SHA `X` is read as\n  `X..<head_sha>`, `<head_sha>` being `<review-file>`'s frontmatter value. A\n  review file with no `🔴 Critical` row, or no cycle-1 review file with a\n  `Diff range:` line, is a usage error: print\n  `design-solution: --rework needs a 🔴 Critical row and a cycle-1 Diff range` and\n  stop without writing a doc.\n- **Output**: `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md` with the\n  same nine sections, same headings, same order as step 3, preceded by one\n  source line directly under the H1 title, exactly\n  `Source review: <review-file> (head_sha <head_sha>)` - the review file path\n  as given and its frontmatter `head_sha`. Phase 6 compares that line before\n  reusing a doc, so a design reviewed for one cycle's findings never supplies\n  the contract for another's. An existing file at that path is overwritten.\n- **`## Architecture fit` opens with a `Prior fix:` paragraph** -\n  what the prior fix changed and why it regressed, quoting the CRITICAL rows'\n  evidence and the files the prior-cycle `git diff --stat` names, and saying\n  whether each CRITICAL was introduced by that fix or only exposed by it. On\n  cycle 1 it reads exactly `Prior fix: none - there was no prior rework fix.`\n- **`## Interfaces & contracts` is the sole contract source** for the cycle's\n  CRITICAL fix tasks: Phase 6 copies it verbatim into each CRITICAL\n  `[D{cycle}]` task's `### Contract` block, so name every symbol exactly, and\n  open each entry with the 🔴 row it closes (`Closes: <row text>`) so a task\n  owner is readable from the shared block.\n- **Review** (step 4): the same three-dispatch procedure, the same 3-dispatch ceiling,\n  prompt package, minimum-engagement check and Claude fallback, unchanged. The\n  prompt additionally carries the CRITICAL rows verbatim so a reviewer judges\n  the fix design against the finding it must close.\n- **Terminal result line** (step 5): after the exit report is decided, append\n  its `result:` value as the last line of `## Review log`, unindented - exactly\n  `result: ok` or `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)`. The Review log\n  is the ninth section, so this is the doc's last non-empty line; Phase 6 reads\n  it as the pass gate. Default mode writes no such line.\n- **Exit report**: the first line is `design-solution: <prd-stem> (rework cycle <n>)`\n  and `doc:` names the rework path; the remaining lines are unchanged. Open\n  cardinal sins or blockers after dispatch 3 end the report with\n  `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)` exactly as step 5 describes;\n  the caller routes the failure.\n\n## Workflow\n\n### 1. Resolve the PRD and load context\n\nResolve the PRD path per Inputs. Read the PRD in full. Load the architecture\ncontext files that exist. Identify the capabilities and features the PRD asks for\n- these drive the reuse sweep and the interface design.\n\n### 2. Reuse sweep (before designing any new code)\n\nSearch the codebase (Bash `rg`; the native Grep tool is absent in this build,\nsee rules/tools.md) for existing helpers and patterns that already do what the PRD\nneeds, per the synonym sets in `~/.claude/rules-library/rationalizations.md` (when present)\n(\"Synonyms-to-grep\"). For each capability:\n\n- Search **both** the verb and the noun synonyms (e.g. `format` / `render` /\n  `serialize` AND `date` / `timestamp`).\n- If a search returns nothing, re-run it with a term you know is present to prove\n  the pattern works before concluding the helper is absent.\n\nRecord findings in `## Reuse inventory`: one entry per existing helper as\n**(path + how to use it)**, or, when nothing exists, an explicit\n`nothing found, greps tried: ...` line naming the searches you ran.\n\n### 3. Write the design doc\n\nWrite `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md` with **exactly these nine\nsections, these headings, in this order**:\n\n1. `## Architecture fit` - the target layers/modules this work lands in, drawn\n   from the atlas / capsule.\n2. `## Module placement` - which changes are new files vs edits to existing\n   files, with paths.\n3. `## Interfaces & contracts` - the exact signatures, types, enum values, field\n   names, file/hook kinds, and thresholds. Write these **verbatim-ready**:\n   `/autopilot:plan-tasks` copies them byte-for-byte into task `Contract` sections, so name\n   every symbol exactly.\n4. `## Data flow` - how data moves through the changed components.\n5. `## Reuse inventory` - from step 2.\n6. `## Alternatives considered` - 2-3 design options, the chosen one, and why.\n   One option must be the smallest-diff version of the idea; if the chosen\n   design is larger, say what the extra size buys.\n7. `## Risks & edge cases` - include the 2-3 likely next changes after this\n   PRD and anything in this design that boxes them in.\n8. `## Test strategy outline`.\n9. `## Review log` - start empty; the review loop (step 4) fills it.\n\nKeep `## Interfaces & contracts` precise enough that a planner who never reads the\nPRD could copy a contract verbatim and be correct.\n\n### 4. Autonomous adversarial review (up to 3 dispatches)\n\nCritique the draft with reviewers, then fix what they find. The review runs a\n**cross-model** loop: dispatch 1 is a fresh Claude subagent, dispatch 2 is a\n**mandatory codex** reviewer (a rival model catches the echo-chamber defects the\nauthoring model cannot see in itself), and dispatch 3 is a conditional codex\nverification pass. Ceiling: **3 dispatches**.\n\n**Each dispatch** sends the reviewer ONE self-contained prompt containing:\n\n- the current draft design doc, and\n- a short summary of the PRD (the problem + the capabilities), and\n- the **severity taxonomy**:\n  - the cardinal-sins list, inlined by reading\n    `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/design-solution/references/cardinal-sins.md` at dispatch\n    time (read it and paste its content into the prompt - do **not** copy the\n    list into this skill file; that file is this skill's source of truth), plus\n  - three-line definitions of the other severities:\n    - **Blocking** - a defect that makes the design wrong or unbuildable as\n      written; must be fixed before planning.\n    - **Non-blocking** - a real concern that does not block planning; record it,\n      do not fix it now.\n    - **Question** - an ambiguity a competent reader could misread; record it, do\n      not fix it now.\n  - the calibration rule: **not everything is a blocker** - overflagging dilutes\n    signal.\n\nThe reviewer returns findings only; it **never edits files**. Each finding has\nthe shape:\n\n```\n{severity: cardinal-sin|blocker|non-blocker|question, title, evidence, suggested_fix}\n```\n\n**Dispatch sequence:**\n\n1. **Dispatch 1 - Claude** (fresh subagent). Fix every cardinal sin and blocker\n   in the doc.\n2. **Dispatch 2 - codex** (mandatory, cross-model). It **always runs,\n   even when dispatch 1 found zero blockers** - that clean-dispatch-1 case is\n   exactly where a second, rival-model opinion matters most. Fix every cardinal\n   sin and blocker.\n   Run codex as a **direct background Bash command** (never a Task subagent - a\n   subagent that shells out to a CLI hangs), absolute paths:\n   ```\n   Bash tool (run_in_background: true):\n     ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-codex/scripts/codex-run.sh -f \"{codex_prompt_file_abs}\" -o \"{abs_repo_path}/docs/dev/tmp/design-codex-output-{id}.txt\"\n   ```\n   codex is **read-only** by default (no `-a`/`-y` -> `--sandbox read-only`) and\n   never edits files; the prompt is self-contained (the same package the Claude\n   reviewer gets), so no `-d`. Then wait with ONE foreground Bash call, the Bash\n   tool's timeout parameter set to 600000: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/await_reviewer_outputs.py --budget 570 <the -o path above>`.\n   On WAITING run it once more; a second WAITING is the deadline below. Between\n   the launch and the read of the `-o` file run nothing else about the lane: no\n   pgrep, ps, wc or sleep, no Monitor or ScheduleWakeup, no reading of the helper\n   scripts. Once that wait returns DONE, read the `-o` output file for codex's\n   findings.\n3. **Dispatch 3 - codex verification** (conditional). Runs **only if dispatch 2\n   found cardinal sins or blockers**; a fresh codex call is acceptable. Open\n   cardinal sins/blockers remaining after it terminate the review non-zero (step 5).\n\n**Claude fallback on codex outage.** If codex is unavailable - `codex-run.sh`\nmissing/non-executable, it exits non-zero, the timed wait ceiling trips, or its\noutput is unparseable as findings - degrade that dispatch to a fresh Claude\nreviewer subagent (identical prompt). Append, loudly, `dispatch <n>: codex\nunavailable, Claude fallback` before its summary line, and use the reviewer token\n`claude-fallback` in that line. **Never PAUSE on a codex outage** - the review\ncompletes unattended either way (mirrors Phase 8's codex-with-Claude fallback).\nThe fallback rule applies to every codex dispatch (2 and 3).\n\n**After each dispatch:**\n\n- Fix **every** cardinal sin and blocker by editing the design doc, then proceed\n  to the next dispatch (up to the 3-dispatch ceiling).\n- Append every non-blocker and question to `## Review log` (do **not** fix them).\n- Append a one-line summary of the dispatch to `## Review log`, in this **exact\n  pinned format** (one line per dispatch, so the run-autopilot Phase 1.5 execution\n  gate can match it with a single fixed pattern):\n  ```\n  dispatch <n> (<claude|codex|claude-fallback>): cardinal-sin <c>, blocker <b>, non-blocker <nb>, question <q>\n  ```\n  `<n>` is the dispatch number; `<c>/<b>/<nb>/<q>` are per-severity integer\n  counts; the reviewer identity token is exactly one of `claude`, `codex`,\n  `claude-fallback` (dispatch 1 -> `claude`; dispatch 2 -> `codex` or\n  `claude-fallback`; dispatch 3 -> `codex` or `claude-fallback`). A dispatch\n  marked WEAK by the minimum-engagement check below appends ` weak` to the end\n  of this line (after `question <q>`) — the Phase 1.5 gate pattern still matches,\n  it is not `$`-anchored.\n\n**Minimum-engagement check (mirrors review-with-doubt's \"fewer than 3 doubts = look harder\").** A rubber-stamp review is worse than none — it reads as coverage that never happened. After a substantive dispatch (1, 2, or a dispatch-3 that ran), test it for engagement: it is **under-engaged** when it returns **fewer than 3 total findings** OR **not one finding anchors to a specific design-doc section or `file:symbol`** (real design review cites where — e.g. \"`## Interfaces & contracts` declares `foo(x: int)` but the PRD says `str`\"). On under-engagement, **re-dispatch that same reviewer ONCE** with a sharper prompt: name the specific sections/interfaces/modules it must inspect and require every finding — and every \"checked, correct\" note — to cite a doc section or `file:symbol`. This engagement re-run is a per-dispatch quality retry (capped at one per dispatch); it does **not** consume the 3-dispatch cross-model ceiling, so the mandatory codex dispatch still runs. If the re-run **still** shows no section-anchored evidence (it could not show it engaged), mark that dispatch **WEAK**: append ` weak` to its `## Review log` line and list it in the exit report. WEAK is advisory — it flags low confidence, it does not by itself fail the review. A thorough zero-blocker review that cites the sections it verified is NOT weak; engagement, not raw finding count, is the test after the re-run.\n\nBound each codex dispatch with a concrete deadline, not an open-ended wait.\nIf the second wait call above still returns WAITING, treat the dispatch as a\ncodex outage and take the Claude fallback above. A hung reviewer must never\nblock an unattended run (the autopilot session wall-clock cap is the\nbackstop).\n\n### 5. Terminate\n\n- **All cardinal sins and blockers resolved** (or none found): print the design\n  doc path and the exit report, exit 0.\n- **A cardinal sin or blocker is still open after dispatch 3**: print the design\n  doc path, list every open cardinal-sin / blocker finding, print the exit\n  report, and **exit non-zero**. The caller (autopilot) treats this as a\n  sub-skill failure and PAUSEs; a manual run surfaces the open findings to the\n  user.\n\n## Exit report (always printed)\n\n```\ndesign-solution: <prd-stem>\n  doc: docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md\n  reviewer dispatches: <n>/3\n  findings: cardinal-sin <c>, blocker <b>, non-blocker <nb>, question <q>\n  open cardinal sins/blockers: <none, or a list>\n  weak dispatches: <none, or a list of dispatch numbers flagged by the minimum-engagement check>\n  result: ok | failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)\n```\n\nThe exit report always lists the iteration count (reviewer dispatches) and the\nper-severity finding counts.\n\nIn rework mode the first line reads `design-solution: <prd-stem> (rework cycle <n>)`.\n\n## Notes\n\n- One reviewer dispatch per loop iteration; never two in flight at once.\n- The skill writes only the design doc (and creates `docs/dev/project-management/designs/`). It\n  never edits the PRD, the task list, or autopilot state.\n- Downstream blind review and doubt review stay PRD-only by design; this design\n  doc feeds `/autopilot:plan-tasks` and the work-completion review, not the spec-only\n  surfaces.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_18","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/git-ferry/0.5.1/skills/catchup/SKILL.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: catchup\ndescription: Use when starting work on a project and need local branch/repo context (full diff, GitHub state, capsule refresh). Triggers on \"catchup\", \"catch up\", \"catch-up\", \"what changed on this branch\", \"project overview\", \"refresh capsule\".\n---\n\n# Catch Up\n\nHydrate context before starting work. Load raw sources directly. The capsule captures derived insight (invariants, decisions, health signals), not paraphrases of files you can read.\n\nLoad generously, but the diff and changed files are the priority. On a clearly huge branch, fall back to a stat-only pass rather than blowing the context window.\n\n## Phase 1: Gather (run concurrently)\n\nRun the scripts and read the files in parallel; don't serialize.\n\n**Scripts** (skip on failure, note the gap):\n\n```bash\n\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/branch-diff.sh\"   # skip if on master\n\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/github-state.sh\"  # skip if no gh / no remote\n\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/load-memories.sh\" # skip if no memories\n```\n\nIf a script fails, read it and run its git/gh commands directly.\n\n**Sources** (read each if it exists):\n\n- `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` / `GEMINI.md` — **first**. They may define project-specific catchup rules, priority areas, or \"always check X\" constraints. Follow any project catchup checklist in addition to this workflow, and let these rules shape what you flag in Phase 5.\n- `README.md`, `agent_docs/*`, PRDs in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`\n- Build/config: `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `pyproject.toml`, `go.mod`, `Makefile`, etc.\n- Top 3 levels of `src/`/`lib/`/`app/`; domain model dirs (`models/`, `types/`, `schemas/`, `entities/`)\n- `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md` (prior invariants/health), `docs/dev/project-management/meta/decisions.md`, `docs/dev/project-management/meta/troubleshooting.md`, `~/.claude/decisions.md`. These keepers live in `docs/dev/project-management/meta/`; if `meta/` has no copy, read the older `dev/local/meta/<name>`, then `dev/local/<name>`, instead (unmigrated store).\n\n**Recent master:**\n\n```bash\ngit log --oneline -20 master\n```\n\n**Review harvest** (skip on failure, note the gap):\n\nHarvest this repo's review files into engram, best-effort, so their findings survive once those files are garbage-collected. Skip if `engram` is not on PATH, or if a glob below matches no files.\n\n```bash\nengram harvest docs/dev/project-management/reviews/*.md docs/dev/tmp/*review*.md\n```\n\n**Related context** (never silently absent — on any failure, write the section with a one-line gap note):\n\nRetrieve prior work related to what this session is about, so the capsule can point at it. If `engram` is not on PATH, skip the commands — but still write the section, saying engram was unavailable.\n\nBuild ONE topic string from what the session is already about: the current branch name (drop the `feature/`-style prefix and turn separators into spaces) plus, when `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` holds exactly one PRD, that PRD's title (its first `# ` heading). On master with no single wip PRD there is no topic: skip the queries rather than searching a branch name that says nothing, and record that as the gap note. Do not drop the section — \"no topic this session\" is itself worth telling the reader, and on a master-default workflow it is the common case.\n\n**The topic is untrusted input.** It is built from a branch name and a PRD title, either of which can contain `\"`, a backtick, or `$(`. Never paste it into a double-quoted shell string. Put it in a variable and pass that variable quoted, so the shell treats it as one literal argument:\n\n```bash\ntopic='<topic>'                                # single quotes; escape any literal ' in the topic\nengram index                                   # refresh this repo first (defaults to --scope repo)\nengram query --scope repo \"$topic\" -k 5\nengram query --scope portfolio \"$topic\" -k 5\nengram status --scope portfolio                # staleness of the widest scope you queried\n```\n\n`engram index` refreshes the repo scope only, so the portfolio hits may come from an older index — that is what the staleness stamp in the capsule section records. Ask `status` for `--scope portfolio` so the stamp actually covers the portfolio query above it; a repo-scoped stamp would describe a narrower scope than the hits it sits under. A nonzero `engram status` means stale or dead rows; report the stamp, don't hide it.\n\n## Phase 2: Branch context (feature branches only, skip on master)\n\nAfter `branch-diff.sh`, load the full picture:\n\n```bash\ngit diff $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD             # full diff, don't sample\ngit diff $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD --name-only # then read each changed file in full\n```\n\nThe diff shows what changed; the full file shows how it fits.\n\n**Blast radius:** for each changed file, trace its consumers (imports + call sites of any changed symbol) to surface ripple effects the diff alone won't show. Prefer `ast-grep`/`sg` over text grep — it won't false-positive on comments or strings. Read any consumer that looks impacted; always trace consumers of changed utilities, types, and interfaces.\n\n**The \"why\":** extract issue/PR references (`#NNN`, `fixes #NNN`) from branch commit messages and load full bodies:\n\n```bash\ngit log $(git merge-base origin/master HEAD)..HEAD --format=\"%B\"\ngh issue view {number} --json title,body,labels,state,comments\ngh pr view --json title,body,comments,reviews   # if an open PR exists\n```\n\n## Phase 3: Synthesize\n\nUpdate or create `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`, creating `meta/` if absent. Write there even when an older `dev/local/meta/project-capsule.md` or `dev/local/project-capsule.md` is what you read. It is NOT a summary of what you read — it captures cross-file insight no single file holds.\n\n```markdown\n# Project Capsule: {project name}\n\nGenerated: {date}\n\n## Key Invariants\n{domain rules, boundaries, data-flow constraints; implicit/undocumented rules; what agents most often get wrong}\n\n## Architecture Decisions\n{why it's structured this way; tradeoffs; patterns that look wrong but are intentional}\n\n## Component Boundaries\n{what talks to what; which modules own which data; where the seams are}\n\n## Active Work\n{current branch purpose, PRDs in wip/, recent focus; if autopilot batch active: completed/remaining PRDs, cycle counts}\n\n## Related context\n{engram hits for this session's topic, from Phase 1. Repo hits first, then portfolio. One line per hit: `file:line — score`, plus a half-line on why it is relevant. End with the topic queried and the staleness stamp from `engram status --scope portfolio`. Always write this section: when there were no hits, no topic, or engram was unavailable, say so in one line instead — a silently missing section reads as \"nothing related exists\", which is a different and wrong claim}\n\n## GitHub State\n{open issues + notable ones; open/stale PRs; active/orphaned branches; latest release + unreleased commits; failing/recurring CI}\n\n## Project Health\n{is CI green? are PRs flowing? is debt accumulating? risks or blockers}\n\n## Project Memories\n{gotchas, patterns, feedback from memory files — omit section entirely if none}\n```\n\nRules: don't restate README/CLAUDE.md/config (already in context). Focus on cross-file insight (\"auth assumes X because Y\", not \"auth is in src/auth/\"). Update changed sections, leave accurate ones alone. First-time capsule: leave Architecture/Health sparse, they fill in over sessions.\n\n## Phase 4: Restore tasks\n\nAuto-restore the task list from the most-recent prior session. No prompt; silent if nothing to restore.\n\n```bash\n\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/list-task-sessions.sh\"   # JSON: {\"sessions\":[...]} or {\"error\":...}\n```\n\nHandle the result:\n\n- `{\"sessions\": [...]}` non-empty → take `sessions[0].sessionId` (most recent with tasks), proceed below.\n- Empty `sessions`, or `error` in (`no_project_data`, `no_tasks_dir`, `no_index`) → skip Phase 4 silently.\n- `error` is `schema_unexpected` or `index_unreadable` → **do not skip silently.** Claude Code's on-disk layout drifted and the script can no longer find tasks. Flag it in the Phase 5 report: \"task restore disabled — `list-task-sessions.sh` needs updating (`{detail}`).\"\n\nWhen proceeding, dump the chosen session:\n\n```bash\n\"${CLAUDE_SKILL_DIR}/scripts/dump-tasks.sh\" <sessionId>   # JSON array of {id,subject,description,activeForm,status,blocks,blockedBy}\n```\n\nFor each task in original `id` order: call `TaskCreate` with `subject`, `description`, `activeForm`. Then for any task with non-empty `blockedBy`, call `TaskUpdate` with `addBlockedBy`. Do NOT restore `status` — every restored task starts pending so the new session re-evaluates progress.\n\nNote in the Phase 5 report: `Restored N tasks from session {sessionId-short} ({modified-date})`.\n\n## Phase 5: Report\n\nSummarize what you loaded and learned. Flag:\n\n- **Gaps**: missing arch docs, no tests, unclear boundaries\n- **Risks**: failing CI, stale PRs, dependency/security advisories\n- **Blast radius**: impacted files not on the branch (reverse deps), open PRs touching the same areas\n- **CI status**: if red, include the specific errors/stack traces, not just \"CI is red\"\n- **Linked context**: issues/decisions explaining why current work exists\n- **AGENTS.md flags**: project rules/priorities that should guide upcoming work\n- **Suggestions**: things to address before starting new work\n\n## Capsule maintenance during work\n\nUpdate the capsule when you discover something that belongs there (new invariant, architecture decision, clarified boundary, PRD moved/started). Keep it surgical: change the section, bump the date, move on. GitHub State is refreshed only on catchup runs, not during work.\n\n## Error handling\n\n| Situation | Action |\n|-----------|--------|\n| On master, no capsule | Load sources + GitHub state, generate capsule, skip branch diff |\n| On master, capsule exists | Load sources, update stale capsule sections |\n| No remote | Use local master as base for branch diff |\n| Detached HEAD | Report current commit, ask user for base branch |\n| Not a git repo | Load sources only, skip all git/GitHub operations |\n| `gh` missing/unauthenticated, no GitHub remote, or rate limited | Skip GitHub state, note gap in report |\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

No plugins are published yet.\n\n| Plugin | Purpose | Version |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| [autopilot](plugins/autopilot/README.md) | Gated review-contract foundation; no host certification or publication. | 0.10.0 |\n\n## Portable scope\n\nAgent Plugins v1 standardizes two portable component types:\n\n- Agent Skills at `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.\n- MCP servers in an optional root `mcp.json`.\n\nCustom agents, commands, hooks, rules, and LSP servers are not portable v1\ncomponents. Keep those in a client-documented reverse-domain extension such as\n`com.github.copilot/`, or in that client's compatibility package. Never add\nclient-only fields directly to the closed portable `plugin.json` schema.\n\n## Repository layout\n\n```text\n.\n├── plugins/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/\n│       ├── plugin.json\n│       ├── README.md\n│       ├── CHANGELOG.md\n│       ├── skills/\n│       │   └── <skill-name>/\n│       │       ├── SKILL.md\n│       │       ├── scripts/       # optional\n│       │       ├── references/    # optional\n│       │       └── assets/        # optional\n│       ├── mcp.json               # optional\n│       └── <reverse.domain.client>/ # optional client extension\n├── templates/example-plugin/\n├── scripts/\n│   ├── validate.py\n│   └── test_validate.py\n├── tools/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/             # maintainer tools, never shipped\n├── tests/\n│   └── <plugin-name>/             # maintainer tests, never shipped\n├── .agents/skills/                # maintainer-only skills, never shipped\n└── .github/\n    ├── workflows/validate.yml\n    └── dependabot.yml\n```\n\nEvery plugin must be usable as though its directory were distributed alone.\nDo not reference files above the plugin root or use symlinks that resolve\noutside it.\n\n`plugins/specflow/` is specflow's only distributable root. Its maintainer\ntools, tests, skills, and scratch files stay outside it, in `tools/specflow/`,\n`tests/specflow/`, `.agents/skills/`, and `docs/dev/tmp/specflow/`.\n\n## Add a plugin\n\nStart from the valid example package:\n\n```bash\ncp -R templates/example-plugin plugins/my-plugin\n```\n\nThen:\n\n1. Rename the plugin and skill directories.\n2. Update `plugin.json`, including `name`, `version`, and description.\n3. Update each skill's `SKILL.md`; its `name` must match its directory.\n4. Remove the example skill or replace it with real instructions.\n5. Add `mcp.json` only when the plugin provides an MCP server.\n6. Document setup, permissions, data access, and a safe first test in the\n   plugin README.\n7. Record user-visible changes in the plugin's `CHANGELOG.md`.\n8. Validate the repository:\n\n   ```bash\n   python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts\n   python3 scripts/validate.py\n   ```\n\nThe repository validator enforces the pinned v1.0.0 manifest shape, names,\nportable layout, basic Agent Skills metadata, MCP transport configuration, and\npackage path containment. The published\n[Agent Plugins specification](https://agent-plugins.org/specification) and\n[Agent Skills specification](https://agentskills.io/specification) remain\nauthoritative.\n\nSee [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the publishing checklist.\n\n## Distribution\n\nAgent Plugins deliberately leaves installation and catalogs to clients. This\nrepository therefore has no invented \"universal marketplace\" manifest.\nClient-specific catalogs will be added only after that client is tested; if\nmore than one catalog is needed, they should be generated from the portable\nplugin manifests to prevent metadata drift.\n\nThe Claude Code catalog, `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`, is generated from\nthe portable manifests by `python3 scripts/generate_marketplace.py`, is never\nedited by hand, and CI checks it with `--check`.\n\nThe current list of implementations is maintained on the\n[compatible clients](https://agent-plugins.org/compatible-clients) page.\n\n## Security\n\nPlugin instructions and MCP servers can cause tools or code to run with the\nuser's permissions. Never commit\ncredentials in `mcp.json`, environment values, headers, fixtures, or examples.\nUse client-managed authentication and `${PLUGIN_DATA}` for writable runtime\nstate.\n\nReport vulnerabilities as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md).\n\n## License\n\n[MIT](LICENSE). +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_23","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc /Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/git-ferry/0.5.1/skills/catchup/scripts/load-memories.sh","aggregated_output":"--- autocodex-pause-recovery.md ---\n---\nname: autocodex-pause-recovery\ndescription: \"How to clear an autocodex clarification pause by hand in this repo (state CLI verbs, gitignored state.json, task-body refresh, codex wait false-DONE)\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: a511aef8-d874-4e86-847a-20d6d673106e\n  modified: 2026-10-27T20:44:26.530Z\n---\n\nRecovering a paused autocodex run (done 2026-10-26 for AP 00012 Task 2):\n`~/.config/autocodex/host.md` wants the fix made interactively, then an\nexplicit state-CLI resume, then `autocodex` relaunched by the user.\n\n**Why:** the wrapper exits immediately while `phase` is `paused`, and\n`state.json` is gitignored (`docs/dev/project-management/.gitignore`), so\nnothing but the on-disk state carries the resume; a wrong edit path (Write/Edit\non state.json) bypasses the single validated writer.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Fix the blocker in its durable home first (here: the design doc), run the\n  design-solution review loop by hand (Claude `Plan` agent, then\n  `codex-run.sh -f <prompt> -o <out>` in the background; the mandatory codex\n  dispatch), and end the `## Review log` with a `result: ok` line.\n- Task bodies embed the design's `## Interfaces & contracts` entries verbatim\n  between `Contract (verbatim):` and `Acceptance criteria:`, but ONLY the `###`\n  entries the task's Location files implement. Embedding the whole section\n  (55 KB in AP 00012) made every body 55 KB, Devon's prompt 69 KB against the\n  50 KB dispatch cap, and the replan then parked the PRD (a 110 KB reference\n  copy cannot fit the 75 K replan budget). Regenerate every pending body and\n  apply with `statectl.py <state> task-set-body <id> <file>` or Tess keeps\n  reading the stale contract.\n- Parked PRD + empty backlog: the build session drains (`phase: done`,\n  `next_phase: \"\"`, `prd` kept) and the adapter paused it as \"build skipped\n  the fresh review handoff\" until the hold/ exemption (2026-10-27). Un-park\n  with `mv hold/ -> backlog/`, set phase/next_phase build, del pause_reason,\n  restore `work_start_sha` to the PRD's original base, and pass planning\n  constraints with `autocodex --scope docs/dev/project-management/plans/<file>.md`.\n- Resume with the shim `skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state>`:\n  `set-contract-card <file>`, `set phase '\"build\"'`, `set next_phase '\"build\"'`,\n  `del pause_reason`; then `autopilot resume-target --state <state>` should print\n  `/work continues at first non-completed task N`.\n- `await_reviewer_outputs.py` returns `DONE` while codex is still reasoning (the\n  `-o` file is a streaming transcript that goes quiet); trust the background\n  task's completion notification or `pgrep -f \"codex exec\"`, and read the\n  findings from the last `codex` section of the `-o` file.\n- The autocodex session `.jsonl` and `autocodex-metrics.jsonl` are the\n  wrapper's own bookkeeping; leave them unstaged for its next state commit.\n- `site: commit_signing` (\"1Password: agent returned an error\", 2026-10-26)\n  means codex ran outside `~/bin/run-agent`, which swaps signing to\n  `ssh-keygen` + `~/.ssh/agent_github`; the `autocodex` shell function now wraps\n  run-agent (needs a fresh shell to reload). Recovery: make the exact commit\n  codex attempted from a run-agent Claude session (signature shows `G`), reset\n  `phase`/`next_phase` to `build`, `del pause_reason`, and leave\n  `stall_reason`/`task_aborts` alone so Phase 0 runs the overrun replan\n  (`resume-target` prints `replan: clear tasks, ...`). Any warrant codex filed\n  for the 1Password commit just expires (no deny verb; `warrant list` is\n  denied in the sandbox). Dotfile edits are sandbox-denied: patch a scratchpad\n  copy, `diff -u --label a/... --label b/...` into an mbox, warrant one\n  `git --git-dir=~/.buvis --work-tree=~ am <mbox>` with `--cwd ~`.\n\nRelated: [[review-work-completion-recipe]].\n\n--- autopilot-work-host-quirks.md ---\n---\nname: autopilot-work-host-quirks\ndescription: \"In autopilot work sessions here, a formatter hook reflows any file a subagent touches, and sonnet-run.sh Pat dispatch fails on revoked OAuth\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 82a9d050-1cab-4615-9f4f-8b28368a9436\n  modified: 2026-11-01T19:15:44.747Z\n---\n\nSeen 2026-11-01 (PRD 00013 build):\n- A formatter hook re-wraps (black-style, 88 cols) every Python file a subagent reads or edits, including already-committed test files. Before staging, `git diff --stat` the tree and `git checkout --` formatter-only churn; apply one-line test fixes with `sed -i` (retry once past the Echo hook) so the formatter does not reflow the file.\n- `sonnet-run.sh` (nested `claude -p`) exits \"OAuth token revoked\". Run Pat via native `autopilot:worker-opus` with `model: sonnet` instead; see [[host-tests-from-inside-a-session]] for the setup-token route.\n- `git show <rev>:<path> --output=...` ignores `--output` and dumps the blob to stdout; never use it for large files.\n\n**Why:** each cost a retry or ~25K context. **How to apply:** check these before the first task of a work session.\n\n--- copilot-review-empty-verdict.md ---\n---\nname: copilot-review-empty-verdict\ndescription: \"Copilot PR review banner \\\"Needs a closer look\\\" beside \\\"No open issues\\\" means zero findings; count reviewThreads via GraphQL instead of reading the banner\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: reference\n  originSessionId: db85b09c-d05f-4b83-95e3-3066e8cdcce6\n  modified: 2026-10-19T06:45:16.586Z\n---\n\nOn PR 5 (2026-10-18) the Copilot review body opened with \"Needs a closer look / One or more issues must be addressed before approval\" and then said \"No open issues\" with a 407-row file table of boilerplate. There were no findings: GraphQL `reviewThreads { totalCount }` was 0, `pulls/5/comments` and `issues/5/comments` were empty.\n\n**Why:** the banner is Copilot's template header, not a verdict; reading the 47KB body or chasing the banner wastes calls.\n\n**How to apply:** check Copilot findings with one call, `gh api graphql` on `pullRequest(number:N) { reviewThreads(first:100) { totalCount nodes { isResolved path comments(first:20) { nodes { body } } } } }`. totalCount 0 means nothing to answer; do not post a \"nothing to address\" comment. See [[review-work-completion-recipe]] for the rest of the close-out.\n\n--- fix-guards-at-source.md ---\n---\nname: fix-guards-at-source\ndescription: \"When a user-owned guard hook misfires on a decided layout, the user wants it fixed at its source repo first, not bypassed for the session\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: feedback\n  originSessionId: e86cf29d-585f-4dee-8a0f-e3636f2af093\n  modified: 2026-10-02T20:57:34.641Z\n---\n\nOn 2026-10-02 the autopilot plugin's `enforce_prd_location.py` blocked every\nedit under `docs/dev/project-management/intake/` (decided 2026-09-27 for\nspecflow). Offered a scratchpad apply script (bypass), fixing the hook first,\nor batching decisions; the user chose \"Fix the hook first\" even though it\nmeant a cross-repo change mid-review.\n\n**Why:** a guard that is wrong stays wrong for every later session if it is\nonly worked around; the user treats their hooks as product code with\nfail-first tests, changelog entries, and releases.\n\n**How to apply:** when a buvis plugin hook blocks a path or action the user\nhas already decided on, fix the hook in its source repo (`claude-autopilot`,\n`claude-aegis`, ...) with a regression test and changelog entry, then patch or\nupdate the installed cache copy; do not route the edit through Bash or a\nscript to dodge the hook. Check whether an autopilot loop is running in that\nrepo first (`docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/`), since the loop stands\ndown on foreign edits. Related: [[specflow-intake-layout]].\n\n--- host-tests-from-inside-a-session.md ---\n---\nname: host-tests-from-inside-a-session\ndescription: \"How to run the real Claude Code and Codex CLIs for specflow host tests from inside a Claude Code agent session (setup token, nested sandboxes, marketplace installs, profile cleanup), learned on 00008 T-043 to T-045\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 64329de9-63ea-47cc-b4d3-8d5e2127e4ff\n  modified: 2026-11-01T19:11:37.555Z\n---\n\nOn 2026-11-01 the 00008 host tests (T-043, T-046, T-045) ran from inside a\nClaude Code agent session instead of the developer's Terminal.\n\n**Why:** the handoff assumed a Terminal run because a nested `run-agent`\nlaunch fails with `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`\n(exit 71). Nested `claude -p` itself works, as `sonnet-run.sh` already\nrelies on; only the nested Seatbelt fails.\n\n**How to apply:**\n- `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is absent from the session's Bash environment,\n  but `~/.local/secret/claude-setup-token` is readable from the sandbox:\n  a launcher script reads it with `$(<file)`, exports it (never prints it),\n  sets `CLAUDE_NESTED=1` and `_CLAUDE_NOTIFY_QUIET=1`, and runs\n  `claude --plugin-dir <abs plugin> --print ... --output-format stream-json\n  --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --allowedTools ...`. The pattern is\n  `docs/dev/tmp/specflow/hosts/claude-start-insession.bash` +\n  `capture-claude.py` in the 00008 worktree; the init event of the stream\n  holds `claude_code_version`, `model`, `plugins[]` (source `<name>@inline`\n  for `--plugin-dir`) and `skills[]` (`specflow:spec-workflow`). A 50-turn\n  skill run cost about 3 USD; a one-word `-p` probe about 0.7 USD.\n- Codex's own sandbox cannot apply inside the session Seatbelt: under\n  `--sandbox read-only` or `workspace-write` every shell command exits 71\n  with the same `sandbox_apply` error (probe it with `echo`). For a scratch\n  workspace run `codex-run.sh -y` (bypasses Codex's sandbox; the session\n  Seatbelt still confines it), forbid writes in the prompt, and prove it\n  with `shasum -a 256` of every workspace file before and after. The\n  `CODEX_SESSION_ID` recursion guard only fires inside a Codex session.\n- Codex plugin installs need no model session: `codex plugin marketplace add\n  <checkout|owner/repo --ref x> --json` then `codex plugin add\n  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json` in a fresh empty `CODEX_HOME`; Codex\n  reads `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` as written and copies the plugin to\n  `$CODEX_HOME/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/`.\n- Claude Code marketplace check in the developer's own profile: `claude\n  plugin marketplace add <checkout> --json`, `claude plugin install\n  specflow@buvis-agent-plugins --json`, `claude plugin details <id>`,\n  then `claude plugin uninstall <id> --json` and `claude plugin marketplace\n  remove <name>`; a folder marketplace reads the plugin in place (`plugin\n  list` says \"Read from: <checkout>/plugins/specflow\") and also writes\n  `~/.claude/plugins/cache/<marketplace>/...`. `claude plugin validate\n  --strict .` validates the root marketplace and advises a README install\n  line (`/plugin install specflow --marketplace <owner>/<repo>`).\n- `gh pr create --base master --head <branch> --body-file <f>` works with\n  the agent PAT; the Validate job finishes in about 30 s.\n- Kiro IDE's GitHub import (Powers panel, Add Custom Power, Import power\n  from GitHub, repository URL) has no headless form: it stays a developer\n  hand-off. See [[review-work-completion-recipe]] for the review side.\n\n--- repo-structure-plan.md ---\n---\nname: repo-structure-plan\ndescription: \"The user's \\\"AI-age repo structure\\\" plan overrides layout recommendations (skill homes, agent-private dirs, links); check it before proposing any\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: reference\n  originSessionId: 02e9b1bf-0c8a-4c00-b452-9fa698cc3aad\n  modified: 2026-10-03T18:57:40.381Z\n---\n\nThe user keeps a repo-structure design at\n`~/.kiro/crew/workspace/ai-age-repo-structure.md` (status on 2026-10-03:\n\"design, for review\", no code yet; the path is a Kiro Crew workspace and may\nmove). On 2026-10-03, during the specflow docs-review walkthrough, the user\npointed me to it after I had recommended committed symlinks under\n`.claude/skills/` and a plugin-owned `.kiro/specs` relink tool. Both\nrecommendations contradicted it and were withdrawn.\n\nRules from it that changed decisions here:\n\n- `.agents/` is the only committed agent config tree; `.agents/skills/` holds\n  the only committed skill copy.\n- No committed `.claude/`, `.kiro/`, `.codex/`, `.cursor/`, and no committed\n  symlinks to them (Windows `core.symlinks` problem). Agent-private dirs are\n  local, gitignored projections made by one idempotent `tools/onboard`.\n- `tools/` holds dev-only scripts; specs live in\n  `docs/dev/project-management/specs/`; decisions are meant to move to\n  `docs/dev/architecture/`.\n\n**How to apply:** before recommending where a skill, config file, link, or\nagent-private folder lives in a buvis repo, read that plan (verify it still\nexists and its status) and frame options against it. My interpretation, not\nthe user's words: treat it as settled intent even while marked \"for review\".\nRelated: [[fix-guards-at-source]].\n\n--- review-work-completion-recipe.md ---\n---\nname: review-work-completion-recipe\ndescription: \"How /autopilot:review-work-completion runs standalone on this specflow-layout repo (no prds/wip, no state.json), which lanes fail every cycle, how the rework after the walkthrough goes, and how a spec closes out once the loop converges\"\nmetadata:\n  node_type: memory\n  type: project\n  originSessionId: 633465ce-871a-420b-925a-f87699fb6773\n  modified: 2026-11-01T20:42:15.985Z\n---\n\nStandalone review cycles of spec 00004 (cycles 1-11, 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-14) ran with no autopilot state and no `prds/wip/`: the target is `docs/dev/project-management/specs/<spec>/requirements.md`, the design doc is `design.md` beside it, and tasks come from a hand-written `docs/dev/tmp/review-tasks-<id>.json` (copy the previous cycle's; all ten are completed since cycle 6).\n\n**How to apply:**\n- Stage with `python3 ~/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/<ver>/skills/run-autopilot/cli/__main__.py review-stage --cycle-id 00004c<N> --repo-root <repo> --tasks-json ... --prd ... --design-doc ... --roster alice,blake,bob,carl --since <prior head_sha> --replay-cmd \"python3 -m pytest\" --prior-findings ... --settled-ledger docs/dev/project-management/reviews/00004-artifact-state-contract-ledger.json --gate-command \"sh <repo>/docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/gate.sh\"`. It finishes in about 10 s.\n- Reusable tooling is saved in `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` (untracked): `gate.sh` runs the five CI steps from `.github/workflows/validate.yml` with `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1`, one log each under `gate-logs/`; `build_bob_retry.py <cycle> <base> <head>` builds Bob's inlined retry prompt from the staged files and those logs. `review-stage` cannot parse unittest counts, so compose the `Tests:` line from the `Ran N tests` lines (cycle 11 review: 12 + 52 + 304 = 368; after its rework the contract suite is 308).\n- The spec has no frontmatter, so `consensus_engine` is `legacy` and `doubt_reviewer` is `codex`; Eve stays disabled (no state file, no codex-implemented task record).\n- The Agent tool in this build has no `run_in_background` parameter; subagents run in the background by default. Dispatch Alice and Blake as `autopilot:alice` / `autopilot:blake` with `effort: high`, with a prompt that tells them to Read their rendered prompt file and follow it. Bob and Carl are background Bash. No Watcher (interactive session).\n- Bob's resumed-thread run refuses for lack of input every cycle (cycles 2-11; codex sandbox blocks reads: `sandbox-exec: sandbox_apply: Operation not permitted`; in 00006 cycle 1 the aegis Fact-Forcing Gate hook blocked his `cat` instead, same remedy). The inlined retry was 773 KB for 00006 (560 KB diff) and codex handled it in a few minutes. In cycle 11 the refusal was prose only, with no `[BOB] ⚪ Cannot statically verify` line, so the three-pattern rule did not match literally; treat it as the refusal (it is also the malformed-output trigger) and dispatch the pre-built inlined retry without `--resume-thread`. Copy the first output to `bob-output-<id>-first.txt` before the retry overwrites it. The retry overwrites `bob-thread-<id>.txt` with its own thread; stamp that one. His `[BOB]` lines were unbulleted in cycles 10-11; strip a `- ` bullet into a `-lines.txt` copy only when present.\n- Carl failed cycles 2-8 with copilot \"Authentication failed\" (exit 1); cycles 9-11 ran fine (exit 0, `gemini-3.8-flash`). Always dispatch him; on failure, one unchanged retry per policy, then record unavailable; nothing to latch standalone. His `-o` file includes copilot's tool transcript before the `[CARL]` line; the consolidator copes. In cycle 11 his shell ran the suite without `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE`, then `find . -name __pycache__ -exec rm -rf {} +` in the repo: check `git status --ignored=matching plugins tools tests` afterwards (00005 and 00006 left `__pycache__` under `tests/` and `tools/`; `git clean -X -d -f -- plugins tools tests` removes only those).\n- The engram pack fails with a readonly sqlite DB every cycle (in a worktree: \"not inside a registered repo\"); degraded, not blocking.\n- From 00005 on (2026-10-16), work happens in per-spec worktrees under `~/git/src/worktrees/agent-plugins/feature-specflow-<spec>`. `review-tools/` hardcodes the main checkout, so copy `gate.sh` and `build_bob_retry.py` into the worktree's `docs/dev/tmp/review-tools/` with the worktree path; CI has 7 steps since 00005 (adds `tests/specflow/rules` and `check_rules.py --area ...`, nine areas since 00006). The 00006 worktree already holds seven-step copies. A standalone cycle 1 in a worktree passes `--since <merge-base with master>`; the whole staging took 8 s and the four reviewers about 25 min (Carl last). `rg` skips gitignored `docs/dev/tmp/` unless `--no-ignore`. aegis blocks shell redirects into `docs/dev/tmp/`: send Carl's stderr to the scratchpad. Commit messages: aegis blocks `Co-Authored-By` trailers.\n- The pytest fail-first replay reports `subTest` failures as passes. Always do the unittest replay by hand: a detached worktree at the base sha, copy HEAD's tests in with `cp -R src/. dst/`, run `python3 -m unittest discover -s tests/specflow/contract -t tests/specflow/contract -k <name> -k <name>...` with bytecode off. The same worktree moved to HEAD (`git checkout -f --detach <head>`) serves mutation runs; remove it with `git worktree remove --force`.\n- `consolidate_findings.py` merges findings on the same file too eagerly: the \"two shared all-digit tokens\" rule fires on requirement IDs like `VAL-001.8` (ledger mis-dismissals, cycle 10), and \"matched only after suffix stripping\" merged two different `checks.py` defects at `:507` and `:528` into one row (cycle 11). Read the merge warning line and the Auto-dismissed block every cycle and split or restore by hand.\n- CI pins Python 3.10 while local `python3` is 3.14: OS-error edge cases differ (`Path.exists()` raises `PermissionError` on 3.10, returns False on 3.14). Probe with `uv run --no-project --python 3.10 python -I <script>`; the contract suite under 3.10 takes 4 s.\n- A ledger entry whose reason is time-bound (\"trial open\") keeps dismissing after the fact changes: cycle 6 restored Blake's Kiro-link finding after T-027 closed. Prune or update such entries when their condition ends.\n- A direct test run writes `plugins/specflow/skills/spec-workflow/scripts/__pycache__`, which then fails `test_script_runs_from_any_python_start_and_leaves_no_bytecode` and `verify_release.py`. Keep `PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE=1` (or `python3 -B` for probes that import the helper). `verify_release.py` also refuses modified tracked package files: commit the fix first, then re-run it.\n- Blake's F23 re-raises (placeholder and bugfix checks, deferred to 00005/00006) and the cycle-10 F10 scans are absorbed by the ledger every cycle; the script prints the placeholder entry's reason for the bugfix line. The consolidator only dismisses a blind reviewer's ledger re-raises when told so: `consolidate_findings.py --ledger <ledger> --ledger-dismiss blake alice:<f> blake:<f> bob:<f> carl:<f>` (00006 cycle 2: three of Blake's rows dismissed, each with the ledger reason).\n- `check_review_file.py` takes `--review-file <path> --require-codex-guard` (a bare path is a usage error). `--prior-findings` is inlined verbatim under \"### Prior cycle findings\", so write `docs/dev/tmp/review-prior-findings-<id>.md` as the prior table with a Disposition column (fixed, accepted, ledger) and the rework commits named; reviewers then verify fixes instead of re-raising rows.\n- A cycle-1 🟠 that gets fixed means an incremental cycle 2: `--since <cycle-1 head_sha>` (the diff then covers the review-doc, decisions, fix and outcome commits), `--prior-findings`, `--settled-ledger`, and Bob with `--resume-thread <cycle-1 thread>`, which refused for lack of input again (00006 cycle 2); the inlined retry for a 200 KB diff was 201 KB and took about four minutes. Cycle 2 staged in 6 s; the reviewers took 5 min (Alice, Bob retry, Carl) to 10 min (Blake). The lead may downgrade a reviewer's 🟠 with evidence (00006 cycle 2, F2 and F3), but ask the developer whether the downgrades stand before calling the cycle converged.\n- The pytest replay flags a coverage test of a branch that already existed (00006 F9's eight tests) as \"passes at base\": a fact, not a defect.\n\n**Rework after the walkthrough (cycle-10 and cycle-11 pattern):** one `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N walkthrough decisions` commit (minutes appended to the review file, ledger entries), then `fix(specflow): apply the 00004 cycle-N review decisions` (code, tests, CHANGELOG line under `### Fixed`, which is the last section), then `docs(specflow): record the 00004 cycle-N outcome`. A `design.md` edit adds a qa-log entry and a re-approval question; a module move that the design's placement text already covers needs none.\n- Write the tests first and run them with `python3 -B -m unittest discover -s tests/specflow/contract -t tests/specflow/contract -k <name>` for the fail-first evidence; a guard test that passes at base by design gets mutation evidence in a worktree at the fix commit instead.\n- Editing a helper module trips two hooks: the Fact-Forcing Gate on the first Edit per file (present in the message the importers from `rg -n \"from \\.module import|from specflow_helper\\.module import\"`, the affected public functions, and the data shapes, then retry) and Echo, which reads a moved function as a duplicate (the retry passes).\n- A finding that needs code moved out of a file the approved design places it in (00005 F2/F3, 800-line limit) means a design edit: ask the developer first (design edit + re-approval vs accept), edit `## Module placement` and the tree, add a qa-log \"Review NNNNN-01 design edits\" entry, fix, then ask the re-approval with blobs and canonical hashes from `hash --json`, write `.specflow.json` (fresh `code-baseline` over the placement paths), and `reconcile`. After the fix, re-read the placement rows against the real diff before recording the approval: in 00005 `checks.py` ended byte-identical to base, so its \"edit\" row was false and `__init__.py` was missing, which cost a second approval question. To register checks from a new module without a bottom-of-file import (E402 plus aegis's ban on `noqa`), import it from `specflow_helper/__init__.py`.\n- `uvx` cannot write `~/.local/share/uv/tools` under the sandbox; run ruff as `uv run --no-project --with ruff ruff check <files>` and `... ruff format --check <files>`. Four findings are pre-existing (`spec_text.py` SIM102 in `sources_value`, `test_checks.py` ISC004 x3).\n- Re-approval mechanics (00006, 2026-10-18): `validate_spec.py hash <spec>/design.md --json` and `... tasks.md --json` give `sha256`, `approvedAt`, `approvedCommit`, `upstreamSha256`; `code-baseline <spec> --paths <repo-relative paths...>` prints `approvedCode` for the placement files (19 for 00006).
