Triggers on \"design solution\", \"design this PRD\".\nargument-hint: \"<prd-path> [--rework <review-file>]\"\n---\n\n# Design Solution\n\nTurn a PRD (the WHAT) into a reviewed implementation design doc (the HOW): module\nplacement, exact interfaces, data flow, reuse of existing code, and alternatives\nweighed - then critique the draft with an autonomous adversarial reviewer before\nhanding it to `/autopilot:plan-tasks`.\n\nThis skill runs **unattended** inside the autopilot build gate. It never asks the\nuser anything. It is **state-agnostic**: it prints the design doc path on success\nand, when unresolved cardinal sins or blockers remain, ends with an explicit\nFAILED report naming them (a model-followed skill has no exit code - the report\nis the observable signal the caller checks); the caller records the path.\n\nIt **never edits the PRD**. The design refines the PRD; acceptance criteria stay\nPRD-owned.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Own files: `references/cardinal-sins.md` (the severity taxonomy, inlined into\n  every reviewer prompt). It ships with this pack; `review-design-doc` keeps its\n  own copy for its own use, so edit the two together when the taxonomy changes.\n- Pack skills (files read at runtime): `use-codex` (`scripts/codex-run.sh`)\n- CLI: `codex` (review dispatch). Unavailable: fall back to the Claude subagent\n  reviewer documented in the review step\n- Optional: `~/.claude/rules-library/rationalizations.md` (host-local; supplies\n  the synonym sets for the reuse sweep). Absent: run the sweep with your own\n  verb/noun synonyms and say so in the sweep's summary line.\n- Optional: cartographer atlas `~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`\n  (skipped silently when absent)\n\n## Inputs\n\n- **PRD path** (argument). If omitted, auto-select the single PRD in\n  `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`. Error and stop if `wip/` holds zero or 2+ PRDs\n  (\"ambiguous - pass the PRD path explicitly\").\n- **Rework mode** (`--rework <review-file>`): design one review cycle's\n  CRITICAL fixes instead of the PRD's first implementation - see\n  `## Rework mode`.\n- **Architecture context**, loaded when present (skip silently if absent):\n  - the cartographer atlas for this repo\n    (`~/.local/share/agents/cartographer/projects/<hash>/atlas.md`)\n  - `docs/dev/project-management/meta/project-capsule.md`\n  - `AGENTS.md` / `agent_docs/`\n\n## Output\n\n`docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md`, where `<prd-stem>` is the PRD filename\nminus its `.md` extension. Create `docs/dev/project-management/designs/` if missing - it is a\ndurable artifact dir, like `docs/dev/project-management/reviews/`.\n\nIn rework mode the output is `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md`,\nwhere `<cycle>` is the review file's `review:` frontmatter value.\n\n## Rework mode\n\n`/autopilot:design-solution <prd-path> --rework <review-file>` designs one\nreview cycle's CRITICAL fixes (PRD 00194). `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6\ninvokes it once per cycle, before any fix task is created. Steps 1-5 run as\nin default mode except where a bullet below says otherwise.\n\n- **Inputs** (step 1): the PRD, plus from `<review-file>`: `<cycle>` = its\n  `review:` frontmatter value, and the CRITICAL rows = every\n  `## Consolidated Findings` table row whose Severity cell is `🔴 Critical`.\n  `<work_start_sha>` = the left side of the `Diff range:` line in the cycle-1\n  review file beside it, `<prd-stem>-review-1.md` (or `-review-01.md`) - under\n  autopilot that range is `work_start_sha..HEAD`, so no flag carries it. Run\n  `git diff --stat <work_start_sha>..HEAD` for the PRD's whole work range, and\n  on cycle 2 or later also `git diff --stat` over `<review-file>`'s own\n  `Diff range:` (the prior cycle's rework commits, the range the prior fix\n  changed); a `Diff range:` holding a single SHA `X` is read as\n  `X..<head_sha>`, `<head_sha>` being `<review-file>`'s frontmatter value. A\n  review file with no `🔴 Critical` row, or no cycle-1 review file with a\n  `Diff range:` line, is a usage error: print\n  `design-solution: --rework needs a 🔴 Critical row and a cycle-1 Diff range` and\n  stop without writing a doc.\n- **Output**: `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-rework-<cycle>-design.md` with the\n  same nine sections, same headings, same order as step 3, preceded by one\n  source line directly under the H1 title, exactly\n  `Source review: <review-file> (head_sha <head_sha>)` - the review file path\n  as given and its frontmatter `head_sha`. Phase 6 compares that line before\n  reusing a doc, so a design reviewed for one cycle's findings never supplies\n  the contract for another's. An existing file at that path is overwritten.\n- **`## Architecture fit` opens with a `Prior fix:` paragraph** -\n  what the prior fix changed and why it regressed, quoting the CRITICAL rows'\n  evidence and the files the prior-cycle `git diff --stat` names, and saying\n  whether each CRITICAL was introduced by that fix or only exposed by it. On\n  cycle 1 it reads exactly `Prior fix: none - there was no prior rework fix.`\n- **`## Interfaces & contracts` is the sole contract source** for the cycle's\n  CRITICAL fix tasks: Phase 6 copies it verbatim into each CRITICAL\n  `[D{cycle}]` task's `### Contract` block, so name every symbol exactly, and\n  open each entry with the 🔴 row it closes (`Closes: <row text>`) so a task\n  owner is readable from the shared block.\n- **Review** (step 4): the same three-dispatch procedure, the same 3-dispatch ceiling,\n  prompt package, minimum-engagement check and Claude fallback, unchanged. The\n  prompt additionally carries the CRITICAL rows verbatim so a reviewer judges\n  the fix design against the finding it must close.\n- **Terminal result line** (step 5): after the exit report is decided, append\n  its `result:` value as the last line of `## Review log`, unindented - exactly\n  `result: ok` or `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)`. The Review log\n  is the ninth section, so this is the doc's last non-empty line; Phase 6 reads\n  it as the pass gate. Default mode writes no such line.\n- **Exit report**: the first line is `design-solution: <prd-stem> (rework cycle <n>)`\n  and `doc:` names the rework path; the remaining lines are unchanged. Open\n  cardinal sins or blockers after dispatch 3 end the report with\n  `result: failed (open cardinal sins/blockers)` exactly as step 5 describes;\n  the caller routes the failure.\n\n## Workflow\n\n### 1. Resolve the PRD and load context\n\nResolve the PRD path per Inputs. Read the PRD in full. Load the architecture\ncontext files that exist. Identify the capabilities and features the PRD asks for\n- these drive the reuse sweep and the interface design.\n\n### 2. Reuse sweep (before designing any new code)\n\nSearch the codebase (Bash `rg`; the native Grep tool is absent in this build,\nsee rules/tools.md) for existing helpers and patterns that already do what the PRD\nneeds, per the synonym sets in `~/.claude/rules-library/rationalizations.md` (when present)\n(\"Synonyms-to-grep\"). For each capability:\n\n- Search **both** the verb and the noun synonyms (e.g. `format` / `render` /\n  `serialize` AND `date` / `timestamp`).\n- If a search returns nothing, re-run it with a term you know is present to prove\n  the pattern works before concluding the helper is absent.\n\nRecord findings in `## Reuse inventory`: one entry per existing helper as\n**(path + how to use it)**, or, when nothing exists, an explicit\n`nothing found, greps tried: ...` line naming the searches you ran.\n\n### 3. Write the design doc\n\nWrite `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md` with **exactly these nine\nsections, these headings, in this order**:\n\n1. `## Architecture fit` - the target layers/modules this work lands in, drawn\n   from the atlas / capsule.\n2. `## Module placement` - which changes are new files vs edits to existing\n   files, with paths.\n3. `## Interfaces & contracts` - the exact signatures, types, enum values, field\n   names, file/hook kinds, and thresholds. Write these **verbatim-ready**:\n   `/autopilot:plan-tasks` copies them byte-for-byte into task `Contract` sections, so name\n   every symbol exactly.\n4. `## Data flow` - how data moves through the changed components.\n5. `## Reuse inventory` - from step 2.\n6. `## Alternatives considered` - 2-3 d\n---\nname: use-sonnet\ndescription: Use when running Anthropic Claude Sonnet via the native claude CLI (headless) for code analysis, refactoring, or editing. Triggers on \"run sonnet\", \"sonnet analyze\", \"ask sonnet\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the autopilot plugin skill; it ships its own helper script and needs the named model CLI on PATH. Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n> **Paths in this pack.** The helper this skill runs ships here, under\n> `~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/`. A path written as\n> `<autopilot-plugin-root>/...` is the exception: it lives in the autopilot\n> plugin, which ships the rest of the pack, and that step is unavailable without\n> it. Substitute the plugin's root yourself; never pass the literal marker to a\n> shell.\n\n# Sonnet Skill Guide\n\nSonnet is accessed via the native `claude` CLI (headless `-p`). The helper script defaults to the `sonnet` alias (latest base Sonnet) and exposes `-m/--model` for explicit overrides. This uses your Claude quota, not Copilot credits - never route Sonnet (or any model Claude already provides) through `copilot`.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Files read from other skill dirs:\n  `~/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md` - mandatory,\n  applies verbatim (see below)\n  - `<autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py` - optional,\n    for a deterministic reset-epoch parse of a usage-limit banner (see\n    \"Usage-limit banner\" below)\n- CLIs: `claude` (native, headless `-p`); `mise` for resolution\n\n## Dispatch Contract (shared)\n\nBackground dispatch and waiting (TaskOutput-only waiting), following up, error handling, and the always-use-`-f` prompt rule are defined once in `~/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md`. Read it before dispatching; it applies verbatim to this skill.\n\n## Usage-limit banner (claude backend only)\n\n`claude -p` is the one backend that can hit the **Claude usage limit** mid-run: instead of a normal result it returns a banner like `You've hit your session limit · resets 8:10pm (Europe/Prague)` (also `weekly`/`usage` limit; a stream-json run additionally carries a rejected `rate_limit_event` with a machine-readable `resetsAt` epoch). This is neither a task failure nor retryable — the quota is spent until the reset.\n\n**Detect** it by scanning the run's output / `-o` file for the same markers `detect_usage_limit.py` uses: `hit your (session|usage|weekly) limit` or `usage limit reached`, and `resets <HH[:MM]> <am|pm> (<tz>)` for the reset time. For a deterministic reset epoch, run `python3 <autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/detect_usage_limit.py --log <the -o output file>` — exit 0 prints the reset epoch (it parses both the prose banner and a stream-json `resetsAt`); exit 1 means no live limit.\n\n**On a hit:** mark the run **FAILED**, report the reset time in the run report (`usage limit; resets <time>`), and do NOT retry before the reset — a retry re-fails identically. Under autopilot the `autoclaude` wrapper already sleeps-until-reset at the loop boundary; a standalone `use-sonnet` run cannot wait, so it stops and surfaces the reset for the user.\n\n## Effort Policy\n\nThe wrapper passes `--effort` explicitly in every mode. Defaults follow the\nselected model: Haiku/low, Sonnet/medium, Opus/high, Fable/xhigh. Use\n`--effort high` for reviews regardless of the selected model. An explicit\n`--effort` overrides the tier default; invalid levels fail before launching.\nSession and user-global effort settings are not used as wrapper defaults.\n\n## Model Policy\n\n- **Default:** `sonnet` (latest base Sonnet). Use unless the user asks for a different model.\n- **`-m/--model` override:** pass a `claude` alias (`opus`, `haiku`) or a full model id (`claude-sonnet-5`). Opus costs more of your Claude quota - confirm with the user before defaulting to it for routine work.\n\n## Running a Task\n\n1. Select the permission mode required for the task; default to no special flags (interactive approval) unless edits are necessary.\n2. Assemble the command with appropriate options:\n   - `-m, --model MODEL` to override the default (`sonnet`); ask the user first if the override is a costlier tier (e.g. `opus`)\n   - `-f, --file FILE` to read the prompt from a file (preferred - avoids shell escaping)\n   - `-i, --interactive <prompt>` for interactive mode with initial prompt\n   - `-a, --allow-edits` to auto-approve file edits only (maps to `--permission-mode acceptEdits`; Bash and other tools stay gated, so an unattended agentic child can stall on a prompt)\n   - `-y, --yolo` for full permissions (`--permission-mode bypassPermissions`); REQUIRED for unattended agentic dispatches that must run commands. Note: a `-y` child runs with no warden or hook filtering\n   - `-d, --dir <DIR>` to allow access to specific directories (maps to `--add-dir`)\n   - `-s, --silent` accepted for compatibility (claude `-p` output is already clean)\n3. When continuing a previous session, use `-c`/`--continue` or `-r`/`--resume [sessionId]`.\n4. Run the command, capture output, and summarize the outcome for the user.\n5. **After Sonnet completes**, inform the user: \"You can resume this session with 'sonnet resume' or 'claude --continue'.\"\n\n### Quick Reference\n\n| Use case | Key flags |\n| --- | --- |\n| Read-only analysis | `-f prompt.txt` |\n| Interactive with initial prompt | `-i \"prompt\"` |\n| Auto-approve edits only | `-a -f prompt.txt` |\n| Full auto, unattended agentic (edits + commands) | `-y -f prompt.txt` |\n| Allow specific directory | `-d <DIR> -f prompt.txt` |\n| Resume recent session | `--continue` |\n| Resume specific session | `--resume [sessionId]` |\n| Scripting (clean output) | `-s -f prompt.txt` |\n\n## Helper Script\n\n```bash\n# Write prompt to temp file (see the shared dispatch contract), then run\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt\n\n# With auto-approve edits (Bash still gated)\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt\n\n# Override model (only after user approval - costlier tier)\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -m opus -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt\n\n# Full permissions\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -y -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt\n\n# Resume session\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -r\n\n# Capture output to file\nbash ~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -a -o /tmp/result.txt -f /tmp/sonnet-prompt.txt\n```\n\nRun `~/.agents/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh --help` for all options.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_31","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; paths=[\\\"docs/dev/project-management/designs/00018-autopilot-controller-kernel-v1-design.md\\\",\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/design-solution/references/cardinal-sins.md\\\",\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md\\\"]; [print(\\\"FILE \\\"+p+\\\"\\\\n\\\"+Path(p).read_text()) for p in paths if Path(p).exists()]'\"","aggregated_output":"FILE docs/dev/project-management/designs/00018-autopilot-controller-kernel-v1-design.md\n# Autopilot controller kernel and protocol design\n\n## Architecture fit\n\nAP00018 introduces the sole portable workflow writer under `plugins/autopilot/controller/`. It does not activate legacy skills or certify a host. AP00019 adds lifecycle/jobs, AP00020 review authority, AP00021 records. OVCAQ remains untouched. Extraction source is OVCAQ commit `cf8be72214a515c84ee42f0d8b30e65cc2a4ebb7`, inspected with `git show`, never checkout HEAD. All tests use temporary roots.\n\n## Module placement\n\nNew runtime files: `controller/main.py`, `controller/autopilot_state/{__init__,schema,store,paths,protocol,actors}.py`, relative to the plugin root. New bundle files: `contracts/controller/{workflow-v1,fixtures-v1,provenance}.json` and `contracts/controller-v1.json`. New maintainer exporter: `tools/autopilot/export-controller-contract.py`. Tests: `tests/autopilot/test_controller_{kernel,protocol,actors}.py`. Edit `plugins/autopilot/README.md` and `plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md`. Characterization/ownership/source-to-target maps live in `contracts/controller/provenance.json`; fixture inputs and expected outcomes live in `fixtures-v1.json`. No supervisor or launcher imports.\n\n## Interfaces & contracts\n\n### Kernel\n\nPython floor is 3.12; stdlib only. `autopilot_state.schema` exports `SCHEMA_VERSION = 1`, `MAX_STATE_BYTES = 16777216`, `MAX_COMMAND_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 2097152`, `MAX_STRING_BYTES = 1048576`, `MAX_JSON_DEPTH = 32`, `MAX_JSON_INTEGER_DIGITS = 640`, `SchemaError`, `ResourceLimitError`, `decode_json(text: str, *, source: str)`, `validate_state(value: object) -> dict`, and `new_state(*, repo_root: Path, project_id: str, workflow_id: str) -> dict`. Reject duplicate JSON keys, nonfinite numbers, bool integers, unknown owned fields and unsupported durable versions; validate before deep copying. Default review cap is 2. Reject process identity, PID, launcher, heartbeat, resource usage and TUI state as workflow fields. Model/session observations later arrive only as explicitly bounded workflow evidence, never execution authority.\n\nRetain source `StateStore(path: Path, *, boundary_hook=None)`, `read()`, `initialize(initial)`, `transaction(mutator, *, expected_revision=None, publication_guard=None)`, `restore(*, expected_revision=None, precondition=None)`, source exception names and six `DurabilityBoundary` values. Preserve source lock/read/publication guards, single-link regular-file checks, bounded reads, CAS under exclusive flock, deep-copy mutation, revision increment, fsync-before-replace, backup/state pair repair and create-only initialization. Keep one last-good `.bak` and `.lock`; failed validation/conflict/publication cannot change the pair. Restore is an offline forensic library primitive, never a CLI operation or a protocol recovery path. It requires readable valid current state and valid backup and refuses with BackupError unless backup lease_epoch, owner, actors and receipts exactly equal current and no credential-intent.json exists. Check these invariants under the same exclusive lock after decoding backup and before any pair publication; precondition(current) alone is insufficient. Only security-identical backups may be restored, with current revision +1. This deliberate tightening of source restore prevents epoch rollback, credential resurrection and receipt loss; characterize it explicitly. Test acquire followed by restore refuses with exact state/backup/credential bytes preserved, and a security-identical backup restore retains source revision and repair outcomes. Corrupt current state refuses with recovery_required and preserves bytes for operator forensic recovery. Never silently overwrite corruption. Test backup/restore and each injected boundary. Unsupported directory fsync refuses explicitly.\n\n`resolve_project_root(path: Path) -> Path` resolves an existing directory without ancestor workflow inference. The private controller store is `<project-root>/.autopilot/controller/`, directory 0700, with `state.json`, `state.json.bak`, `state.json.lock`, and `actors/`. Before creating any credential, create regular private `.gitignore` files containing `*\\n` in both `.autopilot/` and the private controller directory (parent 0700, files 0600; sibling archives are ignored too), refuse an existing incompatible or aliased ignore file, and verify a temporary Git repository ignores state and actor files. This is separate from the implementation batch's legacy state. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.\n\n### Protocol\n\nCLI argv is `[\"python3\", \"<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py\"]`. Request file limit is 2097152 bytes; snapshot/response output limit is 16777216 bytes. Use strict bounded JSON parsing. Exit 0 for success, 1 for structured rejection, 2 for argument misuse; never print credentials or untrusted request values in diagnostics. Operator job_id is null. Response is exactly `{ok, revision, result, error_code, retryable}`; success has error_code null and retryable false; failure has result null. They are non-negotiable because getting them wrong has asymmetric, usually irreversible cost:\n\n- No rollback plan for stateful changes\n- Secrets in config files, plaintext environment variables, or source code\n- Single point of failure on a write path, without explicit acceptance and justification\n- No identified human owner for production operation\n- No observability for user-visible operations (no way to know if it is broken)\n- \"We will figure it out later\" attached to a load-bearing concern (security, data integrity, observability, compliance)\n- Unbounded resource consumption with no limits, quotas, or backpressure\n- Schema changes without a migration plan\n- Vendor lock-in for critical infrastructure without an exit strategy\n- Authentication or authorization deferred to a later phase\n- Data deletion, correction, or export with no defined path (compliance trap)\n- Persistent data without a backup and tested restore procedure\n- Public API contracts without a versioning strategy\n- Hardcoded credentials, keys, or tokens anywhere in the doc or referenced code\n- Critical decisions made by acclamation without recorded alternatives or rationale\n\n\nFILE /Users/bob/.agents/skills/use-codex/references/dispatch-contract.md\n# Use-Model Dispatch Contract\n\nCanonical shared contract for the four dispatch skills: `use-codex`, `use-gemini`, `use-qwen`, `use-sonnet`. Each skill's SKILL.md keeps only backend-specific content (model/multiplier policy, flag quick-reference, prerequisites) and points here for everything below. When wording here and in a SKILL.md disagree, this file wins.\n\nEvery skill dispatches through its helper: `~/.agents/skills/use-<backend>/scripts/<backend>-run.sh` (backend: codex, gemini, qwen, sonnet).\n\n## Prompt Delivery\n\n**IMPORTANT**: Always use `-f` with a temp file for prompts to avoid shell escaping issues.\n\n```bash\n# Write prompt to temp file, then run\necho 'Your prompt here (can contain \"quotes\", parens(), etc.)' > /tmp/model-prompt.txt\n~/.agents/skills/use-<backend>/scripts/<backend>-run.sh -f /tmp/model-prompt.txt\n```\n\nPrompts pass via argument or `-f` file, never stdin.\n\n## Child Stdin Policy\n\nEvery headless child CLI invocation (the `-p`/`--print`/`codex exec` dispatch paths, plus preflight probes and the `mise env` PATH lookup) redirects the child's stdin with `< /dev/null`, so an unattended background dispatch can never hang on a child reading the inherited stdin (the PRD 00040 hang class). Documented exception: interactive (`-i`), bare `-r`/`--resume`, and `-c`/`--continue` invocations keep stdin - they legitimately need the TTY. Never dispatch those modes unattended.\n\n## Error Stream Convention\n\nUsage and preflight errors (missing prompt, missing prompt file, backend CLI not found) print to stderr and exit non-zero. stdout is reserved for model output and the tee'd `-o` run log.\n\n## Background Dispatch and Waiting\n\nA run-script call can run for many minutes. When you need to do other work while it runs, or you are inside an autopilot run:\n\n1. Dispatch the helper script with `run_in_background: true`. The dispatch tool result returns the task's output file path.\n2. Wait with the `TaskOutput` tool: `TaskOutput(task_id, block=true, timeout=600000)` (600000 ms = 10 min is the max per call). It returns when the task completes or at the deadline. It is the watchdog.\n3. On completion, `Read` the output file. On a timeout return, treat it as an infrastructure hang (see Error Handling); do not silently re-dispatch.\n\n**Never hand-roll a polling loop.** Do not pass a `while`/`if`/`wc -c` stability loop to `Monitor` or `Bash` to detect completion. Such commands contain shell control flow that Warden cannot statically analyze, so they prompt for approval, which stalls an unattended autopilot run. The harness already notifies you when a background task finishes; `TaskOutput` is the only wait primitive you need.\n\n## Following Up\n\n- Attended sessions: after every run-script command, use `AskUserQuestion` to confirm next steps.\n- Unattended sessions (`CLAUDE_UNATTENDED=1`): never call `AskUserQuestion`; take the documented default, log it as `defaulted:<decision>` in the run report, and follow `<autopilot-plugin-root>/skills/run-autopilot/references/unattended-contract.md`.\n- By default each run is independent - a follow-up task is a new run with a new prompt, so restate the relevant context. Where the backend supports resuming, the resumed session carries the original run's model and context over (see each SKILL.md for its resume flags).\n- Restate the permission mode when proposing follow-up actions (attended sessions).\n\n## Error Handling\n\n- Stop and report failures whenever a run-script command exits non-zero. Attended: request direction before retrying. Unattended (`CLAUDE_UNATTENDED=1`): retry at most 2 times, then mark the step FAILED with the captured stderr, per the unattended contract cited above.\n- Before using high-impact permission flags (`-y`/`--yolo` and backend equivalents) ask user permission via AskUserQuestion unless already given; unattended, use them only where the calling skill's documented defaults already grant them.\n- When output includes warnings or partial results, summarize them and ask how to adjust (attended) or log them in the run report and proceed (unattended).\n\n### Error taxonomy\n\nA non-zero exit is not one failure — recognize the class and act per its row before retrying (the retry bounds above still apply: attended asks, unattended retries ≤2 then FAILED). Each row names an observable recognition signal and an observable outcome; a caller that hits this case answers \"what do I do when the CLI fails this way\" from the table, not from memory.\n\n| Class | Recognize by | Action |\n|-------|--------------|--------|\n| **Auth expired** | stderr names auth/login/credentials/token — `not logged in`, `authentication failed`, `401`, `re-authenticate` | Do NOT retry blindly (a retry re-fails identically). Mark the step **FAILED** and print the re-auth hint (the backend's login command — e.g. `codex login`, `gemini`/`copilot` auth). Unattended cannot re-auth, so it stops here rather than burning retries. |\n| **Quota / rate exhausted** | stderr names quota/rate/usage — `monthly quota exceeded`, `rate limit`, `429`, `usage limit`. DISTINCT from auth: the credential is valid, the budget is spent | Mark **FAILED** — retrying spends nothing and fixes nothing. When the CLI reports a reset time, **quote it in the run report** so the caller knows when a retry could succeed. (A Carl/copilot `monthly quota exceeded` is this class — a runtime skip, not a prerequisite failure.) |\n| **CLI died mid-run** | non-zero exit with a truncated/partial `-o` file (crash, OOM-kill, SIGKILL) | **Salvage** what landed in the `-o` file, mark it **PARTIAL** in the run report, and treat the run as FAILED-with-partial — never present a truncated result as the full answer. |\n| **Empty output despite rc 0** | helper exited 0 but the `-o` file is empty (0 bytes) or whitespace-only | Treat as **FAILED**, not success (a silent empty result reads as a passed review that never happened). **Quote the run's stderr** in the report — the real cause is usually there. |\n\n**Codex exit-4 salvage (`codex_review_run.py` callers only).** Exit 4 and the `codex-review-last.jsonl` sidecar are produced by `run-autopilot/scripts/codex_review_run.py`, **not** by `codex-run.sh` — that helper returns codex's real exit code and writes no sidecar. So this row applies to callers dispatching through `codex_review_run.py` (the review path); a caller using `codex-run.sh` directly never sees exit 4 and has nothing to salvage. Exit 4 means codex ran but the wrapper flagged failure (e.g. quota), and it has a documented FALSE-POSITIVE mode: the quota/error markers can match codex's own command-line args or gateguard ERROR noise while codex actually finished, and the `-o` file may be unwritten even though the work completed. Before treating exit 4 as the Quota class above, check the sidecar (its last-run JSONL): if it holds a COMPLETE result (the expected findings/verdict content), **salvage it and treat the run as succeeded**. Only when nothing salvageable is in the sidecar → FAILED. `review-work-completion` carries the review-specific `D{n}:`-verdict variant (the doubt lens Bob runs). A contract-level retry would stack on top of the ladder's budget and double-spend it. |\n| \"Before using high-impact permission flags (`-y`/`--yolo` and backend equivalents) ask user permission … unattended, use them only where the calling skill's documented defaults already grant them\" | Dispatches with `-a` (edit-enabled sandbox) unattended. | This IS the calling-skill grant the rule points at: `work/references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex dispatch documents `-a` as the rung's default, and `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung records that it runs under a strictly weaker `Bash`-hook set than any Claude rung, with `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG=off` as the revert. The grant is narrow — it covers the implementor rung only, never a reviewer dispatch. |\n\nAn implementor run also has a failure mode no reviewer run has: the helper\nexits 0 with non-empty output but changes **nothing**, because this host's\nPreToolUse hooks denied the edits and codex explained the denial in prose. That\nis classified infra, not capability — see `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung arm 2.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

Each entry: the excuse, why it's wrong, the counter-action, and its trigger terms. Echo's deny messages cite the first entry (file order) whose trigger substring-matches a duplicate symbol name; no match, no citation. Terms match as plain substrings, so keep them distinctive - a term like `fix` also fires inside `prefix`. An entry without a **Triggers** bullet is never auto-cited. Also surfaced in `/architect` planning prompts.\n\n## Excuses\n\n### \"Quick fix, skip the map\"\n\n- **Why it's wrong**: speed without context creates parallel implementations of code that already exists. The \"quick\" fix becomes a long-term tax on every future reader.\n- **Counter-action**: run `/survey` for a codebase brief before any edit. Wanting to skip it is the signal to slow down, not to skip.\n- **Triggers**: quick, hotfix, workaround, stopgap\n\n### \"Couldn't find existing helper\"\n\n- **Why it's wrong**: most \"couldn't find\" is \"didn't grep enough.\" Names diverge across codebases (`format_date`, `to_iso`, `serialize_date`, `date_str` all show up).\n- **Counter-action**: name 2-3 plausible synonyms before writing new code, and grep each. For utilities, search the verb (`format`, `serialize`, `render`) and the noun (`date`, `timestamp`, `iso`). For types, search the domain term and its abbreviations. See **Synonyms-to-grep** below.\n- **Triggers**: format, parse, validate, normalize, serialize, transform, decode, encode, stringify, render\n\n### \"Existing pattern is overkill\"\n\n- **Why it's wrong**: a parallel-implementation rationalization. Patterns feel heavy until you discover they encode invariants (error handling, ordering, retries) that the \"lighter\" version silently drops.\n- **Counter-action**: use the existing pattern even if it feels heavy. If it's genuinely wrong for this case, open a refactor PRD and propose a replacement that updates every call site at once.\n- **Triggers**: simple, lite, basic, mini, naive\n\n### \"I'll add tests later\"\n\n- **Why it's wrong**: later never arrives. The next session has different context, the bug surfaces in production, and the test that would have caught it never gets written.\n- **Counter-action**: ship the regression test with the change (`rules/testing.md`); for bug fixes, watch it fail once against the old code. The test takes minutes; the regression it prevents takes hours.\n- **Triggers**: test, fixture, mock, stub, fake\n\n### \"File is short, I'll just rewrite\"\n\n- **Why it's wrong**: short files often encode invariants in their structure (error messages other code matches against, exact return shapes consumers depend on, side effects in a specific order). A rewrite drops them silently.\n- **Counter-action**: edit in place. If the file is genuinely wrong, open a refactor PRD with the diff plan. Never rewrite as a side effect of a feature task.\n- **Triggers**: rewrite, v2, copy, clone\n\n## Synonyms-to-grep\n\nWhen you suspect a helper exists but the obvious name returns nothing, expand the search:\n\n- **Verbs**: `format` ↔ `render` ↔ `serialize` ↔ `to_*` ↔ `as_*` ↔ `stringify`\n- **Parsers**: `parse` ↔ `from_*` ↔ `decode` ↔ `load` ↔ `read`\n- **Validators**: `validate` ↔ `check` ↔ `assert_*` ↔ `is_valid` ↔ `verify`\n- **Builders**: `build` ↔ `create` ↔ `make` ↔ `new_*` ↔ `init`\n- **Lookups**: `get` ↔ `find` ↔ `lookup` ↔ `resolve` ↔ `select`\n\nGrep both the verb and the noun. If neither hits, grep the verb alone (utilities are sometimes named purely by action).\n\nIf after this you still find nothing, the helper genuinely doesn't exist; write it once, in the layer where its consumers live.\n\n\"\"\"Bounded controller protocol, public metadata, snapshots, and workflow open.\"\"\"\n\nfrom __future__ import annotations\n\nimport copy\nimport json\nimport secrets\nfrom Triggers on \"plan tasks\", \"create tasks from PRD\", \"implement PRD\", \"break down the spec\".\ncompatibility: \"Requires Bob personal Claude/autoclaude environment or equivalent host adapters for sub-agents, state, and review handoffs.\"\n---\n\n# Plan Tasks from PRD\n\nCreate implementation tasks from PRD documents.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Personal skills (files read at runtime): `work` - its `SKILL.md` \"Gemini-first tasks\" list is the single source of truth for the UI/backend split that sets `qwen_eligible`, and `references/qwen-integration.md` carries the qwen infra preflight (absent: qwen counts as unavailable and the eligibility trigger is skipped)\n- State contract with `run-autopilot`: `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md`\n- Optional: `pi` binary plus a reachable llama.cpp endpoint (gated by the preflight, never fatal)\n\n## Workflow\n\n### 1. List available PRDs\n\n```bash\nbash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-tasks/scripts/list-prds.sh\n```\n\nOr manually list PRDs (the native `Glob` tool is absent in this build; see rules/tools.md):\n```bash\nls docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip\nls docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog\n```\n\nIf no PRDs found, inform user and stop.\n\n### 2. Select PRD\n\n- **1 PRD in wip** → auto-select it, don't ask\n- **0 PRDs in wip** → present backlog list, ask user to pick\n- **2+ PRDs in wip** → present list (wip + backlog), ask user to pick\n\n### 2.5. Detect replan mode\n\nBefore reading the PRD, check for `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/replan-context.md`. If present, this invocation is a **replan** triggered by `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 0's abort handler — the prior Work session aborted on a too-big task and autopilot wants the remaining scope re-split into smaller chunks.\n\nWhen `replan-context.md` exists:\n\n1. Read it. The file lists completed-work entries (tasks already done, code already shipped — do NOT re-plan these), an aborted task (the trigger), and a `Budget:` line.\n2. Read the `Budget: {n} tokens per task` line from the file. Use that value as the per-task budget for the rest of this invocation — treat it as the hard threshold in step 4.6's split logic, not 150K. If the line is absent, fall back to 75 000.\n3. Treat the PRD scope as \"everything the PRD asks for **minus** the completed-work entries.\" When analyzing the PRD in step 3 and decomposing in step 4, skip capabilities already listed under \"Completed work\" in `replan-context.md`.\n4. After all `task-add` calls in step 4 succeed (planning completes without stalling), delete `replan-context.md` — it's consumed. Do NOT delete on stall.\n\nWhen `replan-context.md` is absent → normal first-pass planning. Use the 150K threshold.\n\n### 3. Analyze PRD\n\nRead the full PRD. Also load existing codebase architecture context (AGENTS.md, agent_docs/, `docs/dev/project-management/` architecture notes) to cross-reference. Identify reusable existing code before creating tasks.\n\n**Design doc (when present).** Check `state.design_doc` in `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json`; if it is unset, fall back to the glob `docs/dev/project-management/designs/<prd-stem>-design.md` (`<prd-stem>` = the selected PRD's filename minus `.md`). When a design doc exists, read it — it refines the PRD with the implementation design (the HOW): `## Interfaces & contracts` (exact signatures/types/enums), `## Module placement` (file targets), and `## Reuse inventory` (existing helpers). These seed the task `Contract`, `Location`, and `Reuse:` fields in step 4. When no design doc exists, plan from the PRD alone, as today. This detection works unchanged in replan mode.\n\nExtract:\n- Capabilities and features\n- Module structure\n- Dependency graph\n- Implementation phases\n- Existing patterns/utilities that implementers should reuse\n\n**When the PRD has no Functional Decomposition or Dependency Graph section** (many PRDs state only `## Requirements` + `## Acceptance`): do NOT treat the split (step 4.6) and dependency (step 5) inputs as undefined. **Derive** both from the Requirements — treat each requirement (R1, R2, …) as a decomposition unit, and infer ordering from explicit `depends on`/`after`/`blocked by` wording and from data-flow (a requirement that consumes another's output sequences after it); default to no dependency when none is stated. Steps 4.6 and 5 then use this derived structure exactly as they would a stated one. **Note the derivation in the step-6 planning summary** so the reviewer knows the sequencing is inferred, not PRD-pinned.\n\n### 4. Create tasks\n\nPersist each task with statectl — the sole writer for state.json (never hand-edit with Read/Write/Edit):\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json task-add <task-json-file>\n```\n\nBuild one JSON object per task and write it to `<task-json-file>` with the Write tool — a task body carries backticks, quotes and newlines, which break as an inline shell argument. Required key: `\"name\"` (the task title). The body composed per the \"Task description format\" below goes in `\"description\"`; every other field this skill assigns (`files` - the task's expected implementor-writable repo-relative paths, the same slice step 4.7 writes to `plan-<n>-files.txt` - persisted on every task; `blocked_by` in step 5, `estimated_tokens` and `est_context_peak` in step 4.5, `model`, `tier_reason`, `qwen_eligible` and `qwen_excluded_reason` in step 4.7) is a top-level key on the same object — flattened, never nested under a `metadata` key. `task-add` assigns the id and prints it to stdout; capture it (`id=$(python3 …/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json task-add /tmp/task-3.json)`) so later tasks in this same pass can name it in their own `blocked_by` array. Create the tasks in the PRD's dependency/phase order (earlier phases first, so every blocker exists before the tasks it blocks), which is what makes those captured ids available when step 5 builds each `blocked_by` array.\n\nTo fix a task after creation (not the normal create path): `task-set-body <task-id> <body-file>` replaces `description` verbatim from a raw text file, and `task-set-meta <task-id> <meta-json-file>` merges JSON keys onto the task entry (a `null` value deletes that key).\n\nFollow these rules:\n\n**Task qualities**:\n- **Atomic**: Single focused change\n- **Self-contained**: All context in description\n- **Sequenced**: Dependencies explicit\n- **Unambiguous**: No decisions left to implementer\n\n**Task description format**:\n```\n{What to do}\n\nLocation: {file paths or how to find them}\n\nReuse: {existing patterns, utilities, or modules to build on — if any}\n\nPremise: {observed-state facts this task depends on; re-verify before acting}\n\nContract (verbatim — from the design doc's `## Interfaces & contracts` when a design doc exists, else from the PRD; copy exact names, do NOT paraphrase):\n- {every exact field name, enum value, type shape, API signature, file/hook\n   kind, and threshold the PRD specifies for this task}\n\nDetails:\n- {specific requirement 1}\n- {specific requirement 2}\n\nAcceptance criteria:\n- {the PRD's per-task \"Acceptance:\" clause(s), copied verbatim}\n\nVerify: {how to confirm it's done}\n```\n\n**The `Contract` and `Acceptance criteria` sections are mandatory and must be\ncopied verbatim from the PRD — never paraphrased, never summarized.** `/autopilot:work`\nhands each task to a test author (Tess) who writes tests *from the task\ndescription alone*, having never seen the PRD. If the task says \"write the\natlas JSON\" instead of naming the exact keys (`head_sha`, `surveyed_at`,\n`error_style`, …), Tess invents a plausible-but-wrong schema, the implementer\nbuilds to those tests, and TDD locks in the wrong contract — a self-consistent\nfailure that only surfaces at the PRD-level review, after every task is \"done\".\nWhen the PRD pins a name, an enum value, a type, a file kind (\"Stop hook\" vs\n\"PostToolUse hook\"), or a numeric threshold, that exact string goes into the\ntask. This is what the \"Unambiguous\" and \"Self-contained\" task qualities above\nmean in practice. If the PRD itself is vague on a contract the task needs,\nsurface it in step 6 as an ambiguity — do not let the implementer guess.\n\n**The `Premise:` line is optional and PRD-owned.** When the PRD states a\npremise for a task (observed-state facts its action rests on), copy it\n**verbatim** into the `Premise:` line — same discipline as `Contract`, never\nparaphrased. The implementor must re-verify the premise before acting and treat\na false premise as a blocker: stop, report, do not proceed. In loop mode this\nfeeds PRD 00017's stall path (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md`\n\"Loop-mode stall procedure\") — a premise failure is never resolved by\nassumption. When the PRD states no premise, omit the line entirely: no new\nbehavior, nothing inferred or invented.\n\n**Contract source when a design doc exists.** When a design doc is present\n(detected in step 3), the task `Contract` is copied **verbatim from the design\ndoc's `## Interfaces & contracts`** entries — byte-identical, not paraphrased —\nbecause the design doc is the architecturally-vetted refinement of the PRD's\ncontract. `Acceptance criteria` is **ALWAYS** copied verbatim from the **PRD**;\nthe design doc never owns acceptance criteria — those stay PRD-owned. Seed each\ntask's file placement / `Location` from the design doc's `## Module placement`\nand its `Reuse:` lines from `## Reuse inventory`. When NO design doc exists, the\n`Contract` comes from the PRD as described above. **On a PRD-vs-design contract\nconflict, the design doc wins** (it refines the PRD): use the design doc's\ncontract and log the conflict in the step-6 planning summary. This rule works\nunchanged in replan mode.\n\n**If a `task-add` call fails mid-plan** (a statectl error — NOT the oversize stall handled in step 4.6): stop creating tasks and **roll back cleanly**. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json tasks-clear`, which empties the whole task array in one write (same cleanup as the oversize stall below) so no orphan tasks survive to make the next PRD's Phase 2 skip planning. Then record the cause via statectl — `set stall_reason '{\"stalled\": \"taskcreate_failed\", \"detail\": \"<the statectl error>\"}'` — and report the failure. `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 2 reads a non-`oversized_task` stall as a plan-tasks failure (PAUSE interactive; loop mode re-invokes once, then stalls the PRD `sub_skill_fail`); the rollback guarantees the retry starts from a clean tracker. Do NOT move the PRD to `hold/` — a transient `task-add` failure is not an un-splittable PRD.\n\n**On successful completion of all `task-add` calls, clear a stale failure marker:** `statectl get stall_reason` → if it reads `\"taskcreate_failed\"` (a prior attempt failed and this retry succeeded), `statectl del stall_reason`. Otherwise leave it untouched — an `oversized_task` marker is owned by step 4.6, and a fresh plan usually has no marker (do NOT blind-`del`; statectl errors on an absent key).\n\n### 4.5. Estimate per-task context budget\n\nFor each task, compute an estimate so `/autopilot:work` stays under the work-tier model's standard context ceiling (200K on the current tiers).\n\n**Formula:**\n\n```\nestimated_tokens = sum(file_bytes/4 for file in task.files_touched)\n                 + prd_slice_bytes/4\n                 + plan_text_bytes/4\n                 + 55000\n```\n\n- `file_bytes/4`: ~4 chars per token, accurate within ±20% for code (less accurate for prose-heavy markdown; round up when in doubt).\n- `prd_slice_bytes`: bytes of the PRD section(s) this task references.\n- `plan_text_bytes`: bytes of the task's own description/details.\n- `55000`: overhead constant for system prompt + tool defs + skill texts on the current work-tier model (see \"Overhead re-derivation\" under Estimator caveats for provenance).\n\n**Threshold:** 150 000 tokens normally; in replan mode, the value from `replan-context.md`'s `Budget:` line (step 2.5). `est_context_peak = estimated_tokens + 20000` (20K headroom for response generation).\n\n**Persist** both values as top-level keys in the task's `task-add` JSON payload (flattened, not nested under a `metadata` key):\n\n```json\n{\"estimated_tokens\": 87000, \"est_context_peak\": 107000}\n```\n\n**Worked example:** a task touches three files (80KB, 40KB, 20KB) with a 25KB PRD slice and a 3KB plan text.\n\n```\nsum(file_bytes/4)   = (80000 + 40000 + 20000) / 4 = 35 000\nprd_slice_bytes/4   = 25000 / 4                   =  6 250\nplan_text_bytes/4   = 3000 / 4                    =    750\noverhead            =                              55 000\n                                                  ───────\nestimated_tokens    =                              97 000\nest_context_peak    = 97 000 + 20 000           = 117 000\n```\n\nBelow the 150K threshold → task ships as-is.\n\n### 4.6. Split tasks (context + eligibility)\n\nStep 4.6 has **two independent split triggers**. The existing context-budget trigger is unchanged; the eligibility trigger pushes separable backend work toward the qualified single-file shape that `/autopilot:work` can route to qwen (PRD 00174).\n\n- **Context-budget trigger** (always active): when `estimated_tokens > THRESHOLD` (150K normally; replan-context.md budget in replan mode), the task is too big for a single context window.\n- **Eligibility trigger** (infra-gated, see the qwen infra preflight subsection below): a **backend** task (UI/backend definition: see step 4.7 — UI matches the \"Gemini-first tasks\" list in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/SKILL.md`, everything else is backend) touching `>=2` files may split into one-file pieces so each subtask can route to qwen. The split is valid only when **cleanly separable** — judged from the PRD's Functional Decomposition and Dependency Graph, with each resulting piece required to independently compile and carry its own passing tests (no piece depends on a symbol another piece introduces). **A trait definition cannot be split from its implementations.** Correlated implementation/test, interface/implementation, and implementation/caller edits remain together and route above Qwen; do not manufacture a task boundary to gain eligibility.\n\nAn inseparable two-file task stays one task and is Qwen-ineligible (`files`); a separable two-file task may become two independently gated one-file tasks. Count only expected implementor writes: Tess-owned tests that Ivan must only read are outside that write set, while tests Ivan must edit count as writes.\n\nWhen **both** triggers apply to the same task, a **single split pass** satisfies both — do not run two passes. After splitting, each subtask is re-estimated per step 4.5 and re-classified per step 4.7 (so `qwen_eligible` reflects the new file count).\n\n**Qwen infra preflight (gates the eligibility trigger only):**\n\nBefore applying the eligibility split trigger, `plan-tasks` runs the qwen infra preflight defined in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/qwen-integration.md` (PRD 00031) — `pi` on PATH, the llama.cpp endpoint reachable, the configured model id present, and a real 1-token completion succeeding (the only check that proves the inference worker actually spawns). It is cheap on the common path; it exists so the eligibility split is only paid for when qwen can actually consume the result — a backend that lists the model but can't serve a token (`completion_failed`) skips the split rather than marking tasks qwen-eligible that would only fall back at dispatch.\n\n- **Healthy** → the eligibility trigger is active for this PRD's tasks.\n- **Unhealthy, or the probe is unavailable** (any failure mode reported by the probe — see `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/qwen-integration.md` for the current check list; absence of that file itself, e.g. before PRD 00031 has landed, also counts as unavailable) → the eligibility trigger is **skipped entirely**; tasks keep their original shape and route to Claude.\n\nThe **context-budget trigger is not gated** by the preflight and remains active regardless of qwen's status. The **step-4.7 `qwen_eligible` computation is not gated** either — it is always computed and persisted on every task (staying inert until `work` reads it).\n\n**Risk exemption (skips the eligibility trigger only):**\n\nA task carrying either risk fact (`contract_edit` or `algorithmic_risk`) is **not split for eligibility**. A risk fact normally lands the task on `opus`, which is never qwen-eligible, so the split would buy nothing. The exemption holds either way, and does not depend on that tier landing: a test-only or packaging-only slice pins `sonnet` before either fact is read. Judge both facts under step 4.7's evidence rules before splitting, and reuse the same values there. The exemption short-circuits the eligibility trigger and the task keeps its original shape. The context-budget trigger is unaffected: a risky task that also exceeds the context budget is still split for that reason.\n\nThe existing context-budget split mechanics, the one-split-attempt rule, and the stall behavior below are **unchanged** by the eligibility trigger — both triggers share them:\n\n1. **File boundary first.** Split into one task per file. The PRD slice prorates equally; the 55K overhead applies once per task. Re-estimate each subtask.\n2. **Capability boundary second.** If a task touches only one file and still exceeds the threshold, split along capability boundaries inside the PRD's Functional Decomposition section (or the decomposition derived from the Requirements in step 3 when the PRD states none).\n3. **One split attempt only.** If a task still exceeds the threshold after splitting, mark the PRD as stalled (use the threshold value in the stall_reason).\n\n**Stall behavior:**\n\nWhen unable to split below the threshold (150K standard, 75K in replan mode), **merge** a `stall_reason` key into the existing `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` via statectl — the sole writer for state.json (never hand-edit with Read/Write/Edit; see `/autopilot:run-autopilot`):\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json set stall_reason '{\"stalled\": \"oversized_task\", \"task\": \"<task-id>\", \"estimated_tokens\": <int>}'\n```\n\nstatectl merges the key and preserves the existing `phase`, `phases_completed`, `tasks`, `batch`, etc.\n\n**Then delete every task you already created** for this PRD with a single call: `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json tasks-clear`. `/autopilot:plan-tasks` calls `task-add` before the per-task budget check, so by the time the stall fires there are orphan tasks in the tracker. Cleaning up here makes the stall self-contained: any caller (not just `/autopilot:run-autopilot`) gets the same post-stall state. `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 2 also performs this cleanup as a backstop.\n\nAfter both writes succeed, end the session's work with the stall recorded (the `stall_reason` key in state.json IS the observable stall signal — a model-followed skill has no exit code); `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 2 reads it, detects the stall, moves the PRD from `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/` to `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` (creating the directory if missing), clears the stall key from state, and proceeds to the next backlog item without user prompt. See `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 2 for the consumer-side contract.\n\n### Estimator caveats\n\nThe bytes/4 heuristic is accurate within ±20% for source code, less accurate for prose-heavy markdown. When the largest input is markdown (PRD prose, docs), round up. When estimates land within 10% of the threshold (150K standard / 75K replan), prefer splitting — the runtime context cap hook (Phase 2 of PRD 00024) will abort tasks that overrun anyway, and a planned split is cheaper than a runtime abort.\n\n**Overhead re-derivation:** The constant is measured by reading `input_tokens + cache_read_input_tokens + cache_creation_input_tokens` from the first `message.usage` line in a fresh Work-phase transcript on the current work-tier model (zero task context loaded — just the system prompt, tool defs, and active skills). Re-derive when upgrading the model or adding/removing skills: start an empty `/autopilot:work` session, read the first usage line from `~/.claude/projects/<hash>/<session>.jsonl`, sum the three token fields. Update the constant and the worked example if the new value differs by more than 5K. Provenance of the current 55K (2026-07-11): five fresh headless opus-4.8 work-phase transcripts measured 74,560-74,809 (~74.7K), minus PRD 00043's measured always-loaded reduction (run-autopilot SKILL.md 33.0K → 7.3K core, +5.4K gate file read back in ≈ −20K net) ≈ 55K, rounded. Those transcripts predate the 00043 restructure; re-measure directly at the next batch and correct if the fresh number moves more than 5K.\n\n**Pending re-derivation (PRD 00084 R3, LIVE):** the 55K/150K constants are measured on `opus-4.8`, but PRD 00076 ended Opus as the default autopilot **build**-phase model: build sessions now launch Sonnet-first and promote to `claude-opus-5` only when the build-model routing (`build_model` in run-autopilot's `cli/routing.py`, since PRD 00106) finds difficulty evidence for the PRD. `_AUTOPILOT_MODEL_BUILD` is an operator env override / kill-switch, not a hardcoded constant. That makes this trigger live: re-derive per the mandate above on real Sonnet build transcripts once a few Sonnet build batches exist, not from a single ad-hoc session or a non-build transcript.\n\n### 4.7. Assign per-task model tier\n\nFor each task, `classify_tier.py` decides the model tier. Persist what it prints as top-level `model: \"haiku\"|\"sonnet\"|\"opus\"` and `tier_reason` keys, so `/autopilot:work` dispatches each subagent at the right tier (PRD 00025) and every reader of the plan can see why that tier was chosen (PRD 00160).\n\n**Inputs, per task:** that task's file slice, its title plus description, its estimated lines-changed (rough: pull from the task plan or estimate from the file slice), and the two facts below. Neither the PRD body nor `estimated_tokens` is an input any more, because size and vocabulary stopped deciding tiers with PRD 00160.\n\n**Two per-task facts.** Judge these booleans once per task, from that task's own `Contract`, `Location`, `Details` and file slice, before the step-4.6 split, then reuse the same values here. Both default to false; assert one only on the evidence named:\n\n- `contract_edit` is true only when the task itself changes an exported API signature, a persisted schema, a wire format or a hook registration shape. Calling or documenting a contract does not count.\n- `algorithmic_risk` is true only when the task's own `Details` name a new algorithm it implements (not one it calls), shared mutable state across threads, processes or async tasks, or a transform of persisted data (a migration). Words in the PRD body, the PRD title or the task name alone never qualify, and neither do `design`, `architect`, `introduce`, `refactor across`, file count or `estimated_tokens`.\n\n**Run the classifier, once per task.** Write the task's file slice to `docs/dev/tmp/plan-<n>-files.txt` (one repo-relative path per line) and its title plus description to `docs/dev/tmp/plan-<n>-text.txt`, with `<n>` the task's position in this pass, then run:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/plan-tasks/scripts/classify_tier.py --files-file docs/dev/tmp/plan-<n>-files.txt --text-file docs/dev/tmp/plan-<n>-text.txt --lines <lines-changed> [--contract-edit] [--algorithmic-risk] [--default-model <floor>]\n```\n\nPass `--contract-edit` only when that task's `contract_edit` is true, `--algorithmic-risk` only when its `algorithmic_risk` is true, and `--default-model <floor>` only when the PRD frontmatter sets one (see the override below). Task-authored prose crosses as files, never as shell words.\n\nThe command prints one JSON line, `{\"model\": \"<tier>\", \"tier_reason\": \"<reason>\"}`. Take `model` and `tier_reason` from that line exactly as printed and persist both on this task's payload (see **Persist** below).\n\n**Legal `tier_reason` values.** The classifier emits exactly one of `test_port`, `packaging`, `contract`, `algorithmic_risk`, `mechanical`, `default` or `floor`; any other value in a plan is corrupt state, not a new reason.\n\n**What the classifier does with those inputs**, in precedence order: a file slice that is all test paths gives `sonnet` / `test_port`, and a slice that is all test or packaging paths gives `sonnet` / `packaging`. Then `contract_edit` gives `opus` / `contract`, and `algorithmic_risk` gives `opus` / `algorithmic_risk`. Then the mechanical row gives `haiku` / `mechanical`, and everything left gives `sonnet` / `default`. Last, the `default_model` floor raises the tier when the floor is higher, reporting `floor` when it does.\n\n**The mechanical signal list was widened once and the widening was withdrawn (PRD 00075).**\nSee `references/design-rationale.md` for the counterexamples and why a future widening must move a different axis than the verb.\n\n**Row selection (`_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR`).** An optional `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR` value names which mechanical row this run treats as current. It is a prose-only knob: `classify_tier.py` does not read it, and it does not compose into the `final_tier = max(...)` formula in \"PRD frontmatter override\" below, which is unchanged either way. `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR` is an environment variable, read at step 4.7 entry: run `python3 -c 'import os;print(os.environ.get(\"_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR\",\"\"))'`. Apply the row-selection table below to whatever value comes back, including the empty string (it takes the current row).\n\n| `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR` | Mechanical row applied |\n|---|---|\n| `legacy` | The pre-00075 row verbatim: `files_touched ≤ 2` AND est. lines-changed `≤ 50` AND task text matches one of exactly these nine signals: `add log`, `rename`, `add test for`, `port`, `mirror`, `inline`, `extract constant`, `update import`, `bump version` |\n| `sonnet` | Alias for `legacy` |\n| absent, empty, or any other value | The current mechanical row. An invalid non-empty value logs one warning line before falling back to it |\n\n**The knob is currently a no-op, deliberately.** Because the widening was withdrawn (above), the `legacy` row and the current mechanical row are identical, so every `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR` value names the same row. It ships anyway as the kill-switch the next widening attempt will need: the moment a defensible widened row lands, `_PLAN_TASKS_FLOOR=legacy` reverts to the nine signals above without editing rules. Do not delete it as dead config, and do not assume it is exercised: it has no behavioral test until a widening exists to revert.\n\n**Examples**:\n\n- \"rename `foo` to `bar` in `module/x.rs`\" (1 file, ~10 lines, both facts false) → `haiku` / `mechanical`.\n- \"add a `--json` flag to the export CLI and change the shape of the emitted record\" (2 files, ~90 lines): the task itself changes a wire format, so `contract_edit` is true → `opus` / `contract`.\n- \"add POST /users endpoint with email validation\" (3 files, ~80 lines, both facts false): too many files and lines for the mechanical row, and nothing earlier fires → `sonnet` / `default`.\n\n**PRD frontmatter override**\n\nPRD frontmatter accepts an optional `default_model: haiku|sonnet|opus` field that acts as a **floor** on the classifier output — never a demotion. Parse it from the YAML block at the top of the PRD using the same approach `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 0 uses for `catchup:` (look for `---` delimiters, parse the YAML, accept `haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`). Behavior:\n\n- **Absent frontmatter or unset `default_model:`** → no override (silent; omit `--default-model` and the classifier's tier passes through unchanged). This is what keeps `haiku` reachable without requiring every PRD to opt in explicitly — and matches `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6's `[D]` follow-up behavior.\n- **Malformed frontmatter or invalid `default_model:` value** → no override AND log a one-line warning. The classifier output passes through. `fable` is deliberately not in the accepted set: it is human-gated — use the rescue flow (PRD 00076, `run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Fable rescue), never a frontmatter floor. Warn with that reason rather than a bare \"invalid value\" so the omission reads as policy.\n- **Valid value (`haiku`/`sonnet`/`opus`)** → pass it as `--default-model` and the floor below applies. The floor is all this key does: `default_model: opus` never picks the orchestrator, a PRD that wants an opus build session declares `session_model: opus` beside it (PRD 00200; `run-autopilot/references/state-schema.md` § Build-Session Model Promotion Signals).\n\n`classify_tier.py` applies the floor itself, after its own rules have produced a tier, by taking the maximum across the precedence `haiku < sonnet < opus` (only when `default_model` is a valid value):\n\n```\nfinal_tier = max(classifier_tier, default_model)\n```\n\nThis guarantees:\n\n- `default_model: opus` raises every task to `opus`: a `haiku` or `sonnet` classification is clamped up, an `opus` classification stands. Matches PRD 00025's Critical Scenarios \"PRD frontmatter override\" test.\n- `default_model: sonnet` clamps `haiku` up to `sonnet` and leaves `sonnet` and `opus` alone.\n- `default_model: haiku` is a no-op (`haiku` is already the floor of the precedence; classifier output stands as-is).\n- An `opus` classification is never demoted by any `default_model` value.\n- Review-rework `[D]` tasks take this floor only when they carry a 🔴 finding (`run-autopilot/references/phase-review.md` Phase 6).\n\n**`qwen_eligible` computation**\n\nAfter the classifier has settled `final_tier` (the floor above included), compute the `qwen_eligible` boolean that `/autopilot:work` (PRD 00031) reads to decide qwen routing. The formula (widened by PRD 00019) is:\n\n```\nqwen_eligible = task is backend (not UI) AND model in {haiku, sonnet} AND files_touched == 1 AND task edits no public contract\n```\n\n- `model` is the tier the classifier printed (the same value persisted as the top-level `model` key).\n- Here `files_touched` counts distinct, non-empty expected implementor-writable file paths, excluding read-only context and Tess-owned tests; it does not change the step-4.5 context estimate or the classifier's inputs. Empty or missing file slices are ineligible (`files`).\n- **UI** = the task matches the **\"Gemini-first tasks\"** list in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/SKILL.md`. Anything not matching that list is **backend**. Reuse `work`'s list as the single source of truth so producer and consumer agree by construction — do not restate the list here; if it changes in `work`, this rule inherits the change.\n- **Public contract** = the `contract_edit` fact judged above under its evidence rule. Reuse that value as the single source of truth so the tier and this flag cannot disagree; do not restate the definition here and do not widen its evidence. `contract_edit` false means the task edits no public contract.\n\nEach of the following yields `qwen_eligible = false` independently, with the named `qwen_excluded_reason` code:\n\n- The task matches the UI list (Gemini's domain, not qwen's) → `ui`.\n- `model == \"opus\"` (opus tier is never qwen-eligible) → `tier`.\n- The task edits a public contract, meaning `contract_edit` is true → `contract`.\n- `files_touched >= 2` or `files_touched == 0` (outside the measured single-file scope) → `files`.\n\n**`qwen_excluded_reason`**: on **every** ineligible task, also persist `qwen_excluded_reason` — one of `ui` / `tier` / `files` / `contract`. When several conditions fail, record the FIRST failing one in the order above (`ui` → `tier` → `contract` → `files`). `contract` is recorded ahead of `files` because the codex rung's fence (`run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Codex rung) admits `files` but must exclude `contract`, so a task that both spans many files and edits a public contract has to record `contract`, keeping it off codex. Eligible tasks omit the key. This makes under-routing auditable per batch: the Phase 9 Implementor Mix render counts exclusions by reason (PRD 00019).\n\n**`qwen_excluded_reason: contract` is unreachable on new plans, except on test-only and packaging-only slices.** A task that edits a public contract carries `contract_edit`, the classifier turns that into `opus`, and `tier` is recorded ahead of `contract`, so such a task records `tier` instead. The codex fence is unaffected: opus is never intercepted.\n\nThe flag is computed **from** the classifier output; it does **not** alter the tier.\n\n**Persist** `model`, `tier_reason`, the `qwen_eligible` flag, and (on ineligible tasks) the `qwen_excluded_reason` alongside the existing token estimate as top-level keys in the task's `task-add` JSON payload, e.g.:\n\nA one-file backend task → `qwen_eligible: true`; a two-file backend task → `qwen_eligible: false`, `qwen_excluded_reason: \"files\"` (both Sonnet, no public-contract edit):\n\n```json\n{\"files\": [\"src/export.py\"], \"estimated_tokens\": 72000, \"est_context_peak\": 92000, \"model\": \"sonnet\", \"tier_reason\": \"default\", \"qwen_eligible\": true}\n```\n\n```json\n{\"files\": [\"src/export.py\", \"src/cli.py\"], \"estimated_tokens\": 90000, \"est_context_peak\": 110000, \"model\": \"sonnet\", \"tier_reason\": \"default\", \"qwen_eligible\": false, \"qwen_excluded_reason\": \"files\"}\n```\n\n`qwen_eligible` is persisted on **every** task `plan-tasks` creates. `/autopilot:work` retains that classification and reconciles the concrete `FILE_PATHS` write set before routing, so stale multi-file eligibility cannot bypass the single-file fence (see `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/SKILL.md`).\n\nOn legacy plans created before PRD 00025, `state.tasks[i].model` is simply absent — `/autopilot:work` falls back to omitting the Agent `model` parameter so subagents inherit the session model (backwards-compatible). Plans created before PRD 00160 lack `tier_reason`; readers render the tier as unexplained rather than failing.\n\n### 5. Set dependencies\n\nDependencies are set **inline at creation**, not in a follow-up pass. `task-add` prints each new task's id, and step 4 creates tasks in the PRD's phase order (earlier phases first), so a later task's blockers are already-captured ids by the time its payload is built — put them straight in that task's `\"blocked_by\"` array (array of ints).\n\nFollow PRD's dependency graph:\n- Phase 0 tasks: no blockers\n- Phase 1 tasks: blocked by Phase 0\n- etc.\n\n**Correctness rule:** before you put a task id in a `blocked_by` array, that blocker must already have been created — its id captured from an earlier `task-add` call in this same pass.
