Tasks NOT in the list are skipped entirely — no Tess/Ivan/Devon dispatch, no commits. |\n\n**In rework mode, read `references/rework-mode.md` before the first task** — it carries the `in_progress`/`completed` lifecycle, the `review_cycle` / `escalation_reason` / `escalated_from` attempt fields, and the abort semantics (`rework_task_ids` survives an aborted pass; only Phase 6 clears it).\n\n### 2. Claim and start task\n\nFor the first available task:\n\n1. **Claim the task** with the single compound verb (see Dashboard State Sync) — `task-start` sets `status: in_progress` in the state file, so this call IS the claim:\n   ```bash\n   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/statectl.py <state.json> task-start <task-id>\n   ```\n   Then run `git rev-parse HEAD` and hold it in-session as `<task_base_sha>` — steps 5.6, 5.65, 5.7 and `BASE_SHA` all diff against it. Unlike `<test_commit_sha>` it is defined for every task, including test-only, docs-only, config-only and micro-lane tasks that commit no tests.\n2. **Reset the per-task context-cap marker** so the autopilot PostToolUse hook fires once for THIS task, not once per Work phase. The hook also self-clears when the in-progress task id in `state.json` differs from the id stored in the marker file, but the explicit clear here is a belt-and-braces backstop in case state.json's task-id snapshot lags the actual task switch. Run the shared walk-up helper in `--clear-cap` mode — it resolves symlinks, walks up to the autopilot dir, and removes `<autopilot_dir>/.cap-fired` internally:\n   ```bash\n   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/run-autopilot/scripts/_walk_up.py --clear-cap\n   ```\n   No-op when no ancestor has the dir or the marker is already absent (first task of the phase); always exits 0. Use exactly this single-command form — no `d=$(...)` shell variable, so the permission matcher can resolve it.\n3. **Resume from a rotation scar (PRD 00202).** Read `git log -1 --format=%s`. When the subject ends in \"wip - rotated mid-task\" for this task, read the commit body and continue at the step it names instead of dispatching Tess. A `test(` subject for this task with no wip commit (tests committed, rotation before Devon) continues at step 2.9. On either resume, re-derive both anchors from this task's own commits — `git log --format='%H %s'`, walking back by task, not by subject shape — a `test(<scope>)` commit, a `chore(<scope>): wip - rotated mid-task` commit, or any step-5 commit of this task (its `<scope>` and the task-id reference step 5 asks for; a rotation mid-5.5-retry leaves `wip -> feat -> test` in the log) — stopping at the first commit that is not this task's: `<task_base_sha>` is the parent of the earliest such commit (replacing item 1's HEAD, which is the resume commit itself and would put the pre-rotation half of the task outside steps 5.6, 5.65 and 5.7), and `<test_commit_sha>` is the newest `test(` commit among them (unset when there is none). Any other subject starts at step 2.5 as usual.\n\n### 2.5. Load project context\n\nBefore dispatching the implementor, load relevant context into the prompt:\n\n- AGENTS.md / agent_docs/ architecture docs\n- Active PRD from `docs/dev/project-management/prds/wip/`\n- Key module interfaces relevant to the task\n\n**Ambiguity check (Think Before Coding):** Re-read the task description. If scope, data shape, target surface, or success criteria are unclear, never pick silently. Interactively: stop and ask the user. In loop mode (`$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` set, PRD 00017): never end the turn on a question - nobody answers it, the loop relaunches, and the next session has to reconcile (2026-10-12, 00271 task 9: one session ended on \"that needs your call\", two relaunches and a six-minute reconcile followed). Resolve it by the simplest safe assumption, record it in `state.autonomous_decisions` and via `autopilot defer --prd <filename> --batch <batch_id> --json '{\"type\": \"assumed-ambiguity\", \"question\": ..., \"assumption\": ...}'` (`run-autopilot/references/phase-build.md` \"Loop mode\"), and continue; an acceptance criterion the task's own contract makes unreachable is the same case, with the evidence in the record. Only `pause_on_ambiguity: true` in the PRD frontmatter stalls instead. See `references/code-quality-principles.md` §1 and `references/code-quality-examples.md` §1 for what counts as a hidden assumption worth surfacing.\n\n**Premise check:** If the task description carries a `Premise:` line, verify each stated fact against the current tree (`ls`, `rg`, `git ls-files` as fits) BEFORE dispatching any implementor — cheap read-only probes only, never a mutation. If any fact no longer holds, do not dispatch. Interactively: stop and report which fact failed; the task stays in_progress for the user or the decision gate. In loop mode (post-00017): a failed premise is never assumed through — it takes the loop-mode stall path (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md` \"Loop-mode stall procedure\"), unlike ambiguities, which 00017 resolves by simplest safe assumption. If a probe command itself errors, treat the premise as unverified and surface it as a blocker — never proceed on an unknown. Tasks without a `Premise:` line skip this check entirely (zero behavior change for legacy plans).\n\n### 2.7. Write tests first (Tess - test author)\n\nDispatch a separate agent to write tests from requirements only. This agent must NOT receive implementation hints or architecture deep-dives - only what a user of the API would know.\n\n**Tess runs as:** Claude Code subagent (Agent tool), not a helper-script implementor (`use-gemini`, `use-qwen`, `use-codex`). It's a focused task that benefits from direct file access for reading test patterns.\n\n**Skip for:** test-only, docs-only, or config-only tasks. Skipping Tess here does not skip step 2.9 or 2.95: when this task's Contract names test files an earlier task of this plan committed, those files are this task's tests for both steps.\n\nRender: one Bash call. **Task-authored prose never crosses the shell** — write it to a scratch file with the Write tool and pass `--set-file`; see § Passing values to render_prompt.py. Every interpolated path is `shlex.quote()`-d (or bash's `printf '%q '`) before it lands inside a `--set-cmd` value:\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/tess-prompt.md \\\n  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>.txt \\\n  --set-file TASK_SUBJECT=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-subject.txt \\\n  --set-file TASK_DESCRIPTION=<scratch file: task description plus the exact file paths and symbol names to test> \\\n  --set-file TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-acceptance.txt \\\n  --set-file SAMPLE_TEST_FILE=<one representative existing test file> \\\n  --set-cmd PUBLIC_INTERFACES=\"cat $(printf '%q ' <interface files>)\" \\\n  --set TEST_FRAMEWORK=\"<pytest/jest/vitest/etc>\" --dispatch-kind tess --dispatch-task <task-id> \\\n  --require-file <each absolute path to an existing file the task touches, one flag per path> \\\n  --require-parent <each absolute path to a file the task creates, one flag per path>\n```\n`PUBLIC_INTERFACES` also carries the project's test-harness contract where one exists: for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>`, add `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md` to the `cat` list when that file is on disk (once per distinct file, still no module under test). None present adds nothing.\n\n**Read `references/test-author-prompt.md` § Context Selection before the first Tess dispatch of a batch** — it lists exactly what Tess receives and what she must not, and what `tess-prompt.md` already bakes in (read-only scope, dispatch prologue, Assumptions footer), so nothing is added to the prompt by hand. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source; the render call's stdout integer **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement.\n\nTess prompts must satisfy the **Subagent Dispatch Budget**.\n\n### 2.8. Test quality gate (main session)\n\nBefore committing Tess's tests, run the computed shape check and review them in the main session against the four-check rubric in `references/test-author-prompt.md` § Quality gate (behavior names, real assertions, edge cases, no tautologies); **read that section before running the gate.** If any check fails, dispatch Tess again with specific feedback about what's weak, rendered from `tess-retry-prompt.md` — never author the retry by hand. Max 2 quality gate retries. Then run the step-5.65 gate over the test files only — `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_style_limits.py --diff docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt <each new or changed test file as an absolute path>`, the diff built per that same file's § Style limits on the test files (**read it before the first gate run of a batch**). Exit 1 is a quality-gate failure: feed the violation lines to the Tess retry. It counts toward the two quality-gate retries.\n\n**Total Tess budget:** max 4 dispatches across the entire test authoring phase (1 initial + 2 quality-gate retries + 1 adversarial strengthen, which also covers Devon's one weak-point correction retry). If exhausted, flag weakness in task output and proceed. Don't block the pipeline forever.\n\n### 2.85. Commit tests\n\nTwo Bash calls, never chained: `git add <test_files>`, then `git commit -m \"test(<scope>): add tests for <feature>\"`.\n\nTests are committed separately before implementation, making the TDD boundary auditable in git history — and before Devon, so the quality-gated tests never sit uncommitted through the longest dispatches of a task (a rotation mid-Devon lost a 603-line test file once, and a rotation after a committed test file re-dispatched Tess with the identical prompt; PRD 00202).\n\n**Capture this task's test-commit SHA** immediately and hold it in-session as `<test_commit_sha>` — the last test commit, so a step-2.9 strengthen commit replaces it — **read `references/gate-failure.md` § Test-commit SHA before moving on** for the command and its one reader, step 5.5's ESCALATE reset. Step 5.7's `BASE_SHA` is `<task_base_sha>` from step 2, not this.\n\n### 2.9. Adversarial validation (Devon - devil's advocate)\n\n**Tier gate — Devon runs on the deepest rungs only, `opus` and `fable`.** Read the task's `model` field (`state.tasks[i].model`):\n\n| `state.tasks[i].model` | Devon (step 2.9) |\n|-----------------------|-------------------|\n| `opus` | dispatch Devon (below) |\n| `fable` | dispatch Devon (below) — the rescue rung runs the deepest pipeline, like `opus` |\n| anything else — `haiku`, `sonnet`, absent/legacy or unknown (both treated as `sonnet`) | skip Devon, proceed to step 2.95 |\n\nThe step-2.8 test quality gate is **unchanged** and runs for every tier — only this Agent dispatch is conditional. A Devon dispatch obeys the **Per-task model dispatch** rule (passes `model: opus`, or `model: fable` on a rescued task). Escalation interplay is automatic: when the review gate escalates a review-flagged task to `opus`, the rework attempt regains Devon with no extra mechanism. (Why tier-gated: `references/design-rationale.md` § tier-gated pipeline.)\n\n**Prose gate — Devon skips prose-pin tasks.** When every test file Tess created or changed for this task is a prose pin (its basename ends in `_prose.py`), skip Devon, record `devon: skipped:prose` in the task's attempt entry, and proceed to step 2.95. A substring pin cannot see negation, inversion or past-tense narration, so a Devon dispatch on such a task never breaks the tests (four of four on 2026-09-14/15, about 55 minutes of Opus time with no kept strengthening).\n\n**Earlier-task tests.** When step 2.7 skipped Tess because an earlier task of this plan committed this task's tests, Devon still runs at `opus` and `fable` against those files: his test-runner command names them, and an exploit routes to Tess's one strengthen dispatch exactly as for tests written in this task. A plan that splits tests from implementation must not lose the adversarial round the implementation tier bought.\n\nDevon runs once per task; when he breaks the tests, Tess strengthens once and the task proceeds on the strengthened tests with Devon never dispatched again (seven measured re-checks on 2026-09-25/26 changed no test; the one that named a real exploit was dismissed and the review caught it). See `references/adversarial-test-prompt.md` § Procedure for how Devon runs, and the file's prompt template section for what it receives. Devon prompts must satisfy the **Subagent Dispatch Budget**. Devon's prompt is filled by hand, so measure it and open his row in one call — `record_dispatch.py start --kind devon --task <task-id> --prompt-file <the written prompt>` prints the byte count that **is** his Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement, then the id — before the Agent call, and hold the id for the `end` call (§ Subagent Dispatch Budget and Watchdog, Telemetry).\n\n### 2.95. Red-check — watch the tests fail\n\nRun the newly committed tests once, before any Ivan dispatch, at the narrowest scope (the same commands step 5.5 uses). Red is the point: a failure proves the tests bind behavior that does not exist yet (rules/testing.md fail-first). Implicitly skipped when step 2.7 was skipped and no earlier task of this plan committed this task's tests (nothing to run).\n\n**Read `references/red-check.md` before the first red-check of a batch** — it resolves the target module from the task's `Contract` section and carries the outcome ladder (expected red -> step 3; accidentally green -> back to Tess; cannot run -> `red_check: skipped:<cause>`, fail loud). One verdict stays here: when an **imported** Contract-named target path does not exist on disk yet, skip the invocation entirely and write `red_check = \"n/a:new_module\"` to the attempt entry.\n\n### 3. Implement against tests (Ivan - implementor)\n\nIvan's job: make the failing tests pass. Tests ARE the spec.\n\n**A small rework task skips this whole step.** In rework mode, before rendering anything, check `references/rework-mode.md` § Micro lane: at most two non-CRITICAL findings in at most two files that are clean at claim time, and the orchestrator edits them itself (steps 2.7-2.95 skipped, Pat kept), reverting to the normal lane when the diff overruns.\n\n**Ivan receives:** failing test file paths and their content, architecture context (AGENTS.md, interfaces, relevant modules), and existing code patterns to follow. **Ivan does NOT receive:** the task's acceptance criteria prose (tests replace this) or permission to modify test files.\n\n**Test-only, docs-only and config-only tasks (Tess skipped at 2.7):** there are no failing tests, so write the task's `Verify:` line and its `Acceptance criteria` bullets to `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-checks.txt` and pass that as `--set-file FAILING_TESTS=` instead of the `--set-cmd` below; `FILE_PATHS` is the test, doc or config files the task touches (Ivan may edit test files his allowlist names). Step 2.95 is skipped and the attempt records `red_check` as `n/a:test-only-task`, `n/a:docs-only-task` or `n/a:config-only-task`. Pat's step-5.7 review runs for a test-only task only in rework mode — outside it, step 5.7's own test-only gate skips him and stamps `review: \"skipped:test-only\"`; the docs-only and config-only skip there is unchanged.\n\nRender: one Bash call. **Task-authored prose never crosses the shell** — write it to a scratch file with the Write tool and pass `--set-file`; see § Passing values to render_prompt.py. Every interpolated path is `shlex.quote()`-d (or bash's `printf '%q '`) before it lands inside a `--set-cmd` value:\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/ivan.md \\\n  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-ivan-<task-id>.txt \\\n  --set-cmd FAILING_TESTS=\"cat $(printf '%q ' <test_file_1> [test_file_2 ...])\" \\\n  --set-file ARCHITECTURE_CONTEXT=<a single existing file, e.g. AGENTS.md, when one file covers it> \\\n  --set-file FILE_PATHS=docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-files.txt \\\n  --set RETRY_INSTRUCTION=\"\" --dispatch-kind ivan --dispatch-task <task-id> \\\n  --require-file <each absolute FILE_PATHS entry that exists today, one flag per path> \\\n  --require-parent <each absolute FILE_PATHS entry the task creates, one flag per path>\n```\n`FILE_PATHS` is the newline-separated list from the task's Contract section, written to that scratch file — a Contract path can contain a space or a shell metacharacter, so it is never passed as a `--set` word. Every entry is absolute and every entry appears in a `--require-file`/`--require-parent` flag (§ Passing values to render_prompt.py, Dispatch-target preflight).\nWhen architecture context spans more than one file, use the same `--set-cmd ARCHITECTURE_CONTEXT=\"cat $(printf '%q ' <file_1> <file_2>)\"` shape. `RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is the literal empty string on this, the initial dispatch. The stdout integer from this call **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement — no separate `wc -c`; oversize handling and what `ivan.md` already bakes in are in `references/subagent-dispatch.md`. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-ivan-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source, watchdog per the existing Subagent Watchdog section — unchanged.\n\n**If the task description is ambiguous** (multiple interpretations, unclear scope, unstated format/fields/location), stop before dispatching Ivan and surface the ambiguity to the user. See Example 1 in `references/code-quality-examples.md`. Do not dispatch with guessed-at requirements.\n\n**Deterministic routing table.** Read the claimed task's tier (`state.tasks[i].model`) and qwen-eligibility flag (`state.tasks[i].qwen_eligible`), then cross-reference the \"Gemini-first tasks\" UI definition in **Implementor Selection** above. The planner flag encodes backend + Haiku/Sonnet + exactly one writable file + no public-contract edit; missing eligibility is false. Preserve the existing `ui` → `tier` → `contract` → `files` exclusion precedence.\n\n**Runtime write-set reconciliation (before implementor selection).** Read the exact newline-delimited `FILE_PATHS` scratch file rendered for Ivan; ignore blank lines and count distinct paths. Tess-owned read-only tests are not in this list. After the `fable` override, zero paths fail closed to Claude at the task tier (no Codex interception, `preflight_outcome: null`, attempt `qwen_excluded_reason: \"files\"`). A test-only write set keeps the non-Qwen Claude path at its task tier; derive `is_test_only` from the existing step-2.7 classification using repo-relative paths, never absolute path ancestors, and pass it in the effective copy. For an otherwise Qwen-eligible backend Haiku/Sonnet task, two or more paths replace eligibility with false and exclusion with `files` **in a per-task effective copy only**; stamp the eventual attempt `qwen_excluded_reason: \"files\"`, `preflight_outcome: null`. Apply the table and all six Codex interception fences to that effective copy: two/three-file tasks can still take Codex, otherwise Claude at tier. Exactly one non-empty path may reach row 5. Do not rewrite planner metadata or unrelated state, and do not replace an existing UI, tier, or contract exclusion. This fence also applies under `legacy`.\n\nApply the rows in this order — the first match wins (in practice `qwen_eligible == true` already excludes UI and `opus`, so the order resolves any apparent overlap deterministically):\n\n| # | Task class | Implementor | Reference |\n|---|------------|-------------|-----------|\n| 1 | UI / visual task (per \"Gemini-first tasks\") | Gemini if available, else Claude at `state.tasks[i].model` | `references/gemini-integration.md` |\n| 2 | Backend `opus` tier | Claude Opus (Agent dispatch) | — |\n| 3 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"`, qwen capability breaker tripped (`qwen_breaker.tripped == true`, after the batch-scope check below) | Claude at the task's ORIGINAL tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) — **skip the preflight probe**, stamp the eventual attempt `breaker_skipped:true` | qwen capability breaker (below) |\n| 4 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, and `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_memory_pressure.py --max-level <ladder § Memory gate value>` exits non-zero | Claude at the task's ORIGINAL tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) — **skip the preflight probe**; stamp the attempt `preflight_outcome: null` and `qwen_excluded_reason: \"memory_pressure\"` (exit 1) or `\"memory_probe_failed\"` (exit 2) | `scripts/check_memory_pressure.py` |\n| 5 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, row 4 did not fire, healthy qwen infra | Local qwen via `use-qwen` helper | `references/qwen-integration.md` |\n| 6 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, row 4 did not fire, **unhealthy** qwen infra | Claude at the task's original tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) | `references/qwen-integration.md` (Preflight) |\n| 7 | Backend, effective `qwen_eligible == false` (or absent) | Claude at the task's tier (e.g. a two-file `sonnet` task → Claude Sonnet, subject to Codex interception) | — |\n\n**Codex rung interception.** After the table above yields its verdict, dispatch **codex** instead of the Claude implementor the table named when all six fences hold (verdict is \"Claude at the task's tier\"/\"ORIGINAL tier\", `codex_eligible(task)`, `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG != \"off\"`, `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"`, a `\"healthy\"` batch probe, and a terminal attempt that was not itself codex). **Read `references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex rung interception before the first codex dispatch of a batch** — it states each fence exactly and why fence 4 is not optional.\n\n**Before a Qwen dispatch**, read `references/qwen-integration.md` § Output guards and run its `check_qwen_output.py before` command. It requires a clean implementation slice and canonical Tess tests, and captures this dispatch's baseline. A failed preparation skips Qwen and uses Claude at tier without spending a Qwen attempt; retain the guard diagnostic in the task output and preserve the actual preflight verdict; do not let pre-existing task edits masquerade as Qwen output.\n\n**`fable` overrides this table outright.** A task carrying `state.tasks[i].model: \"fable\"` — set only by the Fable rescue gate (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md` § Rework escalation exhausted) — never routes to qwen and never to Gemini: dispatch a Claude Agent at `model: \"fable\"`, whatever the rows above would pick. `fable` is never a session model and is never selected autonomously, so the human rescue gate is the only way in (`run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Fable rescue).\n\n**qwen capability breaker (routing-time consult, row 3).** Guarded by `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"` (`model-ladder.md` § Kill-switches) — under `legacy` the breaker is fully off, row 3 never fires, and rows 5-6 behave exactly as today's rows 3-4. The memory-pressure gate (row 4) is a deliberate always-on exception to that kill-switch: it carries no `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION` guard (unlike the breaker) and keeps firing under `legacy` — a host-safety mechanism, not a quality mechanism, so the kill-switch that restores old routing semantics must not also switch off OOM protection.\n\n**Read `references/qwen-integration.md` § Batch-scoped preflight before the first qwen dispatch of a batch** — it carries the breaker's batch-scope reset and row-3 consult, and the `state.qwen_preflight` cache procedure (probe once per batch, reuse the verdict, and the two backend-health signals that force a re-probe). One rule lives here too, because a passing run never opens that reference: a qwen gate pass resets `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive` to 0, so the breaker trips only on two CONSECUTIVE qwen gate failures.\n\n**Re-evaluate the routing table for EVERY claimed task — no session-level memory.** The table is per-task, and so is the qwen one-shot-per-task budget: exactly one qwen dispatch per task (success OR failure) — a qwen attempt on task A never excludes qwen for task B. There is no per-PRD or per-batch qwen cap; every eligible task is routed independently. Do not generalize a fallback (\"qwen was slow on the last task, route the rest to Claude\") — that decision belongs to the table and the preflight, not to session memory (observed failure: `references/design-rationale.md` § no session memory). Self-check before each initial Ivan dispatch: use the **effective routing decision**, not the persisted eligibility alone. A Claude fallback must be justified by a non-healthy preflight, breaker/pressure exclusion, write-set or test-only fence, or a recorded output-guard preparation failure; preserve its actual preflight verdict (null when never run). If none applies, re-run the table. Capability escalations dispatch directly to the higher rung and are not initial routing decisions.\n\n**An escalated tier belongs to its task and dies with it (PRD 00111).** When a task escalates — in-loop at step 5.5, or by review flag through `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 — the higher tier is written to that task's `model` field in `state.tasks[i]`, and nowhere else. Every other task still enters at the tier `/autopilot:plan-tasks` classified for it: a task escalated to `opus` is followed by an unrelated `haiku` task dispatching at `haiku`, in the same PRD and the same session. Do not carry a tier sideways (\"the last task needed opus, so this PRD runs at opus\") — that is the same session-memory mistake the routing rule above forbids, priced one rung higher. Nothing escalation-related survives into the next PRD either: `autopilot reset-prd` drops `tasks` (the per-task tiers), `rework_task_ids`, `cap_rotations` and `stall_reason`, and zeroes `replan_count` (`run-autopilot/cli/records.py` `PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`). Session-model decay is the separate, matching rule in `run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Decay.\n\nA helper that does not resolve, or fails at runtime, falls back to Claude at the task's tier, and every dispatch of either kind satisfies the **Subagent Dispatch Budget** and the **Subagent Watchdog**. **Read `references/gemini-integration.md` § Availability before the first UI-task dispatch of a batch** (what \"Gemini if available\" probes, row 1); the helper-vs-Agent mechanics are in `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Mechanism and tier.\n\n**Codex implementor mechanics.** The HOW of the codex rung — batch health probe, dispatch checklist, TOOL-GATE NOTICE — lives in `references/codex-implementor.md`; **read it in full before the first codex probe or dispatch of a batch**. Two invariants worth repeating at the call site: never `-y` (the `-a` grant covers this rung only), and on any codex timeout `TaskStop` + verify-gone BEFORE dispatching the Claude fallback.\n\n### 4. Handle result\n\nA **Success** from Qwen must first run `check_qwen_output.py after` per `references/qwen-integration.md` § Output guards, **before staging, committing, or running step 5.5**. Only exit 0 continues to step 5; exit 1 enters `references/gate-failure.md` § Qwen output rejection; exit 2 stops acceptance until the guard/canonical tests can be verified. After a non-success Qwen result (including timeout/lost result), first stop the helper and verify it is gone, then run the same guard with `--tests-only` before any fallback or partial-output acceptance; exit 1 takes mutation recovery, exit 2 stops, exit 0 resumes the original failure handler without a no-edit classification. Other successful implementors continue to step 5. For timeout, context exceeded, error, lost/hung result, or a codex dispatch that timed out or wrote nothing: **read `references/gate-failure.md` § Step 4 result table before acting on it.**\n\n### 4.2. Infrastructure-failure circuit breaker\n\nA lost/empty Agent result or a watchdog-killed hang is an infrastructure failure, not a content failure. Do **not** silently re-dispatch in a loop — two back-to-back infrastructure failures on the same task once caused a multi-hour stall (`references/design-rationale.md` § circuit breaker).\n\nRe-dispatch the **same** task at most **once** — that cap is separate from the test-failure retry cap (step 5.5) and the review-cycle cap (step 5.7). **Read `references/gate-failure.md` § Infrastructure-failure circuit breaker before re-dispatching**: it carries the working-tree check and the second-failure stop (attempt entry `cause: \"subagent_infra_failure\"`, `state.stall_reason`, escalate, never advance).\n\n### 4.5. Debug on error\n\nIf the tool returned an error, invoke the `debug-stuck-agent` skill to diagnose the root cause before reporting to the user. If debugging resolves the issue, continue to step 5. If not, report to user and keep task in_progress.\n\n### 5. Commit changes\n\nStage exactly this task's files, then commit in a separate Bash call. **Never `git add -A` or `git add .`** — the worktree is live (the user edits files during dispatches), and a bulk add sweeps foreign uncommitted work into the task commit (memory: feedback_subagents_vs_live_worktree).\n\n1. Build the stage list: the paths from Ivan's `FILES_TOUCHED:` footer (see **Assumptions footer**), plus any build-generated files this task's changes legitimately produced (lockfiles, snapshots, generated bindings) — identified from `git status --porcelain` output, never guessed.\n2. Fallback when the footer is absent or `none` while the tree is dirty (legacy retry prompts, malformed report): stage the intersection of dirty paths with the exact files the plan task names; treat every other dirty path as foreign.\n3. Run `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_reflow.py <stage list>` over that list: exit 1 → stamp `reflow: \"<path>:<hunks>\"` (`;`-joined for several) on the attempt and name the files in the phase report; exit 2 → `reflow: \"failed:<stderr>\"`; exit 0 → no field. Staging and the commit proceed unchanged in every branch — see `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Reflow tripwire.\n\n```bash\ngit add <path> [<path> ...]\n```\n```bash\ngit commit -m \"<type>(<scope>): <description>\"\n```\n\nAny other dirty path is **foreign**: leave it unstaged and untouched, and name it in the phase report (fail loud) — the same never-commit-foreign-work rule the step-5.5 ESCALATE reset guard enforces. A store write (state.json, a ledger append, a review file) is never foreign dirt here: `autopilot dirty` is store-exempt, and that is the check this rule means.\n\nNever chain these with `&&` in a single Bash call. Commit message rules: conventional commit format, one line, no period, reference the task ID if available.\n\nBefore committing a `feat`/`fix` (or breaking) change, verify CHANGELOG.md is staged in the same commit per rules/changelog.md — repos with a declared no-changelog exception (e.g. the buvis home repo) skip this check.\n\n**If a commit (or its `git add`) is rejected** — `aegis`'s `validate_commit_msg.py` blocks a non-conventional message (boilerplate trailer, HEREDOC, bad format — `rules/development-workflow.md`), or warden denies the `git add`/`git commit` command: read the deny reason from the blocked tool result (aegis names the format violation; warden's reason usually names the preferred command form), fix the message or the command accordingly, and **retry the commit ONCE**. Still rejected after the one repair → ESCALATE: append an attempt-log entry (`outcome: \"aborted\"`, `cause: \"commit_rejected\"`), then report to the user (interactive) or take the loop-mode stall path (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md`, `site: \"sub_skill_fail\"`, `detail` = the deny reason) — never leave the task's work uncommitted-and-unrecorded, and never reach for `--no-verify` to bypass the hook. This branch applies to every commit this skill makes (step 2.85 tests and the step-2.9 strengthen commit, step 5 implementation, the step-5.5/5.7 re-commits, the step-5.6 deslop commit).\n\n### 5.5. Do NOT run the full project test suite, smoke tests, integration tests, or lint here — those run once at the end of the phase (step 7).\n\n- Target the narrowest scope that covers the new tests — **read `references/gate-failure.md` § Narrow scope before the first gate run of a batch** for the per-language commands.\n- Never dispatch Tess to weaken tests.\n- **Retry prompts** (feedback retry, repair re-dispatch, escalation dispatch, step 5.7's confirmed findings, step 7's regression fix) re-render `ivan.md` in full from `references/gate-failure.md` § Retry render — only `FAILING_TESTS` and `RETRY_INSTRUCTION` change, and a missing placeholder exits 1.\n\n**Do not run here:** `cargo test --workspace`, `cargo clippy --workspace`, `./tests/smoke.sh`, `./tests/integration.sh`, `cargo test-full`, or any equivalent full-suite command. Commit tests\n\nTwo Bash calls, never chained: `git add <test_files>`, then `git commit -m \"test(<scope>): add tests for <feature>\"`.\n\nTests are committed separately before implementation, making the TDD boundary auditable in git history — and before Devon, so the quality-gated tests never sit uncommitted through the longest dispatches of a task (a rotation mid-Devon lost a 603-line test file once, and a rotation after a committed test file re-dispatched Tess with the identical prompt; PRD 00202).\n\n**Capture this task's test-commit SHA** immediately and hold it in-session as `<test_commit_sha>` — the last test commit, so a step-2.9 strengthen commit replaces it — **read `references/gate-failure.md` § Test-commit SHA before moving on** for the command and its one reader, step 5.5's ESCALATE reset. Step 5.7's `BASE_SHA` is `<task_base_sha>` from step 2, not this.\n\n### 2.9. Adversarial validation (Devon - devil's advocate)\n\n**Tier gate — Devon runs on the deepest rungs only, `opus` and `fable`.** Read the task's `model` field (`state.tasks[i].model`):\n\n| `state.tasks[i].model` | Devon (step 2.9) |\n|-----------------------|-------------------|\n| `opus` | dispatch Devon (below) |\n| `fable` | dispatch Devon (below) — the rescue rung runs the deepest pipeline, like `opus` |\n| anything else — `haiku`, `sonnet`, absent/legacy or unknown (both treated as `sonnet`) | skip Devon, proceed to step 2.95 |\n\nThe step-2.8 test quality gate is **unchanged** and runs for every tier — only this Agent dispatch is conditional. A Devon dispatch obeys the **Per-task model dispatch** rule (passes `model: opus`, or `model: fable` on a rescued task). Escalation interplay is automatic: when the review gate escalates a review-flagged task to `opus`, the rework attempt regains Devon with no extra mechanism. (Why tier-gated: `references/design-rationale.md` § tier-gated pipeline.)\n\n**Prose gate — Devon skips prose-pin tasks.** When every test file Tess created or changed for this task is a prose pin (its basename ends in `_prose.py`), skip Devon, record `devon: skipped:prose` in the task's attempt entry, and proceed to step 2.95. A substring pin cannot see negation, inversion or past-tense narration, so a Devon dispatch on such a task never breaks the tests (four of four on 2026-09-14/15, about 55 minutes of Opus time with no kept strengthening).\n\n**Earlier-task tests.** When step 2.7 skipped Tess because an earlier task of this plan committed this task's tests, Devon still runs at `opus` and `fable` against those files: his test-runner command names them, and an exploit routes to Tess's one strengthen dispatch exactly as for tests written in this task. A plan that splits tests from implementation must not lose the adversarial round the implementation tier bought.\n\nDevon runs once per task; when he breaks the tests, Tess strengthens once and the task proceeds on the strengthened tests with Devon never dispatched again (seven measured re-checks on 2026-09-25/26 changed no test; the one that named a real exploit was dismissed and the review caught it). See `references/adversarial-test-prompt.md` § Procedure for how Devon runs, and the file's prompt template section for what it receives. Devon prompts must satisfy the **Subagent Dispatch Budget**. Devon's prompt is filled by hand, so measure it and open his row in one call — `record_dispatch.py start --kind devon --task <task-id> --prompt-file <the written prompt>` prints the byte count that **is** his Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement, then the id — before the Agent call, and hold the id for the `end` call (§ Subagent Dispatch Budget and Watchdog, Telemetry).\n\n### 2.95. Red-check — watch the tests fail\n\nRun the newly committed tests once, before any Ivan dispatch, at the narrowest scope (the same commands step 5.5 uses). Red is the point: a failure proves the tests bind behavior that does not exist yet (rules/testing.md fail-first). Implicitly skipped when step 2.7 was skipped and no earlier task of this plan committed this task's tests (nothing to run).\n\n**Read `references/red-check.md` before the first red-check of a batch** — it resolves the target module from the task's `Contract` section and carries the outcome ladder (expected red -> step 3; accidentally green -> back to Tess; cannot run -> `red_check: skipped:<cause>`, fail loud). One verdict stays here: when an **imported** Contract-named target path does not exist on disk yet, skip the invocation entirely and write `red_check = \"n/a:new_module\"` to the attempt entry.\n\n### 3. Implement against tests (Ivan - implementor)\n\nIvan's job: make the failing tests pass. Tests ARE the spec.\n\n**A small rework task skips this whole step.** In rework mode, before rendering anything, check `references/rework-mode.md` § Micro lane: at most two non-CRITICAL findings in at most two files that are clean at claim time, and the orchestrator edits them itself (steps 2.7-2.95 skipped, Pat kept), reverting to the normal lane when the diff overruns.\n\n**Ivan receives:** failing test file paths and their content, architecture context (AGENTS.md, interfaces, relevant modules), and existing code patterns to follow. **Ivan does NOT receive:** the task's acceptance criteria prose (tests replace this) or permission to modify test files.\n\n**Test-only, docs-only and config-only tasks (Tess skipped at 2.7):** there are no failing tests, so write the task's `Verify:` line and its `Acceptance criteria` bullets to `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-checks.txt` and pass that as `--set-file FAILING_TESTS=` instead of the `--set-cmd` below; `FILE_PATHS` is the test, doc or config files the task touches (Ivan may edit test files his allowlist names). Step 2.95 is skipped and the attempt records `red_check` as `n/a:test-only-task`, `n/a:docs-only-task` or `n/a:config-only-task`. Pat's step-5.7 review runs for a test-only task only in rework mode — outside it, step 5.7's own test-only gate skips him and stamps `review: \"skipped:test-only\"`; the docs-only and config-only skip there is unchanged.\n\nRender: one Bash call. **Task-authored prose never crosses the shell** — write it to a scratch file with the Write tool and pass `--set-file`; see § Passing values to render_prompt.py. Every interpolated path is `shlex.quote()`-d (or bash's `printf '%q '`) before it lands inside a `--set-cmd` value:\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/agents/ivan.md \\\n  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-ivan-<task-id>.txt \\\n  --set-cmd FAILING_TESTS=\"cat $(printf '%q ' <test_file_1> [test_file_2 ...])\" \\\n  --set-file ARCHITECTURE_CONTEXT=<a single existing file, e.g. AGENTS.md, when one file covers it> \\\n  --set-file FILE_PATHS=docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-files.txt \\\n  --set RETRY_INSTRUCTION=\"\" --dispatch-kind ivan --dispatch-task <task-id> \\\n  --require-file <each absolute FILE_PATHS entry that exists today, one flag per path> \\\n  --require-parent <each absolute FILE_PATHS entry the task creates, one flag per path>\n```\n`FILE_PATHS` is the newline-separated list from the task's Contract section, written to that scratch file — a Contract path can contain a space or a shell metacharacter, so it is never passed as a `--set` word. Every entry is absolute and every entry appears in a `--require-file`/`--require-parent` flag (§ Passing values to render_prompt.py, Dispatch-target preflight).\nWhen architecture context spans more than one file, use the same `--set-cmd ARCHITECTURE_CONTEXT=\"cat $(printf '%q ' <file_1> <file_2>)\"` shape. `RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is the literal empty string on this, the initial dispatch. The stdout integer from this call **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement — no separate `wc -c`; oversize handling and what `ivan.md` already bakes in are in `references/subagent-dispatch.md`. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-ivan-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source, watchdog per the existing Subagent Watchdog section — unchanged.\n\n**If the task description is ambiguous** (multiple interpretations, unclear scope, unstated format/fields/location), stop before dispatching Ivan and surface the ambiguity to the user. See Example 1 in `references/code-quality-examples.md`. Do not dispatch with guessed-at requirements.\n\n**Deterministic routing table.** Read the claimed task's tier (`state.tasks[i].model`) and qwen-eligibility flag (`state.tasks[i].qwen_eligible`), then cross-reference the \"Gemini-first tasks\" UI definition in **Implementor Selection** above. The planner flag encodes backend + Haiku/Sonnet + exactly one writable file + no public-contract edit; missing eligibility is false. Preserve the existing `ui` → `tier` → `contract` → `files` exclusion precedence.\n\n**Runtime write-set reconciliation (before impleme\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

A no-owner call cannot consume reserve capacity. Maximum response/descriptor growth for both emergency operations fits within 2 MiB under these explicit core bounds; test byte saturation independently of receipt-count saturation and reject oversized candidates before preparing intent. This prepublication check is part of the transaction admission, not a later _canonical_bytes failure after credentials changed. At 4096 entries the workflow is sealed against all new mutations; exact receipt retrieval and snapshot remain available. Capacity is an explicit terminal boundary, not an unspecified future repair. Operator exit procedure: finish/reconcile jobs (none supported here), release/recover ownership using reserve capacity, verify an owner-null snapshot, copy the entire private controller directory to a private offline archive and verify every file hash, then rename the original private directory into a sibling private archive named by workflow ID, and open a new workflow at the fixed empty controller path. Never delete the archive. Archived state, credentials, receipts and schema remain replayable by placing the original directory back at its original project binding while the new workflow is offline; never merge identities. README documents the ordered manual procedure; tests saturate normal capacity, clear the owner through reserved capacity, validate the archive/hash/restore roundtrip and open a distinct workflow. No archival or state removal runs automatically. If an active owner reaches hard capacity through externally corrupted state, return recovery_required and retain all evidence rather than overriding it. Top-level `lease_epoch` starts at 0 and increases on acquire/recover/release, retained even while owner is null.\n\n### Protocol\n\nCLI argv is `[\"python3\", \"<installed-plugin-root>/controller/main.py\"]`. Commands are `--json contract`, `--json snapshot --project-root PATH`, `--json apply --project-root PATH --request FILE`; apply accepts `--actor-file PATH`. No shell invocation or process launch. +{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_46","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/work/references/subagent-dispatch.md\\\").read_text()[:23000])'\"","aggregated_output":"# Subagent Dispatch\n\nHow to safely make an Agent call from `/autopilot:work`. Two rules apply to **every**\nAgent dispatch (Tess, Ivan, Devon, or the code reviewer): the Dispatch Budget and\nthe Watchdog. Read this file before your first Agent dispatch in a session.\nBare step numbers below (`step 4`, `step 4.2`, `step 2`, `step 6`) refer to\n`SKILL.md`'s Workflow sections.\n\n## Role effort\n\nCoordinator effort is not worker effort. For a Claude task dispatch, use\n`subagent_type: \"autopilot:worker-<tier>\"` with the task's selected\n`model: <tier>` and the complete rendered persona as its prompt. These native\nagent definitions set haiku/low, sonnet/medium, opus/high, and fable/xhigh.\nDo not dispatch a generic agent that would inherit coordinator effort. Keep\nall persona, test-author, adversary, allowlist and evidence obligations intact.\nThe model ladder and human-gated Fable authorization remain authoritative.\nAlice and Blake use their named reviewer definitions at high effort; external\nClaude task reviews use `sonnet-run.sh --effort high`. External implementations\nuse `--effort medium` for Sonnet, `--effort high` for Opus, and `--effort xhigh`\nonly for a human-authorized Fable rescue. Host adapters for other providers\nretain their own explicit role mappings.\n\n## Subagent Dispatch Budget\n\nEvery prompt passed to the Agent tool (Tess the test author, Ivan the implementor, Devon the adversary, or code reviewer) must be **≤ 50 000 bytes**.\n\nPostToolUse hooks do not fire inside subagents (see `SKILL.md` \"CRITICAL: One Task at a Time\"), so the runtime context cap from PRD 00024 cannot abort a subagent that grows past 200K. The bound must be enforced at dispatch time, before the Agent call.\n\n**Procedure before every Agent dispatch:**\n\n1. Render the prompt from its persona with `scripts/render_prompt.py`, per the call shape `SKILL.md` gives for that dispatch (Tess 2.7, Ivan 3 / 5.5 / 7, Pat 5.7). The orchestrator does **not** assemble the prompt string itself: the persona files carry every fixed block, and `SKILL.md` § Passing values to render_prompt.py decides which flag each value takes.\n2. Measure: the byte count `render_prompt.py` prints on stdout **is** the measurement. There is no separate `wc -c` step and no scratch copy to measure — the render already wrote the file to its `--out` path (`docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-<persona>-<task-id>.txt`, a per-task filename, since a fixed name collides when independent rework tasks dispatch in parallel).\n3. If the prompt exceeds 50 000 bytes:\n   - Trim by removing the lowest-priority context first (large example files, full architecture docs). Re-measure.\n   - If still oversized after one trim pass, abort the task. Wire the abort\n     through the same handoff the runtime context-cap hook uses, so\n     `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 0 of the next session replans the PRD in place\n     (PRD stays in `wip/`; see Phase 0 step 1's replan procedure — parallel\n     to `context_overrun`):\n     1. Append to `state.task_aborts[]`:\n        ```json\n        {\"task_id\": \"<id>\", \"turn\": -1, \"total_input_tokens\": <prompt-bytes/4>, \"cause\": \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"}\n        ```\n     2. Set `state.stall_reason`:\n        ```json\n        {\"stalled\": \"subagent_prompt_overrun\", \"task\": \"<id>\", \"prompt_bytes\": <prompt-bytes>}\n        ```\n        In the same state write, set `state.phase` and `state.next_phase`\n        to `\"build\"`. Planning is a build sub-step, not a valid phase.\n        Keep `stall_reason` set: Phase 0 handles it before task dispatch\n        and follows `references/recovery.md`'s replan procedure. This also\n        routes review-phase rework overruns to the build recovery handler.\n     3. Do not write a signal file. The wrapper reads `state.stall_reason`\n        and `state.next_phase` after the turn ends; a manual invocation\n        uses the same state. Preserve task history and abort evidence for\n        the recovery handler before it clears tasks.\n     4. Append an attempt-log entry per `references/attempt-logging.md`:\n        `outcome: \"aborted\"`, `cause: \"subagent_prompt_overrun\"`,\n        `model` from `state.tasks[i].model`,\n        `review_cycle: null` (Phase 3) or current `state.cycle` (rework).\n     5. Report cause `subagent_prompt_overrun` and stop work on this task.\n4. The abort-instruction line is **baked into the persona files**, so there is nothing to prepend:\n   ```\n   Abort and report if you read more than 100K of total input. Return the partial result and an abort_reason: context_overrun field.\n   ```\n   `agents/ivan.md` and `references/tess-prompt.md` both carry it verbatim, and a render therefore cannot omit it. Trimming at step 3 removes context, never this line. If you add a new persona to the dispatch set, put the line in the persona file rather than re-introducing a prepend step here — a prepend that some call sites remember and others forget is exactly how Tess lost this guard once.\n\n**Rationale:** soft enforcement — the subagent honors the instruction — but `/autopilot:plan-tasks`'s 150K per-task budget bounds how much context `/autopilot:work` can plausibly hand off anyway. Combined, the 50K dispatch cap, the 100K subagent-internal cap, and the 150K per-task cap keep subagent contexts well under any work-tier model's window (200K for the base tiers; the `claude-fable-5[1m]` default carries 1M).\n\n## Subagent Watchdog\n\nEvery Agent dispatch in this skill (Tess, Ivan, Devon, or the code reviewer) must be wrapped in a watchdog. A dispatched subagent can crash, lose its result, or hang silently — and a foreground `Agent` call then blocks this session **indefinitely** with no signal. Observed failure: a dead subagent left the parent session blocked for 1.5 hours until the user manually intervened.\n\n**Dispatch protocol — applies to every Agent call:**\n\n1. Dispatch with `run_in_background: true` (plus `model` per `SKILL.md` \"Per-task model dispatch\"). Record the dispatch wall-clock time. Arm the watchdog as a `Monitor` timer (`sleep 900; echo \"WATCHDOG: ...\"`) — **15 minutes is a check-in, not a kill deadline**.\n2. When the agent's completion notification arrives first, `TaskStop` the watchdog timer immediately (a stale timer fires later and reads as a hang that is not there), retrieve the result, close the dispatch row (§ Dispatch telemetry below), and continue to `SKILL.md` step 4.\n3. **When the timer fires first, probe for progress before any kill** — two cheap read-only checks:\n   - `git status --porcelain` (the repo's own git context): have the task's AUTHORIZED surfaces changed since dispatch?\n   - `ls -la` on the dispatch's `<task-id>.output` file: is its mtime/size still advancing? (Never Read that file — it is the full subagent transcript and will overflow context.)\n   Branch on the evidence:\n   - **Progress on either probe** → the agent is working, not hung. Re-arm the timer (10-15 min) and keep waiting. Hard cap: **45 minutes wall-clock per dispatch**, after which treat it as hung regardless of probes.\n   - **No progress on BOTH probes across two consecutive checks** (or the 45-min cap) → `TaskStop` the agent, then close its dispatch row exactly once for this attempt, on what `TaskStop` reports (§ Dispatch telemetry): if it reports the task **already completed**, the \"hang\" was a late completion notification — treat it as a normal completion, not a failure, and close the row `ok`; otherwise close it `--outcome timeout` and handle it as the **Result lost / hung** row of `SKILL.md`'s Handle result table (step 4) → the infrastructure-failure circuit breaker (step 4.2). Do **not** treat a hung agent as a content **Timeout**: it produced no usable work, so splitting the task (the Timeout remedy) would split nothing.\n4. **After ANY kill, inspect before re-dispatching.** Run `git status` over the authorized surfaces:\n   - **Qwen prerequisite:** verify the helper is gone, then run `check_qwen_output.py after --tests-only` with its captured snapshot per `qwen-integration.md` § Output guards, before any verification below. Exit 1 takes Qwen test-mutation recovery; exit 2 stops acceptance. Only exit 0 permits independent verification or continuation against canonical tests.\n   - **Work looks complete** → the kill landed at the agent's verification/reporting tail (the common case — measured 2026-07-31: 5 kills in one session, 0 true hangs; 3 had complete work on disk). Verify the work INDEPENDENTLY (run the task's own verify commands yourself); green → accept it as a normal completion. The report footers are lost with the agent, so reconstruct `FILES_TOUCHED:` from the tree and record the missing `ASSUMPTIONS:` footer in the assumptions ledger.\n   - **Work is partial** → the step-4.2 re-dispatch must be a CONTINUATION brief that names the completed surfaces (verified by you) so the fresh agent does not redo or clobber them.\n\n**Right-size multi-surface briefs — the main driver of slow dispatches.** A dispatch touching 3+ files, or any file over ~400 lines, must carry a READING BUDGET in its brief: exact `rg`/Read line anchors per surface, an ordered per-surface work plan, and per-surface verification so partial progress survives a kill. Measured 2026-07-31: an anchored continuation finished in one window a job whose unanchored first dispatch had produced zero edits in 18 minutes of reading.\n\nA background dispatch does **not** relax the one-task-at-a-time rule: dispatch one agent, wait for it (or its watchdog), then proceed. Never have two plan-task agents in flight at once. The watchdog converts a silent infinite block into a detectable failure that the Handle result table routes to the circuit breaker.\n\n**Helper-script dispatches** (`use-codex`/`use-gemini`/`use-qwen` helper scripts, which run as background Bash tasks) follow the same protocol: dispatch with `run_in_background: true`, then wait with `TaskOutput(task_id, block=true, timeout=600000)` (600000 ms = 10 min, the max per call) — it returns on completion or at the deadline; on a still-running return, re-issue the wait once, then treat a second timeout as a hang. Close the dispatch row when `TaskOutput` returns (`ok`, or `error` on a non-zero exit) or after that second timeout (`timeout`) — § Dispatch telemetry. Never hand-roll a `while`/`if`/`wc -c` stability loop in `Monitor` or `Bash` to detect completion: its shell control flow cannot be statically analyzed by Warden, so it prompts for approval and stalls an unattended autopilot run.\n\n**qwen helper-script deadline.** qwen dispatches use the **10 min × 2 `TaskOutput`** wait pattern above — the same as `use-codex` and `use-gemini` — NOT the 15-min `Monitor` watchdog (which applies to Agent dispatches like Tess / Ivan / Devon / reviewer). The `pi` invocation that `qwen-run.sh` wraps is a Bash helper-script dispatch, so the helper-script deadline applies. Local-inference latency on a 30B-parameter qwen model can routinely exceed several minutes; the 10-min × 2 budget accommodates that without conflating it with the Agent watchdog.\n\n**Six deadlines exist, by mechanism — keep them distinct:**\n\n- **15 min check-in, progress-probed extensions, 45 min hard cap** — `Monitor` watchdog on Tess/Ivan/Devon/reviewer dispatches (this section). Honest single-task dispatch runtimes measured 2026-07-31 ranged 2-30 min (median ~12; multi-surface tasks 19-30), so a fixed 15-min kill destroys nearly-finished work.\n- **10 min × 2** — `TaskOutput` waits on `use-codex`/`use-gemini` helper-script Bash dispatches (paragraph above).\n- **20 min** — `Monitor` waits on backgrounded `cargo` full-suite runs (see `SKILL.md` \"CRITICAL: Never Ask the User to Run Commands\").\n- **60000 ms** — the Bash `timeout` on a foreground inspection call (§ Foreground command budgets below).\n- **300000 ms** — the Bash `timeout` on a foreground lint or narrow-test call (§ Foreground command budgets below).\n- **600000 ms** — the Bash `timeout` on a foreground full suite, the tool's maximum (§ Foreground command budgets below).\n\nThey differ because the work differs — a full Rust test suite legitimately runs longer than a single-task subagent, and a `git status` longer than neither. Do not unify them into one number.\n\n## Foreground command budgets\n\nThe Watchdog above bounds Agent dispatches and helper scripts. It does not bound plain Bash: a foreground `ruff`, `pytest`, `git` or inspection call carries no deadline of this pack's choosing, no no-output probe and no kill path — it inherits the Bash tool's own default (120000 ms) whatever it is doing. That default is not a reliable stop: measured 2026-08-27, a command that combined an inspection read with a Ruff invocation stalled for 17 min 48 s, wrote nothing, and needed a manual interrupt — in a loop whose whole premise is that nobody is watching. The only bound worth relying on is the one the call passes explicitly.\n\nSo every foreground Bash call this pack makes passes an explicit `timeout` (milliseconds; the tool's default is 120000 and its maximum 600000):\n\n| Class | Commands | `timeout` |\n|---|---|---|\n| Inspection | `git diff`, `git status`, `rg`, `ls`, a render call | 60000 |\n| Lint and narrow tests | `ruff check`, `eslint`, step 5.5's narrow test command, step 2.95's red-check, a queued verification check | 300000 |\n| Full suite | step 7's documented or improvised suite, run in the foreground | 600000 |\n\nA command whose class is not documented takes the **inspection** budget. A backgrounded full suite is unchanged — it keeps the 20 min `Monitor` wait in the list above. This section shrinks no deadline this pack already documents. It does tighten one default: an unclassified foreground call used to inherit the Bash tool's own 120000 ms default and now takes the 60000 ms inspection budget. Class a command explicitly rather than leaving it to the catch-all when it legitimately runs longer than a minute.\n\n**When a budget fires.** Re-run the command once at the next larger budget when its class has one (inspection → 300000, lint and narrow tests → 600000). The full suite is already at the tool maximum, so it has no larger budget: its **first** timeout is terminal and is recorded at once, with no re-run.\n\nRecord every timeout, whatever the class: name the command and the budget it blew in the phase report. Step 5.5's narrow tests also stamp `verification: \"timeout:<command>\"` on the task's attempt (`references/attempt-logging.md` § Best-effort gate stamps). Two neighbours record elsewhere, in the field that already owns their outcome: a step-2.95 red-check that times out is a runner that could not execute the tests, so it takes `red_check: \"skipped:<cause>\"` from that step's own ladder (`references/red-check.md`), never `verification`. And step 7 runs after every attempt entry has been written, so a step-7 timeout has no entry to stamp at all and the phase report is its whole record (`references/final-verification.md` § Timed-out commands). Then proceed: the record is a fail-loud marker, not a block, and a timed-out command is never reported as a passed one.\n\n## Never combine inspection with verification\n\nA single Bash call runs **either** an inspection (read, list, search, diff) **or** a verification (test, lint, build) — never both, and never two verifications chained. Split them into two calls, each carrying its own budget from the table above.\n\nRationale: a combined command has two ways to hang and one exit code, so neither the exit status nor the output can be attributed to either half. The pack's existing \"do not chain with `&&`\" instructions (`references/final-verification.md` § What to run, `SKILL.md` step 5's commit pair) are scoped to those two places, so a combined inspect-and-verify command was unremarkable everywhere else — which is how the 17-minute stall above got built.\n\n## Blocked verification and backgrounded commands\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` § CRITICAL: Never Ask the User to Run Commands\n(PRD 00119-v2). Read this when a verification run will not complete.\n\n**When test verification is blocked** (e.g. all cargo processes were backgrounded and the build lock was contended): if the code compiles cleanly and the logic change is correct by inspection, commit and proceed — and record `verification: skipped:<cause>` in the task's attempt entry and the phase report (fail loud; a skipped check must never read as a passed one). The full-suite verification run at the end of the phase will catch regressions. Do not stop and ask the user to run anything.\n\n**When cargo commands get backgrounded by the session**: the Bash tool may background long-running commands regardless of the `run_in_background` flag. Wait for background completions via Monitor (up to 20 minutes for full test suites). Never launch a second cargo command while one is still running — they contend on the build lock and jam the shell. If a Monitor times out, read the output file directly; if the file is empty the build lock was still held, wait longer before retrying.\n\n## Passing values to render_prompt.py\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` § Passing values to render_prompt.py (PRD\n00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the never-`--set` rule and the dispatch-target\npreflight. **Read this section before your first render call in a session.**\n\nEvery render call in the work skill (Tess 2.7, Ivan 3 / 5.5 / 7, Pat 5.7) picks a flag by where the value comes from, not by convenience:\n\n| Value | Flag |\n|---|---|\n| Task-authored prose — subject, description, acceptance criteria, Contract file paths, findings blocks | `--set-file`, from a scratch file written with the **Write tool** |\n| A file that already exists on disk | `--set-file <path>` |\n| Several existing files concatenated | `--set-cmd \"cat $(printf '%q ' <paths>)\"` |\n| A fixed string this skill composes itself, containing no task text | `--set` |\n\nThe `--set-cmd` quoting rule is separate and still applies: any path interpolated into a `--set-cmd` value crosses into a nested shell (`subprocess.run(..., shell=True)`), so quote it with `printf '%q '` or `shlex.quote()` before composing the flag.\n\nA render fills EVERY placeholder the persona carries or exits 1 naming the first missing one. If the printed size exceeds 50 000, trim per the one-pass rule above, then re-render (still one call). `ivan.md` bakes in the code-quality rules block, the abort-instruction line, the read-only-scope note, the dispatch prologue, and the Assumptions/FILES_TOUCHED footers permanently — nothing further needs adding to the prompt by hand.\n\n## Mechanism and tier (moved from SKILL.md, PRD 00119-v2)\n\n`use-qwen`, `use-gemini`, and `use-codex` are Bash helper-script dispatches; Claude implementor passes are Agent dispatches at the task's tier. All three must satisfy the **Subagent Dispatch Budget** and the **Subagent Watchdog**.\n\nThe **Subagent Dispatch Budget** applies regardless of tier. Haiku doesn't earn a smaller cap; opus doesn't earn a larger one.\n\n## Reflow tripwire (step 5, PRD 00148)\n\nA formatter sweep once rewrote a whole file (58 hunks: trailing commas, line splits) during an unrelated dispatch. Nobody asked for it, the trigger is still unknown, and step 5 had no way to see it — so an unattended run stages it into the task commit and the next review cycle re-reads 58 formatting hunks as the task's work. The tripwire does not prevent that. It makes it visible, so the record says what happened and the trigger can eventually be found from data.\n\nRun it after building the stage list and before `git add`, over the same paths:\n\n```bash\npython3 <plugin root>/skills/work/scripts/check_reflow.py <path> [<path> ...]\n```\n\n(`<plugin root>` is the value `SKILL.md` resolves for `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`; a placeholder written in this file would reach the shell empty.) It counts `@@` lines in `git diff -U0 HEAD -- <path>` per path and prints `<path>\\t<hunks>` for each one at or above `--threshold` (default 20; a targeted edit is well under 10). Add `--git-dir`/`--work-tree` in a bare-repo home, the same pair step 5.65's gate already passes.\n\n| Exit | Meaning | Attempt field |\n|---|---|---|\n| 0 | nothing at or above the threshold | `reflow` absent |\n| 1 | at least one path flagged | `reflow: \"<path>:<hunks>\"`, `;`-joined for several, and the phase report names the files |\n| 2 | git could not answer (stderr says why) | `reflow: \"failed:<stderr>\"` |\n\nStaging and the commit proceed unchanged in all three branches. Hunk-scoping a sweep out of a commit stays a manual call (`git apply --cached`), and exit 2 is deliberately not fatal: a broken probe must not block a task, but it must never be recorded as a clean one either.\n\n## Dispatch telemetry (PRD 00168)\n\nNothing above says when anything happened: the attempt record carries no timestamp, and `loop-metrics.jsonl` is one row per session. Measured 2026-08-27, a PRD's review and rework commits spanned 15.3 hours with a 6-hour and a 3.6-hour gap, and no artifact could say whether that was model work, a quota wait, a hung tool or a session handoff. So every dispatch in this skill writes two rows and every session handoff writes one at each end, to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl`, mirrored line for line into `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/ledger/dispatch-metrics.jsonl`. Both are tracked work-management artifacts; the ledger mirror remains the canonical durable copy. `scripts/record_dispatch.py` is the writer; `render_prompt.py` imports it for the start row.\n\n**A telemetry failure is never a dispatch failure.** An unresolvable autopilot dir, an unwritable file or an id with no start row all exit 0 (a failed write says so on stderr, once; a mirror append that fails after the working-copy append succeeded leaves that row in the working copy only, and the stderr line is its whole record), and no gate, result table or phase transition reads these rows. Never retry a telemetry call, never stamp anything on the attempt record for it, and never let it change a dispatch's outcome.\n\n### Row catalogue\n\n| Row | Written by | Shape |\n|---|---|---|\n| start | the render call, when it carries both flags below; `record_dispatch.py start` for a hand-built prompt | `{\"id\": \"<8 hex>\", \"kind\": \"<persona>\", \"task\": \"<task-id>\", \"queued_at\": <epoch s>, \"prompt_bytes\": <the count the render printed>}` |\n| end | `record_dispatch.py end` | `{\"id\": ..., \"ended_at\": <epoch s>, \"elapsed_s\": <int \\| null>, \"outcome\": ..., \"detail\": <string \\| null>}` — `elapsed_s` is `ended_at` minus the start row's `queued_at`, and `null` in either of two cases: no start row was found for the id (none exists, or the working file could not be read), or the dispatch spanned a session handoff (§ The null-elapsed rule below) |\n| handoff | `record_dispatch.py handoff` | `{\"kind\": \"handoff\", \"site\": \"build\"\\|\"review\"\\|\"done\", \"edge\": \"leave\"\\|\"resume\", \"at\": <epoch s>, \"phase\": <state.phase>, \"prd\": <state.prd>}` |\n\n**Lost at handoff.** A `handoff` call first closes every id that still has a start row but no end row, writing one end row per open id before it writes its own handoff row: `{\"id\": ID, \"e\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

This keeps a completed PRD's complete review trail intact after the batch closes (`references/design-rationale.md` § Verified moves).\n\n### Resuming\n\nWhen `/autopilot:run-autopilot` is invoked and `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` exists with `batch.completed_prds`, this is a continuation after a session restart. Preserve `batch.completed_prds` (including `batch.id`) and proceed to the build gate's Phase 0 to pick the next PRD.\n\nDelete `state.pause_reason` from `state.json` if present — unconditional, on every invocation, NOT gated on `batch.completed_prds`. A new session means any pause is being resumed; `pause_reason` belongs only to an unresolved pause and is not overwritten by normal progression, so it must be cleared here or it halts the resumed PRD's next hand-off. Cap-pause detection is unaffected — it keys on `cap_pause_reason`, which this delete does not touch.\n\n### Operator runbook (unattended batches)\n\nAll interaction with a running `autoclaude` batch happens at session boundaries — the only safe point. (Operator-shell commands for the human's own terminal, not for the model's Bash tool — `tail -f` would hang a session and pipes are hook-blocked.)\n\n- **Watch**: `tail -f docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/last-session.log` — the wrapper tees the live event log of the running headless turn there.\n- **Pause**: `touch docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/pause-requested` — the wrapper consumes the marker at the next session boundary, notifies \"paused by operator\", and stops the loop with state intact. It leaves `paused-by-operator` behind so tracon shows `⏸ paused` rather than `⚠ orphaned`; plain `autoclaude` resumes (nothing to clear, no decision to make). The marker may carry a JSON reason, `{\"reason\": \"...\"}`, which the stop line and the notification quote; a session that stands down for a peer writes one with a `condition` beside it, after asking the peer first (§ Session Loop, stand-down procedure).\n- **Take over**: with the loop stopped (pause marker, or Ctrl-C on the wrapper), run `/autopilot:run-autopilot` in a normal interactive session — resume-by-artifact reads the same `state.json`, and full interactive semantics (questions, PAUSEs) apply because `$_AUTOPILOT_LOOP` is unset. Restart `autoclaude` afterwards to go unattended again.\n- **Resume after a PAUSE** (`phase: \"paused\"` in `state.json`, \"session paused\" banner/ntfy): same take-over recipe, and it is the ONLY way forward — re-running `autoclaude` reads the paused state and exits again immediately. Interactively, the phase that paused re-runs with `AskUserQuestion` available, so the blockers that halted the loop are asked as decisions instead. Answer them, let the session hand off or finish the PRD, then re-run `autoclaude`.\n- **Un-park a sidelined PRD**: a PRD the loop parked (a `wrapper_died` death-park, or a loop-mode `design_gate` / `blocking_escalation` stall) sits in `docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/` with its stall recorded in the batch deferred JSON; the batch kept draining without it. To resume it, `mv docs/dev/project-management/prds/hold/<00XXX-…>.md docs/dev/project-management/prds/backlog/` (keep the `00XXX-` prefix). Autopilot never reads `hold/`, so the next `/autopilot:run-autopilot` (or `autoclaude` relaunch) re-selects it from `backlog/` and re-enters the build gate, reusing its existing design doc via the Phase 1.5 artifact skip (a `design_gate` park then re-fires the gate interactively). Batch-end review lists every parked PRD (`{m} stalled`), so none is silently forgotten.\n- **Forensics**: `claude --resume <session-id>` (the id is in the init event at the top of `last-session.log`) reopens a finished headless conversation for questioning. Harmless by construction: sessions are disposable; `state.json` plus the artifacts are the only orchestration contract, so a resumed chat cannot fork the loop.\n- **Run a wave (parallel lanes)**: `autopilot wave plan`, then `autopilot wave launch`, `autopilot wave status` and `autopilot wave abort` — one detached loop per lane worktree, each over its own slice of the backlog. Full operator surface, including what is deferred: `references/waves.md`.\n- **Product QA (agoge)**: once a batch drains at least one PRD, the loop runs a single product-QA pass (`/run-agoge` over the repo), logging to `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/reports/{batch}-agoge.log`. A batch that drained nothing skips it with a line saying so; a QA failure is recorded and swallowed, never turning a successful drain into a failed one. `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_CAP` (default 3600s) bounds a hung run.\n\n- **One loop per repo**: a second `autoclaude` on a repo that already has a live loop refuses to start, naming the incumbent loop's PID (both the tracon front-end and the plain/headless path check the loop registry via `scripts/tracon_wrapper_alive.py` before registering). This prevents two loops double-draining the backlog and racing `state.json` writes. If the refusal is wrong (the named PID is dead), the stale registry entry is pruned automatically on the next launch; force it by deleting `~/.claude/autopilot-loops/<pid>.json`.\n\nA running headless turn is interrupted by the wrapper's wall-clock cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX`, default 7200s; review-phase launches use `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_MAX_REVIEW`, default 10800s) and, independently, by the idle watchdog at any point after launch: it kills a session whose log has gone silent for `_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_IDLE` seconds (default 1200s; `0` disables pre-cap idle kill, restoring the old kill-at-cap-only behavior) as long as nothing is in flight (`session_busy`) - this fires before the cap, not only past it. Fifteen minutes before the cap (`_AUTOPILOT_SESSION_WARN`, seconds, `0` disables) the wrapper writes the same `.handoff-requested` marker the context-cap hook writes, so a session that reaches a task boundary inside that window hands off cleanly instead of being killed mid-task. Once the wall-clock cap itself is reached, the same idle-silence watchdog applies, or the session is SIGTERMed at twice the cap (the ceiling), whichever comes first.\n\nA PRD whose session metrics ledger spend since `state.prd_budget_since` exceeds `_AUTOPILOT_PRD_BUDGET_USD` (float; default 300; `0` disables; an unparseable value keeps 300) is parked (`park_site: \"budget\"`) rather than left to burn further sessions unattended.\n\nThe agoge run above arms the runtime-security lane by default, passing `--authorized autoclaude-drain`; `_AUTOPILOT_AGOGE_AUTHORIZED=0` is the kill switch, dropping just that flag so QA still runs, unarmed. Only the literal `0` disables it: anything else, including `false`, `no`, `off`, or `0` with a trailing space, leaves it armed, because a security brake should fail toward armed, not away from it. It brakes a default-on assertion; it is not a separate way to invoke one, since the assertion itself stays invocation-only.\n\n### Task Counts\n\n`tasks_total` and `tasks_completed` are maintained by whoever writes the `state.tasks` snapshot: recompute both in the same write — `tasks_total = len(tasks)`, `tasks_completed = count(status == \"completed\")` (the pidash-era PostToolUse sync hook is retired, PRD 00063). The model does not re-derive these counts by any other means; the arithmetic runs on the snapshot already in hand. Keep `state.tasks` accurate at phase transitions and recompute the counts alongside each `tasks` snapshot, applying all three with `statectl set` (§ State Management), keeping the dashboard progress bar live.\n\n### Live Dashboard\n\n`autoclaude` launches `tracon` (`scripts/tracon/`) in the foreground by default (PRD 00062), so the loop terminal shows the live dashboard with no extra step. It reads `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/state.json` — no action needed from autopilot beyond keeping the state file updated. `q` detaches (loop keeps running, wrapper prints the reattach command), `p` pauses at the next session boundary, `Ctrl-C` stops the loop with full cleanup. When there is no tty, no `uv`, or `_AUTOPILOT_TRACON=0`, the loop terminal shows the `render_stream.py` fallback with per-lane subagent tags instead. Full operator surface: `references/dashboard-format.md`.\n\n### Phase Banners\n\nPrint a banner at each phase transition:\n\n```\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: {PHASE} ──────────────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Phase: REVIEW ── Cycle {n} ─────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── Cycle {n} rework complete ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── handing off to fresh session for cycle {n+1} ───────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PAUSED ── {n} issue(s) need your decision ──────────\n── AUTOPILOT ── PRD: {prd-name} ── DONE ── {n} cycles ─────────────\n```\n\n## Session Loop\n\nUnattended mode runs each session headless: the `autoclaude` wrapper (in `~/.config/bash/plugins/development.plugin.bash`) hands off to `autopilot loop` — the CLI loop driver, `cli/loop.py` (PRD 00106) — which launches `claude -p \"/autopilot:run-autopilot\"`; the session runs exactly one turn, and the process exits at turn end. There is no signal file and no Stop-hook choreography — **`state.json` is the entire hand-off contract** (`references/design-rationale.md` § Headless sessions). For a single hand-off rather than a whole batch — the hybrid track's fresh-session review and finalize hops — run `autopilot review-once`: it runs the same preflights and one routed session for
