Matches codex-run.sh / gemini-run.sh.\nif command -v mise &>/dev/null; then\n    PATH=\"$(mise env -s bash < /dev/null 2>/dev/null | sed -n \"s/^export PATH='\\\\(.*\\\\)'/\\\\1/p\"):$PATH\"\nfi\n\n# Don't leak autopilot loop state into the nested claude: the autopilot Stop\n# hook gates its signal-file write on _AUTOPILOT_LOOP, and a reviewer subprocess\n# must never write that signal. One unset covers both the Diana subagent and the\n# foreground blind-review call site.\n# ponytail: single env guard, not a wrapper.\nunset _AUTOPILOT_LOOP\n\n# Mark the child as a nested dispatch so the parent's hooks stay useful:\n# track_cost tags the row nested:true (real spend, attributed), while notify /\n# strunk-ruling-inject / observe_tool early-exit (no pings, injections, or\n# per-call observations for reviewer children). Warden and aegis stay active.\nexport CLAUDE_NESTED=1\n\n# The unset above also re-enables the nested claude's notify.py hook (it gates\n# on _AUTOPILOT_LOOP), so every reviewer dispatch pinged \"done\" mid-batch.\n# Mark the nested session quiet instead: notify.py silences Stop/idle_prompt\n# when this is set; permission_prompt still pages.\nexport _CLAUDE_NOTIFY_QUIET=1\n\n# `sonnet` alias always resolves to the latest base Sonnet. No Copilot\n# multiplier to dodge anymore - override with -m only when you need a specific\n# model id or a different tier.\nDEFAULT_MODEL=\"sonnet\"\nMODEL=\"$DEFAULT_MODEL\"\n\nMODE=\"prompt\"  # prompt, interactive, resume, continue\nPERM=\"\"        # -a = acceptEdits (edits auto-approved, Bash still gated); -y = full bypass\nADD_DIRS=()\nTOOLS=()       # -t \"\" pins a reviewer to the prompt: no tools, no reading around\nSESSION_ARGS=()      # -S fixes a new session's id, -R resumes one; --print only\nRESUME_PRINT_ID=\"\"\nPROMPT=\"\"\nPROMPT_FILE=\"\"\nOUTPUT_FILE=\"\"\n\nusage() {\n    echo \"Usage: $0 [options] [prompt]\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Runs Claude Sonnet via the native claude CLI (default model: $DEFAULT_MODEL).\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Options:\"\n    echo \"  -m, --model MODEL      Override model (default: $DEFAULT_MODEL; e.g. opus, claude-sonnet-5)\"\n    echo \"  -i, --interactive      Interactive mode with initial prompt\"\n    echo \"  -a, --allow-edits      Auto-approve file edits (--permission-mode acceptEdits; other tools stay gated)\"\n    echo \"  -y, --yolo             Full permissions (--permission-mode bypassPermissions); required for unattended agentic runs\"\n    echo \"  -s, --silent           Accepted for compatibility (claude -p output is already clean)\"\n    echo \"  -d, --dir DIR          Allow access to directory (can repeat)\"\n    echo \"  -f, --file FILE        Read prompt from file\"\n    echo \"  -o, --output FILE      Write output to file (via tee)\"\n    echo \"  -t, --tools LIST       Pass --tools=LIST to claude (prompt mode); -t \\\"\\\" grants none\"\n    echo \"  -S, --session-id UUID  Fix the id of a new --print run, so -R can resume it later\"\n    echo \"  -R, --resume-print ID  Resume session ID in --print mode with the -f prompt\"\n    echo \"  -r, --resume [ID]      Resume session interactively (optionally specify ID)\"\n    echo \"  -c, --continue         Resume most recent session\"\n    echo \"  -h, --help             Show this help\"\n    echo \"\"\n    echo \"Examples:\"\n    echo \"  $0 'Analyze the codebase'\"\n    echo \"  $0 -a 'Fix the bug in auth.ts'\"\n    echo \"  $0 -m opus -p 'Hard reasoning task'\"\n    echo \"  $0 -r\"\n}\n\n# Parse arguments\nwhile [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do\n    case $1 in\n        -m|--model)\n            MODEL=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -i|--interactive)\n            MODE=\"interactive\"\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -a|--allow-edits|--allow-tools)\n            # --allow-tools kept as a deprecated spelling of -a; it now grants\n            # acceptEdits, NOT bypass (the old mapping made -a a silent -y).\n            PERM=\"--permission-mode acceptEdits\"\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -y|--yolo)\n            PERM=\"--permission-mode bypassPermissions\"\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -s|--silent)\n            # claude -p prints only the final assistant message; nothing to strip.\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -d|--dir)\n            ADD_DIRS+=(\"--add-dir\" \"$2\")\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -f|--file)\n            PROMPT_FILE=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -o|--output)\n            OUTPUT_FILE=\"$2\"\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -t|--tools)\n            # An empty LIST is meaningful (grant nothing), so the value cannot be\n            # inferred from emptiness - a missing one is a usage error.\n            if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then\n                echo \"ERROR: -t/--tools requires a value (use -t \\\"\\\" for no tools)\" >&2\n                usage >&2\n                exit 1\n            fi\n            # `--tools=LIST` as ONE token, never the two-token `--tools LIST`:\n            # claude's flag is variadic (`--tools <tools...>`), so the separate\n            # form keeps eating argv and swallows the prompt. Verified live —\n            # the two-token form dies with \"Input must be provided either\n            # through stdin or as a prompt argument when using --print\".\n            TOOLS=(\"--tools=$2\")\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -S|--session-id)\n            if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then\n                echo \"ERROR: -S/--session-id requires a value\" >&2\n                usage >&2\n                exit 1\n            fi\n            # claude owns UUID validation; re-checking the shape here would\n            # only drift from whatever it accepts.\n            SESSION_ARGS+=(\"--session-id\" \"$2\")\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -R|--resume-print)\n            if [ $# -lt 2 ]; then\n                echo \"ERROR: -R/--resume-print requires a value\" >&2\n                usage >&2\n                exit 1\n            fi\n            RESUME_PRINT_ID=\"$2\"\n            SESSION_ARGS+=(\"--resume\" \"$2\")\n            shift 2\n            ;;\n        -r|--resume)\n            MODE=\"resume\"\n            if [[ -n \"${2:-}\" && ! \"$2\" =~ ^- ]]; then\n                PROMPT=\"$2\"\n                shift\n            fi\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -c|--continue)\n            MODE=\"continue\"\n            shift\n            ;;\n        -h|--help)\n            usage\n            exit 0\n            ;;\n        *)\n            PROMPT=\"$1\"\n            shift\n            ;;\n    esac\ndone\n\n# -R resumes inside --print; -r/-c/-i deliberately drop --print and want a TTY.\n# One run cannot be both, and silently picking a winner would drop a flag the\n# caller passed on purpose.\nif [ -n \"$RESUME_PRINT_ID\" ] && [ \"$MODE\" != \"prompt\" ]; then\n    echo \"ERROR: -R/--resume-print cannot be combined with -r, -c or -i\" >&2\n    usage >&2\n    exit 1\nfi\n\n# Read prompt from file if specified\nif [ -n \"$PROMPT_FILE\" ]; then\n    if [ ! -f \"$PROMPT_FILE\" ]; then\n        echo \"ERROR: Prompt file not found: $PROMPT_FILE\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    PROMPT=$(cat \"$PROMPT_FILE\")\nfi\n\n# Build and run command\nrun_cmd() {\n    if [ -n \"$OUTPUT_FILE\" ]; then\n        \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee \"$OUTPUT_FILE\"\n    else\n        \"$@\"\n    fi\n}\n\ncase $MODE in\n    resume)\n        if [ -n \"$PROMPT\" ]; then\n            run_cmd claude --model \"$MODEL\" $PERM --resume \"$PROMPT\"\n        else\n            run_cmd claude --model \"$MODEL\" $PERM --resume\n        fi\n        ;;\n    continue)\n        run_cmd claude --model \"$MODEL\" $PERM --continue\n        ;;\n    interactive)\n        if [ -z \"$PROMPT\" ]; then\n            echo \"ERROR: Prompt required for interactive mode\" >&2\n            usage >&2\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        run_cmd claude --model \"$MODEL\" $PERM \"${ADD_DIRS[@]}\" \"$PROMPT\"\n        ;;\n    prompt)\n        if [ -z \"$PROMPT\" ]; then\n            echo \"ERROR: Prompt required\" >&2\n            usage >&2\n            exit 1\n        fi\n        # Headless (--print) dispatch: the prompt travels as the child's stdin,\n        # never as a positional argv token that could be parsed as a flag. The\n        # finite pipe also guards against a child hanging on the inherited\n        # wrapper stdin (PRD 00040 hang class). Interactive/resume/continue\n        # modes keep stdin - they need the TTY.\n        # ponytail: the test stub always drains, so it can't model a real\n        # `claude` exiting 0 without draining a >64 KiB prompt before closing\n        # its stdin - that races SIGPIPE against printf's write and reports\n        # 141 for a successful run under `set -eo pipefail`; if this is ever\n        # observed, feed the prompt from a temp file instead of this pipe.\n        printf '%s' \"$PROMPT\" | run_cmd claude --print --model \"$MODEL\" $PERM \"${SESSION_ARGS[@]}\" \"${ADD_DIRS[@]}\" \"${TOOLS[@]}\"\n        ;;\nesac\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

then\n    if [ ! -f \"$PROMPT_FILE\" ]; then\n        echo \"ERROR: Prompt file not found: $PROMPT_FILE\" >&2\n        exit 1\n    fi\n    PROMPT=$(cat \"$PROMPT_FILE\")\nfi\n\nif [ -z \"$EFFORT\" ]; exit 1 ;;\nesac\n\n# Build and run command\nrun_cmd() {\n    if [ -n \"$OUTPUT_FILE\" ]; then\n        \"$@\" 2>&1 | tee \"$OUTPUT_FILE\"\n    else\n        \"$@\"\n    fi\n}\n\n# Pinning the session id only makes sense for a fresh headless run: resume and\n# continue already carry an id, and interactive claude picks its own.\nSESSION_ARGS=()\nif [ -n \"$SESSION_ID\" ]; Always pass the prompt with `-f <file>`. The qualified Qwen3.8 model is `unsloth/Qwen3.8-27B-GGUF:UD-Q6_K_XL`. An autopilot dispatch runs under `--approved-only`; preflight selects a live approved id and the dispatch must pass that same id with `-m`, so it does not rely on the external helper's default. Inference is local and free — no API cost, no token billing.\n\nQwen is a speculative one-shot implementor. The last valid qualification is\nQwen3.8's 6/6 single-file round; autonomous trust remains `single-file-only`.\nThe 2026-09-03 multi-file eval in agent-skills reported Qwen 4/6 versus Sonnet\n6/6, but its first completion review found contaminated baselines and missing\nline-history checks. That comparison remains pending review and a clean rerun;\nit is not decision-grade evidence for widening trust. Sonnet remains the\ncorrectness fallback and reviewer.\n\nPlanning and dispatch both require exactly one expected implementor-writable\nfile, in addition to the backend, tier and no-public-contract predicates.\nTwo-or-more-file tasks route above Qwen through the existing Codex/Claude\nfences; `work` reconciles stale planner flags against the concrete `FILE_PATHS`\nbefore selection. Empty write sets fail closed to Claude. Healthy preflight\nalone does not grant task eligibility.\n\n## Preflight\n\nA four-check probe MUST run before any qwen dispatch. The probe takes one of two terminal verdicts: **healthy** (proceed to dispatch) or **failed** with the specific failing check named. Checks short-circuit in order — the first failure is the verdict.\n\nThe four checks, in order:\n\n1. **`pi` resolvable on PATH.** `command -v pi` exits 0. On failure: `preflight_outcome = \"pi_missing\"`.\n2. **llama.cpp `/v1/models` endpoint reachable.** An HTTP GET against the configured base URL's `/v1/models` returns a 2xx response within **2 seconds** (a healthy local llamacpp responds in tens of ms; 2s is conservative slack for a busy laptop). Read the base URL from `~/.pi/agent/models.json` at JSON path `.providers.llamacpp.baseUrl`. On any failure (connection refused, timeout ≥ 2s, non-2xx, missing config): `preflight_outcome = \"endpoint_unreachable\"`.\n3. **An APPROVED model id is live on the endpoint.** Parse the `/v1/models` JSON response (`data[].id` — a server can list SEVERAL ids, so check every entry, never just the first). At least one listed id must appear in the approved registry (`~/.agents/skills/use-qwen/scripts/approved-models.txt`); that approved id is the one check 4 probes and the dispatch runs. On absence: `preflight_outcome = \"model_id_missing\"`. **The registry, not the config, is the authority here.** This is exactly the gate `qwen-run.sh --approved-only` applies at dispatch, and the preflight MUST apply it too: a preflight that verdicts `healthy` on an unapproved-but-live engine sends `/autopilot:work` into a dispatch the script then refuses — which consumes the one-shot qwen attempt (see \"Helper exits non-zero\") on a task qwen never actually ran, and logs `preflight_outcome: \"healthy\"` for an attempt that never happened. The Fallback rule below is the intended path instead.\n4. **Real 1-token completion succeeds.** Checks 2-3 only enumerate configured models — LlamaBarn (and any on-demand server) lists the model straight from config and spawns the inference worker *lazily, on the first completion*. They pass even when the worker cannot start, so this is the only check that exercises the spawn. POST to `${baseUrl}/chat/completions` with body `{\"model\": <the approved id selected by check 3>, \"messages\": [{\"role\": \"user\", \"content\": \"ping\"}], \"max_tokens\": 1, \"stream\": false}`, timeout **120 seconds**. A 2xx response → the check passes (verdict `healthy`). Any non-2xx (e.g. `500 \"failed to spawn server instance\"`), connection error, or timeout → `preflight_outcome = \"completion_failed\"`. The 120s ceiling covers a cold model load (the ~18.5 GB GGUF takes tens of seconds the first time); the probe doubles as a warm-up, so the model is resident when the real dispatch follows — the load is not wasted. A backend that cannot emit one token in 120s would blow the task watchdog anyway: treat it as failed and fall back.\n\n**Inputs**: PATH, the llama.cpp server endpoint and its `/chat/completions` route (from `~/.pi/agent/models.json`'s `baseUrl`), the ids the endpoint actually reports at `/v1/models`, and the approved-model registry (`~/.agents/skills/use-qwen/scripts/approved-models.txt`).\n\n**The one-command probe**: `qwen-run.sh --preflight --approved-only` performs checks 1-4 exactly as written and exits 0 only on `healthy`. Prefer it over a hand-rolled probe — running the same script the dispatch runs is what keeps the preflight verdict and the dispatch decision from ever disagreeing.\n\n**Outputs**: Health verdict — `\"healthy\"`, or one of `\"pi_missing\"` / `\"endpoint_unreachable\"` / `\"model_id_missing\"` / `\"completion_failed\"`.\n\n**Fallback rule**: ANY preflight failure → fall back to Claude at the task's original tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet). Behavior in this fallback is byte-for-byte identical to today's Claude dispatch for the same task; the only addition is the recorded `preflight_outcome` in the attempt log (see `references/attempt-logging.md`). A failed probe does NOT consume the one-shot qwen attempt budget — no qwen attempt happened.\n\nThe preflight is **batch-scoped**, not per task: its verdict is cached in `state.qwen_preflight` under the batch id that produced it, so the first qwen-routed task of a batch pays for the probe and the rest reuse the verdict (§ Batch-scoped preflight below is the authority; it mirrors the `codex_probe` idiom). Two backend-health signals invalidate the cache mid-batch and force a re-probe: the Subagent Watchdog judging a qwen dispatch hung or lost, and `qwen-run.sh` itself failing at real dispatch time with an infra-shaped outcome despite a cached `\"healthy\"`. An ordinary step-5.5 gate failure on a healthy backend is deliberately NOT such a signal.\n\nThe probe is skipped entirely when the qwen capability breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) reroutes a qwen-eligible task to Claude before it would run. That attempt records `preflight_outcome: null`, because the probe never ran. null\n}\n```\n\n**Timing is deliberately not an attempt field.** No timestamp, duration or prompt size is stamped here: an attempt spans several dispatches — Tess, Ivan, Pat and their retries — so one pair of stamps could not say which of them took the hour. Those live in the dispatch ledger, `docs/dev/project-management/autopilot/dispatch-metrics.jsonl` (a start row and one or more end rows per dispatch, joined on `id`, plus one row per session-handoff edge; `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Dispatch telemetry), and a task's runtime is read from its rows there, keyed on `task`.\n\n**Cardinality (PRD 00065)**: today `/autopilot:work` appends exactly one entry per task at exit. Under in-loop escalation the rule widens to one entry per rung/dispatch-group: each rung that dispatched writes its own entry when the task escalates away from it or exits on it. `attempt` numbers stay sequential across rungs (`len(existing)+1`). This is a widening, not a break — a task that never escalates still writes exactly one entry, byte-identical to today.\n\n**Field semantics**:\n\n- `attempt`: 1-indexed; `len(existing) + 1`.\n- `model`: the tier `/autopilot:work` used for this pass. Read from `state.tasks[i].model` when set. On legacy plans where `state.tasks[i].model` is absent, record the effective session-inherited tier as a string (e.g. `\"sonnet\"` for a Work-phase Sonnet 4.6 launch). Always a string — never `null`.\n- `outcome`: `/autopilot:work` writes `\"completed\"`, `\"aborted\"`, or `\"escalated\"`. The `\"escalated\"` value (PRD 00065) is stamped on the entry for a rung the task was reset away from and escalated up; the final rung's entry carries the real terminal outcome (`completed`/`aborted`), and the escalated-away entry keeps its true `implementor` (a qwen rung escalated to Sonnet keeps `implementor:\"qwen\"`). Later phases upgrade earlier entries — `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 (Rework) step 2 rewrites a `\"completed\"` entry's outcome to `\"review_flagged\"` at the start of escalation, then later rewrites a flagged entry's outcome to `\"rework_failed\"` when the rework pass also fails at the top of the chain.\n- `review_cycle`: `null` on a first/Phase-3 attempt; set to the current `state.cycle` integer when the pass is a rework re-dispatch (see `SKILL.md` step 1.5 \"Rework-mode task filter (PRD 00025)\").\n- `cause`: `null` on success; on abort or output rejection, the reason — `\"context_overrun\"`, `\"subagent_prompt_overrun\"`, `\"timeout\"`, `\"error\"`, `\"subagent_infra_failure\"`, `\"commit_rejected\"` (a commit blocked by `validate_commit_msg`/warden that the one-retry repair could not fix — `SKILL.md` step 5), `\"codex_no_edit\"` (PRD 00077; the no-edit infra arm, stamped when the codex helper exited 0 with a non-empty output file but produced no working-tree change — the hook-blocked, prose-only case; classified as INFRA, so the attempt falls back to Claude at the task's own tier with no `escalation_reason` stamp). Qwen output rejections use `\"qwen_no_edit\"` (no task-owned implementation diff) or `\"qwen_test_mutation\"` (Tess tests differ from their test commit), with `outcome: \"escalated\"` on the rejected Qwen row; both are capability failures before staging/gating, never infra.\n- `implementor`: which agent actually ran the attempt — `\"claude\"` (Agent dispatch at any Claude tier, including a Claude fallback when qwen preflight failed), `\"gemini\"` (UI task via `use-gemini` helper), `\"qwen\"` (backend qwen-eligible task with healthy preflight, dispatched via `use-qwen` helper), `\"codex\"` (a codex-eligible backend task the step-3 interception routed to the codex rung, dispatched via the `use-codex` helper), or `\"orchestrator\"` (PRD 00148; a rework task the micro lane kept in-session — the orchestrator edited it with the Edit tool and no implementor subagent dispatched at all). Sourced from the routing decision in `work` SKILL.md step 3 — the value reflects what dispatched, not what the routing table initially picked: a qwen-eligible task that preflight-failed and fell back to Claude records `\"claude\"`; likewise, a codex-eligible task whose batch health probe came back unhealthy and fell back to Claude records `\"claude\"`, not `\"codex\"`. **Multi-implementor pass (qwen → Claude retry):** under default escalation, each rung writes its own entry: the rejected Qwen row stays `implementor: \"qwen\"`, `outcome: \"escalated\"`, and the Sonnet row records `implementor: \"claude\"`, `escalation_reason: \"gate_failure\"`, `escalated_from: \"qwen\"`. This also applies to pre-commit output rejections under `legacy`, which must retain their failure cause. The old single task-exit row applies only to legacy test-gate retries that committed Qwen code, not output rejections. Tess / Devon / code reviewer dispatches do not write attempt entries themselves; this field labels the Ivan-implementor pass.\n- `preflight_outcome`: only meaningful for attempts on qwen-eligible tasks (those whose effective eligibility remains true after write-set reconciliation). For qwen-eligible attempts: one of `\"healthy\"`, `\"pi_missing\"`, `\"endpoint_unreachable\"`, `\"model_id_missing\"`, `\"completion_failed\"` — the verdict of the four-check probe defined in `references/qwen-integration.md` (Preflight section). For non-qwen-eligible attempts: `null`. A qwen-eligible attempt that the breaker (row 3) or the memory-pressure gate (row 4) rerouted also records `null`, because the probe never ran. Sourced from the preflight probe in `work` SKILL.md step 3.\n- `pipeline`: which pipeline depth this attempt ran, keyed on the task tier (PRD 00044) — `\"minimal\"` (haiku: Tess + Ivan, 2 subagents), `\"lean\"` (sonnet: + step-5.7 reviewer, 3 subagents), or `\"full\"` (opus: + Devon at step 2.9, 4 subagents). Mapped from `state.tasks[i].model`: `haiku` → `\"minimal\"`, `sonnet` → `\"lean\"`, `opus` → `\"full\"`; absent/legacy `state.tasks[i].model` is treated as `sonnet` → `\"lean\"` (matching the step-2.9 and step-5.7 tier gates). Written at every task exit alongside `implementor`. A Phase-6 escalation to `opus` therefore records `\"full\"` for the rework attempt. Always a string — never `null`. **In-loop escalation (PRD 00065):** an escalation re-dispatches the implementor for the higher rung and re-runs the tier-appropriate post-implementor gates (step 5.7 reviewer for sonnet+, plus the step-5.5 gate); Devon (step 2.9, pre-implementation adversarial tests) is NOT re-run mid-task. So an in-loop opus escalation stamps `pipeline:\"lean\"` (implementor+reviewer), reserving `\"full\"` for a from-scratch opus task/rework that actually ran Devon.\n- `escalation_reason` (PRD 00065): string?; `\"gate_failure\"` stamped directly by `/autopilot:work` on the entry of the rung it escalated INTO (in-loop diagnosis). `\"review_flag\"` reaches the entry a different way: phase-review Phase 6 writes it (with `escalated_from`) into `state.tasks[i]` via `task-set-meta`, and `/autopilot:work`'s attempt write copies both from `state.tasks[i]` onto the rework entry (`SKILL.md` step 6 point 1 / step 1.5) — the task entry is the carrier, the copy is the wiring. Absent = neither (legacy / no escalation).\n- `escalated_from` (PRD 00065): string?; a tier (`\"qwen\"`|`\"codex\"`|`\"haiku\"`|`\"sonnet\"`|`\"opus\"`) — on the entry of the rung escalated INTO, the immediate-prior rung it came from. Step 5 commits the implementation before the step-5.5 gate, so the porcelain is clean at 5.5 for both a successful codex run and a no-edit run; checking there cannot distinguish them. Capture porcelain for the task's own file slice immediately before the codex dispatch, then capture it again immediately after the helper returns and before step 5's `git add` (both captures are checklist steps in `references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex dispatch); latch the comparison as `codex_no_edit` in the attempt record, and have step 5.5 read only that latched flag — never re-run `git status` here. If either snapshot exits non-zero, the probe is **INDETERMINATE**, not \"no change\": do not latch `codex_no_edit`; record the exit code in `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` and continue through the capability path normally. Clean ->\n  `style_gate: fixed:<sha of the fix commit>`; still exit 1 ->\n  `style_gate: failed:<the violation lines, joined by \"; \">` and proceed to step\n  5.7 anyway (fail loud, never silent).\n- **Exit 2** (or any other non-0/1 exit): the gate could not run at all, so\n  there are no violation lines to hand a fix agent — record\n  `style_gate: failed:<the script's stderr message>`, do NOT dispatch Ivan, and\n  proceed to step 5.7 anyway (fail loud, never silent, same as the\n  still-failing exit-1 case).\n\nA `failed:` value never blocks the task and never changes its `outcome`: it is a\nfail-loud marker, so a skipped check never reads as a passed one.\n\n## Fix dispatch\n\nExit 1 only, and the one Ivan dispatch that carries a widened allowlist —\nsplitting an 800-line file needs sibling modules that are by construction absent\nfrom the task's Contract paths, and `agents/ivan.md` tells a fixer to report a\nblocker rather than touch a file nobody listed.\n\nWrite `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-style-files.txt`: one absolute path per\nviolating file (every violation line names one), then one absolute directory\npath per distinct parent directory of those files, each directory line suffixed\n` (new modules may be created here)`. Parent directories of violating files\nonly — never the repo root, never a directory walked further upward. Every other\nIvan dispatch keeps passing `docs/dev/tmp/ivan-<task-id>-files.txt` unchanged.\n\nRender and dispatch with `references/gate-failure.md` § Style-fix render, whose\n`RETRY_INSTRUCTION` is verbatim:\n\n```\nFix only the listed style-limit violations. You may create new modules in the directories marked above and update imports in the listed files to use them. Do not change behavior, do not touch other code, and do not modify tests except to split a test file a violation line names.\n```\n\n`agents/ivan.md` stays untouched: `{RETRY_INSTRUCTION}` is already free text, and\na persona edit would reach every dispatch instead of this one.\n\n## Split hygiene\n\nRuns immediately after the style-limit ladder above, on the same candidate list\nnarrowed to test paths — `is_test_path` from\n`${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py` decides, so the\nsubset is the one steps 5.6 and 5.7 already agree on. Build it concretely:\n\n```bash\npython3 -c \"import sys;sys.path.insert(0,sys.argv[1]);import work_routing;print('\\n'.join(p for p in sys.argv[2:] if work_routing.is_test_path(p)))\" ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts <every candidate as a REPO-RELATIVE path>\n```\n\nRepo-relative on the way in: `is_test_path` matches directory segments and\nbasenames, so an absolute path drags in `/Users/...` segments it never meant to\nsee. She has NOT seen and must NOT think about implementation.\n\n## Prompt Template\n\nThe prompt template lives in `work/references/tess-prompt.md` (single source\nof truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`\nconsumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table).\n\n## Context Selection\n\nWhen building Tess's prompt, include:\n\n| Include | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Task description + acceptance criteria | The spec Tess tests against |\n| Public types/interfaces | So Tess knows the API surface |\n| One sample test file | So Tess follows project conventions |\n| Test framework config | So imports and assertions are correct |\n| `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md`, when it exists | The project's own harness rules, for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>` the task touches |\n\n| Exclude | Why |\n|---------|-----|\n| Architecture docs | Would leak implementation thinking |\n| AGENTS.md internals | Same - Tess doesn't need to know how things are built |\n| Implementation files | Defeats the entire purpose |\n| \"How to build this\" guidance | Tess is a test author, not an implementor |\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.7 (PRD 00119-v2) — the two lists the\nstep used to spell out inline. **Read this section before the first Tess\ndispatch of a batch.**\n\n**Tess receives:**\n- Task description and acceptance criteria\n- The **exact file paths** the task touches — spelled **absolute** — and the **exact symbol names** to test, taken from the plan task — not \"find the relevant file\"\n- Public interfaces/types relevant to the task\n- The project's test-harness contract when one exists (PRD 00141): for each Contract path `<dir>/<file>`, `<dir>/tests/HARNESS_CONTRACT.md` joins the `PUBLIC_INTERFACES` `--set-cmd`, once per distinct file; no such file adds nothing. It carries harness rules, never implementation — a harness can make a test pass for reasons requirements cannot reveal (a `capture_main` that installs its own `sys.stdin`, so a \"marker checked before stdin\" test passes against the old code too)\n- Existing test patterns (one sample test file from the project)\n- Test framework and conventions used\n\n**Tess does NOT receive:**\n- Implementation strategy or architecture docs (loaded in step 2.5 for the main session and Ivan only)\n- \"How to build this\" context\n- Access to modify non-test files\n\nThe stdout integer from step 2.7's render call **is** the Subagent Dispatch Budget measurement — no separate `wc -c`. `tess-prompt.md` bakes in the read-only-scope instruction, the dispatch prologue, the Assumptions footer and the size limits (rule 12: functions under 50 lines, files under 800) permanently (mirroring `ivan.md`), so nothing further needs adding to the prompt by hand — open-ended discovery is where subagents burn turns and stall, and keeping Tess scoped to the listed files/symbols is the template's job now. Dispatch the Agent tool with the file at `docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>.txt` as the prompt source. The template also embeds Simplicity/Think-Before-Coding/Surgical rules to prevent Tess from writing speculative tests or silently assuming input shape.\n\n## Quality gate (step 2.8)\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 2.8 (PRD 00119-v2). SKILL.md keeps the\ngate rule and the total-Tess budget; the rubric and the retry render live here.\n**Read this section before running the gate on Tess's first test file.**\n\n**Run the computed shape check first**, on every test file Tess wrote or changed:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/review-work-completion/scripts/detect_tautological_tests.py <test file>...\n```\n\nIt prints one `[MECH] {emoji} <test> <reason> | File: <path>:<line> | Task: general` line per test whose shape cannot fail (a constant or self-comparing assert, an `A or B` hedge, a swallowed exception, `raises(Exception)`, no assertion at all) and always exits 0. **Every `[MECH]` line is a check-4 failure**: copy it verbatim into the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` file, then judge the four checks below by reading. The script sees shape only; a test that restates the code in a perfectly valid shape is still check 4's to catch by hand. The same script runs at review (`review-work-completion` step 3), so a shape that slips past here comes back as a `mech-check` finding and a rework cycle — cheaper to fix now.\n\nBefore committing Tess's tests, review them in the main session against this checklist:\n\n1. **Behavior names?** Each test name describes a behavior (\"rejects empty email\"), not an implementation detail (\"calls validateEmail\")\n2. **Real assertions?** Assertions check outputs/effects, not mock internals\n3. **Edge cases?** Empty, null, boundary, error, and concurrent cases covered where relevant\n4. **No tautologies?** Tests don't just restate what the code obviously does\n5. **Exploit classes covered?** Every tested function has the six rule-6a assertions (two fixture values per asserted field, a near-miss negative, a multi-element and an empty input, an accept and a reject case of the same shape, a surfaced error, a dependency assertion); a missing one is a check-5 failure and names the class.\n\nIf any check fails, dispatch Tess again with specific feedback about what's weak. Render the retry the same way as the initial dispatch — never author it by hand:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md \\\n  --out docs/dev/tmp/dispatch-tess-<task-id>-retry-<n>.txt \\\n  --set-file QUALITY_FEEDBACK=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-gate-<n>.txt \\\n  --set-file TASK_DESCRIPTION=<the same scratch file step 2.7 used> \\\n  --set-file TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA=docs/dev/tmp/tess-<task-id>-acceptance.txt --dispatch-kind tess --dispatch-task <task-id>\n```\n\nWrite the gate findings (one per line) to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file with the Write tool. Max 2 quality gate retries.\n\n### Style limits on the test files\n\nOnce the four checks pass, run the step-5.65 gate over the test files only, so an oversized test file is split by a Tess retry now (cheap, tests-only) instead of an Ivan style-fix dispatch after implementation (PRD 00197; `tess-prompt.md` rule 12 already tells her the limits). Build the diff the way `references/style-gate.md` § Diff construction does, over this task's test files alone: `git diff <task_base_sha> --output=${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt -- <tracked test files>` (`--output=` goes before `--`; after it git reads it as a pathspec and prints the diff to stdout instead), then `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <file> >> ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt` per untracked test file (exit 1 is the normal case; only exit ≥2 is a failure), then `mv ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/test-diff-<task-id>.txt docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt`. Then:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_style_limits.py --diff docs/dev/tmp/test-diff-<task-id>.txt <each new or changed test file as an absolute path>\n```\n\nExit 0 is clean. Exit 1 is a quality-gate failure: write the violation lines to the `QUALITY_FEEDBACK` scratch file and render the retry above; it counts toward the two quality-gate retries. Exit 2 (the script could not run) is not a Tess failure: name it in the task output and proceed, step 5.65 measures the same files again after implementation.\n\n## Retry Prompt (after quality gate failure)\n\nThe retry template lives in `work/references/tess-retry-prompt.md` (single\nsource of truth, registry-shaped single-brace placeholders — `render_prompt.py`\nconsumes it directly; see `agent-registry.md` for the placeholder table). It\ntakes `{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}`, `{TASK_DESCRIPTION}` and\n`{TASK_ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA}`, and bakes in the same fixed guards the initial\ntemplate carries (read-only scope, 100K abort line, dispatch prologue,\nASSUMPTIONS footer).\n\n`{QUALITY_FEEDBACK}` is the step-2.8 gate's own findings, one per line, e.g.:\n\n- Test \"handles validation\" is too vague. Name the specific behavior.\n- Test 3 would pass with a function that always returns true. Add constraints.\n- No edge case for empty input.\n\n# Per-Task Review Mechanics (step 5.7)\n\nMoved verbatim out of `SKILL.md` step 5.7 (PRD 00119-v2; situational: consulted\nonce the tier gate says a task IS reviewed). SKILL.md keeps the tier-gate table,\nthe `pat.md` render block and the MEDIUM-retry rule; this file owns the runner\ndispatch and the result-handling ladder. **Read it before the first step-5.7\ndispatch of a batch.**\n\n## Why the lane is tier-gated\n\nA `haiku`-tier task commits after per-task test verification (step 5.5) with **no** review dispatch and proceeds straight to step 6 — it relies on per-task test verification plus the mandated PRD-level review lenses (consensus, blind, doubt — every review cycle reviews every task's diff regardless of tier). The reviewer is a fixed-model helper-script lane (Sonnet via `use-sonnet`) — reviewer capability is deliberately independent of the task's implementor tier. (Why tier-gated: `references/design-rationale.md` § tier-gated pipeline.)\n\n## Test-only diffs\n\nBefore anything below, SKILL.md step 5.7 applies `test_only_gate` (from\n`skills/work/scripts/work_routing.py`) to\n`git diff --name-only <task_base_sha>..HEAD`. When every changed path is test or\nfixture code and the task is **not** in rework mode, the whole step is skipped:\nno render, no dispatch, `review: \"skipped:test-only\"` on the attempt record and\nin the phase report. Every tier takes the skip, `fable` included.\n`dev/bin/release-checks`'s own registration line counts as test code here\ntoo, but only alongside a real test file in the same diff — a diff touching\n`dev/bin/release-checks` alone is never test-only.\n\nA rework task keeps its reviewer even on a test-only diff — its CLOSURE verdicts\nare what end the review cycle, so skipping him would leave nothing to close on.\nOne production path anywhere in the diff runs this file in full.\n\n## Recorded verification\n\nPat is dispatched with no tools, so he cannot run the tests himself. Before the\nrender, write `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-verification.txt` with the **Write\ntool** (never a shell redirect — command output carries quotes and newlines):\nthe exact command(s) step 5.5 ran, each exit code, and the runner's own summary\nline (for example `12 passed in 0.4s`). When step 5.5 could not run, write the\nattempt's literal `verification: skipped:<cause>` value instead. That file is\nwhat `--set-file VERIFICATION_RESULT=` reads, and it is the only test evidence\nPat has.\n\n## Dispatch\n\nDispatch via the sonnet runner (helper-script dispatch — the **Subagent Watchdog** applies), after SKILL.md step 5.7's render call has written the prompt file:\n\n```bash\nbash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -t \"\" -S \"<pat_session_id>\" -f docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prompt.md -o docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md\n```\n\nRun it as a plain foreground Bash call (the Bash tool's `timeout`, 600000 ms,\nthe tool's maximum, bounds it), never with `run_in_background`. A headless loop session that ends\nits turn while a background job is still running is torn down together with\nthe job: the output file reads `[killed]`, Pat's dispatch row reads `lost`, and\nthe wrapper relaunches a session that re-orients and re-runs him (2026-09-14,\n00191 T1 and agent-skills 00052 T2, one session lost each). If a run was\nbackgrounded anyway, the next call is `Monitor` on its output file, never a\nbare end of turn.\n\n`-t \"\"` grants the child no tools at all: Pat judges the diff, the task text and\nthe recorded verification, and nothing else. No `-a`/`-y` either — the reviewer\nneeds no write access, and a read-only dispatch must never run with bypassed\npermissions.\n\n`-S \"<pat_session_id>\"` (step 5.7 item 1) fixes this conversation's id so a later\ncycle can resume it. Everything else about the first dispatch is unchanged, and\nwhen no id could be generated the flag is simply dropped.\n\n## Delta re-runs\n\nEvery cycle after the first resumes the conversation that raised the findings\ninstead of starting over. Pat already read `<task_base_sha>..<last_reviewed_sha>`;\nre-sending it is what made a second dispatch cost a whole task diff — a measured\n369 KB prompt, sent twice, to check a one-file fix.\n\n**Check the delta is non-empty first.** An empty `git diff <last_reviewed_sha>..HEAD`\nmeans the fix never committed, and `render_prompt.py` exits 4 on a `--set-cmd`\nthat produces no output. Do not dispatch: there is nothing new to judge, the\nprevious cycle's findings stand, and the loop continues through the CRITICAL/HIGH\nrow below whose 3-cycle cap is what ends it.\n\nFor cycle `<n>` (2 or 3):\n\n1. Write the findings you sent the fixer, verbatim, one per line, to\n   `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prior-<n>.txt` with the **Write tool**. A\n   finding line carries backticks and pipes, so it never crosses the shell as a\n   `--set` word.\n2. Render the re-run prompt:\n\n   ```bash\n   python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/render_prompt.py ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/references/pat-rerun-prompt.md \\\n     --out docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-rerun-<n>.md \\\n     --set-file PRIOR_FINDINGS=docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-prior-<n>.txt \\\n     --set-cmd DELTA_DIFF=\"git diff <last_reviewed_sha>..HEAD\" \\\n     --set UNCHANGED_NOTE=\"You already reviewed <task_base_sha>..<last_reviewed_sha> earlier in this conversation. That range is unchanged and is not repeated here.\" --dispatch-kind pat --dispatch-task <id>\n   ```\n\n3. Dispatch it with `-R` where the first dispatch had `-S`, same output file:\n\n   ```bash\n   bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/use-sonnet/scripts/sonnet-run.sh -t \"\" -R \"<pat_session_id>\" -f docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-rerun-<n>.md -o docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md\n   ```\n\n4. Advance `<last_reviewed_sha>` to the HEAD this dispatch just read, so cycle\n   3's delta is cycle 2's fix alone and never the accumulated range.\n\nThe reply goes through the same `parse_review.py` gate and the same ladder below:\nthe reporting contract is unchanged, so nothing downstream cares that the prompt\nwas a delta. A correction retry (exit 1) re-renders `pat.md`, not this template —\na reply that broke the line shape is not a resume problem.\n\n**No `<pat_session_id>` means no delta lane at all.** When step 5.7 could not\ngenerate an id, or § Resume failure dropped it, every cycle takes the full-diff\ndispatch of § Dispatch with neither `-S` nor `-R` — exactly today's behavior.\nNever dispatch `-R \"\"`.\n\n## Resume failure\n\nA `-R` dispatch that exits non-zero or leaves the output file empty (a session\nthat no longer resolves exits 1 with `No conversation found with session ID:`)\nre-dispatches **once** with today's full-diff prompt: re-render `pat.md` exactly\nas SKILL.md step 5.7 item 2 does, with `--set-cmd DIFF=\"git diff <task_base_sha>..HEAD\"`,\nand run the § Dispatch command above with neither `-S` nor `-R`. Record\n`resume_failed` on the attempt record's `review` field (`references/attempt-logging.md`\n§ `review` for the shape) and name the fallback in the phase report — a cheap\nreview that silently did not happen is worse than an expensive one that did.\n\nThen **drop `<pat_session_id>`** and advance `<last_reviewed_sha>` to the HEAD\nthat fallback read. The session is gone; leaving the id in place would aim every\nremaining cycle at a `-R` that is already known to fail, spending a doomed\ndispatch each time.\n\nThat is the same single retry the runner-failure row below grants, not an extra\none: a second failure takes that row's `review: failed:<cause>` path.\n\n## Result handling\n\n**Validate the reply first.** Every read of the output file, including each\nre-run inside the ladder below, goes through the parser:\n\n```bash\npython3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/parse_review.py docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>.md\n```\n\n- **Exit 0** — the JSON on stdout (`no_findings`, `findings`, `closures`) is what\n  the ladder below reads. Do not re-parse the raw text by hand.\n- **Exit 1** — the reply broke the reporting contract. Write this text verbatim\n  to `docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-correction.txt` with the **Write tool**,\n  re-render `pat.md` with every flag identical except\n  `--set-file CONTRACT_CORRECTION=docs/dev/tmp/review-task-<id>-correction.txt`,\n  then dispatch **once** more — with `-R \"<pat_session_id>\"`, never `-S`. The\n  session already exists by then, and re-passing `-S` with the same id exits 1\n  on `Error: Session ID <id> is already in use.` (verified live 2026-08-28),\n  which would spend the whole correction retry on a runner failure. No id in\n  hand → neither flag. A `-R` that fails here takes §\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The planner flag encodes backend + Haiku/Sonnet + exactly one writable file + no public-contract edit; missing eligibility is false. Preserve the existing `ui` → `tier` → `contract` → `files` exclusion precedence.\n\n**Runtime write-set reconciliation (before implementor selection).** Read the exact newline-delimited `FILE_PATHS` scratch file rendered for Ivan; ignore blank lines and count distinct paths. Tess-owned read-only tests are not in this list. After the `fable` override, zero paths fail closed to Claude at the task tier (no Codex interception, `preflight_outcome: null`, attempt `qwen_excluded_reason: \"files\"`). A test-only write set keeps the non-Qwen Claude path at its task tier; derive `is_test_only` from the existing step-2.7 classification using repo-relative paths, never absolute path ancestors, and pass it in the effective copy. For an otherwise Qwen-eligible backend Haiku/Sonnet task, two or more paths replace eligibility with false and exclusion with `files` **in a per-task effective copy only**; stamp the eventual attempt `qwen_excluded_reason: \"files\"`, `preflight_outcome: null`. Apply the table and all six Codex interception fences to that effective copy: two/three-file tasks can still take Codex, otherwise Claude at tier. Exactly one non-empty path may reach row 5. Do not rewrite planner metadata or unrelated state, and do not replace an existing UI, tier, or contract exclusion. This fence also applies under `legacy`.\n\nApply the rows in this order — the first match wins (in practice `qwen_eligible == true` already excludes UI and `opus`, so the order resolves any apparent overlap deterministically):\n\n| # | Task class | Implementor | Reference |\n|---|------------|-------------|-----------|\n| 1 | UI / visual task (per \"Gemini-first tasks\") | Gemini if available, else Claude at `state.tasks[i].model` | `references/gemini-integration.md` |\n| 2 | Backend `opus` tier | Claude Opus (Agent dispatch) | — |\n| 3 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"`, qwen capability breaker tripped (`qwen_breaker.tripped == true`, after the batch-scope check below) | Claude at the task's ORIGINAL tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) — **skip the preflight probe**, stamp the eventual attempt `breaker_skipped:true` | qwen capability breaker (below) |\n| 4 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, and `python3 ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/skills/work/scripts/check_memory_pressure.py --max-level <ladder § Memory gate value>` exits non-zero | Claude at the task's ORIGINAL tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) — **skip the preflight probe**; stamp the attempt `preflight_outcome: null` and `qwen_excluded_reason: \"memory_pressure\"` (exit 1) or `\"memory_probe_failed\"` (exit 2) | `scripts/check_memory_pressure.py` |\n| 5 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, row 4 did not fire, healthy qwen infra | Local qwen via `use-qwen` helper | `references/qwen-integration.md` |\n| 6 | Backend, `qwen_eligible == true`, row 3 did not fire, row 4 did not fire, **unhealthy** qwen infra | Claude at the task's original tier (`haiku` → Haiku, `sonnet` → Sonnet) | `references/qwen-integration.md` (Preflight) |\n| 7 | Backend, effective `qwen_eligible == false` (or absent) | Claude at the task's tier (e.g. a two-file `sonnet` task → Claude Sonnet, subject to Codex interception) | — |\n\n**Codex rung interception.** After the table above yields its verdict, dispatch **codex** instead of the Claude implementor the table named when all six fences hold (verdict is \"Claude at the task's tier\"/\"ORIGINAL tier\", `codex_eligible(task)`, `_WORK_CODEX_RUNG != \"off\"`, `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"`, a `\"healthy\"` batch probe, and a terminal attempt that was not itself codex). **Read `references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex rung interception before the first codex dispatch of a batch** — it states each fence exactly and why fence 4 is not optional.\n\n**Before a Qwen dispatch**, read `references/qwen-integration.md` § Output guards and run its `check_qwen_output.py before` command. It requires a clean implementation slice and canonical Tess tests, and captures this dispatch's baseline. A failed preparation skips Qwen and uses Claude at tier without spending a Qwen attempt; retain the guard diagnostic in the task output and preserve the actual preflight verdict; do not let pre-existing task edits masquerade as Qwen output.\n\n**`fable` overrides this table outright.** A task carrying `state.tasks[i].model: \"fable\"` — set only by the Fable rescue gate (`run-autopilot/references/recovery.md` § Rework escalation exhausted) — never routes to qwen and never to Gemini: dispatch a Claude Agent at `model: \"fable\"`, whatever the rows above would pick. `fable` is never a session model and is never selected autonomously, so the human rescue gate is the only way in (`run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Fable rescue).\n\n**qwen capability breaker (routing-time consult, row 3).** Guarded by `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION != \"legacy\"` (`model-ladder.md` § Kill-switches) — under `legacy` the breaker is fully off, row 3 never fires, and rows 5-6 behave exactly as today's rows 3-4. The memory-pressure gate (row 4) is a deliberate always-on exception to that kill-switch: it carries no `_AUTOPILOT_ESCALATION` guard (unlike the breaker) and keeps firing under `legacy` — a host-safety mechanism, not a quality mechanism, so the kill-switch that restores old routing semantics must not also switch off OOM protection.\n\n**Read `references/qwen-integration.md` § Batch-scoped preflight before the first qwen dispatch of a batch** — it carries the breaker's batch-scope reset and row-3 consult, and the `state.qwen_preflight` cache procedure (probe once per batch, reuse the verdict, and the two backend-health signals that force a re-probe). One rule lives here too, because a passing run never opens that reference: a qwen gate pass resets `qwen_gate_failures_consecutive` to 0, so the breaker trips only on two CONSECUTIVE qwen gate failures.\n\n**Re-evaluate the routing table for EVERY claimed task — no session-level memory.** The table is per-task, and so is the qwen one-shot-per-task budget: exactly one qwen dispatch per task (success OR failure) — a qwen attempt on task A never excludes qwen for task B. There is no per-PRD or per-batch qwen cap; every eligible task is routed independently. Do not generalize a fallback (\"qwen was slow on the last task, route the rest to Claude\") — that decision belongs to the table and the preflight, not to session memory (observed failure: `references/design-rationale.md` § no session memory). Self-check before each initial Ivan dispatch: use the **effective routing decision**, not the persisted eligibility alone. A Claude fallback must be justified by a non-healthy preflight, breaker/pressure exclusion, write-set or test-only fence, or a recorded output-guard preparation failure; preserve its actual preflight verdict (null when never run). If none applies, re-run the table. Capability escalations dispatch directly to the higher rung and are not initial routing decisions.\n\n**An escalated tier belongs to its task and dies with it (PRD 00111).** When a task escalates — in-loop at step 5.5, or by review flag through `/autopilot:run-autopilot` Phase 6 — the higher tier is written to that task's `model` field in `state.tasks[i]`, and nowhere else. Every other task still enters at the tier `/autopilot:plan-tasks` classified for it: a task escalated to `opus` is followed by an unrelated `haiku` task dispatching at `haiku`, in the same PRD and the same session. Do not carry a tier sideways (\"the last task needed opus, so this PRD runs at opus\") — that is the same session-memory mistake the routing rule above forbids, priced one rung higher. Nothing escalation-related survives into the next PRD either: `autopilot reset-prd` drops `tasks` (the per-task tiers), `rework_task_ids`, `cap_rotations` and `stall_reason`, and zeroes `replan_count` (`run-autopilot/cli/records.py` `PER_PRD_RESET_FIELDS`). Session-model decay is the separate, matching rule in `run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md` § Decay.\n\nA helper that does not resolve, or fails at runtime, falls back to Claude at the task's tier, and every dispatch of either kind satisfies the **Subagent Dispatch Budget** and the **Subagent Watchdog**. **Read `references/gemini-integration.md` § Availability before the first UI-task dispatch of a batch** (what \"Gemini if available\" probes, row 1); the helper-vs-Agent mechanics are in `references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Mechanism and tier.\n\n**Codex implementor mechanics.** The HOW of the codex rung — batch health probe, dispatch checklist, TOOL-GATE NOTICE — lives in `references/codex-implementor.md`; **read it in full before the first codex probe or dispatch of a batch**. Two invariants worth repeating at the call site: never `-y` (the `-a` grant covers this rung only), and on any codex timeout `TaskStop` + verify-gone BEFORE dispatching the Claude fallback.\n\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_67","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-patterns/SKILL.md\\\").read_text()[:8000]); print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/python-testing/SKILL.md\\\").read_text()[:8000])'\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: python-patterns\ndescription: Use when writing, reviewing, or refactoring Python code. Covers idioms, naming, traps, toolchain, and security. Triggers on Python file edits, \"pythonic\", \"PEP 8\", \"python best practices\", \"python idioms\", \"bandit\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the strunk plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n# Python Patterns\n\nPick a side. These are the rulings, not a tutorial.\n\n## Idioms that earn their place\n\n| Rule | Why |\n|------|-----|\n| `X \\| Y`, not `Union[X, Y]` | 3.10+ runtime syntax; clearer. On 3.9 it parses only under `from __future__ import annotations` and still breaks `get_type_hints`/`isinstance` — keep `Optional`/`Union` if you support 3.9. |\n| `Protocol`, not `ABC`, for duck typing | Structural typing; no inheritance you don't control. |\n| `@dataclass(frozen=True)` for immutable records, plain `dataclass` only when you must mutate, `NamedTuple` for lightweight immutable rows | Pydantic only when you need validation. |\n| `raise New(...) from e` | Marks the explicit cause. A bare `raise New()` still chains implicitly (\"During handling...\"); use `from None` to suppress. |\n| `@functools.wraps` on every decorator | Without it the wrapper loses `__name__`, `__doc__`, signature. |\n| `pathlib.Path`, not `os.path` | One object, no string surgery. |\n\n## Naming (PEP 8)\n\n`snake_case` for modules, functions, variables. `CapWords` for classes. `UPPER_SNAKE_CASE` for constants. Leading `_` for internal names.\n\n**Never name a `.py` file in kebab-case.** `my-script.py` is not importable (`import my-script` is a `SyntaxError`). Kebab-case belongs only in the `pyproject.toml` distribution name and the CLI command, both of which map to a `snake_case` module.\n\n## Traps\n\n```python\n# Mutable default argument — shared across calls\ndef bad(items=[]): ...\ndef good(items=None):\n    items = [] if items is None else items\n\n# Bare except — swallows SystemExit, KeyboardInterrupt\ntry: ...\nexcept Exception as e: ...        # name the exception\n\n# __slots__ kills __dict__ and dynamic attributes — use only on fixed,\n# memory-sensitive classes you won't extend.\n\n# __double_leading is name-mangled to _Class__double_leading.\n# Surprises you in subclasses, pickling, and monkey-patching.\n\nif value is None: ...             # never == None\n```\n\nAvoid `from module import *`. Use `isinstance`, never `type(x) ==`.\n\n## Toolchain\n\n**black** to format, **isort** for imports, **ruff** to lint. Type annotations on every function signature — no exceptions for \"obvious\" returns.\n\n## Resources and laziness\n\nContext managers (`with`) for anything holding a resource. Generators for lazy iteration over anything you would otherwise materialize into a list.\n\n## Security\n\n- Read secrets with `os.environ[\"API_KEY\"]`, never `.get()` — a missing secret must raise `KeyError` at startup, not surface as `None` at request time.\n- `python-dotenv` loads a local `.env` in development only. Never commit one.\n- `bandit -r src/` for static security analysis.\n\n---\nname: python-testing\ndescription: Use when writing, fixing, or reviewing Python tests with pytest. Covers TDD, fixtures, mocking, parametrization, coverage. Triggers on \"pytest\", \"python test\", \"conftest\", \"pytest.mark\", \"parametrize\", \"pytest fixture\", \"python mock\".\ncompatibility: \"Portable standalone compatibility copy of the strunk plugin skill for agents without that plugin; Claude Code uses the namespaced plugin skill.\"\n---\n\n# Python Testing\n\nTDD: write the failing test (RED), make it pass (GREEN), refactor. One behavior per test. No logic in tests. Coverage target 80%, higher on critical paths.\n\n## Rulings\n\n**Mocking**\n- Patch where the name is *used*, not where it's defined: `@patch(\"myapp.service.requests\")`, not `@patch(\"requests\")`.\n- `autospec=True` so the mock rejects calls the real API would reject.\n- Mock at the boundary (I/O, network, clock). Never mock the thing under test.\n- Async: assert with `assert_awaited_once()`, not `assert_called_once()`.\n\n**Fixtures**\n- `yield` for teardown; the line after `yield` is the cleanup.\n- Default to function scope. Widen to `module`/`session` only for genuinely expensive resources.\n- `autouse` hides dependencies — use sparingly; prefer explicit injection.\n- `tmp_path` for temp files (auto-cleanup, `Path` API), not `tempfile`.\n\n**Parametrize**\n- `@pytest.mark.parametrize` over loops — distinct test IDs, filterable with `-k`.\n- Pass `ids=[...]` when params are objects or tuples; pytest already auto-names plain str/int/bool readably.\n\n**Config**\n- One config in `pyproject.toml` (`[tool.pytest.ini_options]`), not a separate `pytest.ini`.\n- `--strict-markers` so a typo'd marker fails instead of silently passing.\n- Register custom markers — e.g. `slow`, `@pytest.mark.unit`, `@pytest.mark.integration` — so `--strict-markers` catches a typo.\n- Coverage locally: `pytest --cov=src --cov-report=term-missing` — the missing-line report is the point; a bare percentage is not actionable.\n\n**Async (pytest-asyncio)**\n- Default mode is `strict`: an async test with no `@pytest.mark.asyncio` is silently not collected. Set `asyncio_mode = \"auto\"` in `[tool.pytest.ini_options]` to drop the per-test marker.\n- Use `@pytest_asyncio.fixture` for async fixtures in strict mode.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_69","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.claude/plugins/cache/buvis-plugins/autopilot/0.10.0/skills/run-autopilot/references/model-ladder.md\\\").read_text()[:6500])'\"","aggregated_output":"# Model-Escalation Ladder\n\nThis file declares the escalation ladder for `/autopilot:work`: every rung, budget, and\nswitch that governs which backend runs a task and when it escalates.\nConsumers (`plan-tasks`, `work`, `phase-review`) cite this file instead of\nrestating it. Every number appears exactly once, here.\n\n## Rungs\n\nLowest to highest:\n\n| Rung | Backend | Activation status |\n|------|---------|--------------------|\n| `qwen` | local llama.cpp backend | **ACTIVE** |\n| `codex` | Codex CLI (`skills/use-codex/scripts/codex-run.sh`) | **ACTIVE** (PRD 00077) |\n| `claude-haiku` | Claude Haiku | **ACTIVE** |\n| `claude-sonnet` | Claude Sonnet | **ACTIVE** |\n| `claude-opus` | Claude Opus | **ACTIVE** |\n| `fable` | Claude Fable | **ACTIVE (human-gated)** — entered only through the rescue gate (§ Fable rescue): one dispatch per PRD, ever, and only after a human approves. Never a session model, never selected autonomously. |\n\nOrder (cheapest to most capable - this is the **cost order** used at\nrouting-time selection, NOT a capability-escalation chain; the escalation\nedges are declared in § Capability ladders and deliberately differ):\nqwen -> codex -> claude haiku/sonnet/opus -> fable. The last edge is the\nonly one no skill may take on its own: `opus` exhaustion does not escalate to\n`fable`, it stops at the human-gated rescue (§ Fable rescue).\n\n## Tier -> backend map\n\n| Tier | Backend |\n|------|---------|\n| `haiku` | Claude Haiku |\n| `sonnet` | Claude Sonnet |\n| `opus` | Claude Opus |\n| `fable` | Claude Fable — reachable only via the rescue gate, never by the plan-tasks classifier |\n\n`qwen` is the local backend used for qwen-eligible backend tasks at haiku/sonnet\ntier. It is not a tier of its own.\n\nThe INITIAL tier authority is plan-tasks step 4.7's classifier (the\n`qwen_eligible` formula plus the `default_model` floor). This file cites that\nclassifier; it does not re-derive it.\n\n## Per-rung budgets\n\n| Rung(s) | Budget |\n|---------|--------|\n| Claude rungs (haiku / sonnet / opus) | **2 dispatches**: initial + one feedback retry. The 2nd gate failure at a rung triggers diagnosis. |\n| qwen | **1 dispatch per task**: no same-tier feedback retry. A qwen gate failure escalates immediately (this is the qwen one-shot-per-task budget; the Capability ladders section below names it the `qwen -> sonnet` edge). Scoped per task, not per PRD or per batch — every qwen-eligible task gets its own independent one-shot budget. |\n| codex | **2 dispatches**: initial + one feedback retry, identical to the Claude rungs (PRD 00077: \"same as every rung\"). |\n| `fable` | **1 capability dispatch per PRD, ever**: no same-tier feedback retry, no repair. An *infra* failure (watchdog / lost result) still falls back at the same tier per § Infra vs capability — infra is not a capability attempt. Scoped per PRD, not per task: one approved rescue buys one Fable attempt for the whole PRD. |\n| Repair | **At most 1 per task, total** (Claude rungs only; qwen and codex never get a repair). |\n\nWorst-case examples:\n\n- A qwen-eligible `sonnet` task: qwen (1 fail -> escalate) -> Sonnet (2\n  dispatches, +1 possible repair) -> Opus (2 dispatches) -> opus exhaustion.\n- A non-qwen `haiku` task: haiku (2 dispatches +1 repair) -> sonnet (2\n  dispatches) -> opus (2 dispatches) -> exhaustion.\n- A `files`-band `sonnet` task (excluded from qwen for file count, so\n  codex-eligible): codex (2 dispatches) -> Sonnet (2 dispatches, +1 possible\n  repair) -> Opus (2 dispatches) -> exhaustion.\n\n## Capability ladders\n\n- `qwen -> sonnet` (skips haiku AND skips codex)\n- `codex -> claude at the task's own tier` (haiku -> Haiku, sonnet -> Sonnet)\n- `haiku -> sonnet -> opus`\n\nOpus-rung exhaustion (2 failures at opus) flows into the existing abort/stall\nmachinery (PRD 00017), through the Fable rescue gate (§ Fable rescue) on the\nway. No new halt class. A `fable` attempt has **no rung above it**: its gate\nfailure goes straight to the same exhaustion path, never to an escalation.\n\nQwen output causes `qwen_no_edit` and `qwen_test_mutation` are capability\nfailures on that same one-shot edge, detected before staging or test execution.\nThey never retry Qwen, take Codex, or invalidate a healthy preflight cache.\nThe runtime single-file fence applies before the table; stale two/three-file\ntasks use the effective `files` exclusion for the existing Codex interception,\nwhile zero paths fail closed to Claude at tier. Planner metadata is unchanged.\n\n## Fable rescue\n\nThe `opus -> fable` edge is a human gate, not a ladder step. In ladder terms:\n\n- Exhaustion at `opus` records a rescue **request** for the PRD — one per PRD,\n  ever. A PRD that already has an entry (`requested`, `approved`, `rejected`,\n  or `consumed`) never gets a second one.\n- A human decides it out of band: `autoclaude approve-fable <prd>` (or\n  `autoclaude reject-fable <prd>`). If the wrapper is unavailable, the\n  documented fallback is invoking `fablectl.py` directly - see\n  `references/state-schema.md` § `fablectl.py`.\n- The next exhaustion for that PRD spends the approval on exactly one\n  Fable-tier dispatch, and the entry flips to `consumed` regardless of\n  outcome. A failed Fable attempt therefore stalls the PRD normally, with no\n  new request.\n\nThe ledger that holds those states is `references/state-schema.md` § Fable\nrescue ledger. The procedure — when the gate runs, in what order it writes,\nand what each `fablectl` exit means — lives in `references/recovery.md`\n§ \"Rework escalation exhausted\" and is not restated here.\n\n## Infra vs capability\n\n- An **infra** failure (qwen preflight failure, subagent watchdog timeout /\n  lost result) is NOT a capability failure: it falls back at the SAME tier,\n  never increments the qwen capability breaker, never enters diagnosis.\n  (Existing behavior, unchanged.)\n- A **capability** failure (a real test-gate failure) escalates UP the\n  capability ladder, after diagnosis.\n\n## Codex rung\n\n- **Position**: between `qwen` and the Claude tiers, exactly as the order\n  line in § Rungs already states. The `qwen -> sonnet` capability edge\n  (§ Capability ladders) is UNCHANGED.\n- **Fences**: the eligibility predicate, evaluated at routing time from\n  existing plan-time metadata (no new plan-tasks field):\n\n  ```\n  codex_eligible(task) =\n        task.qwen_eligible == true\n     OR task.qwen_excluded_reason == \"files\"\n  ```\n\n  Absent `qwen_eligible` (legacy plans) -> `false`. Any\n  `qwen_excluded_reason` of `ui`, `tier`, or `contract` -> `false`. UI stays\n  gemini; `opus` tier st\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

The design says \\\"Preserve source lock/read/publication guards\\\" but never says whether the flock blocks, has a timeout, or is non-blocking. Callers only get a 30-second test deadline. A stuck process holding the lock would hang every CLI call, and no error code fits a timeout. Only revision_conflict is retryable.\",\n      \"suggested_fix\": \"Specify non-blocking flock with a bounded wait. Map expiry to an existing code, and say which and whether it is retryable. This is an infrastructure failure, not real work — apply the **infrastructure-failure circuit breaker** (step 4.2). |\n\n**Qwen carve-out.** After any non-success result, stop the helper and verify it is gone, then run the `after --tests-only` output guard before applying this table. A mutation uses Qwen output rejection; an indeterminate guard stops acceptance. Only unchanged canonical tests resume the original failure handler; no-edit applies only to exit-zero success.\n\n**Codex carve-out.** A codex dispatch's timeout, missing/empty `-o` output, and a watchdog-killed hang are all arm 1 (Infra) per `model-ladder.md` § Codex rung — never the generic Timeout / Result-lost-hung rows above, never split-task, never the 4.2 breaker. On timeout, apply the kill-before-fallback rule from the codex dispatch checklist (`references/codex-implementor.md` § Codex dispatch): `TaskStop` the codex background task and verify it is gone BEFORE dispatching the Claude fallback — an orphaned `--sandbox workspace-write` codex keeps write access to the very files the fallback implementor is about to edit, so its late writes either get swept into the fallback's commit or land as unexplained foreign paths. Fall back to Claude at the task's tier, no escalation stamp. The `codex_no_edit` / `codex_no_edit_probe_exit` flags latched during dispatch (step 3) are likewise not resolved here — they are consumed by step 5.5's classification (arm 2), per the same ladder section.\n\n## Narrow scope (step 5.5)\n\nMoved verbatim out of SKILL.md step 5.5 (PRD 00119-v2). Target the narrowest scope that covers the new tests:\n\n- Rust: run `cargo check -p <crate>` first — a compile failure IS the gate failure (skip the test run, go straight to the retry path with the compiler output); then `cargo test -p <crate> --test <test_file>` or `cargo test -p <crate> <module::test_name>`\n- Python: `pytest path/to/test_file.py::test_name`\n- JS/TS: `vitest run path/to/test_file` or `jest path/to/test_file`\n\nEvery one of these is a **lint and narrow tests** command: pass `timeout: 300000` on the Bash call (`references/subagent-dispatch.md` § Foreground command budgets), and run it alone — never combined with an inspection in the same call. A command that hits the budget re-runs once at 600000 ms; a second timeout stamps `verification: \"timeout:<command>\"` on the attempt, names the command and its budget in the phase report, and the task proceeds rather than looping on it.\n\n## Test-commit SHA (step 2.85)\n\nMoved verbatim out of SKILL.md step 2.9 (PRD 00119-v2; the commit step is 2.85\nsince PRD 00202 moved it ahead of Devon). The ESCALATE reset in the flow above\nresets to exactly this commit — the LAST test commit, so when step 2.9's\nstrengthen round committed `test(<scope>): strengthen <feature>`, that commit is\n`<test_commit_sha>`.\n\nStep 5.7's `BASE_SHA` is **not** derived from it: `BASE_SHA` is `<task_base_sha>`,\ncaptured by step 2 right after `task-start`. The two coincide whenever step 2.85\ncommitted tests, but `<task_base_sha>` is also defined for the tasks that commit\nnone — test-only, docs-only, config-only and micro-lane — where the old\nparent-of-the-test-commit rule had nothing to point at. The ESCALATE reset is\n`<test_commit_sha>`'s one remaining reader.\n\n**Capture this task's test-commit SHA** immediately — step 5.5's ESCALATE reset resets to exactly this commit (never a prior task's):\n```bash\ngit rev-parse HEAD\n```\nHold the returned SHA in-session as `<test_commit_sha>` for this task; step 5.5's ESCALATE path reads it.\n\n# Task Splitting\n\nRead this when the Handle-result table (`SKILL.md` step 4) routes a task to\n**Timeout** or **Context exceeded**, or when a task proves too complex to finish\nin one dispatch.\n\n**Note:** With 1M context, context-exceeded failures are rare. Split primarily for timeout or task complexity, not context limits.\n\nWhen a tool can't complete a task (timeout/complexity), split it:\n\n1. Analyze what was accomplished\n2. Create 2-4 smaller tasks covering remaining work\n3. Create each subtask with `task-add <task-json-file>` — a JSON payload file\n   carrying at minimum `name`, plus `description`/`model`/`estimated_tokens`\n   and any other field the original task's metadata warrants. Capture the id\n   `task-add` prints to stdout.\n4. Set sequential dependencies via each subtask's `blocked_by` array (list of\n   ints) in its own `task-add` payload, naming the captured ids of subtasks\n   created earlier in this same split that must finish first.\n5. Mark original task as blocked or completed (if partially done)\n\n## Split criteria\n\n| Original scope | Split into |\n|----------------|------------|\n| Multiple files | One task per file |\n| Multiple features | One task per feature |\n| Large refactor | Extract → transform → cleanup |\n| Full-stack feature | Backend task (qwen or Claude per the routing table) → Frontend task (Gemini) |\n\n## Parallel dispatch for independent rework fixes\n\nIf `superpowers:dispatching-parallel-agents` is in the available skills list and the current batch contains 2+ tasks that:\n- Touch completely different files (no overlap)\n- Have no `blockedBy` dependencies on each other\n- Are all tagged `[C{n}]` or `[D{n}]` (rework tasks, not original plan tasks)\n\nThen dispatch them in parallel using the dispatching-parallel-agents pattern, **with at most 2 agents in flight at once**. Parallel agents share one working tree — one `cargo` target dir and one build lock — so their compiles serialize on that lock, but each `cargo` invocation still spawns a full `rustc` fleet. Bounding that fleet is what keeps RAM safe: rely on the global `~/.cargo/config.toml` `[build] jobs` cap and **never raise `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS`, pass `--jobs`, or run a full-workspace `cargo build` / `cargo test --workspace` / `clippy` inside a parallel agent** (per-task verify in step 5.5 is single-crate; the full suite runs once in step 7). An uncapped fan-out once locked the whole machine (`design-rationale.md` § parallel rework cap).\n\n**Never parallelize original plan tasks** - the one-at-a-time rule remains for all non-rework tasks: `state.tasks` accuracy and per-task attempt logging depend on it.\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}

+{"type":"item.completed","item":{"id":"item_94","type":"command_execution","command":"/opt/homebrew/bin/bash -lc \"python3 -c 'from pathlib import Path; print(Path(\\\"/Users/bob/.agents/skills/debug-stuck-agent/SKILL.md\\\").read_text())'\"","aggregated_output":"---\nname: debug-stuck-agent\ndescription: Use when an agent is failing repeatedly, looping on tools, drifting from the task, or burning tokens without progress. Triggers on \"agent introspection\", \"debug agent\", \"agent stuck\", \"agent loop\", \"diagnose failure\", \"why is this stuck\".\n---\n\n# Debug Stuck Agent\n\nA workflow skill, not a hidden runtime: it teaches the agent to debug itself\nsystematically before escalating to a human.\n\n## Dependencies\n\n- Plugin skills (`autopilot` plugin), referenced only as escalation pointers\n  and never invoked here: `autopilot:review-work-completion`,\n  `autopilot:review-blindly`. Without the plugin, verify recovered work with\n  whatever review the host offers; nothing in this workflow hard-fails.\n\n## Scope Boundaries\n\nActivate this skill for:\n- maximum tool call / loop-limit failures, or repeated retries with no forward progress\n- context growth or prompt drift that starts degrading output quality\n- file-system or environment state mismatch between expectation and reality\n- tool failures likely recoverable with diagnosis and a smaller corrective action\n\nDo not use this skill as the primary source for:\n- feature verification after code changes; use `autopilot:review-work-completion` or `autopilot:review-blindly`\n- framework-specific debugging when a narrower skill already exists\n- runtime promises the current harness cannot enforce automatically\n\n## Four-Phase Loop\n\n### Phase 1: Failure Capture\n\nBefore trying to recover, record the failure precisely — fill every field of\nthe \"Failure Capture\" template in `references/capture-templates.md` (error,\nlast tool sequence, goal in progress, context pressure, environment\nassumptions).\n\n### Phase 2: Root-Cause Diagnosis\n\nMatch the failure to a known pattern before changing anything.\n\n| Pattern | Likely Cause | Check |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Maximum tool calls / repeated same command | loop or no-exit observer path | inspect the last N tool calls for repetition |\n| Context overflow / degraded reasoning | unbounded notes, repeated plans, oversized logs | inspect recent context for duplication and low-signal bulk |\n| `ECONNREFUSED` / timeout | service unavailable or wrong port | verify service health, URL, and port assumptions |\n| `429` / quota exhaustion | retry storm or missing backoff | count repeated calls and inspect retry spacing |\n| file missing after write / stale diff | race, wrong cwd, or branch drift | re-check path, cwd, git status, and actual file existence |\n| tests still failing after \"fix\" | wrong hypothesis | isolate the exact failing test and re-derive the bug |\n\nDiagnosis questions:\n- is this a logic failure, state failure, environment failure, or policy failure?\n- did the agent lose the real objective and start optimizing the wrong subtask?\n- is the failure deterministic or transient?\n- what is the smallest reversible action that would validate the diagnosis?\n\n### Phase 3: Contained Recovery\n\nRecover with the smallest action that changes the diagnosis surface\n(checklist: \"Recovery Action\" in `references/capture-templates.md`).\n\nSafe recovery actions:\n- stop repeated retries and restate the hypothesis\n- trim low-signal context and keep only the active goal, blockers, and evidence\n- re-check the actual filesystem / branch / process state\n- narrow the task to one failing command, one file, or one test\n- switch from speculative reasoning to direct observation\n- escalate to a human when the failure is high-risk or externally blocked\n\nDo not claim unsupported auto-healing actions like \"reset agent state\" or \"update harness config\" unless you are actually doing them through real tools in the current environment.\n\n### Phase 4: Introspection Report\n\nEnd with a report that makes the recovery legible to the next agent or human\n(template: \"Agent Self-Debug Report\" in `references/capture-templates.md`).\nNever end with \"I fixed it\" alone — the filled report is the deliverable.\n\n## Recovery Heuristics\n\nPrefer these interventions in order:\n\n1. Restate the real objective in one sentence.\n2. Verify the world state instead of trusting memory.\n3. Shrink the failing scope.\n4. Run one discriminating check.\n5. Only then retry.\n\nBad pattern: retrying the same action three times with slightly different\nwording. Good pattern: capture → classify → one direct check → change the\nplan only if the check supports it.\n\n## Related Skills\n\n- `autopilot:review-work-completion` after recovery if code was changed\n- `convene-council` when the issue is decision ambiguity, not technical failure\n- `git-ferry:resolve-git-conflicts` when the failure came from conflicting local state\n- `git-ferry:catchup` if the failure came from missing project context\n\n","exit_code":0,"status":"completed"}}
