diff --git a/tests/autopilot/test_controller_owner_v2.py b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_owner_v2.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..6371128
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_owner_v2.py
@@ -0,0 +1,419 @@
+"""Receipt authority survives rotation without granting retired credentials a lease."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from controller_cli_support import canonical, private_path, tree
+from controller_owner_support import OwnerCLITest, credential
+
+
+class OwnerV2Test(OwnerCLITest):
+    def test_wrong_binding_reports_selected_root_revision_and_preserves_both_projects(self) -> None:
+        _, _, operator = self.bootstrap()
+        _, _, owner, _ = self.acquire(operator)
+        request = self.request(owner, "owner.release", "cross-project-release")
+        original_root = self.root
+        original_before = tree(private_path(original_root))
+        selected_root = self.base / "project-extra"
+        selected_root.mkdir()
+        self.response(self.apply(request, owner, root=selected_root),
+                      "wrong_binding", revision=0)
+        self.assertFalse(private_path(selected_root).exists())
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(original_root)) == original_before,
+                        "empty selected-root rejection changed original project evidence")
+        self.root = selected_root
+        _, _, selected_operator = self.bootstrap()
+        _, _, selected_owner, _ = self.acquire(selected_operator)
+        self.clear(selected_owner)
+        selected_revision = self.state()["revision"]
+        self.assertEqual(selected_revision, 2)
+        selected_before = tree(private_path(selected_root))
+        self.root = original_root
+        self.assertEqual(self.state()["revision"], 1)
+        self.response(self.apply(request, owner, root=selected_root),
+                      "wrong_binding", revision=selected_revision)
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(selected_root)) == selected_before,
+                        "rejection changed selected project evidence")
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(original_root)) == original_before,
+                        "rejection changed original project evidence")
+
+    def history(self, tag: str) -> tuple[list[tuple], dict[int, Path], Path]:
+        fresh, opened, operator = self.bootstrap()
+        operators = {0: self.retain(operator, f"{tag}-operator-zero.json")}
+        first, first_response, owner, operator = self.acquire(
+            operator, "manual", f"séance-{tag}", f"{tag}-acquire")
+        operators[1] = self.retain(operator, f"{tag}-operator-one.json")
+        released, released_response, operator = self.clear(
+            owner, request_id=f"{tag}-release")
+        operators[2] = self.retain(operator, f"{tag}-operator-two.json")
+        second, second_response, second_owner, operator = self.acquire(
+            operator, "supervised", f"séance-{tag}-extra", f"{tag}-acquire-extra")
+        operators[3] = self.retain(operator, f"{tag}-operator-three.json")
+        recovered = self.request(operator, "owner.recover", f"{tag}-recover", {
+            "reason": f"Explicit reconciliation {tag}", "reconciled_job_ids": []})
+        recovered_response = self.response(self.apply(recovered, operator), revision=4)
+        self.assert_transition(recovered, recovered_response, operators[3])
+        records = [(fresh, opened, None), (first, first_response, operators[0]),
+                   (released, released_response, owner),
+                   (second, second_response, operators[2]),
+                   (recovered, recovered_response, operators[3])]
+        self.assertNotEqual(owner, second_owner)
+        issued = [*operators.values(), operator, owner, second_owner]
+        digests = {hashlib.sha256(credential(path)["secret"].encode()).digest()
+                   for path in issued}
+        self.assertEqual(len(digests), len(issued), "issued secrets must be distinct")
+        return records, operators, operator
+
+    def test_canonical_receipts_replay_after_rotation_with_different_json_encodings(self) -> None:
+        parent = self.root
+        for tag in ("alpha", "alpha-extra"):
+            self.root = parent / tag
+            self.root.mkdir()
+            records, _, operator = self.history(tag)
+            before = tree(private_path(self.root))
+            for request, response, historical in records:
+                reordered = dict(reversed(tuple(request.items())))
+                reordered["payload"] = dict(reversed(tuple(request["payload"].items())))
+                raw = json.dumps(reordered, ensure_ascii=True, indent=3).encode()
+                self.assertNotEqual(raw, canonical(request))
+                actors = ((None,) if historical is None else
+                          (historical, operator) if request["operation"] != "owner.release"
+                          else (historical,))
+                for actor in actors:
+                    actual = self.response(self.apply(request, actor, raw=raw))
+                    self.assertEqual(actual, response)
+                    self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == before, "private evidence changed")
+            recovered = records[-1][0]
+            for jobs in (["job-alpha", "job-beta"], ["job-alpha-extra", "job-beta-extra"]):
+                changed = recovered | {"payload": recovered["payload"] | {
+                    "reconciled_job_ids": jobs}}
+                self.reject_unchanged(changed, operator, "invalid_request")
+            self.assert_fresh_requests_validate_revision_payload_and_operation(operator, tag)
+            self.assertIsNone(self.snapshot()["owner"])
+
+    def test_retired_intermediate_operator_cannot_borrow_another_epochs_receipt_authority(self) -> None:
+        records, operators, current = self.history("authority")
+        before = tree(private_path(self.root))
+        for request, response, historical in (records[1], records[3], records[4]):
+            epoch = request["lease_epoch"]
+            self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, historical)), response)
+            self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, current)), response)
+            for retired_epoch, actor in operators.items():
+                if retired_epoch != epoch:
+                    self.reject_unchanged(request, actor, "wrong_binding")
+            self.reject_unchanged(request, None, "wrong_binding")
+            self.reject_unchanged(request | {"request_id": request["request_id"] + "-extra"},
+                                  historical, "wrong_binding")
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == before, "private evidence changed")
+        self.assertEqual(self.state()["lease_epoch"], 4)
+        self.assertEqual(set(self.state()["actors"]), {credential(current)["actor_id"]})
+        for request, _, historical in (records[1], records[3], records[4]):
+            for source in (historical, current):
+                self.assert_replay_rejects_changed_credential_bindings(request, source)
+        _, _, owner, operator = self.acquire(current, request_id="authority-current-owner")
+        wrong_release = self.request(operator, "owner.release", "authority-operator-release")
+        self.reject_unchanged(wrong_release, operator, "wrong_binding")
+        wrong_acquire = self.request(owner, "owner.acquire", "authority-owner-acquire", {
+            "mode": "manual", "native_session_id": "authority-wrong-role"})
+        self.reject_unchanged(wrong_acquire, owner, "wrong_binding")
+
+    def test_exact_receipt_replay_still_checks_credential_file_safety(self) -> None:
+        records, _, current = self.history("private")
+        for request, response, historical in (records[1], records[2], records[4]):
+            for index, source in enumerate((historical, current)):
+                if index and request["operation"] == "owner.release":
+                    continue
+                stem = f"{request['request_id']}-{index}"
+                valid = self.retain(source, stem + ".json")
+                self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, valid)), response)
+                forged = self.retain(source, stem + "-forged.json")
+                value = credential(forged)
+                value["secret"] = self.changed_secret(value["secret"])
+                forged.write_bytes(canonical(value))
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, forged, "wrong_binding")
+                invalid = self.base / (stem + ".json-extra")
+                invalid.symlink_to(valid)
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, invalid, "wrong_binding")
+                linked = self.base / ("prefix-" + stem + ".json")
+                os.link(valid, linked)
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, valid, "wrong_binding")
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, linked, "wrong_binding")
+                linked.unlink()
+                valid.chmod(0o644)
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, valid, "wrong_binding")
+                valid.chmod(0o600)
+                self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, valid)), response)
+                for raw in (b"", b"{}", b"{\"secret\":\"x\",\"secret\":\"y\"}"):
+                    invalid_copy = self.retain(source, stem + "-malformed.json")
+                    invalid_copy.write_bytes(raw)
+                    self.reject_unchanged(request, invalid_copy, "wrong_binding")
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def changed_secret(secret: str) -> str:
+        return ("A" if secret[0] != "A" else "B") + secret[1:]
+
+    def assert_replay_rejects_changed_credential_bindings(self, request: dict,
+                                                        source: Path) -> None:
+        original = credential(source)
+        changes = {"project_id": "0" * 64,
+                   "workflow_id": original["workflow_id"] + "-extra",
+                   "lease_epoch": original["lease_epoch"] + 1, "role": "owner"}
+        for field, replacement in changes.items():
+            with self.subTest(operation=request["operation"], credential_field=field):
+                forged = self.retain(source, f"binding-{field}.json")
+                forged.write_bytes(canonical(original | {field: replacement}))
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, forged, "wrong_binding")
+
+    def assert_fresh_requests_validate_revision_payload_and_operation(self, operator: Path,
+                                                                    tag: str) -> None:
+        stale = self.request(operator, "owner.acquire", f"{tag}-stale-acquire", {
+            "mode": "manual", "native_session_id": "stale-session"})
+        stale["expected_revision"] -= 1
+        self.reject_unchanged(stale, operator, "revision_conflict")
+        invalid = (({"reason": "", "reconciled_job_ids": []}, "invalid_request"),
+                   ({"reason": "é" * 2049, "reconciled_job_ids": []}, "invalid_request"),
+                   ({"reason": "Attended", "reconciled_job_ids": [1]}, "invalid_request"),
+                   ({"reason": "Attended", "reconciled_job_ids": ["job", "job"]},
+                    "invalid_request"),
+                   ({"reason": "Attended", "reconciled_job_ids": ["job"]},
+                    "rejected_evidence"))
+        for index, (payload, error) in enumerate(invalid):
+            with self.subTest(recovery_payload=index):
+                request = self.request(operator, "owner.recover", f"{tag}-invalid-{index}",
+                                       payload)
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, operator, error)
+        unknown = self.request(operator, "owner.unknown", f"{tag}-unknown-operation")
+        self.reject_unchanged(unknown, operator, "invalid_request")
+
+    def prepared_crash(self, name: str, tag: str) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
+        _, _, operator = self.bootstrap()
+        actor = operator
+        if name != "owner.acquire":
+            _, _, owner, operator = self.acquire(
+                operator, "supervised", f"session-{tag}", f"{tag}-initial-acquire")
+            actor = owner if name == "owner.release" else operator
+        payload = ({"mode": "manual", "native_session_id": f"session-{tag}-extra"}
+                   if name == "owner.acquire" else
+                   {"reason": f"Attended reconciliation {tag}", "reconciled_job_ids": []}
+                   if name == "owner.recover" else {})
+        return self.request(actor, name, tag, payload), actor
+
+    def assert_crash_completes_once(self, request: dict, historical: Path) -> None:
+        before = tree(private_path(self.root))
+        receipts = set(self.state()["receipts"])
+        intent = private_path(self.root) / "credential-intent.json"
+        if intent.exists():
+            changed = request | {"request_id": request["request_id"] + "-extra"}
+            self.reject_unchanged(changed, historical, "recovery_required")
+            for field, value in (("project_id", "0" * 64),
+                                 ("workflow_id", request["workflow_id"] + "-extra")):
+                changed = request | {field: value}
+                self.reject_unchanged(changed, historical, "wrong_binding")
+            self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == before, "private evidence changed")
+        completed = self.response(self.apply(request, historical),
+                                  revision=request["expected_revision"] + 1)
+        self.assert_transition(request, completed, historical)
+        self.assertFalse(intent.exists())
+        after = tree(private_path(self.root))
+        self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, historical)), completed)
+        if request["operation"] != "owner.release":
+            current = Path(completed["result"]["operator_actor_file"])
+            self.assertEqual(self.response(self.apply(request, current)), completed)
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == after, "private evidence changed")
+        self.assertEqual(set(self.state()["receipts"]), receipts | {request["request_id"]})
+        self.snapshot()
+
+    @staticmethod
+    def response_objects(value: object) -> list[dict]:
+        # Locate contract-defined responses without assuming an intent field name.
+        if isinstance(value, dict):
+            responses = ([value] if set(value) == {
+                "ok", "revision", "result", "error_code", "retryable"} else [])
+            return responses + [response for item in value.values()
+                                for response in OwnerV2Test.response_objects(item)]
+        if isinstance(value, list):
+            return [response for item in value
+                    for response in OwnerV2Test.response_objects(item)]
+        return []
+
+    def tamper_pending_evidence(self, damage: str, request: dict,
+                               initial_paths: set[Path], index: int = 0) -> tuple[Path, bytes]:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        if damage == "response":
+            path = root / "credential-intent.json"
+            original = path.read_bytes()
+            value = json.loads(original)
+            responses = [response for response in self.response_objects(value)
+                         if response["revision"] == request["expected_revision"] + 1]
+            self.assertTrue(bool(responses), "intent must retain its complete response")
+            responses[index]["revision"] += 7
+        elif damage == "state":
+            path = root / "state.json"
+            original = path.read_bytes()
+            value = json.loads(original)
+            value["revision"] += 7
+        else:
+            stages = [path for path in (root / "actors").iterdir()
+                      if path not in initial_paths and path.is_file()
+                      and credential(path).get("role") == "operator"
+                      and credential(path).get("lease_epoch") == request["lease_epoch"] + 1]
+            self.assertEqual(len(stages), 1, "one staged operator credential is required")
+            path = stages[0]
+            original = path.read_bytes()
+            value = credential(path)
+            value["secret"] = self.changed_secret(value["secret"])
+        path.write_bytes(canonical(value))
+        return path, original
+
+    def assert_tampered_crash_preserves_evidence(self, name: str, damage: str,
+                                               parent: Path) -> None:
+        tag = f"{name}-tampered-{damage}"
+        self.root = parent / name / f"tampered-{damage}"
+        self.root.mkdir(parents=True)
+        request, actor = self.prepared_crash(name, tag)
+        historical = self.retain(actor, tag + "-historical.json")
+        initial_paths = set((private_path(self.root) / "actors").iterdir())
+        self.crash(request, actor, "intent_dir_fsynced")
+        intent = private_path(self.root) / "credential-intent.json"
+        probes = (len([response for response in self.response_objects(json.loads(intent.read_bytes()))
+                       if response["revision"] == request["expected_revision"] + 1])
+                  if damage == "response" else 1)
+        self.assertGreater(probes, 0, "intent must retain its complete response")
+        for index in range(probes):
+            with self.subTest(response_copy=index):
+                path, original = self.tamper_pending_evidence(damage, request, initial_paths, index)
+                self.reject_unchanged(request, historical, "recovery_required")
+                self.assertTrue(intent.exists())
+                path.write_bytes(original)
+        self.assert_crash_completes_once(request, historical)
+
+    def pending_cleanup_files(self, request: dict, actor: Path,
+                              historical: Path) -> tuple[dict[tuple[str, int], Path],
+                                                         dict[Path, bytes]]:
+        actors = private_path(self.root) / "actors"
+        initial_paths = set(actors.iterdir())
+        before = self.state()
+        self.crash(request, actor, "intent_dir_fsynced")
+        self.assertEqual(self.state(), before)
+        stages = {}
+        for path in set(actors.iterdir()) - initial_paths:
+            value = credential(path)
+            key = (value["role"], value["lease_epoch"])
+            self.assertNotIn(key, stages, "staging evidence must be unambiguous")
+            self.assertEqual(value["project_id"], request["project_id"])
+            self.assertEqual(value["workflow_id"], request["workflow_id"])
+            stages[key] = path
+        expected = {("operator", request["lease_epoch"]),
+                    ("operator", request["lease_epoch"] + 1)}
+        if request["operation"] == "owner.acquire":
+            expected.add(("owner", request["lease_epoch"] + 1))
+        self.assertEqual(set(stages), expected)
+        intact = tree(private_path(self.root))
+        for key, path in stages.items():
+            with self.subTest(missing_before_publication=key):
+                original = path.read_bytes()
+                path.unlink()
+                try:
+                    self.reject_unchanged(request, historical, "recovery_required")
+                    self.assertTrue((private_path(self.root) / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+                finally:
+                    path.write_bytes(original)
+                    path.chmod(0o600)
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == intact,
+                        "restoring missing evidence must preserve the pending transaction")
+        staged_bytes = {path: path.read_bytes() for path in stages.values()}
+        self.crash(request, historical, "state_published")
+        return stages, staged_bytes
+
+    def assert_corrupt_cleanup_evidence_is_retained(self, request: dict, historical: Path,
+                                                   evidence: dict[Path, bytes]) -> None:
+        intact = tree(private_path(self.root))
+        for index, (path, staged) in enumerate(evidence.items()):
+            with self.subTest(corrupt_after_publication=index):
+                original = path.read_bytes() if path.exists() else None
+                value = json.loads(staged)
+                value["secret"] = self.changed_secret(value["secret"])
+                path.write_bytes(canonical(value))
+                path.chmod(0o600)
+                try:
+                    self.reject_unchanged(request, historical, "recovery_required")
+                    self.assertTrue((private_path(self.root) / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+                finally:
+                    if original is None:
+                        path.unlink(missing_ok=True)
+                    else:
+                        path.write_bytes(original)
+        self.assertTrue(tree(private_path(self.root)) == intact,
+                        "corruption controls must restore every original byte")
+
+    def test_partial_cleanup_recovers_owner_receipts_without_waiving_evidence_checks(self) -> None:
+        parent = self.root
+        for name in ("owner.acquire", "owner.release", "owner.recover"):
+            for removed in ("stage", "rollback", "stage-and-rollback"):
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, removed=removed):
+                    tag = f"{name}-partial-cleanup-{removed}"
+                    self.root = parent / tag
+                    self.root.mkdir()
+                    request, actor = self.prepared_crash(name, tag)
+                    historical = self.retain(actor, tag + "-historical.json")
+                    stages, staged_bytes = self.pending_cleanup_files(request, actor, historical)
+                    committed = self.state()
+                    response = committed["receipts"][request["request_id"]]["response"]
+                    self.assert_transition(request, response, historical)
+                    store = private_path(self.root)
+                    pair = {path: path.read_bytes() for path in
+                            (store / "state.json", store / "state.json.bak")}
+                    finals = [Path(response["result"]["operator_actor_file"])]
+                    if name == "owner.acquire":
+                        finals.append(Path(response["result"]["actor_file"]))
+                    final_bytes = {path: path.read_bytes() for path in finals}
+                    self.assert_corrupt_cleanup_evidence_is_retained(
+                        request, historical, staged_bytes | final_bytes)
+                    self.assertTrue(stages[("operator", request["lease_epoch"])].is_file())
+                    epochs = ((request["lease_epoch"] + 1,) if removed == "stage" else
+                              (request["lease_epoch"],) if removed == "rollback" else
+                              (request["lease_epoch"] + 1, request["lease_epoch"]))
+                    for epoch in epochs:
+                        stages[("operator", epoch)].unlink(missing_ok=True)
+                    self.assertTrue((store / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+                    self.assert_crash_completes_once(request, historical)
+                    self.assertEqual(self.state(), committed)
+                    self.assertTrue(all(path.read_bytes() == raw for path, raw in pair.items()),
+                                    "cleanup replay must not republish committed state or backup")
+                    self.assertTrue(all(path.read_bytes() == raw
+                                        for path, raw in final_bytes.items()),
+                                    "cleanup replay must not rotate final credentials again")
+                    self.assertTrue(all(not path.exists() for path in stages.values()),
+                                    "successful reconciliation must finish credential cleanup")
+
+    def test_intact_owner_crash_evidence_finishes_and_replays_exactly_once(self) -> None:
+        parent = self.root
+        common = ("stage_fsynced", "intent_dir_fsynced", "operator_credential_published",
+                  "state_published", "cleanup_dir_fsynced")
+        for name in ("owner.acquire", "owner.release", "owner.recover"):
+            for damage in ("response", "staged-credential", "state"):
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, damage=damage):
+                    self.assert_tampered_crash_preserves_evidence(name, damage, parent)
+            boundaries = common + (("owner_credential_published",)
+                                   if name == "owner.acquire" else ())
+            for boundary in boundaries:
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary):
+                    tag = f"{name}-{boundary}"
+                    self.root = parent / name / boundary
+                    self.root.mkdir(parents=True)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared_crash(name, tag)
+                    historical = self.retain(actor, tag + "-historical.json")
+                    state = self.state()
+                    self.crash(request, actor, boundary)
+                    if boundary == "stage_fsynced":
+                        self.assertEqual(self.state(), state)
+                    self.assert_crash_completes_once(request, historical)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
diff --git a/tests/autopilot/test_controller_recovery_characterization.py b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_recovery_characterization.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d5b4565
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_recovery_characterization.py
@@ -0,0 +1,173 @@
+"""Pinned ownership and closed protocol examples without an OVCAQ checkout."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import json
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from jsonschema import Draft202012Validator
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
+CONTRACTS = ROOT / "plugins" / "autopilot" / "contracts" / "controller"
+sys.path.insert(0, str(ROOT / "plugins" / "autopilot" / "controller"))
+
+from autopilot_state import schema
+
+FIXTURES = json.loads((CONTRACTS / "fixtures-v1.json").read_text())
+CASES = {case["name"]: case for case in FIXTURES["cases"]}
+CONTRACT = json.loads((CONTRACTS / "workflow-v1.json").read_text())
+
+
+class RecoveryCharacterizationTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def assert_state_rejected(self, value: object) -> None:
+        validator = Draft202012Validator({**CONTRACT, "$ref": "#/$defs/state"})
+        self.assertFalse(validator.is_valid(value))
+        with self.assertRaises(schema.SchemaError):
+            schema.validate_state(value)
+
+    def test_kernel_field_ownership_matches_pinned_source_characterization(self) -> None:
+        provenance = json.loads((CONTRACTS / "provenance.json").read_text())
+        ownership = FIXTURES["kernel_field_ownership"]
+        pin = "cf8be72214a515c84ee42f0d8b30e65cc2a4ebb7"
+        self.assertEqual(provenance["source"]["commit"], pin)
+        self.assertEqual(ownership["source_commit"], pin)
+        self.assertEqual(len(provenance["field_ownership"]), 144)
+        mappings = {
+            row["source"]: row["target"]
+            for row in provenance["field_ownership"]
+            if row["disposition"] in ("preserved", "redesigned")
+        }
+        self.assertEqual(ownership["core_mappings"], {
+            "WorkState.repo_root": "repo_root",
+            "ReviewState.cap": "workflow.review.cap",
+            "State.schema_version": "schema_version",
+            "State.revision": "revision",
+        })
+        self.assertEqual(mappings, ownership["core_mappings"])
+        self.assertEqual(CASES["kernel-initial"]["input"]["workflow"], {
+            "batch": None, "work": None, "tasks": [], "review": {"cap": 2},
+            "recovery": None, "jobs": [],
+        })
+
+    def test_kernel_field_ownership_rejects_unowned_fields(self) -> None:
+        ownership = FIXTURES["kernel_field_ownership"]
+        self.assertEqual(ownership["expected_error"], "invalid_request")
+        validator = Draft202012Validator({**CONTRACT, "$ref": "#/$defs/state"})
+        for name in ("kernel-initial", "kernel-owned"):
+            original = CASES[name]["input"]
+            validator.validate(original)
+            self.assertEqual(schema.validate_state(original), original)
+            for field in ownership["unowned_fields"]:
+                for location in ((), ("workflow",)):
+                    changed = copy.deepcopy(original)
+                    target = changed[location[0]] if location else changed
+                    target[field] = None
+                    with self.subTest(case=name, field=field, location=location):
+                        self.assertFalse(validator.is_valid(changed))
+                        with self.assertRaises(schema.SchemaError):
+                            schema.validate_state(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_state_requires_every_owned_top_level_field(self) -> None:
+        self.assert_state_rejected({})
+        original = CASES["kernel-initial"]["input"]
+        for field in original:
+            changed = copy.deepcopy(original)
+            del changed[field]
+            with self.subTest(missing=field):
+                self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_revision_rejects_noninteger_text(self) -> None:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-initial"]["input"])
+        changed["revision"] = "nonsense"
+        self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_revisions_and_epochs_reject_negative_values(self) -> None:
+        locations = (
+            ("revision",), ("lease_epoch",), ("owner", "lease_epoch"),
+            ("actors", "operator-synthetic", "lease_epoch"),
+            ("actors", "owner-synthetic", "lease_epoch"),
+            ("receipts", "open-synthetic", "authorizing_actor", "lease_epoch"),
+            ("receipts", "open-synthetic", "response", "revision"),
+            ("receipts", "open-synthetic", "response", "result", "lease_epoch"),
+        )
+        for location in locations:
+            changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-owned"]["input"])
+            target = changed
+            for field in location[:-1]:
+                target = target[field]
+            target[location[-1]] = -1
+            with self.subTest(location=location):
+                self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_owner_rejects_process_identity(self) -> None:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-owned"]["input"])
+        changed["owner"]["process_identity"] = "synthetic-process"
+        self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_actor_registry_rejects_three_valid_descriptors(self) -> None:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-owned"]["input"])
+        extra = copy.deepcopy(changed["actors"]["operator-synthetic"])
+        extra["actor_id"] = "operator-extra"
+        changed["actors"]["operator-extra"] = extra
+        validator = Draft202012Validator({**CONTRACT, "$ref": "#/$defs/actor"})
+        for descriptor in changed["actors"].values():
+            validator.validate(descriptor)
+        self.assertEqual(len(changed["actors"]), 3)
+        self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_tasks_cannot_be_populated(self) -> None:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-initial"]["input"])
+        changed["workflow"]["tasks"] = ["synthetic-task"]
+        self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_review_cap_remains_two(self) -> None:
+        changed = copy.deepcopy(CASES["kernel-initial"]["input"])
+        changed["workflow"]["review"]["cap"] = 99
+        self.assert_state_rejected(changed)
+
+    def test_kernel_accepts_independent_states_beyond_frozen_examples(self) -> None:
+        validator = Draft202012Validator({**CONTRACT, "$ref": "#/$defs/state"})
+        for revision in (0, 2):
+            value = {
+                "schema_version": 1, "revision": revision,
+                "project_id": "f" * 64,
+                "workflow_id": f"independent-workflow-{revision}",
+                "repo_root": "/independent/project", "lease_epoch": 0,
+                "owner": None, "actors": {}, "receipts": {},
+                "workflow": {
+                    "batch": None, "work": None, "tasks": [],
+                    "review": {"cap": 2}, "recovery": None, "jobs": [],
+                },
+            }
+            with self.subTest(revision=revision):
+                validator.validate(value)
+                self.assertEqual(schema.validate_state(value), value)
+
+    def test_contract_examples_reject_unowned_envelope_payload_and_response_fields(self) -> None:
+        self.assertEqual({example["case"] for example in FIXTURES["contract_examples"]}, {
+            "open-fresh", "open-existing", "acquire", "release", "recover",
+            "open-result", "acquire-result", "release-result", "recover-result",
+        })
+        for example in FIXTURES["contract_examples"]:
+            case = CASES[example["case"]]
+            validator = Draft202012Validator({
+                **CONTRACT, "$ref": f"#/$defs/{case['definition']}",
+            })
+            self.assertTrue(case["valid"])
+            self.assertEqual(example["expected_error"], "invalid_request")
+            validator.validate(case["input"])
+            for location in example["unowned_locations"]:
+                changed = copy.deepcopy(case["input"])
+                target = changed
+                for field in location:
+                    target = target[field]
+                target["process_identity"] = "synthetic-unowned"
+                with self.subTest(case=example["case"], location=location):
+                    self.assertFalse(validator.is_valid(changed))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
diff --git a/tests/autopilot/test_controller_staging_limits.py b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_staging_limits.py
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..3ee8ad8
--- /dev/null
+++ b/tests/autopilot/test_controller_staging_limits.py
@@ -0,0 +1,565 @@
+"""Bound real pre-intent crash evidence before bootstrap and owner admission."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+import secrets
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from controller_cli_support import MAIN, fresh_request, private_path
+from controller_owner_support import CRASH_SCRIPT, OwnerCLITest
+from test_controller_bootstrap_recovery import CRASH_DRIVER
+
+FILE_LIMIT = 64
+BYTE_LIMIT = 16777216
+OPERATIONS = ("workflow.open", "owner.acquire", "owner.release", "owner.recover")
+BOUNDARIES = ("stage_fsynced", "intent_replace")
+KERNEL_BOUNDARIES = ("backup_temp_fsynced", "state_temp_fsynced")
+DAMAGE_KINDS = ("unreadable", "permissions", "symlink", "hardlink", "directory", "fifo")
+
+# Stop immediately before publishing the fixed intent. This leaves the real
+# fsynced intent temporary and credential stages, without reading runtime code.
+INTENT_REPLACE_CRASH = r'''
+import os, runpy, sys
+from pathlib import Path
+main, project = sys.argv[1:3]
+root = Path(project) / ".autopilot" / "controller"
+real_replace = os.replace
+
+def destination(value, directory):
+    path = Path(os.fsdecode(value))
+    if path.is_absolute() or directory is None:
+        return path.absolute()
+    info = os.fstat(directory)
+    current = root.stat()
+    if (info.st_dev, info.st_ino) == (current.st_dev, current.st_ino):
+        return root / path
+    return None
+
+def replace(source, target, *args, **kwargs):
+    if destination(target, kwargs.get("dst_dir_fd")) == root / "credential-intent.json":
+        os._exit(89)
+    return real_replace(source, target, *args, **kwargs)
+
+os.replace = replace
+sys.argv = [main] + sys.argv[3:]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(main).parent))
+runpy.run_path(main, run_name="__main__")
+'''
+
+# Supply the documented public boundary hook to the real CLI's StateStore.
+# Abrupt process exit retains the publication temporary instead of unwinding it.
+STORE_TEMP_CRASH = r'''
+import os, runpy, sys
+from pathlib import Path
+main, boundary = sys.argv[1:3]
+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(main).parent))
+from autopilot_state.store import StateStore
+real_initialize = StateStore.__init__
+
+def initialize(self, path, *, boundary_hook=None):
+    def stop(item):
+        if boundary_hook is not None:
+            boundary_hook(item)
+        if item.value == boundary:
+            os._exit(88)
+    real_initialize(self, path, boundary_hook=stop)
+
+StateStore.__init__ = initialize
+sys.argv = [main] + sys.argv[3:]
+runpy.run_path(main, run_name="__main__")
+'''
+
+
+def signature(path: Path, *, changed: bool = True) -> tuple:
+    """Compare evidence without putting credential plaintext in test failures.
+
+    The inode change time exposes writes hidden by restored bytes or reset
+    modification times. Only an attended archive rename omits it, and the
+    contract's state.json.lock sidecar, whose metadata every locked call
+    refreshes; its bytes, mode and mtime still count.
+    """
+    info = path.lstat()
+    content = None
+    if stat.S_ISLNK(info.st_mode):
+        content = hashlib.sha256(os.fsencode(os.readlink(path))).hexdigest()
+    elif stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
+        try:
+            content = hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
+        except PermissionError:
+            content = "unreadable"
+    value = (info.st_dev, info.st_ino, info.st_mode, info.st_nlink,
+             info.st_uid, info.st_gid, info.st_size, info.st_mtime_ns, content)
+    if not changed or path.name == "state.json.lock":
+        return value
+    return value + (info.st_ctime_ns,)
+
+
+def evidence(root: Path) -> dict:
+    return {path: signature(path) for path in [root, *root.rglob("*")]}
+
+
+class ControllerStagingLimitsTest(OwnerCLITest):
+    def project(self, label: str) -> None:
+        self.root = self.base / label
+        self.root.mkdir()
+
+    def prepared(self, name: str, label: str) -> tuple[dict, Path | None]:
+        if name == "workflow.open":
+            return fresh_request(self.root, f"open-{label}"), None
+        _, _, operator = self.bootstrap()
+        actor = operator
+        if name != "owner.acquire":
+            _, _, owner, operator = self.acquire(operator, session=f"session-{label}")
+            actor = owner if name == "owner.release" else operator
+        payload = ({"mode": "manual" if label.endswith("0") else "supervised",
+                    "native_session_id": f"native-{label}"}
+                   if name == "owner.acquire" else
+                   {"reason": f"Attended orphan admission {label}", "reconciled_job_ids": []}
+                   if name == "owner.recover" else {})
+        return self.request(actor, name, f"mutate-{label}", payload), actor
+
+    def crash_attempt(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None,
+                      boundary: str) -> tuple[subprocess.CompletedProcess, int]:
+        if boundary == "intent_replace":
+            prefix = [sys.executable, "-c", INTENT_REPLACE_CRASH,
+                      str(MAIN), str(self.root)]
+            crash_code = 89
+        elif actor is None:
+            prefix = [sys.executable, "-c", CRASH_DRIVER, str(MAIN),
+                      str(self.root), "stage_fsynced"]
+            crash_code = 97
+        else:
+            prefix = [sys.executable, "-c", CRASH_SCRIPT, str(MAIN),
+                      str(self.root), "stage_fsynced",
+                      str(request["expected_revision"] + 1)]
+            crash_code = 87
+        return self.apply(request, actor, prefix=prefix), crash_code
+
+    def checked_response(self, completed: subprocess.CompletedProcess,
+                         request: dict, error: str | None = None) -> dict:
+        self.assertTrue(completed.returncode == (0 if error is None else 1),
+                        "CLI did not surface the expected structured outcome")
+        value = json.loads(completed.stdout)
+        self.assertTrue(set(value) == {"ok", "revision", "result", "error_code", "retryable"})
+        self.assertIs(value["ok"], error is None)
+        self.assertTrue(value["error_code"] == error)
+        self.assertIs(value["retryable"], False)
+        revision = request["expected_revision"] + (
+            error is None and request["operation"] != "workflow.open")
+        self.assertTrue(type(value["revision"]) is int and value["revision"] == revision)
+        if error is not None:
+            self.assertIsNone(value["result"])
+        return value
+
+    def stages_after_crash(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None,
+                           boundary: str) -> list[Path]:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        old = set(root.rglob("*")) if root.exists() else set()
+        completed, crash_code = self.crash_attempt(request, actor, boundary)
+        self.assertTrue(completed.returncode == crash_code, "pre-intent crash was not reached")
+        self.assertTrue(completed.stdout == b"", "crash acknowledged an unfinished mutation")
+        self.assertFalse((root / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+        stages = [path for path in root.rglob("*") if path not in old
+                  and path.name not in {".gitignore", "state.json.lock"} and path.is_file()]
+        self.assertTrue(bool(stages), "crash must leave real owned staging evidence")
+        for path in stages:
+            self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(path.stat().st_mode), 0o600)
+            self.assertEqual(path.stat().st_nlink, 1)
+        if boundary == "intent_replace":
+            self.assertTrue(any(path.parent == root for path in stages),
+                            "intent temporary must participate in resource admission")
+        return stages
+
+    def refuse_unchanged(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None) -> None:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        before = evidence(root)
+        self.checked_response(self.apply(request, actor), request, "recovery_required")
+        self.assertTrue(evidence(root) == before,
+                        "refusal changed evidence or created proposed files")
+        self.assertFalse((root / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+
+    def refuse_without_authority(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None) -> None:
+        """Bad revisions and forged credentials report state, never request echoes."""
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        current = self.state()["revision"] if (root / "state.json").exists() else 0
+        cases = [(request | {"expected_revision": request["expected_revision"] + 7}, actor, None)]
+        if actor is not None:
+            forged = self.retain(actor, f"forged-{self.serial}.json")
+            fields = json.loads(forged.read_bytes()) | {"secret": secrets.token_urlsafe(32)}
+            forged.write_bytes(json.dumps(fields).encode("utf-8"))
+            cases.append((request, forged, "recovery_required"))
+        for candidate, credential, excluded in cases:
+            before = evidence(root)
+            completed = self.apply(candidate, credential)
+            self.assertTrue(completed.returncode == 1, "invalid authority was not rejected")
+            value = json.loads(completed.stdout)
+            self.assertIs(value["ok"], False)
+            self.assertIsNone(value["result"])
+            self.assertTrue(type(value["revision"]) is int and value["revision"] == current,
+                            "rejection did not carry the current state revision")
+            self.assertTrue(value["error_code"] not in {None, excluded},
+                            "staging admission ran before actor authentication")
+            self.assertTrue(evidence(root) == before, "rejection changed evidence")
+
+    def crash_until_refused(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None, boundary: str,
+                            stages: list[Path]) -> list[Path]:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        stages = list(stages)
+        for _ in range(FILE_LIMIT + 1):
+            before = evidence(root)
+            completed, crash_code = self.crash_attempt(request, actor, boundary)
+            if completed.returncode != crash_code:
+                self.checked_response(completed, request, "recovery_required")
+                self.assertTrue(evidence(root) == before)
+                return stages
+            self.assertTrue(completed.stdout == b"")
+            new = [path for path in root.rglob("*") if path not in before and path.is_file()]
+            self.assertTrue(bool(new), "repeated crash must retain new evidence")
+            self.assertTrue(all(signature(path) == value for path, value in before.items()
+                                if path.is_file()))
+            stages.extend(new)
+            self.assertLessEqual(len(stages), FILE_LIMIT)
+            self.assertLess(sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages), BYTE_LIMIT // 2)
+            self.assertFalse((root / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+        self.fail("repeated crashes did not reach a fail-closed resource boundary")
+
+    def admit_at_count_boundary(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None, owned: list[Path],
+                                archivable: list[Path], proposal: int) -> None:
+        """Archive real orphans offline to one file over, then exactly at, the limit."""
+        self.assertGreater(len(owned) + proposal, FILE_LIMIT,
+                           "refused although the complete proposal fit the file limit")
+        owned, archivable = list(owned), list(archivable)
+        while len(owned) + proposal > FILE_LIMIT:
+            if len(owned) + proposal == FILE_LIMIT + 1:
+                self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+            path = archivable.pop()
+            self.archive_one(path)
+            owned.remove(path)
+        self.assertEqual(len(owned) + proposal, FILE_LIMIT)
+        self.succeed_preserving(request, actor, owned)
+
+    def succeed_preserving(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None,
+                           orphans: list[Path]) -> None:
+        before = {path: signature(path) for path in orphans}
+        historical = self.retain(actor, f"replay-{self.serial}.json") if actor is not None else None
+        response = self.checked_response(self.apply(request, actor), request)
+        self.assertTrue({path: signature(path) for path in orphans} == before,
+                        "successful admission removed or rewrote orphan evidence")
+        state = self.state()
+        self.assertEqual(state["repo_root"], str(self.root))
+        self.assertEqual(state["project_id"], request["project_id"])
+        self.assertTrue(state["receipts"][request["request_id"]]["response"] == response)
+        committed = evidence(private_path(self.root))
+        self.assertTrue(self.checked_response(self.apply(request, historical), request) == response)
+        self.assertTrue(evidence(private_path(self.root)) == committed)
+
+    def archive_one(self, path: Path) -> None:
+        archive = self.base / f"offline-{self.root.name}"
+        archive.mkdir(mode=0o700, exist_ok=True)
+        # A rename legitimately updates the inode change time.
+        before = signature(path, changed=False)
+        destination = archive / path.name
+        path.rename(destination)
+        self.assertTrue(signature(destination, changed=False) == before,
+                        "attended fixture archive did not retain the original evidence")
+
+    def read_only_at_saturation(self) -> None:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        before = evidence(root)
+        state = self.state()
+        opened = state["receipts"]["open-first"]["response"]
+        operator = Path(opened["result"]["actor_file"])
+        snapshot = self.snapshot()
+        self.assertEqual(snapshot["lease_epoch"], state["lease_epoch"])
+        original = fresh_request(self.root)
+        replay = self.checked_response(self.apply(original, operator), original)
+        self.assertTrue(replay == opened, "saturation changed an existing exact receipt")
+        self.assertTrue(evidence(root) == before,
+                        "read-only calls changed saturated staging evidence")
+
+    def test_repeated_pre_intent_crashes_stop_at_file_budget_without_changing_evidence(self) -> None:
+        proposals: dict[str, int] = {}
+        for name in OPERATIONS:
+            # An intent_replace crash stages the complete proposal; measure it first.
+            for boundary in reversed(BOUNDARIES):
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary):
+                    label = f"count-{name}-{boundary}"
+                    self.project(label)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                    stages = self.stages_after_crash(request, actor, boundary)
+                    if boundary == "intent_replace":
+                        proposals[name] = len(stages)
+                    self.assertIn(name, proposals, "complete proposal size was not measured")
+                    proposal = proposals[name]
+                    self.assertLessEqual(len(stages), proposal)
+                    fixed = {path: signature(path) for path in private_path(self.root).rglob("*")
+                             if path.is_file() and path not in stages}
+                    stages = self.crash_until_refused(request, actor, boundary, stages)
+                    self.assertGreater(len(stages), 1)
+                    self.assertTrue(all(signature(path) == value for path, value in fixed.items()))
+                    self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+                    self.refuse_unchanged(request | {"request_id": request["request_id"] + "-near"}, actor)
+                    self.refuse_without_authority(request, actor)
+                    if actor is not None:
+                        self.read_only_at_saturation()
+                    # Retain crash files offline one at a time: one file over
+                    # the limit still refuses, an exact fit is admitted.
+                    self.admit_at_count_boundary(request, actor, stages, stages, proposal)
+
+    def test_byte_budget_refuses_below_at_and_above_limit_independently_of_count(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS:
+            for boundary in BOUNDARIES:
+                for delta in (-1, 0, 1):
+                    with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary, delta=delta):
+                        label = f"bytes-{name}-{boundary}-{delta}"
+                        self.project(label)
+                        request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                        stages = self.stages_after_crash(request, actor, boundary)
+                        self.assertLess(len(stages), FILE_LIMIT // 2)
+                        other = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages[1:])
+                        with stages[0].open("r+b") as stream:
+                            stream.truncate(BYTE_LIMIT + delta - other)
+                        self.assertEqual(sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages), BYTE_LIMIT + delta)
+                        self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+                        self.refuse_unchanged(request | {"request_id": request["request_id"] + "-near"}, actor)
+                        self.refuse_without_authority(request, actor)
+                        if actor is not None:
+                            self.read_only_at_saturation()
+
+    def test_complete_proposed_byte_batch_fits_exact_ceiling_but_next_byte_refuses(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS:
+            for delta in (0, 1):
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, excess_bytes=delta):
+                    label = f"inclusive-{name}-{delta}"
+                    self.project(label)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                    stages = self.stages_after_crash(request, actor, "intent_replace")
+                    proposal = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages)
+                    other = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages[1:])
+                    self.assertLess(2 * len(stages), FILE_LIMIT)
+                    self.assertLess(2 * proposal, BYTE_LIMIT)
+                    with stages[0].open("r+b") as stream:
+                        stream.truncate(BYTE_LIMIT + delta - proposal - other)
+                    existing = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages)
+                    self.assertEqual(existing + proposal, BYTE_LIMIT + delta)
+                    if delta:
+                        self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+                        self.refuse_without_authority(request, actor)
+                        if actor is not None:
+                            self.read_only_at_saturation()
+                    else:
+                        self.succeed_preserving(request, actor, stages)
+
+    def publication_orphans(self, request: dict, actor: Path,
+                            boundary: str) -> tuple[list[Path], dict]:
+        root = private_path(self.root)
+        before = set(root.iterdir())
+        historical = self.retain(actor, f"kernel-authorizer-{self.serial}.json")
+        prefix = [sys.executable, "-c", STORE_TEMP_CRASH, str(MAIN), boundary]
+        completed = self.apply(request, actor, prefix=prefix)
+        self.assertTrue(completed.returncode == 88, "kernel temporary crash was not reached")
+        self.assertTrue(completed.stdout == b"", "crash acknowledged unfinished publication")
+        self.assertTrue((root / "credential-intent.json").is_file())
+        orphans = [path for path in root.iterdir() if path not in before
+                   and path.name not in {"credential-intent.json", "state.json", "state.json.bak"}
+                   and path.is_file()]
+        self.assertTrue(bool(orphans), "public kernel boundary must retain a real temporary")
+        retained = {path: signature(path) for path in orphans}
+        response = self.checked_response(self.apply(request, historical), request)
+        self.assertFalse((root / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+        self.assertTrue({path: signature(path) for path in orphans} == retained,
+                        "matching intent reconciliation changed the kernel orphan")
+        self.assertTrue(self.state()["receipts"][request["request_id"]]["response"] == response)
+        committed = evidence(root)
+        self.assertTrue(self.checked_response(self.apply(request, historical), request) == response)
+        self.assertTrue(evidence(root) == committed)
+        return orphans, response
+
+    def following_mutation(self, name: str, response: dict) -> tuple[dict, Path]:
+        operator = Path(response["result"]["operator_actor_file"])
+        next_name = "owner.recover" if name == "owner.acquire" else "owner.acquire"
+        payload = ({"reason": "Attended kernel orphan recovery", "reconciled_job_ids": []}
+                   if next_name == "owner.recover" else
+                   {"mode": "manual", "native_session_id": "after-kernel-orphan"})
+        return self.request(operator, next_name, "after-kernel-orphan", payload), operator
+
+    def test_reconciled_kernel_publication_orphans_count_toward_next_mutation_byte_budget(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS[1:]:
+            for boundary in KERNEL_BOUNDARIES:
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary):
+                    label = f"kernel-{name}-{boundary}"
+                    self.project(label)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                    self.assertIsNotNone(actor)
+                    orphans, response = self.publication_orphans(request, actor, boundary)
+                    self.assertLess(len(orphans), FILE_LIMIT // 2)
+                    other = sum(path.stat().st_size for path in orphans[1:])
+                    with orphans[0].open("r+b") as stream:
+                        stream.truncate(BYTE_LIMIT - other)
+                    self.assertEqual(sum(path.stat().st_size for path in orphans), BYTE_LIMIT)
+                    following, operator = self.following_mutation(name, response)
+                    self.refuse_unchanged(following, operator)
+                    self.refuse_without_authority(following, operator)
+                    self.read_only_at_saturation()
+
+    def test_reconciled_kernel_publication_orphans_count_toward_next_mutation_file_budget(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS[1:]:
+            for boundary in KERNEL_BOUNDARIES:
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary):
+                    label = f"kernel-count-{name}-{boundary}"
+                    self.project(label)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                    orphans, response = self.publication_orphans(request, actor, boundary)
+                    following, operator = self.following_mutation(name, response)
+                    batch = self.stages_after_crash(following, operator, "intent_replace")
+                    owned = self.crash_until_refused(following, operator, "intent_replace",
+                                                     orphans + batch)
+                    self.refuse_without_authority(following, operator)
+                    self.read_only_at_saturation()
+                    # Only crash stages are archived, so every kernel orphan
+                    # stays in the owned set at both count boundaries.
+                    crashed = [path for path in owned if path not in orphans]
+                    self.admit_at_count_boundary(following, operator, owned, crashed, len(batch))
+
+    def test_unsafe_kernel_publication_orphans_refuse_next_mutation_without_touching_evidence(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS[1:]:
+            for boundary in KERNEL_BOUNDARIES:
+                with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary):
+                    label = f"kernel-unsafe-{name}-{boundary}"
+                    self.project(label)
+                    request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                    orphans, response = self.publication_orphans(request, actor, boundary)
+                    following, operator = self.following_mutation(name, response)
+                    for kind in DAMAGE_KINDS:
+                        for target in orphans:
+                            self.refuse_damaged(following, operator, target, kind)
+                    # Every orphan is restored, so the same mutation is admitted.
+                    self.succeed_preserving(following, operator, orphans)
+
+    def test_safe_orphans_below_both_limits_allow_real_mutations_and_exact_replay(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS:
+            for boundary in BOUNDARIES:
+                for size in (1048576, 2097152):
+                    with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary, size=size):
+                        label = f"allowed-{name}-{boundary}-{size}"
+                        self.project(label)
+                        request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                        stages = self.stages_after_crash(request, actor, boundary)
+                        with stages[0].open("r+b") as stream:
+                            stream.truncate(size)
+                        self.assertLess(len(stages), FILE_LIMIT)
+                        self.assertLess(sum(path.stat().st_size for path in stages), BYTE_LIMIT)
+                        self.succeed_preserving(request, actor, stages)
+
+    def damage(self, path: Path, kind: str) -> Path | None:
+        if kind == "unreadable":
+            path.chmod(0)
+            self.addCleanup(path.chmod, 0o600)
+            return None
+        if kind == "permissions":
+            path.chmod(0o640)
+            return None
+        outside = self.base / f"outside-{self.serial}"
+        outside.write_bytes(path.read_bytes())
+        outside.chmod(0o600)
+        path.unlink()
+        if kind == "symlink":
+            path.symlink_to(outside)
+        elif kind == "hardlink":
+            os.link(outside, path)
+        elif kind == "directory":
+            path.mkdir(mode=0o700)
+        else:
+            os.mkfifo(path, 0o600)
+        return outside
+
+    def restore(self, path: Path, kind: str, outside: Path | None) -> None:
+        """Put the original bytes back as a safe private file after a refusal."""
+        if outside is None:
+            path.chmod(0o600)
+            return
+        if kind == "directory":
+            path.rmdir()
+        else:
+            path.unlink()
+        outside.rename(path)
+
+    def refuse_damaged(self, request: dict, actor: Path | None, target: Path, kind: str) -> None:
+        outside = self.damage(target, kind)
+        before = signature(outside) if outside is not None else None
+        self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+        if outside is not None:
+            self.assertTrue(signature(outside) == before)
+        self.restore(target, kind, outside)
+
+    def test_unsafe_or_unreadable_owned_artifacts_refuse_without_touching_evidence(self) -> None:
+        for name in OPERATIONS:
+            for boundary in BOUNDARIES:
+                for kind in DAMAGE_KINDS:
+                    with self.subTest(operation=name, boundary=boundary, kind=kind):
+                        label = f"unsafe-{name}-{boundary}-{kind}"
+                        self.project(label)
+                        request, actor = self.prepared(name, label)
+                        stages = self.stages_after_crash(request, actor, boundary)
+                        # Exercise the root intent temporary first, then every
+                        # credential stage and rollback copy the crash left.
+                        ordered = sorted(stages, key=lambda path: path.parent != private_path(self.root))
+                        target = ordered[0]
+                        outside = self.damage(target, kind)
+                        before = signature(outside) if outside is not None else None
+                        self.refuse_unchanged(request, actor)
+                        self.refuse_unchanged(request | {"request_id": request["request_id"] + "-near"}, actor)
+                        self.refuse_without_authority(request, actor)
+                        if outside is not None:
+                            self.assertTrue(signature(outside) == before)
+                        self.restore(target, kind, outside)
+                        for path in ordered[1:]:
+                            self.refuse_damaged(request, actor, path, kind)
+
+    def test_empty_staging_set_allows_bootstrap_and_all_owner_mutations(self) -> None:
+        for suffix in ("alpha", "beta"):
+            with self.subTest(project=suffix):
+                self.project(f"empty-{suffix}")
+                request, actor = self.prepared("workflow.open", suffix)
+                self.succeed_preserving(request, actor, [])
+                operator = Path(self.state()["receipts"][request["request_id"]]["response"]["result"]["actor_file"])
+                _, _, owner, operator = self.acquire(operator, mode="manual", session=f"native-{suffix}")
+                _, _, operator = self.clear(owner, request_id=f"release-{suffix}")
+                _, _, _, operator = self.acquire(operator, mode="supervised", session=f"next-{suffix}",
+                                                  request_id=f"reacquire-{suffix}")
+                self.clear(operator, "owner.recover", request_id=f"recover-{suffix}")
+                self.assertIsNone(self.state()["owner"])
+                self.assertFalse((private_path(self.root) / "credential-intent.json").exists())
+
+    def test_retained_historical_final_credentials_do_not_consume_staging_file_budget(self) -> None:
+        _, _, operator = self.bootstrap()
+        historical = []
+        for index in range(FILE_LIMIT + 2):
+            _, _, owner, operator = self.acquire(
+                operator, session=f"history-session-{index}", request_id=f"history-acquire-{index}")
+            content = owner.read_bytes()
+            _, _, operator = self.clear(owner, request_id=f"history-release-{index}")
+            # Retain the exact returned final path and bytes if revocation
+            # removes that file. No staging filename is invented here.
+            if not owner.exists():
+                owner.write_bytes(content)
+                owner.chmod(0o600)
+            self.assertTrue(owner.read_bytes() == content)
+            historical.append(owner)
+        self.assertGreater(len(set(historical)), FILE_LIMIT)
+        before = {path: signature(path) for path in historical}
+        request = self.request(operator, "owner.acquire", "after-history",
+                               {"mode": "supervised", "native_session_id": "history-final"})
+        self.succeed_preserving(request, operator, historical)
+        self.assertTrue({path: signature(path) for path in historical} == before)
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+"""Adversarial publication and initialization checks for the public store API."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import copy
+import errno
+import json
+import os
+import stat
+import subprocess
+import sys
+import tempfile
+import time
+import unittest
+from pathlib import Path
+from unittest import mock
+
+import test_controller_kernel as kernel
+
+
+INITIALIZER = """
+import json, os, sys, time
+from pathlib import Path
+sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
+from autopilot_state.store import StateStore, StateExistsError
+path, gate, ready, rendezvous = map(Path, sys.argv[2:6])
+candidate = json.loads(sys.argv[6])
+real_open = os.open
+
+def coordinated_open(file: str | bytes | os.PathLike, flags: int, *args: object, **kwargs: object) -> int:
+    if os.fspath(file) in (str(path), path.name) and flags & os.O_CREAT:
+        rendezvous.write_text('at creation')
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 2
+        peers = [rendezvous.parent / ('creation-' + str(index)) for index in range(2)]
+        while not all(peer.exists() for peer in peers) and time.monotonic() < deadline:
+            time.sleep(0.005)
+    return real_open(file, flags, *args, **kwargs)
+
+os.open = coordinated_open
+ready.write_text('ready')
+deadline = time.monotonic() + 15
+while not gate.exists():
+    if time.monotonic() > deadline:
+        raise RuntimeError('initializer start gate timeout')
+    time.sleep(0.005)
+try:
+    result = StateStore(path).initialize(candidate)
+    print(json.dumps({'outcome': 'initialized', 'state': result, 'bytes': path.read_bytes().hex()}))
+except StateExistsError:
+    print(json.dumps({'outcome': 'exists'}))
+"""
+
+
+class StoreGuardTest(unittest.TestCase):
+    def setUp(self) -> None:
+        self.temporary = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
+        self.addCleanup(self.temporary.cleanup)
+        self.base = Path(self.temporary.name)
+        self.path = self.base / "state.json"
+        self.backup = self.base / "state.json.bak"
+        self.store = kernel.StateStore(self.path)
+        self.initial = kernel.frozen_state()
+
+    def seed_pair(self) -> dict:
+        self.store.initialize(self.initial)
+        return self.store.transaction(lambda value: None, expected_revision=0)
+
+    def pair(self) -> tuple[bytes, bytes]:
+        return self.path.read_bytes(), self.backup.read_bytes()
+
+    def test_file_contents_are_synced_before_their_publication_boundaries(self) -> None:
+        self.seed_pair()
+        synced = []
+        snapshots = {}
+        real_fsync = os.fsync
+
+        def fsync(fd: int) -> None:
+            info = os.fstat(fd)
+            real_fsync(fd)
+            if stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode):
+                synced.append((info.st_dev, info.st_ino))
+
+        def boundary(item: kernel.DurabilityBoundary) -> None:
+            if item.name in ("BACKUP_TEMP_FSYNCED", "STATE_TEMP_FSYNCED"):
+                self.assertTrue(synced, f"{item.name} requires a successful file fsync")
+                snapshots[item.name] = tuple(synced)
+                synced.clear()
+            elif item.name in ("BACKUP_REPLACED", "STATE_REPLACED"):
+                target = self.backup if item.name == "BACKUP_REPLACED" else self.path
+                info = target.stat()
+                key = item.name.replace("REPLACED", "TEMP_FSYNCED")
+                self.assertIn((info.st_dev, info.st_ino), snapshots[key])
+
+        store = kernel.StateStore(self.path, boundary_hook=boundary)
+        with mock.patch("os.fsync", side_effect=fsync):
+            result = store.transaction(lambda value: None, expected_revision=1)
+        self.assertEqual(result, dict(self.initial, revision=2))
+        self.assertEqual(self.store.read(), result)
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.backup.read_bytes()), dict(self.initial, revision=1))
+        self.assertEqual(set(snapshots), {"BACKUP_TEMP_FSYNCED", "STATE_TEMP_FSYNCED"})
+
+    def test_file_fsync_errors_reject_publication_and_preserve_the_exact_pair(self) -> None:
+        current = self.seed_pair()
+        before = self.pair()
+        real_fsync = os.fsync
+        for ordinal, boundary in enumerate((kernel.DurabilityBoundary.BACKUP_TEMP_FSYNCED,
+                                            kernel.DurabilityBoundary.STATE_TEMP_FSYNCED), 1):
+            synced = []
+            observed = []
+
+            def fsync(fd: int) -> None:
+                if stat.S_ISREG(os.fstat(fd).st_mode):
+                    synced.append(fd)
+                    if len(synced) == ordinal:
+                        raise OSError(errno.EIO, "file contents fsync failed")
+                real_fsync(fd)
+
+            with self.subTest(boundary=boundary):
+                store = kernel.StateStore(self.path, boundary_hook=observed.append)
+                with mock.patch("os.fsync", side_effect=fsync):
+                    with self.assertRaises(kernel.StateIOError):
+                        store.transaction(lambda value: None, expected_revision=1)
+                self.assertGreaterEqual(len(synced), ordinal)
+                self.assertNotIn(boundary, observed)
+                self.assertEqual(self.pair(), before)
+                self.assertEqual(self.store.read(), current)
+
+    def test_replacement_mutators_reject_changed_guards_at_every_boundary(self) -> None:
+        for revision in (1, 2):
+            for boundary in kernel.DurabilityBoundary:
+                directory = self.base / f"{revision}-{boundary.value}"
+                directory.mkdir()
+                path = directory / "state.json"
+                backup = directory / "state.json.bak"
+                seed = kernel.StateStore(path)
+                seed.initialize(self.initial)
+                for _ in range(revision):
+                    current = seed.transaction(lambda value: None)
+                before = (path.read_bytes(), backup.read_bytes())
+                replacement = copy.deepcopy(current)
+                replacement["repo_root"] = "/synthetic/replacement-project"
+                self.assertEqual(kernel.schema.validate_state(replacement), replacement)
+                calls = []
+                observed = []
+
+                def guard() -> None:
+                    observed.append(tuple(calls))
+                    if boundary in calls:
+                        raise RuntimeError(f"publication evidence changed: {boundary.value}")
+
+                with self.subTest(boundary=boundary, revision=revision):
+                    store = kernel.StateStore(path, boundary_hook=calls.append)
+                    with self.assertRaisesRegex(RuntimeError, f"changed: {boundary.value}"):
+                        store.transaction(lambda value: replacement, expected_revision=revision,
+                                          publication_guard=guard)
+                    expected = list(kernel.DurabilityBoundary)
+                    expected = expected[:expected.index(boundary) + 1]
+                    self.assertEqual(calls, expected)
+                    self.assertIn(tuple(expected), observed)
+                    self.assertEqual((path.read_bytes(), backup.read_bytes()), before)
+                    self.assertEqual(seed.read(), current)
+                    self.assertEqual(seed.read()["revision"], revision)
+
+    def run_initializers(self, candidates: list[dict]) -> list[dict]:
+        gate = self.base / "start-gate"
+        processes = []
+        for index, candidate in enumerate(candidates):
+            ready = self.base / f"ready-{index}"
+            rendezvous = self.base / f"creation-{index}"
+            command = [sys.executable, "-c", INITIALIZER, str(kernel.CONTROLLER),
+                       str(self.path), str(gate), str(ready), str(rendezvous), json.dumps(candidate)]
+            process = subprocess.Popen(command, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
+                                       cwd=self.base, env=dict(os.environ, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE="1"))
+            processes.append(process)
+            self.addCleanup(kernel.StoreTest.stop_process, process)
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 20
+        while not all((self.base / f"ready-{index}").exists() for index in range(len(candidates))):
+            self.assertLess(time.monotonic(), deadline, "initializers must reach the start gate")
+            time.sleep(0.01)
+        gate.write_text("start")
+        results = []
+        for process in processes:
+            output, error = process.communicate(timeout=30)
+            self.assertEqual(process.returncode, 0, error.decode(errors="replace"))
+            self.assertEqual(error, b"")
+            results.append(json.loads(output))
+        return results
+
+    def test_competing_initializers_publish_exactly_one_intact_winner(self) -> None:
+        candidates = [dict(self.initial, repo_root=f"/synthetic/initializer-{index}")
+                      for index in range(2)]
+        for candidate in candidates:
+            self.assertEqual(kernel.schema.validate_state(candidate), candidate)
+        results = self.run_initializers(candidates)
+        self.assertEqual([item["outcome"] for item in results].count("initialized"), 1)
+        self.assertEqual([item["outcome"] for item in results].count("exists"), 1)
+        success = next(item for item in results if item["outcome"] == "initialized")
+        winner = success["state"]
+        self.assertIn(winner, candidates)
+        self.assertEqual(self.path.read_bytes(), bytes.fromhex(success["bytes"]))
+        self.assertEqual(json.loads(self.path.read_bytes()), winner)
+        self.assertEqual(self.store.read(), winner)
+        self.assertEqual(stat.S_IMODE(self.path.stat().st_mode) & 0o077, 0)
+        self.assertFalse(self.backup.exists())
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()
